title: Touch design pass: markers/popovers/drawing assume mouse
description:
Honest-map item: hover-discovery, popover anchoring, and draw gestures have no touch design. Needs a deliberate pass (tap targets, long-press vs drag semantics, popover placement on small viewports).

---

## Scope note, 2026-07-25 (Viewer UX audit): unreduced, and now demonstrably two-sided

The viewer audit produced 76 findings across six reader journeys and **every one was driven on a
desktop pointer**. Nothing in it touched this ticket's scope, so its scope is not reduced by any of
that work — and the audit surfaced concrete viewer-side instances of exactly what this describes:
hover-discovery on canvas marks, popover anchoring (the note card floats beside the canvas), and
floating chrome placement on small viewports ([Archie-40fe]).

Treat this as covering BOTH apps. A touch pass on Studio alone would leave the read surface — the
one an institutional visitor actually meets, and the one most likely to be opened on a phone —
untouched.

## TAP TARGETS: SHIPPED 2026-07-27 (5defa37). The DESIGN half remains.

**DONE — the measurable half.** At 390x844 with touch emulation the viewer's reader chrome shipped
ELEVEN controls between 19 and 23 px: object-nav arrows 20x19, the four reading toggles 23, "Hide
all" 19, "Hide notes" 20x20, "Back to Exhibit" 23, filmstrip toggle 22. Each only a pixel or three
short, each set by its own component's padding — which is how a floor drifts when it is never stated.
Now stated once in `atmosphere.css` (24px min-height/min-width on every control), with the SC's own
two carve-outs: inline text links are exempt (enlarging one breaks the sentence), and the resize
divider is widened to 24px only under `@media (pointer: coarse)` since it takes its width from the
panes it divides on every pointer. Gate: `apps/viewer/e2e/touch-targets.spec.ts`, driven with
hasTouch/isMobile so the browser reports `pointer: coarse`. 11 -> 0; full viewer e2e 149/149 twice,
so the global min-height reflowed nothing.

Two SPECIFICITY traps worth knowing, both found by re-measuring rather than by reading CSS:
`.carousel .cnav { min-width: 1.25rem }` beat the shared floor; and the divider's media query written
in the app's GLOBAL sheet silently lost to Svelte's scoped hash class — it has to live in the
component. Anything else that tries to set a global floor here will hit both.

**REMAINING — the design half, which is what this ticket was really about.** Unreduced:
- long-press vs drag semantics for drawing (no touch design exists)
- popover/note-card anchoring on small viewports (the card floats beside the canvas — see Archie-40fe)
- hover-discovery on canvas marks: there IS no hover on touch, so anything discoverable only by
  hovering is undiscoverable on a phone. This is the biggest one and it is a design question.
- STUDIO is untouched by the above; the tap-target sweep covered the viewer, the surface the scope
  note calls out as most likely to be opened on a phone. Studio needs the same sweep.
These need a real device and decisions, not assertions.

title: Accessibility pass: screen-reader walk + overlay contrast gate
description:
Honest-map item: aria/keyboard exist piecemeal; no SR testing has ever been done. Overlay contrast is v1.1-gated (CONTEXT orphan gap 4) — schedule before first institutional pilot.

---

## Scope call, 2026-07-25 (Viewer UX audit): NEITHER folds in NOR narrows to Studio

`Archie-c831` asked at resolution whether the read surface's a11y subset should fold into this
ticket. Answer: no, and this ticket does not narrow to Studio either. They are different activities.

- The per-finding structural work — roles, accessible names, focus behaviour, tab-stop counts — is
  being done ON each map as defects (viewer: c831 merged, [Archie-3d55] open for the canvas).
- This ticket is a SCREEN-READER WALK, which has never been done anywhere in the repo, plus the
  overlay contrast gate. Structural correctness is a precondition for that walk being worth
  running, not a substitute for it. A surface can have perfect roles and still be unusable to
  narrate.

So: the viewer's fixes REDUCE what this walk will find; they do not replace it. Keep it
cross-cutting over both apps. Run it after [Archie-3d55] lands, so the walk is not just
rediscovering known structural gaps.

## OVERLAY CONTRAST GATE: SHIPPED 2026-07-27 (665d605). The SCREEN-READER WALK remains.

This ticket is two activities. One is now done; the other is the one that needs a human.

**DONE — the overlay contrast gate** (`packages/render-core/src/query/marker-contrast.ts` + its test).
Two rules, because contrast alone is the wrong instrument: WCAG contrast is a LUMINANCE ratio, so it
cannot tell you whether two markers are distinguishable — two colours of equal lightness and opposite
hue are obviously different and score ~1.0.
  1. VISIBILITY — >=3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) against BOTH white and black, since a marker sits over an
     arbitrary photograph and there is no known background. Note contrast-vs-white x contrast-vs-black
     is always 21, so this confines every swatch to a mid-luminance band; it is a real constraint.
  2. DISTINGUISHABILITY — CIE76 dE in Lab, re-measured under simulated deuteranopia and protanopia
     (Vienot-Brettel-Mollon).

**Rule 2 found a live defect.** The shipped palette's rust `#a3553a` and ochre `#8a6d3b` collapsed to
**dE 1.3** under deuteranopia — indistinguishable to ~8% of men, with no signal that two different
readings were on screen. `#4c5d8a`/`#6b4c8a` were nearly as bad. Replaced with an Okabe-Ito-derived
set whose worst pair is **dE 13.6** across all three vision types; `#3A8C5D` kept first because it is
also `BASE_MARKER`. Only the picker's swatches changed — stored reading colours are untouched. The old
palette is pinned as a regression-guard test.

**REMAINING — the screen-reader walk.** Unchanged and genuinely human: drive both apps with a real
screen reader (Orca on this machine, or NVDA/VoiceOver) and record what is unnarratable. The scope
call above still holds — the per-finding structural work is done on each map as defects (Archie-3d55
is now CLOSED, so its stated precondition is met), and those fixes REDUCE what the walk finds without
replacing it. A surface can have perfect roles and still be impossible to narrate.

Note `Archie-ea57` shipped an axe ratchet over the published static pages (which found and fixed 676
contrast violations), so automated coverage of THAT artifact exists now; it does not cover the app
surfaces, and no automated check substitutes for the walk.

     is always 21, so this confines every swatch to a mid-luminance band; it is a real constraint.
  2. DISTINGUISHABILITY — CIE76 dE in Lab, re-measured under simulated deuteranopia and protanopia
     (Vienot-Brettel-Mollon).

**Rule 2 found a live defect.** The shipped palette's rust `#a3553a` and ochre `#8a6d3b` collapsed to
**dE 1.3** under deuteranopia — indistinguishable to ~8% of men, with no signal that two different
readings were on screen. `#4c5d8a`/`#6b4c8a` were nearly as bad. Replaced with an Okabe-Ito-derived
set whose worst pair is **dE 13.6** across all three vision types; `#3A8C5D` kept first because it is
also `BASE_MARKER`. Only the picker's swatches changed — stored reading colours are untouched. The old
palette is pinned as a regression-guard test.

**REMAINING — the screen-reader walk.** Unchanged and genuinely human: drive both apps with a real
screen reader (Orca on this machine, or NVDA/VoiceOver) and record what is unnarratable. The scope
call above still holds — the per-finding structural work is done on each map as defects (Archie-3d55
is now CLOSED, so its stated precondition is met), and those fixes REDUCE what the walk finds without
replacing it. A surface can have perfect roles and still be impossible to narrate.

Note `Archie-ea57` shipped an axe ratchet over the published static pages (which found and fixed 676
contrast violations), so automated coverage of THAT artifact exists now; it does not cover the app
surfaces, and no automated check substitutes for the walk.

closeReason: GRILLED 2026-07-19, decisions final. SCOPE: full — new mints change AND existing libraries migrate in place. IDS: migrated objects get deterministic composed ids <exhibitId>.<oldOrdinal> (ex-voynich.o1) so independently-migrated copies converge and the merge layer survives; NEW mints get ULID-style random ids (logicalId family) because deterministic mints collide on concurrent adds; nextObjectId retired — grilling found it can REUSE a deleted object's ordinal (tombstoned notes could resurrect onto the wrong object). Both shapes opaque; only the migration parses ids. REWRITE: in place, full history incl tombstones, DAG shape untouched; five classes (object metas, annotation targets, archie: link refs via parseLinkRef, SectionRecord.objectId, pending-notes sidecar); carry sentinel + exhaustiveness fixture; seeds move to new grammar; localStorage per-object prefs = documented accepted loss; assets never move. title: SNAG: zoom-band (1.1) and arrival-pulse (1.3) CSS are INERT — Annotorious 3 renders marks to WebGL canvas
description:
Browser probe 2026-06-11 (verify-readings-rail work): annotation layer is canvas.a9s-gl-canvas; svg.a9s-annotationlayer has NO per-annotation children, so CSS targeting .a9s-annotation (Canvas.svelte zoom-band weights, Reader.svelte arrival breathe, and the pre-existing drop-shadow rule) styles nothing. Redo both through the JS style channel: zoom band → modulate readingMarkerStyle via setStyle on zoom-band change; arrival pulse → timed style-expression sweep (or OSD overlay). The comparing regime is UNAFFECTED (it already rides DrawingStyleExpression).

## Triage note 2026-07-19 — RE-PROBE BEFORE FIXING
The 2026-06-11 premise (svg.a9s-annotationlayer has NO per-annotation children) may be stale: Canvas.svelte:~102 now queries .a9s-annotation[data-id] SVG nodes for the Q-5 a11y marker labels, and that shipped through browser-verified a11y merges (9d33b29/32ed159). Either Annotorious renders per-annotation SVG after all (→ the CSS may NOT be inert, and this ticket shrinks or closes) or the a11y labels query phantom nodes (→ a second bug). First step is a live-browser probe of the DOM under the annotation layer; do it AFTER the d48e chrome rewrite lands so the probe is against a stable tree.

## Probe result 2026-07-19 (ledgers/PROBE-annotorious-dom-2026-07-19.md)
Re-probe CONFIRMS the premise — not stale. Live studio probe (Rosettes exhibit, 5 notes, 4 checkpoints incl. 104x zoomOnSelect): svg.a9s-annotationlayer's only child is one empty transform <g>; .a9s-annotation matches 0 nodes ALWAYS; marks render via canvas.a9s-gl-canvas (WebGL/PixiJS). Zoom-band + arrival-pulse CSS confirmed inert; silent (zero console errors). FIX SHAPE: reimplement weight-by-zoom inside the Annotorious style callback (where @render/mount configures the style function), NOT as CSS. Viewer Reader.svelte:326 rides the same pipeline — same fix channel. Side finding forked to Archie-3e12 (dead labelMarkers a11y post-pass).
closeReason: Merged 835ec8a (wf/style-channel 1cdde6c, base d179432). SNAG resolved in two acts: (1) re-probe CONFIRMED the 2026-06-11 premise — Annotorious 3 renders zero per-annotation SVG at every state incl 104x zoom, marks are WebGL (ledgers/PROBE-annotorious-dom-2026-07-19.md); (2) both effects reimplemented through the ONE DrawingStyleExpression channel as pure post-modulations over readingMarkerStyle's spec: withZoomBand (studio; memoized $derived band string — re-mints styleOf only on far/mid/near crossings, never per zoom frame) and withArrivalPulse (viewer; rAF-bounded 1400ms, stops at k=0, cancelAnimationFrame on unmount). Inert .a9s-annotation CSS deleted in all three places. Browser-verify found+fixed a REAL bug: arrival originally fired at island-mount but createMount awaits remote OSD open (>1.4s on Yale IIIF) so the pulse decayed invisibly — now armed on object landing, fired on canvas-ready first onzoom; rapid-nav race clean ({#key} remount + cancel). Comparing regression PASS (outline-only preserved; hover restyle proof). 22 marker-style unit tests. Opus review APPROVE-WITH-NITS; both nits carried: transient fill up to 0.3k on comparing marks during the pulse (reads as presence reveal; noted, untested), and zoom-band restored studio-only though the inert CSS lived in shared Canvas — viewer scale-aware weight question moved to c1d9. Gates on merged tree: render-core 975, render-mount 122, render-svelte 7, studio 695+tsc+svelte-check 0/0 (629), viewer 99+astro 0. Unblocks c1d9, 3e12.

title: QA desktop-lane quarantine: native fs/dialog flows (add-media, project-binding, portable-zip-open) need tauri-build smoke; logic tested via fs-seam, native shell waived per-turn
description:
(This ticket had no description; its content was entirely in the title.)

--- PARTIALLY ADDRESSED 2026-07-26 ---

This ticket predicted the gap exactly: native fs/dialog flows with no tauri-build smoke. The first
time anyone drove the packaged app, THREE defects fell out of it, each invisible to a different layer
of the existing gates:

  fs:allow-rename ungranted   every durable write failed at its temp-then-rename commit point (P0,
                              Archie-91e7). fs/tauri.test.ts runs over node:fs, which has no
                              permission system, so no unit suite could see it.
  Object.assign throws in     the folder picker died on webkitRelativePath. NO static check can see
  JavaScriptCore              this — jsdom and Playwright's Chromium both implement the permissive
                              shape WebKitGTK does not (Archie-ce7a). It had ALSO been breaking
                              drag-and-drop folder import and the flatten path, unnoticed.
  scope refuses dot-paths     command granted, PATH refused; the asset job rejected after its bytes
                              had landed and the UI blamed disk space (Archie-7b48).

WHAT NOW EXISTS:
  scripts/desktop-smoke.sh        assertions over a driven/booted profile — packaged ORIGIN (a cargo
                                  build bakes devUrl and can silently drive another worktree), no
                                  0-byte files, no leftover .tmp-*, library.json parses, optional
                                  MIN_ASSETS. Red-greened three ways.
  scripts/desktop-boot.sh         orchestration: throwaway profile, Xvfb, boot, wait, assert.
  .github/workflows/desktop.yml   CI, path-filtered. Red-greened against the real P0.
  check-tauri-capabilities.mjs    now TWO audits — permissions (derived from the TauriFsBridge
                                  interface) and scope (dot-segments derived from the app's own
                                  getFile/getDirectory call sites).

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, and why this ticket should stay open:
  - The CI gate BOOTS, it does not DRIVE. It covers the write-path class; it does NOT exercise
    ingest, so the dot-path/scope class has no automated coverage. Driving GTK+WebKit via xdotool is
    fragile (inline autocompletion corrupts typed paths; Enter does not commit the GTK location bar),
    so it is currently a local recipe only — documented in desktop-smoke.sh's header.
  - project-binding and the other native dialog flows named in this ticket are still undriven.
  - The Xvfb requirement is load-bearing and non-obvious: on a Wayland session the app renders to a
    surface X cannot read, root capture is refused, and synthetic input never arrives. None of that
    announces itself — you get a blank window and clicks that do nothing.


--- ORGANISED 2026-07-26: batch:packaged-drive ---
The remaining scope here (the CI gate BOOTS but does not DRIVE; project-binding and the other native
dialog flows undriven) needs the same packaged session as Archie-9ece, Archie-e47d and Archie-7e2e.
Archie-9ece carries the 7-row checklist; this ticket keeps the wider drive-vs-boot gap.

title: Studio UX overhaul
description:
## Notes

- Source: ledgers/UX-AUDIT-studio-wireframes.md (findings W1-W25) + wireframe board http://localhost:3002/?board=archie-studio-wireframes
- Domain: Archie Studio - Svelte 5 SPA, dual-target (browser + Tauri/Flatpak webview). Gates: per-app svelte-check / astro check; 1,250-test suite.
- Standing rules: CHECK PRIOR ART before any approach (fff / Prior Art dir); WWWWH-first copy; user-story template. Worktree agents: verify base vs main HEAD after spawn; uncommitted specs must be read from primary tree by absolute path.
- Skills: grilling tickets use /grill-with-docs — USER-INVOKED ONLY: ask the user to type it. Companions: /domain-modeling. Prototypes: /prototype. UI text: product-copy. Layout: interface-design.
- Cross-tracker: ISSUES.md Issue 13 (collab identity UI inert) = W23 - resolve together, do not fork.
- TERRITORY RE-ISSUE (2026-07-20): App.svelte no longer belongs to the nav-implementer — Archie-02ae is closed and nav/place-addressable merged. Three open tickets now write App.svelte (07a7 call site, 7e5b, 1244). Claim it per-ticket via the assignee field before editing; do not run two of those as concurrent worktree agents.
- MERGE POLICY (user directive 2026-07-19): merge each branch automatically once its code review is clean and gates are green — no per-branch ask; run full gates post-merge, close tickets with the implementer resolution, push.
- Tickets carry label map:studio-ux-overhaul. Claim (assignee + in_progress) before work. Frontier: sd ready. Conventions: docs/agents/issue-tracker.md. Glossary: CONTEXT.md.

## Decisions so far

- Navigation model: routable views and the overview skip (Archie-02ae) — place-addressable URLs (library/slug/slug+objectId), Overview mandatory (skip removed), push-on-every-place-change, nearest-ancestor fallback + notice, web bare URL=home vs desktop restore-last-place, session-only transient restore; ADR-0024.
- One save vocabulary (Archie-0b7b) — single end-to-end safety state (Failed > Action needed > Saving > Saved) over autosave+binding mirror; editor Save button dies, ⌘S = flush-now, indicator is the control when action needed; "Save" reserved for the one non-automatic act; CONTEXT.md → Persistence.
- Overview canvas mode (Archie-a9fc) — keep both modes, canvas primary (W9 corrected: drag already = reorder); chrome trimmed to first-use legend + Fit/% zoom; density slider removed; Canvas/List + library lens become persisted view preferences (ADR-0024 amendment).
- Where the narrative is edited (Archie-da38) — ADR-0016 §56 upheld (beats authored on canvas, overview spine read-only); friction fixed by beat deep links from spine rows (impl Archie-696d, blocked on nav+canvas merges).
- ADR-0016 amendment confirmed: mandatory Overview supersedes single-emergent auto-open; cross-referenced in ADR-0016 and ADR-0024.
- Editor scope + object-nav (Archie-5e96) — one sidebar, two labeled scope zones (Exhibit / This object, sticky headers); filmstrip rail = the single object-nav scheme, nav-only, minimizable, [/] keyboard face; +Media/+Map and toasts evicted (homes: Archie-beb6 / Archie-b671).
- Modality rules (Archie-389f) — single-scrim invariant (nested opens REPLACE; MediaPicker becomes CmdK's image tab); strict dismissal contract (Esc ladder, scrim-click=Esc, focus return, no close-confirms — autosave payoff); CONTEXT.md → Surfaces.
- Keyboard + colour-independent coding (Archie-d90f) — APG Grid/move-mode for list reorder, notes-panel-as-listbox for canvas markers (WebGL marks can't focus), numbered readings index, roving-tabindex filmstrip; docs/research/a11y-interactions.md; adoption ticket Archie-f260.
- One Details affordance (Archie-3e0a) — labeled 'Details' + ✎ everywhere, ⓘ retired, per-item entries kept with identical presentation; impl Archie-ebf4 (post-merges).
- Editor chrome (Archie-b671, via prototype) — Variant A readings (subordinate sidebar panel); rail expanded default (collapse = view pref); resizable docked NoteEditor (320px, persisted); To-place folds into Notes as badged group; status strip absent when idle; impl Archie-c7ef.
- MERGE WAVE 1 (2026-07-19): nav/place-addressable + save/safety-state + canvas/light-table-trims merged to main (5ffe9b9, f8fc422, f159b94 atop docs fbf1d24); all gates green post-merge (svelte-check 0/11, 342 studio tests, build, cross-app typecheck). Frontier now holds the queued integration tickets.
- Publish continuity (Archie-7d9b) — dialog+wizard become one surface (destination = step 1, in-surface back); Esc mid-auth = clean cancel + session-resumable device code; W21 partial overclaim corrected in ledger; impl Archie-1921 behind modality impl.
- Help surface (Archie-66b0) — deck-centric: tutorial deck is the help investment, HelpMenu its only entry; no new cue system; GH-Pages deck-deploy bug found+fixed (b564ac2); deck refresh = Archie-6595 behind chrome impl.
- Collaboration (Archie-d71c) — WIRE, maximal, UI-only (merge contract = collab-readiness map 697c; keep-both cut/deferred there): non-blocking MergeReview in status strip; attribution chips + editor lens gated on >=2 editors; lazy IdentityPrompt + Details name field (resolves Issue 13); share-a-copy reframe; app-local freshness badge. Impl: Archie-2bf1 / Archie-90f1 / Archie-abf9.
- Library home layout (Archie-2308) — SafetyState to header (same-slot rule), project bar = one quiet line, unified grouped search (lens browses, search finds everything), Examples shelf with auto-collapse; impl Archie-606d.
- Create/import surface (Archie-8482, via prototype) — Variant A scrimmed dialog, 3 text-first paths, paste-validated IIIF, subfolder-grouping disclosure, page-drop graft; impl Archie-51cc. CORRECTION: 14 decision tickets, not 13 — add-grammar (beb6) was blocked, now the LAST one open.

Unblocks modality Archie-5968, deck refresh Archie-6595, and the chrome-adjacent queue (details ebf4, beat links 696d, selection bar 3b03, legend adae, glyphs d7ab).

CROSS-SESSION FLAG: a concurrent session's uncommitted App.svelte WIP wires MediaPicker+NotePicker (stash 'concurrent-session WIP (App/LibraryHome) — modality merge' preserves it) — semantic conflict with the MediaPicker deletion, surfaced to user. Unblocks publish Archie-1921.

Follow-ups: Archie-363e (Save copy), browser drive of the wizard DONE 2026-07-19: all assertions pass in real Chromium (advanced form stays, state persists, back ladder, Esc/reopen; zero console errors; device-code path Tauri-only, correctly absent on web). title: Navigation model: routable views and the overview skip
description:
## Question
W1+W2: what is the navigation model? Should views be routable/addressable (URLs, browser back, deep links, refresh survival) in a dual-target web+Tauri app, and should single-object exhibits still skip the Overview screen (same click lands on different screens today)? Decide the desired behavior, not the mechanism.
closeReason: Resolved: place-addressable navigation. (1) URLs name places only (library / slug=overview / slug+objectId=editor); (2) Overview mandatory, single-object skip removed; (3) every place change pushes history incl. filmstrip switches; (4) unresolvable places degrade to nearest surviving ancestor + notice; (5) launch split: web bare URL=Library Home, desktop restores last place; (6) back restores transient screen state session-only; modals never in history. Full record: docs/adr/0004-place-addressable-navigation.md + CONTEXT.md (Navigation).

title: Routing mechanism for web + Tauri webview
description:
## Question
W1 mechanism: given the decided navigation behavior, how do we implement routable state in a Svelte 5 no-router SPA that also runs inside a Tauri webview? Survey options (hash routing, history API, a router lib, Tauri deep-link plugin), check Prior Art dir, produce a recommendation doc.
closeReason: Resolved: hash routing, hand-rolled over pure apps/studio/src/place.ts, no router dep. Static-host (GH Pages, no rewrites) + base-path /studio/ + Tauri webview: a History-API deep link 404s on refresh on every target; a # fragment reaches no server and runs one code path everywhere. Grammar deliberately reuses the archie-viewer hash cite-ladder (ADR-0021: #/{slug}, #/{slug}/o/{id}) with degrade-upward semantics — Studio and viewer share one address vocabulary. Full rationale docs/research/routing-mechanism.md. Merged to main f8fc422.

title: One save vocabulary
description:
## Question
W5+W19: reconcile the save concepts into one model: autosave vs the Save button vs Saved-check indicator (editor) vs Save-to-disk (library project bar) vs dirty dot vs writer-lock banner. What is THE save state model and its one prominent indicator?
closeReason: Resolved: one safety-state save model. (1) Single end-to-end indicator over both stages (session→store autosave, store→disk mirror); Saved only when both clean. (2) Editor Save button removed; ⌘S = universal flush-now; indicator IS the control when action needed; library bar save buttons collapse into same pattern. (3) One shared component, same header slot at every place; states Failed > Action needed > Saving > Saved; stale file binding + unbound-with-real-work = Action needed (gentle, never for untouched seed content). (4) 'Save' names exactly one act: completing the stage that can't auto-complete. Writer-lock banner explicitly NOT a safety state. Vocabulary: CONTEXT.md → Persistence. No ADR (reversible, unsurprising).

title: One affordance for details editing
description:
## Question
W3: DetailsEditor is reached via 3 different affordances (info-chip, pencil, accordion Detail panel). Pick one icon/entry convention for edit-details across library, overview, and editor.
closeReason: Resolved: one labeled 'Details' affordance everywhere — the word Details, ✎ pencil iconography where space is tight (tooltip 'Details'), opening the details surface at that thing's level. ⓘ retired (it promises read-only info; these entries open an editor). Per-item pencils on cards/plates/rows KEPT as entry points (batch-tidy workflow) but with identical presentation — one affordance in several places, not three affordances. Editor sidebar 'Detail' panel keeps its place in the This-object zone (Archie-5e96) and adopts the same label ('Details'). Copy standardization rides the product-copy pass.

title: New-exhibit create/import surface
description:
## Question
W6: the first-run flow crams 3 ingestion paths (title, media folder, IIIF via window.prompt) into one grid cell. Prototype a proper create/import surface with validation and preview. Use /prototype.
closeReason: Resolved via prototype (prototypes/create-surface, both variants Playwright-verified): VARIANT A — one scrimmed 'New exhibit' dialog, three paths as in-surface expanding cards (Start empty / From a media folder / From a IIIF link), single-scrim compliant; B's best trait grafted: page-level folder drop opens the dialog pre-populated. IIIF validation auto-starts on paste (debounced; plain-language errors lifted from ManifestImportError). Text-first paths — no new bare glyphs (W18 discipline); decorative marks allowed, meaning never rides on them. Subfolder grouping = progressive disclosure: only when the folder contains media subfolders, offer 'one exhibit from everything / one per subfolder (n)'. Surface built scope-parameterizable ('into exhibit X') but add-to-existing is Archie-beb6's decision. Replaces the grid-cell trio incl. window.prompt IIIF (W6).

title: Library home layout: project bar, search, templates
description:
## Question
W5+W7+W8: with the save model decided, redesign the library home top: where does storage/project state live (not dominating the primary bar), how does search stay unambiguous across the Exhibits/All-images toggle, and how are Example templates separated from user exhibits?
closeReason: Resolved: (1) SafetyState relocates from project bar to the LIBRARY HEADER (same-slot rule, consistent with editor+overview mounts); project bar demotes to one quiet line — 'Living in {location} · Open a library… · Close · Recents ▾' — no dots, no save buttons, no bar-scale prominence (W5 dissolved). (2) UNIFIED SEARCH: one box always searches both corpora; lens toggle governs browsing only; a typed query renders both groups labeled 'Exhibits (n) · Media (n)' (filterExhibits/filterImages both already computed); W7's silent scope switch eliminated. (3) EXAMPLES SHELF: user exhibits + New-exhibit lead; labeled Examples section below with the playground contract stated at shelf level ('edits here aren not saved unless you keep a copy'); expanded for zero-own-exhibit users, auto-collapses to header line at >=1 own exhibit; badge + editor playground banner unchanged.

title: Overview canvas mode: keep, kill, or rework
description:
## Question
W9+W12: the pan/zoom tableau fights the reading-order domain model (two orderings visible; drag ambiguity; heavy zoom chrome for ~10 items). Keep canvas mode, kill it in favor of list, or rework it? Also: does the density slider survive at toolbar level?
closeReason: Resolved: keep both overview modes, canvas primary, trim the chrome. (1) Light table stays — code already implements position=reading-order, drag=reorder, guarded under sort/filter (audit W9 core claim CORRECTED, see ledger). (2) Chrome trim: legend + hints first-use-only (auto-hide after first successful drag), zoom cluster collapses to Fit + live %. (3) Density slider removed everywhere; list gets one fixed row height. (4) Canvas/List and library Exhibits/All-images become persisted view preferences (last choice = default); transient-vs-preference split added to CONTEXT.md, amendment noted in ADR-0004. List remains the structured home for future keyboard reorder (a11y ticket).

title: Bulk selection and destructive actions
description:
## Question
W10: Select mode morphs the sort toolbar into bulk actions; Remove sits beside Sort/Size with a two-step confirm as only guard. Where do selection and destructive bulk actions live in the reworked overview?
closeReason: Resolved: dedicated selection bar. Toolbar never morphs (search/sort keep their home). Entering Select (toggle or starting a marquee) slides in a distinct bottom tray: 'N selected · Remove N · Clear · Done'; two-step confirm on Remove retained; bar exists only during selection (appears-when-real idiom); Esc = clear selection then exit mode per dismissal ladder; a11y keyboard range-select (Shift+Arrow, Ctrl+A, Space — docs/research/a11y-interactions.md) binds while active.

title: Where the narrative is edited
description:
## Question
W11: the overview shows the whole-exhibit spine read-only; editing requires entering some object editor. Where SHOULD the narrative be authored - overview, editor, or a dedicated surface?
closeReason: Resolved: uphold ADR-0005 + ADR-0016 §56 — narrative beats stay authored in the object editor (a beat is camera + prose; framing needs the canvas); overview spine stays read-only. W11's real residue (round-trip friction) is fixed by navigation, not a second authoring surface: each overview spine row becomes a beat deep link — editor at the beat's object with the Narrative panel open and scrolled to that section; browser back returns to overview (cheap under ADR-0024 places). No new authoring surface, no ADR needed (nothing amended).

title: Editor scope separation and one object-nav scheme
description:
## Question
W15+W16: exhibit-scope Narrative stacks in the same accordion as object-scope Notes/To-place/Detail with no boundary; and 3 parallel object-nav schemes coexist (rail filmstrip, narrative go-to, reading order). Decide the scope structure of the editor and the single navigation scheme.
closeReason: Resolved: (1) Scope boundary = two labeled zones in ONE sidebar — 'Exhibit — {title}' zone (Narrative panel; ADR-0016 always-present honored) above a visually distinct 'This object — {label}' zone (Notes, To place, Detail); sticky zone headers, object zone re-labels with filmstrip position. Tabs rejected (hides narrative, defeats ADR-0016 discoverability); side-split rejected (right edge reserved for docked note editor). (2) The filmstrip rail is the ONE object-nav scheme; navigation becomes its ONLY job; the rail is MINIMIZABLE (collapsible to a slim strip); keyboard face [ / ] prev-next is the same scheme. Rail sheds non-nav cargo: +Media/+Map relocate (home decided by Add-grammar Archie-beb6), toasts/mode-banners relocate (Editor-chrome Archie-b671). Spine go-tos are beat deep links (Archie-da38), reading order is ordering — neither is a competing scheme.

title: Editor chrome: dock the note editor, un-float the overlays
description:
## Question
W13+W14: floating chrome (readings rail, note popover, banners, toasts) occludes the artifact; the note form has two homes toggled by cryptic pin glyphs. Prototype an editor layout with one docked note editor and minimal canvas occlusion. Use /prototype + interface-design.
closeReason: Resolved via prototype reaction (prototypes/editor-chrome, two variants): (1) Readings = Variant A sidebar panel in This-object zone, VISUALLY SUBORDINATE to Notes — a quiet legend, not a peer workspace; (2) rail default EXPANDED, collapsed state persists as a view preference; (3) note dock RESIZABLE (ResizeDivider idiom), 320px default, min ~280, width persisted; (4) To place folds into Notes as a collapsible badged group 'To place (n)' — absent at n=0, full worklist when expanded; (5) status strip ABSENT when idle — renders only with an active mode/toast, collapses away otherwise. Docked editor replaces the floating popover; canvas carries zero chrome. Implementation: Archie-96im-successor (see impl ticket).

title: One grammar for adding things
description:
## Question
W17: add-verbs are scattered (+Media/+Map in rail, Box/Outline/Whole in Notes, Add-a-section in Narrative, Add-media plate in overview) with different placement and grammar. Define one add model across surfaces, given the decided create surface and editor structure.
closeReason: Resolved: the two-kind grammar. (1) BRINGING SOMETHING IN = the one chooser: every add-media affordance (overview Add-media plate, single '+ Add media' in the editor object-zone header) opens the 8482 dialog scoped 'into this exhibit'; Map becomes a fourth path card inside it (AddMapModal retired as a standalone surface — in-surface expansion, single-scrim); separate +Media/+Map buttons die (answers chrome-builder's parked TODO). (2) MAKING SOMETHING HERE = a gesture from its panel: Box/Outline/Whole stay in Notes, Add-a-section stays in Narrative, per ADR-0011 gesture-initiated creation. One-sentence grammar recorded in close + CONTEXT-worthy if it recurs.

title: Label the load-bearing glyphs
description:
## Question
W18: bare glyphs carry load-bearing meaning (drag grip, pin, outline/box/whole, cite, cmd-K). For the chrome that survives the editor redesign, write labels/tooltips/affordance text. Use product-copy skill.
closeReason: Merged (branch copy/glyph-labels, commit 5fa1af1; review: CLEAN). W18 closed for the surviving chrome — and the survey's headline finding is that the redesign already did most of the work: the popover pin, floating rail, +Media/+Map, MediaPicker, AddMapModal and edit-ⓘ all died in earlier tickets, and grips/rail-collapse/ResizeDivider/Details pencils were already labeled. What remained was accessible-name pollution: ~28 decorative Unicode glyphs sitting unhidden beside visible text (a screen reader announced 'black rectangle Box' for the Box button). Every such site across 8 components now wraps the glyph in aria-hidden; the map zoom buttons gained tooltips; the list-row ⠿ grip stays deliberately aria-only (tight footprint, correct aria-label already). Zero wording/behavior/aria-label changes otherwise. Genuine glyph-only gap found in AvEditor (Clear ✕ buttons lack aria-labels) — out of territory, filed as Archie-ba74. Gates post-merge: 0/0, 456/456, build green.

title: Modality rules: cite-flow nesting and surface stacking
description:
## Question
W4+W20: modal-over-modal in the cite flow (CmdK opens MediaPicker); drawers+modals+popovers+banners stack with undefined focus/escape/z-priority. Define the modality rules: what may stack, what must replace, how each dismisses.
closeReason: Resolved: (1) Single-scrim invariant — at most one scrimmed surface ever; opening from inside one REPLACES it; W20 fix: MediaPicker becomes the image tab inside CmdK (one surface, internal tabs, one Esc); drawers are scrimmed surfaces (drawer-vs-dialog is presentational only). (2) Strict dismissal contract: Esc ladder = topmost floater then the scrimmed surface; scrim-click = Esc; focus trapped + returned to opener; NO close-confirmations anywhere (autosave payoff; destructive-act confirms untouched); toasts/banners outside the ladder. Publish wizard mid-auth close = clean cancel, resumable — warn-or-not delegated to Archie-7d9b. Vocabulary: CONTEXT.md → Surfaces. Modals never in history per ADR-0024.

title: Publish flow continuity
description:
## Question
W21: publish is a 3-surface chain (button, dialog, wizard) that exits the app for device-code auth; failure recovery lands outside the app. Redesign for continuity - fewer hops, in-app recovery.
closeReason: Resolved: (1) PublishDialog + Publish wizard merge into ONE scrimmed surface — destination choice (web/local/zip) is step 1, internal steps with in-surface back (modality contract). (2) Esc mid-device-code-auth = clean cancel, SESSION-RESUMABLE, no warning: the machine keeps the pending device code (valid ~15min); reopening Publish resumes at the same waiting state/code; expired code → plain start-again sentence. Consistent with no-close-confirmations (fix the cost, not the exit). AUDIT CORRECTION recorded in ledger: in-surface retry/progress already existed; device-code auth + Pages-enable fallback are inherent to the serverless architecture, not flaws. Local/zip destinations unchanged.

title: Help and onboarding surface
description:
## Question
W22: help is fragmented (menu, iframe tutorial deck, shortcuts sheet) and non-contextual. What is the help model - contextual cues at moments of confusion vs the deck? What survives?
closeReason: Resolved: (b) the tutorial deck is the help investment. HelpMenu remains the deck's only entry point (no Library Home first-run card); shortcuts sheet stays; NO new contextual-cue system beyond the already-built first-use cues (legend/hint, narrative first-add). Deploy bug found + fixed during grilling: build-gh-pages.sh bypassed the package build's sync-learn step, so the gitignored public/learn never shipped from CI and the deployed tutorial iframe 404'd — fixed in b564ac2 (sync before raw vite build; verified CI-simulated). Deck content refresh ticketed behind the chrome implementation.

title: Collaboration: wire it or remove its signals
description:
## Question
W23 (= ISSUES.md Issue 13): IdentityPrompt and MergeReview are built but unmounted while collab signals (toast, writer-lock banner) still show, promising features that dead-end. Wire the collab flow in, or remove the signals? Resolve jointly with ISSUES.md Issue 13.

## Cross-map note - collab identity SoT (from Archie+ collab-readiness map, 2026-07-18)
This ticket is the single source of truth for collaboration IDENTITY. The collab-readiness map's B1 (identity dark-data) was folded here and closed as a duplicate. Audit finding (ledgers/AUDIT-stable-ids.md): annotation author id `lastEditor: ClientId` (wadm/types.ts:225) is ALREADY populated + serialized; `creator?` is inert WADM passthrough, never read; Reading carries a stable id. So there is no "never-populated identity field" to fill for annotations. Residual to decide HERE alongside the wire/remove call: (1) authorship on authored STRUCTURE (readings/sections/exhibit carry no editor field); (2) whether the machine `ClientId` needs a human-facing identity. The merge-SEMANTICS spec + regression tests are a separate ticket, B2 / Archie-697c, which produces the spec MergeReview surfaces - coordinate, do not fork.
closeReason: Resolved: WIRE, maximal — within the cross-map boundary (merge CONTRACT owned by collab-readiness Archie-697c; this map owns the UI that surfaces it; coordinate, never fork). (1) MergeReview NON-BLOCKING: open always completes (lossless merge); summary lands in the status strip (absent-when-idle); Review steps conflict cards at leisure; per-note edit gate enforces resolution (shared with D1 live sync); consumes conflicts source-agnostically (zip open OR live tabs). KEEP-BOTH CUT — would invent merge semantics; deferred to 697c's semantic-conflict fog; component stays keep-one-head via session.resolve (DAG preserves the loser in history). Copy inherits the June-grilled ⑧ panel (Archie-59a8). (2) Attribution chips (note rows + dock: 'Meera · 2d ago') + filter-by-editor lens in Notes panel (composes with Readings) — both gated on ≥2 distinct editors; solo libraries show zero attribution chrome. (3) Round-trip package: lazy IdentityPrompt (first others-notes open or first share; skippable) + permanent Your-name field in Library Details (the missing archie.displayName.v1 writer — jointly resolves ISSUES.md Issue 13); zip destination reframed 'Share a working copy' + one round-trip line; per-exhibit '+N since your last import' badge, app-local watermark (NEVER the model — carry-sentinel territory), collaboration-gated.

title: Keyboard equivalents and colour-independent coding
description:
## Question
W24+W25: drag-first interactions (plates, marquee, grips) have no visible keyboard path; readings are colour-coded only. Research established patterns (a11y for drag-reorder, canvas annotation keyboard models, colour+shape/label coding) and produce a recommendations doc.
closeReason: Resolved: research doc at docs/research/a11y-interactions.md. Key findings: overview LIST reorder = WAI-ARIA APG Grid pattern (not Listbox — rows contain nested interactives) with move-mode grammar (space/enter lift, arrows move, space/enter drop, esc cancel; grammar corroborated by APG + dnd-kit) and live announcements off orderIndexOf; marquee equivalent = Grid row-selection keys (Shift+Arrow, Ctrl+A, Space toggle); readings colour-only gap is specifically the on-canvas marker — fix = shared numbered index across legend/marker/announcements (WCAG 1.4.1 worked example) + optional stroke-dash; WebGL canvas markers can't be focusable (no DOM nodes; matches local prior art 12-accessibility.md) — route keyboard access through the notes-panel list promoted to listbox with roving tabindex, which already drives canvas selection; filmstrip needs only roving-tabindex/aria-current on the decided [/] scheme. svelte-check's 11 warnings are all modal focus gaps — its lint structurally cannot catch these interaction-model issues.

title: Archie full-stack/real-time graduation readiness (static-first)
description:
## Notes

- **North star (set by grill, 2026-07-18): Archie ITSELF graduates to a full-stack, real-time-capable app in the future — in this repo, monorepo-native.** No sibling product, no separate repo (Archie+ concept retired). The graduated server tier (sync server, writable HTTP backend, headless publish) arrives as new workspace packages consuming @render/core via workspace:* — the studio/viewer split is the template. carry.ts compiler guards protect the whole path because everything compiles against one model source.
- **Fixed invariant (unchanged):** every ticket ships standalone value in static Archie today; prep justified only by the future tier is cut.
- Source: ledgers/WORKLIST-realtime-collab-readiness.md; domain SoT: CONTEXT.md; identity facts: ledgers/AUDIT-stable-ids.md; CRDT design: ledgers/PROBE-collab-crdt-mapping.md (Model B + D1 scale-up + API-surface evidence).
- Standing rules: CHECK PRIOR ART before committing; probe riskiest-first with a pre-stated kill criterion, ledgered; run code review on each landing branch (user directive 2026-07-18); per-app test/check gates.
- **Single source of truth for collab IDENTITY** = Studio-UX 'Collaboration: wire it or remove its signals' (Archie-d71c) + ISSUES.md Issue 13 (B1 folded there). B2 (Archie-697c) owns the ONE merge contract (shared by async-zip AND live paths — never fork a second); d71c surfaces it.
- Tickets carry label map:collab-readiness. One ticket per session; claim before work. Frontier: sd ready --label map:collab-readiness. Conventions: docs/agents/issue-tracker.md.

## Decisions so far

- Stable-id audit (Archie-2767): annotation identity is CRDT-ready (global ULID logicalId, id-keyed spine); Exhibit id global; Object/Section/Reading ids stable but exhibit-local only, with array-index ordering + no id-keyed merge for authored structure. Two premise corrections: lastEditor already populated (creator? inert), Reading has a stable id. -> ledgers/AUDIT-stable-ids.md
- CRDT-mapping probe (Archie-70e6): annotation-granular CRDT HOLDS, no model rewrite (PURSUE). Layer = Model B (Yjs/op-sync transports the append-only rev-log; DAG heads/resolveConflict unchanged, branch-and-review preserved). Model A (field-mapping) REJECTED — silent LWW clobber. -> ledgers/PROBE-collab-crdt-mapping.md
- Multi-tab live sync D1 (Archie-a66d): DONE, 12/12 Playwright-verified — real-time collab across tabs, zero backend, real merge machinery unstubbed. Key by rev not logicalId; appendEdit refuses plural heads (UI gates); one merge contract; transport is a seam. -> PROBE ledger, Scale-up section
- C2 grill (Archie-2e27, decision half): sharing mechanism DISSOLVED by the monorepo — no second repo in any named future; graduated tier joins this workspace. API tightening = 4-item pass aimed at the future Node server consumer: (1) sideEffects:false + measure root barrel, (2) id-constructor subpath, (3) exports-map-as-contract documented, (4) dist/.d.ts deferred, trigger recorded = "if render-core ever leaves the repo". title: Probe: does the annotation model map to annotation-granular CRDT merge?

Wire the annotation store to a Yjs (or Automerge) doc behind a LOCAL provider (y-indexeddb / in-memory) on the seed exhibit - NO server. Drive concurrent edits, observe merge outcomes. title: linearHead ignores mergeParents: resolved notes permanently uneditable; classifyLogical throws on logs with past resolutions
description:
## Bug (proven by characterization, ticket Archie-697c / B2)

linearHead (spine/log.ts:46-48) builds its referenced-set from `.parent` only, but resolveConflict (spine/merge.ts:251-252) records non-primary heads in `mergeParents`. After a resolution: headsOf correctly = 1 head, but linearHead still counts {merge node, non-primary head} = plural and THROWS. Consequences (both pinned by tests labelled "(OQ-1 pin, BUG)" in spine/merge-contract.test.ts, C4 ~l171 and C11 ~l332): (1) a resolved note is permanently uneditable/undeletable via appendEdit/appendDelete/session.edit; (2) classifyLogical throws on any log containing a past resolution — the async-zip merge path breaks post-resolve.

Fix shape (per B2 report): one-line — share parentsOf (mergeParents-aware, merge.ts:106-111) with linearHead. BEHAVIOR CHANGE: flip the two OQ-1-pin tests deliberately (they are labelled for exactly this), re-derive C4/C11 clauses in MERGE-CONTRACT.md, full spine suite must stay green otherwise.

Blocks: MergeReview flow (Archie-d71c) — resolve-then-edit is its immediate next action; spine gate (Archie-494c) — OQ-1 must be fixed before write primitives are reused for authored structure. See MERGE-CONTRACT.md "Open questions" for OQ-2..6 (recorded, lower stakes).
closeReason: FIXED, merged. parentsOf (primary parent + mergeParents) moved from merge.ts to log.ts as the ONE shared referenced-set builder; linearHead uses it — structural agreement with headsOf (they build the same set over the same filter; cannot disagree on any log). 2 pin-tests flipped as designed, 3 new regressions (resolve->edit, resolve->delete, post-resolution classify), MERGE-CONTRACT C4/C11 re-derived + OQ-1 marked resolved. 847/847 render-core, studio 342, archie-viewer 108, viewer 94, typecheck clean. Sibling sweep: linearHead was the only wrong parent-only build (lineage/withProvLink/deserialize verified deliberate). d71c inherits: resolved notes fully editable; resolve-live-then-delete sanctioned; resolved libraries round-trip the async-zip path.

title: Self-hosted IIIF loop (GitHub-free publish to own server)
description:
## Notes

**Goal:** a GitHub-free authoring loop — a folder of collections on disk → generated IIIF manifests + web derivatives served from the user's own HTTP server → ingested into Archie **by reference** (zero image bytes copied; avoids the OPFS-quota failure that blocks local import of ~1000 images) → annotations/structure authored locally → published (written back) to the same server.

**STANDING CONSTRAINT (2026-07-19):** push the envelope on Archie **as a static app** — no custom server-side components anywhere in the loop. The server is off-the-shelf config only (static file serving, stock WebDAV, sync daemons). Any proposal requiring a bespoke service is out of bounds.

Charted 2026-07-19 from a design conversation that established the load-bearing constraints below (Notes-level facts, not closed tickets):

- IIIF-manifest ingest stores no bytes (apps/studio/src/ingest-flows.ts:469); local-file import copies masters into OPFS and hits quota.
- Write-back = publishing Archie's projection (itself IIIF P3) BESIDE the generated source manifests. Never mutate source manifests; never re-ingest to recover edits (iiif-import.ts reads only title/canvases/dims — annotations would be dropped).
- The working library is the sole home of authored truth; the server only ever holds a projection.
- Serving rules: honest 404s (no SPA rewrites over the tree), CORS; HTTPS whenever it leaves the LAN.
- Studio's existing web push is GitHub-only (apps/studio/src/deploy/deploy-flows.svelte.ts hardcodes api.github.com — 3 sites). publishLibrary writes through the Filesystem seam via MemoryFilesystem + collectFiles (publish-flows.svelte.ts), so a new destination replaces only the upload half.
- URL-as-identity hazards: renames orphan annotations; NFC/NFD filename normalization; EXIF-orientation dims mismatch silently skews all annotation geometry; TIFF doesn't decode in browsers → derivatives required.
- Server shape (grilling): home/LAN box, fully controlled, sync daemons fine; LAN-first, public later.

**Skills per session:** /grilling + /domain-modeling for decision tickets; /prototype for the generator. Repo rule: check Prior Art (fff over Archie/Prior Art) before committing to any approach.

**Key seams:** packages/render-core/src/fs/http.ts · publish/open.ts · publish/site.ts · apps/studio/src/ingest-flows.ts · iiif-import.ts · publish-flows.svelte.ts · deploy/deploy-flows.svelte.ts · store.ts · folder-backend.ts.

## Decisions so far

- [Working-library platform & durability](Archie-aa69) — browser Studio + FSA folder-bound library; plain files on disk, normal backups.
- [Choose the write-back transport](Archie-7b1f) — static-envelope, both lanes: publish-to-folder onto the served docroot (mount/sync) now; in-app WebDAV destination as the button. No custom server processes.
- [Folder-drift strategy (manifest re-import dedup)](Archie-1e6d) — folder grows regularly → build dedup-by-source re-import (impl: Archie-12e3, gated on first ingest).

## Fog

- Collection-level bulk ingest (IIIF Collection → N exhibits in one paste) — sharpens after the first real ingest shows how much N pastes hurt.
- Publish performance & memory at 1000+ objects (MemoryFilesystem staging, publish duration, incremental publish) — measure after the first full publish; also whether per-file WebDAV PUT needs batching/throttling.
- Viewer performance against the derivative sizes the pipeline chooses — revisit after the derivative survey fixes sizes.
- URL-migration tooling (library-wide source rewrite) — ideally made moot by the URL-scheme decision; revisit only if the scheme fails.
- Multi-machine authoring over the server (zip/merge path, not re-ingest) — deferred until the single-machine loop works end to end.

title: Decide publish tiling posture for referenced images (tileRemote)
description:
## Question

At publish, tileRemote fetches every large CORS-reachable remote image and slices a tile pyramid into the published tree — self-contained + fast viewer, but slow publishes, a re-inflated tree, RAM pressure, and persists pixels (rights posture). Alternatives: pure references (small/fast publish, viewer depends on image server + full-size masters) or a selective/derivative-based middle. Which posture, and should it be a publish-time option?
closeReason: Pipeline tiles: the folder pipeline generates web derivatives + static deep-zoom tiles ONCE, server-side; Archie publishes pure references and tileRemote stays unused for this workflow (publishes stay small/fast; no pixel duplication onto the same host). Decided in grilling 2026-07-19.

title: Survey the folder + derivative pipeline requirements
description:

("Added N notes from a colleague's copy") into the import toast. The two shipped slivers
(memoized `conflicts()`, the S4 editor thunk) stand.

## Progress 2026-07-27 (0d8f444) — S3a and S3b are SHIPPED; only the synced-count toast + the caller remain

Both confirmed defects are closed, ahead of the wiring rather than behind it, so whenever
importChanges gains a caller these paths are already safe:

- **S3a canvas-drag bypass.** `onUpdate` (and `ondelete`, which had the same hole and the ticket did
  not name) now refuse a conflicted note with a curator-voice note and a `bump()`, so the dragged
  marker snaps back to its stored geometry instead of lying about an edit that never landed. The
  uncaught-throw-inside-an-Annotorious-callback failure is gone.
- **S3a duplicate logical ids.** `objAnnotations` deduped — `workingAnnotations()` yields every live
  head, so a conflicted note reached Annotorious as two annotations sharing one id (drawn twice, one
  addressable). Same rule `objNotes` already applied to the sidebar list.
- **S3b half-done removal.** All three removal paths (`removeCurrentObject`, `removeObjectById`,

  longer exists, which is worse than a refusal and invisible to the author.
- The delete loops also stopped visiting a conflicted note once per head.

first object). studio 987/987, e2e 12/12, svelte-check 0/0, tsc clean.

REPLACES via `replaceProjectFrom` — so `session.conflicts()` is still always empty and none of the

App-local only — no model fields (carry-sentinel territory untouched).
closeReason: Merged (branch collab/writer-lock-name, commits ba10fd2+573b5d1). The writer-lock payload now carries the writer's display name so both read-only surfaces can say WHO: the BroadcastChannel fallback's held/beat/takeover messages carry {t, from, name}, and the Web Locks path (which has no payload channel) gained a name-only presence BroadcastChannel ('<lockname>.presence', announce-per-heartbeat) that never drives canWrite/otherTabActive — Web Locks still owns coordination. New otherName getter; App's read-only banner reads '{Name} is editing this library in another tab...' and save-queue's refusal message '...— {Name} is editing this library in another tab...', both falling back to the prior impersonal copy when anonymous/unknown. 9 new tests (named/anonymous both paths, live-rename, takeover name, 60-char cap, no-getter fallback). title: Publish-time torn-store surfacing for BOTH log families (annotation side fully silent)
description:
## Question
Parity finding from Archie-aef4's review fix: at publish time, an all-corrupt log store ships-what-reads. The STRUCTURE side now warns loudly (distinct 'section history was NOT exported' console warn, exhibit named, test-pinned). The ANNOTATION side (loadAllLogs -> AnnotationSession.load -> readAnnotationsReport -> .entries) is FULLY SILENT — all-corrupt annotation history exports as empty with no signal at all, the exact corruption->absence collapse rule 2 forbids, at the boundary where it matters most (a shared artifact). Bring the annotation publish path up to at least the structure side's warn posture; the real fix for both families is surfacing torn stores in the publish UI (before the artifact ships) + a repair path. Context: Archie-aef4 close reason; publish-flows.svelte.ts getStructure comment naming the shared tension.

## Progress 2026-07-19
Warn-parity SHIPPED: publish-warnings.ts#warnAnnotationPublishCorruption (tiny startup-chunk-safe module; publish-flows is lazy), called from App.loadAllLogs(forPublish=true) — publish dep passes true, citation building stays silent. Both branches mirror the structure warns (all-corrupt NOT-exported vs partial advisory). Test-pinned via publish-warnings.test.ts (3 tests, real torn store through AnnotationSession.load). title: noteCountByCanvas counts per-head: conflicted notes inflate overview/library counts by one
description: Found during Archie-d48e re-review (2026-07-19). apps/studio/src/App.svelte noteCountByCanvas (~line 1261) derives from the un-deduped exhibit-wide allNotes, which after an edit-vs-edit merge contains every live head per logicalId — so a conflicted note counts twice in overview/library note counts. PRE-EXISTING behavior (allNotes was never deduped), not a d48e regression; d48e added dedupeHeadsByLogicalId (apps/studio/src/note-heads.ts) at the objNotes seam, so the fix is likely reusing that helper (or a count-distinct-logicalId) in the noteCountByCanvas derivation. Other allNotes consumers are correct as-is: hasMultipleEditors/distinctEditors legitimately want every head's author; lastTouchedByCanvas is a max. Don't dedupe allNotes wholesale — see the deliberate-choice comment near App.svelte:1242.
closeReason: DONE 2026-07-19, merged (wf/publish-counts faa83f4, impl opus, review opus APPROVE). noteCountByCanvas now tallies over dedupeHeadsByLogicalId(allNotes) — a conflicted note (2+ live heads per logicalId) counts once, matching objNotes/inspector. Reviewer audited every other allNotes consumer: lastAnnotatedByCanvas (max — immune), showAttribution/editorOptions (distinct — immune, and deliberately per-head); this was the only inflation site. Non-blocking note: note-heads.test.ts pins the dedup-then-count invariant, not App.svelte's call site (component-scope derived not headless-testable); strengthen if the count derivation ever extracts.

title: Flaky e2e: navigation rapid back/forward expects '#/' gets '' (near-100% headless fail)
description: Found during the Archie-6a16 review (2026-07-20): apps/studio/e2e/navigation.spec.ts:144 'rapid back/forward … no error, no uncaught throw' fails ~9/10 headless on ANY commit (proven on both 4958c55 base and the view-state branch — identical signature, test file unchanged): expects location.hash '#/', gets ''. A history-race in the test or a real rapid-nav hash restoration gap; CI retries:1 likely masks it. Reproduce: vite dev + cached Chromium headless, run the spec 10x. Decide: fix the race in the test, or if the app genuinely drops the hash under rapid back/forward, fix syncUrl.
closeReason: Merged 4a61da4 (wf/nav-flake b11e1dd, base 60aa0c8). Diagnosis: TEST RACE, app fine — evidence trail: the failure always hit the un-retried 'expect(await hashOf(page))' single-shot reads in expectLibrary/Overview/Editor (never inside the history.go bursts); hashchange timing probes showed the hash lands ~100-300ms after the library card appears (marker visible on loadLibraryMeta resolve, hash written by applyPlace's replaceState several awaits later in the same onMount chain); a burst-free control passed 8/8, so the bursts' lingering session-flush work widens the normally-sub-frame gap on the NEXT boot. Fix: the three hash assertions became 'await expect.poll(() => hashOf(page))' — same auto-retry semantics the marker locator checks already had, uses the existing expect.timeout, no bespoke sleeps, still pins the canonical end-state invariant; rationale documented in-file. title: Dublin Core metadata
description:
## Notes

- Goal: descriptive metadata on Library / Exhibit / Object per Dublin Core (dc, 15 elements) + DCMI Terms (dcterms, the extended vocab). Charted 2026-07-19; spine decisions from the charting grill: scope = the three RightsFields levels (not sections/notes); purpose = viewer display AND interop/export AND preserve-on-import (all three); UI = pick-from-vocab (Tropy/Omeka style — default field set + add-field from the full vocab); values = repeatable plain strings (language tags deliberately deferred).
- Ground truth (metadata-surface survey 2026-07-19): model carries only title/summary + RightsFields (packages/render-core/src/model/model.ts:66 — rights, requiredStatement); a dormant seam already exists: IIIFRightsProps.metadata?: IIIFLabelValue[] (iiif/presentation.ts:36) is typed but never populated; apps/studio/src/iiif-import.ts drops third-party manifest metadata/rights/summary entirely; publish emits IIIF P3 + WADM, no DC anywhere; editing UI home = DetailsEditor.svelte + RightsEditor.svelte; any new model field is gated by carry sentinels (rule render-core-data-integrity — AObject 3 sites in publish/working.ts + iiif/manifest.ts, Exhibit 2, Library hand-maps in working.ts).
- Prior art anchors: Tropy (../tropy) ships res/vocab/dc.n3 + dcterms.n3 and a template system (res/ttp, src/ontology) — the pick-from-vocab model to study; IIIF metadata is deliberately non-semantic label/value display pairs. Repo rule: CHECK PRIOR ART and cite it on every ticket (fff over the Image/ dir).
- Skills: grilling tickets → /grill-with-docs (USER-INVOKED ONLY — ask the user to type it), companion /domain-modeling; prototypes → /prototype; UI text → product-copy; research → /research.
- Tickets carry label map:dc-metadata. Claim (assignee + status in_progress) before any work. Frontier: sd ready filtered to the label. Conventions: docs/agents/issue-tracker.md.

- MERGE POLICY (user directive 2026-07-19): merge each branch automatically once its review is green (full gates for app-code branches) — no per-branch ask. Prototypes merged: 80a209d (panel, Archie-0ba5) + 9f12bea (editor, Archie-e100), reactions pending; pipeline branch wf/metadata-pipeline merges after review + gates.

## Decisions so far

- Survey dc/dcterms vocab and prior-art metadata models (Archie-a58e, closed) — asset docs/research/dublin-core-vocab.md; dc 15 + dcterms 55; native title/summary/rights/requiredStatement ARE the IIIF typed slots, so the DC layer excludes them; IIIF metadata[] is display-only; prior-art defaults are narrow (Tropy generic 10 / Omeka 2), URI decoupled from display label.
- Model home and record shape for descriptive metadata (Archie-8176, closed) — RightsFields gains metadata?: MetadataEntry[] ({ property: "dcterms:x", value }), ordered, repeats as entries; dcterms:-only canonical prefix; DISJOINT from native title/summary/rights (exclusion list → default-field-set ticket); entry widened in the batched grill to { property?; label?; value } (≥1 of property/label); named hazard: studio rightsOf reconstructors must not drop the new field.
- Default field set per level and pick-from-vocab rules (Archie-2bd8, closed) — defaults are UI-only scaffolding; Library creator/publisher/date/identifier, Exhibit creator/date/subject, Object = Tropy generic; excluded: title/description/abstract/rights/license; add-field = searchable flat dcterms list.
- IIIF import: preserve third-party manifest metadata (Archie-bbad, closed) — map-when-confident (original label kept as override), verbatim otherwise; manifest rights/attribution/summary fill natives; excluded-property labels stay verbatim.
- Publish projection (Archie-246c, closed) — metadata[] populated at all three IIIF levels (lang-map none, same-label repeats merged); raw entries round-trip via archieMetadata extension property; exhibits.json carries entries for the viewer panel; JSON-LD/meta-tags deferred to fog.
- Implementation plan → BUILT + MERGED (Archie-5a9b, closed) — pipeline on main: RightsFields.metadata + validator, model/dcterms.ts (55 props/aliases/exclusions/defaults), carry sentinels, iiif/metadata.ts (display metadata[] + lossless archieMetadata, presence-gated = byte-stable), IIIF import preservation, exhibits.json pass-through.
- Studio metadata editor → MERGED (Archie-458e, closed) — MetadataEditor.svelte + metadata-rows.ts, tabbed into DetailsEditor at all three levels; keyed partial patches only.
- Viewer metadata panel → MERGED (Archie-b50f, closed) — metadata-display.ts + MetadataList/MetadataRun, Notes|Details tablist + exhibit-header run.
- GATES on main after all three merges: render-core 1035/1035 (90 files), studio 820/820 (61 files) + typecheck clean + svelte-check 651 files 0/0, archie-viewer 114/114, viewer astro check 0 errors + tsc clean + vitest 112/112 + manual svelte-check 1 error/10 warnings (PRE-EXISTING baseline, unchanged).
- Prototype: pick-from-vocab metadata editor (Archie-e100, closed) — approved by reaction; BINDING: metadata joins the Studio right panel TABBED, not stacked; relabel→row overflow, within-run reorder, free-text values are a stated decision.
- Prototype: viewer metadata panel (Archie-0ba5, closed) — approved by reaction; BINDING: Notes|Details TAB in the viewer sidebar (also cures long-value/notes-below-fold tension); variant A + exhibit-header run for exhibit fields; repeats need a separator.
- [apps/viewer has no .svelte type gate](Archie-fae0) — ALREADY DONE, closed without work: the gate shipped 2026-07-20 (`apps/viewer/package.json:18` `check:svelte` = `svelte-check --workspace . --fail-on-warnings`; wired at `.github/workflows/checks.yml:131`) and the 1-error/10-warning baseline was burned to zero. Verified 2026-07-24 by RUNNING the gate: 1464 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. `--fail-on-warnings` means a new warning now fails CI. Durable artifact: `.claude/rules/svelte-no-typecheck-net.md`.

- [The rights and metadata surfaces render nothing on the read side (V103/V104)](Archie-a5b1) — SHIPPED `ead0ad7`, evidence in `ledgers/FIX-a5b1-rights-metadata-2026-07-26.md`. **The ticket premise was half wrong and the correction matters:** V104’s *renders nothing anywhere* is FALSE for the SPA (3 exhibit rows, 9 object rows, driven) and TRUE for the **archival published page** — the surface `Archie-c405` was actually auditing. V103 fired on both halves: no exhibit or library set `rights` anywhere in the corpus, AND the page emitted the licence only into JSON-LD. Fix is one `rightsHtml` block in `static-pages.ts` at all three levels. Artifact, counted on both sides: `dl class="meta"` 0→26, `<dt>` 0→216, `rel="license"` 0→40. Three levels left DELIBERATELY unlicensed (contents carry 2–3 licences; a blanket claim would be false); six URIs with no human label left alone and PINNED BY A TEST. Spawned [Archie-36e6](Archie-36e6) — a IIIF MUST-display violation for single-object exhibits.

- [Decide: should the read boundary reject excluded dcterms properties, or display them?](Archie-aafd) — DECIDED 2026-07-27 (human): **demote to verbatim, preserve the source property for re-export, drop that memory on edit.** The ticket's framing was off and the real defect is worse: `metadataRows` rule 1 already drops excluded properties on DISPLAY, so a foreign `dcterms:title` becomes *an editable Studio row that renders nowhere* — an invisible-edit trap. Demotion follows precedent already in-repo at `iiif-import.ts:85`, making the zip path and the import path one rule. `sourceProperty` keeps an untouched foreign tree byte-faithful on re-publish (Archie is an archival tool; silently re-typing someone else's metadata is not a thing it should do), and dropping it on edit stops Archie emitting a typed claim its source never carried. A publish preflight was considered and rejected. Implementation: [Archie-d25f](Archie-d25f).

## Fog

- Bulk metadata editing (BulkRightsDialog sibling) — after the editor prototype settles single-record UX.
- Studio search/filter over metadata values (CmdK integration?) — unscoped.
- SEO/unfurl meta tags on published viewer pages (Omeka/Scalar emit og: + DC meta tags) — still fog; the dcterms-keyed entries now exist to feed them.
- Machine-harvest targets beyond IIIF (schema.org JSON-LD? feeds?) — depends on the publish-projection answer.
- Language-tagged values — deferred at charting; revisit only if a real import demands them.
- Metadata on sections/readings/notes — out of scope now; revisit on demand.

title: Survey dc/dcterms vocab and prior-art metadata models (Tropy, Omeka S, IIIF)
description:
## Question

What exactly is in dc (15 elements) and dcterms (extended), and how do the prior-art tools model pick-from-vocab metadata? Produce docs/research/dublin-core-vocab.md covering: (a) a property inventory — URI, label, comment per property — read from Tropy's local authoritative copies ../tropy/res/vocab/dc.n3 and dcterms.n3; (b) how Tropy templates (res/ttp, src/ontology) select a working subset and type values; (c) how Omeka S resource templates and IIIF's metadata guidance (non-semantic label/value pairs) handle the same problem; (d) a recommended default field set per level (Library / Exhibit / Object) to seed the later grilling. Inventory + recommendation only — no model decisions here.
closeReason: Asset: docs/research/dublin-core-vocab.md. dc=15, dcterms=55 (15 same-name refinements; long tail = date/relation/rights refinements), parsed from Tropy's bundled n3. Key findings: (1) Archie's native title/summary/rights/requiredStatement ARE IIIF P3's typed descriptive slots — a DC layer must exclude those properties, covering creator/date/subject/type/identifier/relations only; (2) IIIF P3 metadata (spec §3.1) is display-only label/value — property URIs don't survive to the viewer, so DC is an authoring/interchange convenience; (3) prior-art defaults are narrow (Omeka: title+description; Tropy generic template: 10 fields), both decouple property URI from display label and allow overrides; cardinality differs (Tropy single, Omeka repeatable). Recommended defaults: Library creator/publisher/date/identifier; Exhibit creator/date/subject; Object creator/date/subject/type/identifier/source (= Tropy generic).

title: Model home and record shape for descriptive metadata
description:
## Question

Where does descriptive metadata live in the model, and what is a record? Decide: (1) model home — extend the RightsFields mixin (lands on Library/Exhibit/AObject at once, packages/render-core/src/model/model.ts:66) vs a new sibling field; (2) record shape — property identifier form (dcterms:-prefixed name vs full URI) with repeatable string values; (3) the overlap policy — title, summary, rights, requiredStatement already exist and map onto dc:title / dcterms description / dc:rights: alias them into the metadata view, or keep disjoint and exclude those properties from the pick-list; (4) which carry sentinels and mappers the choice touches (publish/working.ts, iiif/manifest.ts — see map Notes; rule render-core-data-integrity). Bring docs/research/dublin-core-vocab.md.
closeReason: RESOLVED (grill with user, 2026-07-19): (1) MODEL HOME — extend RightsFields with metadata?: MetadataEntry[] (model.ts:66; its doc comment already reserved 'metadata' as additive). Lands on Library/Exhibit/AObject at once; additive-optional, no migration; update the mixin doc comment to reflect the widened role. (2) SHAPE — ordered array of { property: string; value: string }; repeats = repeated entries with the same property; array order = display order (IIIF ordered-pairs + the repo's array-order convention). (3) IDENTIFIER — prefixed name, canonicalized to dcterms: for all 55 properties; dc: is never stored (dcterms same-name-covers the 15 elements; DCMI guidance since 2008). (4) OVERLAP — DISJOINT: a property whose meaning a native typed field already carries (title/summary/rights/requiredStatement) is excluded from metadata; natives stay the single source of truth and keep projecting to IIIF's typed slots. Exact exclusion list is owned by Archie-2bd8. (5) ENTRY STAYS MINIMAL — future label?: display-override or property-less verbatim entries are sanctioned ADDITIVE widenings, decided by their owning tickets (labels: Archie-2bd8/Archie-e100; verbatim: Archie-bbad). MAPPER IMPACT (rule render-core-data-integrity): carry sentinels publish/working.ts:160/:214 + iiif/manifest.ts:166 (AObject), working.ts:154/:208 (Exhibit); hand-maps workingToLibrary/libraryToWorking working.ts:164/:225; WorkingObjectMeta/WorkingExhibitMeta extend RightsFields so types widen automatically but sentinels force acknowledgment. title: Default field set per level and pick-from-vocab rules
description:

title: IIIF import: preserve third-party manifest metadata
description:
## Question

What happens to a third-party IIIF manifest's metadata block on import? Its labels are arbitrary display strings, not DC properties. Decide: store verbatim (label/value alongside DC-keyed fields), map recognized labels onto dcterms, or both (map where confident, verbatim otherwise)? Also: per-canvas metadata → per-object metadata; and manifest rights / requiredStatement / summary → the existing model fields (apps/studio/src/iiif-import.ts currently drops all of it — see map Notes).
closeReason: RESOLVED (batched grill with user, 2026-07-19): MAP-WHEN-CONFIDENT, VERBATIM OTHERWISE. A pair whose label case-insensitively matches a dcterms preferred label (plus a small alias table, e.g. author→creator) imports as { property, label: original-when-different, value } — display byte-identical to the source manifest, semantics gained, mapping reversible. Unrecognized labels import verbatim { label, value } (enabled by the entry widening). RIDERS: manifest-level rights/requiredStatement/summary fill the NATIVE typed fields (all currently dropped by apps/studio/src/iiif-import.ts); per-canvas metadata → that object's entries, manifest-level metadata → the exhibit's; a label mapping to an EXCLUDED property (Title, License, …) is stored verbatim — never double-authored into metadata, never clobbering a native.

title: Publish projection: IIIF metadata[] and real dcterms emission
description:
## Question

How does metadata leave the system at publish? Decide: (1) populating the dormant IIIFRightsProps.metadata[] (label/value render of DC fields) in toManifest / collection — and the round-trip read back in objectsFromManifest; (2) whether to ALSO emit machine-readable dcterms URIs somewhere (JSON-LD in the published tree? meta/link tags on viewer pages?) or leave IIIF label/value as the only projection; (3) what Gallery/exhibits.json carries so the viewer panel can render without fetching manifests.
closeReason: RESOLVED (batched grill with user, 2026-07-19): (1) DISPLAY — populate metadata[] at Collection (library entries) / Manifest (exhibit) / Canvas (object): label = override ?? vocab default; values as IIIF language maps keyed 'none'; same-label repeats merged into one pair with multiple values. Pure IIIF viewers (Mirador) show it for free. (2) ROUND-TRIP — also emit raw entries as one extension property archieMetadata: [{property?, label?, value}] at the same three levels (P3 clients must ignore unknown properties); objectsFromManifest reads it back losslessly — the manifest stays the round-trip source, matching how summary/rights already return. (3) VIEWER — exhibits.json carries the entries pass-through (as rights/requiredStatement already mirror) so the viewer panel renders without fetching manifests. (4) Machine-readable beyond that (schema.org JSON-LD context, meta tags) stays in fog with the SEO item. title: Decide: should the read boundary reject excluded dcterms properties, or display them?
description:
## Question

Flagged by the Archie-458e reviewer as an UNSTATED decision (currently an accident, not a choice). `isMetadataEntry` (packages/render-core/src/model/model.ts) validates only the dcterms: prefix, NOT the exclusion set. So a hand-edited tree or a third-party .archie.zip carrying `dcterms:title` seeds an editable metadata row even though METADATA_EXCLUDED_PROPERTIES hides that property from the picker — the ONE path where a native-equivalent renders as a metadata row, contradicting the disjointness principle (Archie-8176). Defensible as lossless display (silently dropping curator data is the worse failure), but it should be a decided policy with a comment and a test, not an omission. Decide: reject at the read boundary, keep-and-display (documenting the exception), or migrate such entries into the native field.
closeReason:
DECIDED 2026-07-27 (human). Policy: DEMOTE TO VERBATIM, PRESERVING THE SOURCE PROPERTY FOR RE-EXPORT, AND DROP THAT MEMORY ON EDIT.

THE TICKET'S FRAMING WAS OFF, AND THE REAL DEFECT IS WORSE. It says an excluded property 'seeds an editable metadata row', implying the read side renders it. It does not: metadataRows rule 1 (metadata-display.ts:99) already drops any entry whose property is in METADATA_EXCLUDED_PROPERTIES. What actually happens to a foreign .archie.zip carrying dcterms:title is:

  1. isMetadataEntry (model.ts:86) ACCEPTS it — it validates only the dcterms: prefix
  2. seedRows (metadata-rows.ts:88) maps it straight through into an EDITABLE Studio row
  3. metadataRows rule 1 DROPS it on display

So the curator gets an editable field that renders nowhere. They can type into it and nothing appears, anywhere. That is an invisible-edit trap, and it is a worse failure than either option this ticket originally posed.

THE DECISION, in four parts:

1. DEMOTE, don't reject and don't display-as-typed. At the deserialize boundary (the single call site, model.ts:104), an entry whose property is excluded becomes a VERBATIM entry: strip the property, keep the value under its vocabulary label (dctermsLabel). Lossless in the value, renders on the page, and never claims the native slot — so disjointness (Archie-8176) holds. PRECEDENT IS ALREADY IN-REPO: iiif-import.ts:85 does exactly this for IIIF imports. Adopting it makes the zip path and the import path ONE rule instead of two.

2. PRESERVE THE SOURCE PROPERTY for re-export. The entry carries sourceProperty (e.g. 'dcterms:title') so serialize writes back what came in. An untouched foreign tree round-trips byte-faithful through Archie. Rejected the simpler 'let the demotion stick' because Archie is an archival tool and silently re-typing someone else's metadata on re-publish is not a thing it should do.

3. DROP sourceProperty ON EDIT. It is a PROVENANCE record — 'this arrived as dcterms:title with THIS value'. Once the curator changes the value it is no longer that datum, so the record no longer applies and the row becomes an ordinary verbatim entry. This is what stops Archie emitting a typed dcterms:title claim carrying a value its source never had — which would be the two-disagreeing-surfaces failure the exclusion set exists to prevent, with Archie's own name on it. Needs no UI and nothing to explain to the curator.

4. NOT a publish-preflight refusal. Considered and rejected: it blocks a publish that would otherwise work, and costs a whole surface, to solve a case rules 1-3 already handle silently and correctly.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES for whoever takes it: sourceProperty is a new model field, so it needs a carry sentinel per .claude/rules/render-core-data-integrity.md rule 3 — every boundary that hand-maps model fields carries a 'satisfies Record<keyof Source, CarryDisposition>'. Writing a new mapper without one is what that rule exists to make a compile error. Assert the ROUND TRIP in a test (foreign entry in, byte-identical entry out) and assert the EDIT drops it; a test that only checks the demotion renders would pass against code that loses the source property.

Filed separately as the implementation ticket.
