title: Add JSDoc composition context to every Studio component
description:
## Loop: claim-vs-reality diff

**Teaches:** documentation drift — documented context that isn't in the components is invisible to agents; every agent that opens a component file builds on incomplete context.

**Claims source:** `.interface-design/system.md` component table + surface/sibling descriptions + `design/_after-tokens.md`. The system.md names 18 components and describes their surface, siblings, and role. The code has none of this in the files themselves.

**Ledger:** ledgers/CLAIMS-composition.md — component | surface (claimed) | in file? | @composes documented? | resolution | commit | recheck

**Territory (documentation-only, zero code/logic/style changes):**
18 Svelte components in apps/studio/src/ — <script> JSDoc blocks only

**Phases:**
1. Extract every claim system.md makes about each component's surface, siblings, and role. Record claimed-vs-present for every component — fix nothing, finish the full diff first
2. Per row: add a JSDoc composition block immediately after `<script lang="ts">`:
   <!--
     @surface   canvas | paper | gallery | drawer | header | dialog
     @composes  sibling/slot components
     @variants  inline | popover | sidebar | card
     @constraint  when it should NOT render standalone
   -->
   One commit per component (or batch surface-aligned groups)
3. Re-run the diff — if any component still lacks its block, record and fix

**Surface map (from system.md):**
canvas: CanvasWorkspace · paper: NotesSidebar, NoteCard, NoteEditor, MetadataEditor, DetailsEditor, NarrativeEditor · gallery: GalleryWall, GalleryThumb, LibraryHome, ExhibitOverview · header: StudioHeader, SafetyState · drawer: Marginalia · dialog: PublishDialog, MergeReview, CmdK · overlay: CreateExhibitDialog, BulkRightsDialog, IdentityPrompt, HelpMenu

**Gates:** studio svelte-check 0/0, studio typecheck — doc-only, no code paths changed

**Done when:** re-running the full diff finds every component carrying its composition block, and svelte-check + typecheck are green.
closeReason: COMPLETED — measured 2026-07-26: 29 of 30 apps/studio/src/*.svelte carry a composition docblock (@surface/@composes). The one without it is Spinner.svelte, a primitive that is NOT in the ticket's territory (system.md's 18-component surface map, all of which are covered). ledgers/CLAIMS-composition.md exists as the diff ledger. Done-when is satisfied.

title: Grill: reconcile shadow-rule contradiction — spec §7 vs tokens.css + atmosphere.css
description:
## Conversation card: pre-mortem

**Not a loop — a decision gate.** `design/_after-tokens.md` §7: "zero box-shadow." tokens.css defines 5 shadow tokens with the comment "kept from Soft Static." atmosphere.css and ~15 components use them. The spec and the code contradict each other. Someone needs to decide which one yields before any code moves.

**The contradiction:**
- Spec §7: "Still zero box-shadow. Elevation reads from the verdant bloom, the always-on grain, the vignette forest-shade at corners, and moss translucency tiers."
- tokens.css: --shadow-lift-low, --shadow-lift-mid, --shadow-signal-glow, --shadow-text-haze, --shadow-inset-fog
- atmosphere.css: .soft-card, .soft-btn:hover, .pixel-btn, .details-pencil:hover all use box-shadow
- Every dialog/modal (CreateExhibitDialog, BulkRightsDialog, IdentityPrompt, MergeReview, CmdK) uses box-shadow for elevation

**The question:** which option resolves the contradiction?
A. Amend §7 — accept shadows, document the soft-blur model as deliberate
B. Remove all shadows — replace with translucency tiers + borders per §6
C. Compromise — shadows only on floating surfaces (dialogs, popovers); remove from cards, buttons, hover states

**What to weigh:**
- Visual regression risk (B touches every elevated surface)
- The Soft Static legacy (tokens.css comment: "kept from Soft Static")
- Spec fidelity vs practical elevation (can translucency alone distinguish a dialog from a card?)
- Component churn per option

**Deliverable:** one decision recorded on this ticket — the chosen option + rationale. If B or C: a grep list of every selector that must change.

**Done when:** the decision is recorded. Implementation is a separate ticket.

---

## DECISION (2026-07-21): Option C — shadows only on floating surfaces

**Rationale:**

The authoritative spec is `.interface-design/system.md` § Depth, which predates and contradicts the current token values. It reads:

> "1–2px subtle shadows only where a surface floats above the canvas (popup, drawer); No heavy card shadows, no material-style elevation ramps."

This IS Option C — it was never a compromise, it is the spec the code drifted from. The current tokens (`--shadow-lift-low: 0 24px 48px -24px`, `--shadow-lift-mid: 0 40px 80px -32px`) are massive soft-blur shadows applied to cards, buttons, and hover states — precisely what the "no heavy card shadows" clause forbids.

**Why not A (amend the spec):** The Verdant Clearing identity thesis — "Depth is built from blur + light, never from a hard offset shadow" (atmosphere.css preamble) — is stronger than the convenience of keeping existing shadows. Amending the spec to accept them would make it a post-hoc description rather than a design constraint. Spec drift becomes precedent. The grain, bloom, vignette, and translucency tiers already carry elevation; shadows dilute the thesis.

**Why not B (remove all shadows):** Floating surfaces need plane separation. A scrimmed dialog over dark parchment without any shadow risks blending into the background. The spec itself carves out "popup, drawer" — those are floating surfaces that genuinely lift above the canvas. Translucency tiers distinguish a card from the canvas (same plane); they cannot distinguish a dialog from a card behind it (different planes). A 1–2px soft shadow on a scrim provides the necessary separation without becoming a material-design elevation ramp.

### Token classification

The five shadow tokens fall into four categories with distinct fates:

**Category 1: Lift shadows (`--shadow-lift-low`, `--shadow-lift-mid`) — elevation cues**
→ RESTRICT to floating surfaces only. Remove from all static surfaces, hover states, buttons, cards.
→ Token VALUES also need recalibration from 24-40px soft blur to spec-level 1-2px subtle lift (implementation ticket).

**Category 2: Signal glow (`--shadow-signal-glow`) — rationed attention signals**
→ KEEP. These are NOT elevation cues. They signal active/primary/selected states. The spec's restriction is on elevation, not on signal indicators. Uses:
  - `header > button.publish-signal` / `:hover` (App.svelte:2759-60) — the ONE rationed signal
  - `.create-add` (App.svelte:2905) — primary sidebar CTA
  - `.ns-start` (ExhibitOverview.svelte:1006) — "Start a narrative" CTA
  - `.frame-box.sel` (AvEditor.svelte:461) — selected frame indicator
  - `.capture-hint` (AvEditor.svelte:465) — capture-mode status
  - `.markbar .add` (AvEditor.svelte:496) — add-mark CTA
  - `.save` / `:hover` (NoteEditor.svelte:187-88) — Done button
  - `.primary` (IdentityPrompt.svelte:76, Publish.svelte:1111, SaveZipDialog.svelte:79)
  - `.signal-tile` (atmosphere.css:70) — primary card
  - `.swatch.on` (ReadingsEditor.svelte:74) — active reading dot
  - `.add button` (ReadingsEditor.svelte:101) — add reading CTA

**Category 3: Inset fog (`--shadow-inset-fog`) — recessed depth cues**
→ KEEP. These are depression, not elevation ("moss translucency tiers" per spec). Uses:
  - `.obj-thumb` (App.svelte:2972) — thumbnail inset
  - `main.drawing .canvas-plate::after` (App.svelte:3021) — draw-mode depth
  - `.vt-track` (AvEditor.svelte:470) — timeline track
  - `.cmd`, `.preview`, code blocks (Publish.svelte:1001,1025,1053) — inset code/preview

**Category 4: Text haze (`--shadow-text-haze`) — display text treatment**
→ KEEP. Used on headings (wordmark, stage h1, library h1, dialog h2). Not an elevation cue — it's a text rendering flourish.

title: Published-site deep links: should viewer URLs mirror Studio place grammar?
description:
## Question

Should published viewer deep links mirror Studio's place-addressable grammar (ADR-0024)?

Studio exposes `library/slug/slug+objectId` as real paths. The viewer reaches rungs below the
exhibit by **hash fragment**, and that is a deliberate, documented choice — not a defect.

## Correction (2026-07-20) — the "canonical URL drops deep rungs" framing was wrong

An earlier assessment proposed retargeting this ticket as a bug: that `/viewer/<slug>/` honours no
rung below the exhibit while `[slug].astro` calls itself the deep-link surface. Checked against the
files, that is not a defect:

- `apps/viewer/src/pages/sitemap.xml.ts:1-2` states the rule outright — "static pages only:
  hash-routed deep links can't appear (crawlers ignore fragments)" (Archie-b4f2, ADR-0013). Deep
  links are hash-routed BY DESIGN, and their absence from the sitemap is the correct consequence.
- The sitemap/`exhibitSlugs` vs `[slug].astro` `getStaticPaths` difference is also deliberate
  (Archie-77b2): every slug builds a page so an `unlisted` exhibit stays reachable by direct URL,
  while only the listed subset is advertised. The two enumerations are meant to differ.

So the real question is unchanged and still open: **should the viewer move from hash-routed to
path-routed deep links to mirror Studio's grammar?**

## What constrains the answer

- **ADR-0013** (canonical origin = GitHub Pages, static hosting): path-based deep rungs need either
  pre-rendering every object/note rung or a SPA fallback. That cost is the crux.
- **ADR-0024** (Studio place grammar) — the shape being mirrored.
- **ADR-0022** (IIIF content-state interop) — an existing external deep-link grammar the viewer may
  already owe compatibility to.
- Crawlability: the current hash scheme means no rung below the exhibit is indexable. Whether that
  matters is a product call, and it is the strongest argument for changing.
- Secondary scope: the `place.ts` / `route.ts` encode/decode asymmetry (unverified; check before use).

## Note on the dependency edge

The edge blocking this on Viewer parity (Archie-7aef) was cut: the URL-grammar question can be
framed and answered without first settling which surfaces propagate. Re-add it if that proves false.

## Input from the viewer-ux map (Archie-d5cd, 2026-07-25)

Stays on THIS map by decision — d5cd changes no grammar, so nothing pre-empts the Studio<->viewer
symmetry question. Measured input it now has:

- **V100 was never a grammar flaw.** route.ts parses every frozen rung correctly. The note rung
  failed because note-arrival.ts compared a URL ULID against a full published IRI. Fixed in
  Archie-67b6 without touching route.ts.
- **V24/V101** — the viewer READ four rungs it never WROTE; Archie-99b1 makes the address bar write
  every rung the grammar reads. So by the time this ticket is worked, the viewer side of the
  grammar is fully exercised in both directions, which is the state it should be compared from.
- route.ts remains the SINGLE definition; apps/studio/src/place.ts mirrors it (place.ts:27-31).
closeReason: DECIDED 2026-07-27 (A3): no — keep the hash. Mirroring Studio's path grammar buys visual symmetry and costs the 'works on any static host with zero config' property, which is the viewer's whole premise. The ticket had already self-corrected to note the hash is deliberate; this confirms it as settled rather than pending.

title: Viewer parity: which Studio decisions propagate to the viewer, at what fidelity?
description:
## Question

Which Studio redesign decisions must propagate to the published viewer, and at what fidelity?

This is a **scoping** ticket: its output is a decision about surface and fidelity, not a build.

## Scope the answer must cover

The candidate surface is the narrative reading surface plus the shared `NotePopup` — one component
used by both `Reader` (grid / steps-objects) and `NarrativeReader` (narrative / steps-sections).

Parity has **four** consumers, not two. Any decision must say what each gets:
1. `apps/viewer` (Astro + Svelte islands, read-only)
2. `packages/archie-viewer` (the embeddable bundle)
3. `packages/render-mount` (the framework-free mount seam)
4. the published static tree itself

## Governing prior decisions

- **ADR-0019** (embeddable read-only viewer) and **ADR-0021** (viewer target contract) — these
  constrain what the viewer is ALLOWED to grow. Read before proposing any propagation.
- The map's closed decisions are the input list; go through them one at a time and mark each
  Studio-authoring-only (must NOT propagate) or viewer-relevant.
- Reconcile with the two existing Phase 3 plans rather than inventing a parallel table.

## Why this matters beyond itself

It was the only bridge from the Studio overhaul to the viewer. Its edge to Published-site deep links
(Archie-33bf) has been cut — that question is answerable independently — so this ticket now blocks
nothing and can be taken whenever.
closeReason:
NO PARITY PROPAGATION from this map. The viewer is declared out of scope for the Studio UX overhaul, and gets its own audit as a separate wayfinder map (Viewer UX audit, label map:viewer-ux).

Rationale (user decision, grilling 2026-07-24):
- The map's declared source, ledgers/UX-AUDIT-studio-wireframes.md, has zero viewer mentions. Every closed decision on this map was reasoned about authoring affordances only. Propagating them to a read surface nobody audited is guesswork dressed as consistency.
- ADR-0019 forecloses visual parity anyway: the embed drops Annotorious/PixiJS and renders regions as a DOM-SVG overlay while Studio keeps Annotorious. Studio and the embed can never match at the marker layer; only contracts can.
- Most of this map's decisions have no read analogue at all (save vocabulary, create/import, add grammar, bulk selection, publish continuity, collaboration, editor chrome, Details affordance, narrative authoring locus).
- The couplings that do exist are already STRUCTURAL, not decisions to propagate: packages/render-core/src/query/marker-style.ts readingMarkerStyle is the single style source for App.svelte:1482 and ExhibitView.svelte:277; packages/render-core/src/url/route.ts is the single address grammar (and predates apps/studio/src/place.ts, which mirrors it).

CORRECTION recorded here, contradicting ledgers/MAP-READINESS-studio-ux-overhaul-2026-07-20.md:136-137: the viewer's ReadingLegend carrying no reading number is NOT a WCAG 1.4.1 gap. docs/research/a11y-interactions.md:102-104 names that exact component (ReadingLegend.svelte:38-39, swatch + name in role=radiogroup) as a surface that already satisfies 1.4.1, and :128-129 says don't touch it. The real 1.4.1 gap is the on-canvas marker, which is shared render-core code and therefore not a viewer-parity question.

Also dead, do not carry forward: the embed overlay keyboard/AT dead end, closed by Archie-9413 (merged 4178a7b); read-overlay.ts:184-191 sets role, aria-label, tabindex=0 and a keydown handler.

Successor: the Viewer UX audit map. Its first move is producing the read-side equivalent of UX-AUDIT-studio-wireframes.md; it must reconcile with docs/plans/EMBED-VIEWER-IMPLEMENTATION-STRATEGY.md:73-82 (Phase 3 route ladder) and docs/plans/SCALE-GALLERY-PLAN.md:100 (Phase 3 viewer parity) rather than inventing a parallel table.

## Question

source is **`docs/learn/`**, and it ships via build (`sync-learn`; the GH-Pages deploy bug was fixed
in b564ac2).

## What is already done — do not redo it

Archie-6595 (closed 2026-07-19) **already refreshed all seven decks against the shipped redesign**,
verifying every load-bearing claim against source before writing. Read its close reason first: it
records exactly what was rewritten and, importantly, that **five real-pixel screenshots could not be
honestly re-shot headlessly** — two structurally-wrong ones were removed (flagged in-file), three
conceptually-correct ones kept with re-shoot flags.

So the real question is narrower: **what landed after 2026-07-19 that invalidates a deck?**
Use `git log` since that date over `apps/studio/src` and `docs/learn`. One known item: **Deck 3 is
materially false on desktop after b7a747e** (unverified — confirm before rewriting).

## Governing inputs this ticket originally omitted

  HelpMenu its only entry, and no new cue system is to be built. This bounds any answer here.
- **Archie-6595's close reason** — the state of the decks and the human re-shoot list.

title: Visual/design-system pass over surviving Studio chrome
description:
## Question

After the structural redesign wave, does the surviving Studio chrome hold together visually —
palette, spacing, typography, depth — across the reworked header, sidebar, rail, overview and
dialog surfaces? This is visual QA, not structure and not new features.

## This ticket now carries the shadow-rule implementation (absorbed from Archie-5c1d)

Archie-5c1d grilled the shadow-rule contradiction (spec §7 vs tokens.css + atmosphere.css) and
**recorded an Option C decision** with a concrete work list. Its promised `Archie-5c1d-impl` was
never filed; rather than file it separately, that work lands here.

From 5c1d's decision, roughly **65 selectors across ~18 files**, with `atmosphere.css` and
`App.svelte` the bulk:

- **Legacy 8-Bit Orbit aliases in tokens.css** now dead or needing re-evaluation:
  `--shadow-pixel`, `--shadow-pixel-strong`, `--shadow-pixel-cyan`, `--shadow-pixel-yellow`,
  `--shadow-pixel-btn`, `--shadow-pixel-btn-pink`, `--shadow-pixel-btn-active`.
- **Floating surfaces that KEEP lift shadows** after recalibration (shadow-lift-mid unless noted):
  BulkRightsDialog `.dialog`, CmdK palette, CreateExhibitDialog `.dialog`, HelpMenu `.help-menu`,
  IdentityPrompt dialog, MergeReview dialog, NotePicker popover, PropsDrawer drawer,
  Publish `.dialog`, ReadingsModal modal, SaveZipDialog `.dialog`, ShortcutsHelp sheet,
  TutorialModal modal, ExhibitOverview `.selection-tray`, MetadataEditor `.row-menu`,
  and Marginalia `.bucket` (shadow-lift-low).

## Added scope

- `atmosphere.css` in **both** apps (not just studio).
- `static-pages.ts:58`.

## Reading

- `design/_after-tokens.md` — the token system (Verdant Clearing); tokens are stable, the components
  wearing them were rewritten.
- `apps/studio/src/tokens.css`, `apps/studio/src/markers.css`.
- Archie-5c1d's full decision body for the selector list in its authoritative form.

## Open: how is a visual pass verified?

A visual QA pass with no artifact and no verification method is unresolvable. Decide the deliverable
before starting. Note: no visual-regression harness was found (grep for
`pixelmatch|toMatchSnapshot|visual.regression|baseline` across package.json, scripts/, apps/studio/e2e)
— but a harness under another name would not have surfaced, so confirm before concluding.

## Related

- Archie-c59a (tokenize markers.css) overlaps — check before duplicating. Its drop-shadow removal
  was the collision 5c1d was grilling.
- Blocks the screenshot half of the onboarding refresh.

--- ORGANISED 2026-07-26 ---
batch:studio-visual — the mechanical half (the ~65-selector shadow list) of one visual pass whose
judgement half is Archie-05e4 (palette/typography/radius coherence). If the palette question is still
live, run 05e4 first: recalibrating shadows against tokens that are about to move is wasted work.

---

## PROGRESS 2026-07-27 — the palette-independent slice is done (468f138)

**Removed: 14 dead tokens, from both copies.** The 7 `--shadow-pixel*` this ticket names all have
ZERO uses across `apps/` and `packages/`. So do the 7 contiguous same-block siblings
(`--pixel-unit`, `--grid-size`, `--border-pixel`, `--border-pixel-bold`, `--bg-grid`,

Verified against this repo's grep hazard: re-checked with `grep -a`, a pattern that also catches
`var(--x, fallback)`, a scan for dynamic name construction, and a real NUL test (both files clean,
UTF-8). Artifact measured, not the exit code: 0 `shadow-pixel` in the rebuilt embed bundle and root
dist.

## FINDING for Archie-05e4 — six MORE dead legacy tokens, deliberately left

The adjacent legacy COLOUR aliases are also unused: `--void`, `--deep-navy`, `--neon-cyan`,

still on the old palette degrade to verdant styling until the component pass rewrites them" — zero
uses means that pass is finished and they can go.

Left in place because they are palette territory and 05e4 is the palette walk. Whoever does 05e4
should delete them. **Still live, do not delete:** `--blush` (2 uses), `--mist-blue` (4),
`--clay-line` (2, one feeding `--annotation-inner-stroke`), `--moss-shadow` (2).

## STILL OPEN — the bulk, and why it did not move

The ~50-selector shadow recalibration (the floating-surfaces list above) is untouched. This ticket's
own ORGANISED note is the reason: run **Archie-05e4** first, because recalibrating shadows against
tokens that are about to move is wasted work. 05e4 is the judgement half and needs the maintainer's
eye.

Also still unanswered: **"how is a visual pass verified?"** No visual-regression harness was
confirmed either way in this pass.

## PROGRESS 2026-07-27 — the token VALUES are recalibrated (branch `task/1244-shadow-recal`)

The half 5c1d called out as needing an implementation ticket ("Token VALUES also need recalibration
from 24-40px soft blur to spec-level 1-2px subtle lift") is **done**, in one file:

```
--shadow-lift-low   0 24px 48px -24px rgba(26,60,35,.30)  ->  0 1px 2px rgba(26,60,35,.14)
--shadow-lift-mid   0 40px 80px -32px rgba(26,60,35,.38)  ->  0 2px 6px -1px rgba(26,60,35,.20)
```

One edit, ~160 use sites across both apps and the embed, all spec-compliant at once. Studio's second
`tokens.css` is gone (Archie-ecf4 unified onto the render-core floor), so there is no second copy to
keep in step any more. The alpha drops with the blur deliberately: 0.30 over 48px is a faint wash;
the same 0.30 over 2px is a hard line.

**Not recalibrated, and the token block now says why** so nobody "finishes the job": `signal-glow`
(a rationed attention bloom — the Verdant thesis asks for bloom; not a plane cue), `text-haze`
(display-type flourish), `inset-fog` (a DEPRESSION cue, the opposite of lift). All three are KEEP
per 5c1d.

### The ticket's open question — "how is a visual pass verified?" — has an answer for this half

Not a harness (none exists; re-confirmed). A **driven before/after pair against the real built
viewer**, shot in one page session so the pair differs by the token and nothing else: shoot with the
shipped values, inject the old values via `addStyleTag`, shoot again.

Both probes printed the SUBJECT before the verdict, and asserted the injection actually changed the
computed `box-shadow` — a pair of screenshots of a modal that never opened is two pictures of
nothing.

| surface | subject proven present | max channel delta OLD vs NEW | pixels differing >2/255 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gallery cards on the gradient | 6x `a.card` 315x~500, computed shadow read back | **19 / 255** | 3.98% |
| `div.finder` modal over `--scrim-dim` | 640x684, computed shadow read back | **10 / 255** | 4.31% |

**The risk 5c1d could only reason about is measured and it was not real.** It weighed whether a
1-2px shadow can still separate a floating surface from a scrimmed background. On the actual modal
the two renderings are indistinguishable — the scrim and the paper/moss contrast were already doing
all the separation, and the 40px shadow was contributing at most 10/255 on any channel. The heavy
values were spec debt with no visual benefit to defend.

(Non-vacuous in the other direction too: ~4% of pixels did move, so the probe can see a difference
when there is one.)

### Gates

render-core 1315/1315 · archie-viewer 211/211 (incl. `tokens.test.ts`, which asserts the embed's
bundled string still equals the canonical file's value) · `sync-dist:check` matches · bundle ratchet
`baseline unchanged`. Artifact measured, not the exit code: the rebuilt embed carries
`--shadow-lift-low: 0 1px 2px rgba(26,60,35,.14)` and **zero** occurrences of either old value.

### Spun out: Archie-2865

Shipping this needed a `dist/` rebuild, which dirtied **35 files** — the committed CDN artifact does
not match what its own source builds, and `sync-dist:check` cannot see it because it compares the two
mirrors to each other and never to the source. Filed as **Archie-2865**.

**Correction, recorded because the first version of that ticket had it wrong:** the drift is NOT
~69 commits of neglect (that number came from how far this branch trailed `main` and was
misattributed). `dist/` is rebuilt constantly. It goes stale at every **merge** — measured at
origin/main `84bab01`, the tip kept parent `2699f3f`'s bundle byte-identical while taking 3 source
files from the other parent. So a per-PR freshness gate cannot help; the fix has to run post-merge
on main. Detail on Archie-2865.

## STILL OPEN — the selector half

The ~65-selector restriction (lift shadows removed from cards, buttons, hover and focus states;
kept only on genuinely floating surfaces) is **untouched**. 5c1d's decision body holds the
authoritative list.

Two things worth knowing before starting it:

- **It is now a spec-fidelity job, not a visual-damage one.** With the token at 1-2px, a stray lift
  on a hover state is no longer a material elevation ramp — it is a 1px line that mostly is not
  visible. The urgency came from the 40px value and that is gone. Do it for correctness, at leisure.
- **5c1d's list is Studio-only.** The viewer wears the same tokens at comparable density —
  `NarrativeReader` (8), `Reader` (5), `NoteLightbox` (5), `Gallery` (5), `ObjectGrid` (4),
  `ExhibitView` (4), plus `apps/viewer/src/atmosphere.css` (5). Any pass that follows 5c1d's list
  verbatim will finish believing it is done and have covered roughly half the codebase. The added
  scope this ticket already records (`atmosphere.css` in BOTH apps, `static-pages.ts:58`) is the
  start of that, not the whole of it.

---

## PHASE 1 DONE — atmosphere.css, both apps (`9671774`)

Seven selectors across the two copies wore a lift; none of them floats.

**Deleted outright rather than recalibrated** (zero consumers in either app, verified against the
whole repo and against dynamic class construction): `.soft-card`, `.pixel-btn`, `.pixel-btn--pink`,
`.pixel-card`. The 8-Bit Orbit safety net exists for classes "still present until the component pass
converts them" — for these four that pass is finished. `.label-pill` and `.pixel-bracket` are still
worn (3 files each), so the net itself stays. The only `.soft-card` left in the repo is
`prototypes/metadata-panel/`, which has its own stylesheet and does not load this file.

**Shadow removed, rule kept** — each already had a non-shadow affordance carrying the real work:

| selector | what carries it now |
| --- | --- |
| `.soft-btn:hover` | background tone shift (it had BOTH; the lift was the redundant one) |
| `.details-pencil` | raised fill inside a hairline border |
| `.details-pencil:hover` | ink AND border-colour both go to the accent |

`box-shadow` also dropped from both transition lists, and `.pixel-btn` from the reduced-motion rule
in BOTH files. **The viewer's reduced-motion rule was missed on the first pass** and was caught by
grepping for dangling references to the deleted classes — not by any gate. Worth knowing for the
remaining phases: deleting a class means grepping the same file for other rules that name it.

**Verified against the artifact**, because svelte-check cannot see CSS at all: the built viewer CSS
has 0 occurrences of `.soft-card` / `.pixel-btn` / `.pixel-card`, and `.soft-btn:hover` emits
`{background:var(--surface-canvas-overlay)}` with no `box-shadow`. studio 1173/1173, studio
svelte-check 1207 files 0/0, viewer svelte-check 1542 files 0/0.

## REMAINING — 145 sites across 47 files, and the estimate on this ticket was low

5c1d estimated "~65 selectors across ~18 files". Measured after phase 1: **145 `shadow-lift` sites
across 47 source files.** The gap is that 5c1d enumerated Studio only. The viewer carries roughly a
third of the total and is not in its list at all:

```
studio   App.svelte 18 · LibraryHome 13 · ExhibitOverview 10 · Publish 6 · AvEditor 5
         NarrativeEditor 4 · CreateExhibitDialog 4 · GalleryWall 3 · (+16 files at 1-2)
viewer   NarrativeReader 8 · Reader 5 · NoteLightbox 5 · Gallery 5 · ObjectGrid 4
         ExhibitView 4 · ViewerShell 3 · NoteMedia 3 · MediaPlayer 3 · (+9 files at 1-2)
shared   render-svelte 2 · archie-viewer element.ts 2 + note-card.ts 1
```

Anyone working 5c1d's list verbatim will finish believing the job is done with about half the
codebase untouched. **Use the grep, not the list.**

### Suggested phase order (≤5 files each, per the repo's multi-file rule)

1. ~~atmosphere.css ×2~~ — done
2. `LibraryHome` 13 + `GalleryWall` 3 — pure card/tile hover+rest, no floating surface among them
3. `ExhibitOverview` 10 — plates and list rows, but `.selection-tray` is floating and KEEPS
4. `App.svelte` 18 — the bulk; do it alone, it holds the tool-strip, rail and note-editor regions
5. viewer: `Gallery` + `ObjectGrid` + `NoteMedia` + `MediaThumbnail` + `Filmstrip` — tiles
6. viewer: `Reader` + `NarrativeReader` — list rows; both are big, consider one each
7. dialog CHILDREN (`Publish`, `CreateExhibitDialog`, `BulkRightsDialog`, `MergeReview`,
   `SaveZipDialog`, `ShortcutsHelp`) — containers KEEP, children lose
8. the KEEP list — verify each floating surface still has its lift and nothing else does

### Two things that make the rest lower-risk than it looks

- **The token is already at 1-2px**, so a missed selector is now a 1px line rather than a 40px
  ramp. This is spec fidelity, not visual repair. No urgency, no big-bang.
- **Every removal needs its replacement affordance named**, as in the phase-1 table above. A hover
  state whose ONLY cue was the shadow must gain a tone/border/ink change in the same edit — do not
  just delete the line. Phase 1 found all three already had one, but that will not hold everywhere.

---

## COMPLETE 2026-07-27 — branch `task/1244-shadow-recal`, 15 commits

Both halves are done. 5c1d's Option C is fully implemented.

**Half 1 — token VALUES recalibrated** (one file, ~160 sites at a stroke):
`--shadow-lift-low` `0 24px 48px -24px .30` → `0 1px 2px .14`;
`--shadow-lift-mid` `0 40px 80px -32px .38` → `0 2px 6px -1px .20`.

**Half 2 — the selector restriction**, 8 phases, 145 sites. **34 lift shadows survive and every one
is a deliberate, annotated keep** (19 dialogs/drawers/sheets/menus, 5 NoteLightbox, 2 badges,
`.rail-pos`, `.selection-tray`, `.credit .panel`, `.archie-note-sheet`, `.bucket`, `.row-menu`,
`.finder`/`.cite`, `.cues button.open`).

### The rule that actually got applied — ratified by the maintainer, and it is NOT 5c1d's

5c1d says "floating surfaces". That word is undecidable at the point of edit. What this pass used:

> **The lift survives where a surface sits over content it does not control.**

It covers dialogs, drawers, popovers, a sticky chip over scrolling tiles, a tray, and badges over
arbitrary photo pixels; it excludes every in-flow card, row, tile, banner, button and segmented
control. It changed four verdicts against 5c1d's list and is decidable by reading, not judging.

### Two hazards this uncovered, both of which a blind sweep would have shipped

**1. `outline: none` + a `box-shadow` is a FOCUS RING wearing an elevation token.** Three instances,
and deleting any would have been a WCAG 2.4.7 regression that no gate in this repo reports:

| site | if swept blindly |
| --- | --- |
| `.zone-name-edit:focus` | only a faint background tint left to signal focus |
| `.object:focus-visible` (ObjectGrid) | the lift was the ONLY declaration — **keyboard focus gone from every object tile** |
| `.tile:focus-visible` (GalleryWall) | ring deleted |

All three now carry a real `0 0 0 2px var(--accent)` — better than before, not merely compliant.
`CreateExhibitDialog`'s `.field input:focus` was already doing it right (`0 0 0 3px`), and is the
donor pattern.

**2. A lift LAYERED with something that is not elevation.** Deleting the declaration deletes both:

| site | the layer that had to survive |
| --- | --- |
| `.plate.over` | `-4px 0 0 accent` — the **drag-and-drop drop indicator** |
| `.card.selected`, `.plate-wrap.selected` | the 2px selection ring |
| `.card.template` | an inset hairline border |
| `.binding-error` | an inset `semantic-warning` stripe |

**The habit both reduce to: grep the DECLARATION, not the token.**

### A hover whose only cue was the shadow needs a replacement, not a deletion

Five found. `.ss-cancel`, `.de-review`, `.del` took the `.soft-btn` idiom (tone shift).
`.ts-tool.armed` took a lighter border ring instead, because a tone shift would fight the fill's AA
text contrast (3.6:1 vs ~5:1, recorded in that file). **`.del:hover` I got wrong first** — the strip
left `.del:hover { }`, an empty rule, i.e. a destructive button with no hover feedback, and
svelte-check passed it at 0/0 because empty CSS is valid. Caught by a scan of every touched file's
`<style>` block; none remain.

### `.cues button.open` — kept, and it is the interesting one

Its comment (with a cited donor) states that playback owns the left edge and fill while selection
owns the lift, *specifically so the two states coexist*. Stripping it collapses two orthogonal
channels into one. Kept under 5c1d's own **Category 2** — "the restriction is on elevation, not on
signal indicators". Maintainer-ratified.

### The estimate on this ticket was wrong, twice

5c1d said "~65 selectors across ~18 files". Measured: **145 sites across 47 files** — it enumerated
Studio only, and the viewer holds a third. It is also **stale**: its `.load-hint .hint` no longer
exists. Classify by what the code IS, not by July's line numbers.

### Verification

Every phase measured the **artifact**, not the exit code, because svelte-check cannot see CSS at
all. Gates at completion: studio 1173/1173 + svelte-check 1207 files 0/0 + typecheck clean; viewer
svelte-check 1542 files 0/0; render-core / render-svelte / archie-viewer suites green;
`sync-dist:check` matches; bundle ratchet "baseline unchanged".

The ticket's standing question — **"how is a visual pass verified?"** — is answered for the value
half: a driven before/after pair against the real built viewer, shot in one page session so the pair
differs by the token alone, with the subject printed and the injection asserted to have changed the
computed style. The risk 5c1d could only reason about was measured and is not real: on the actual
modal-over-scrim the two renderings differ by at most **10/255** on any channel. The scrim was always
doing the separation.

### Not done, deliberately

`Archie-05e4`'s palette/typography walk is untouched — it needs the maintainer's eye, and the six
dead legacy colour aliases noted above belong to it.
closeReason:
Both halves of 5c1d's Option C are implemented on branch task/1244-shadow-recal (15 commits).

Half 1: the lift token VALUES recalibrated to the spec's 1-2px, one file, ~160 sites at a stroke.
Half 2: the selector restriction, 8 phases, 145 sites across 47 files. 34 lifts survive, every one a
deliberate and annotated keep.

The applied rule is maintainer-ratified and sharper than 5c1d's 'floating surfaces': the lift
survives where a surface sits over content it does not control. It changed four verdicts against
5c1d's list and is decidable by reading rather than judging.

Three focus rings and four non-elevation layers (including the drag-drop drop indicator) were found
riding inside lift declarations and preserved; a blind sweep would have deleted them with every gate
green. One hover I broke (.del:hover left empty) was caught and restored.

5c1d's work list was both an undercount (65 -> 145; it enumerated Studio only) and stale (.load-hint
no longer exists) - recorded on the ticket so nobody works from it again.

The open question 'how is a visual pass verified?' is answered for the value half: a driven
before/after pair against the real built viewer. The risk 5c1d could only reason about is measured
and not real - the modal-over-scrim differs by at most 10/255 on any channel.

NOT included, deliberately: Archie-05e4's palette/typography walk (needs the maintainer's eye), plus
the six dead legacy colour aliases that belong with it.

description:

title: tldraw → Archie architecture adoption
description:
## Notes

Domain: evaluating which of tldraw's static-app architecture patterns to adopt in Archie's render-core stack. Source: `ledgers/LEARN-tldraw-merged-2026-07-22.md`. Research: `ledgers/RESEARCH-tldraw-source-scout-2026-07-22.md` (source-backed).

Skills every session should consult: `wayfinder`, `seeds`, `domain-codebooks` (distributed-state/sync patterns for undo), `brainstorming` (for design tradeoffs).

Standing preference: prefer minimal, incrementally-adoptable solutions over full rewrites. The annotation spine is already solid — changes should compose with it, not replace it.

## Decisions so far

- [Research: tldraw signals internals](#) — Resolved. Minimal Archie signals API = ~500 LOC: atom (~140), computed core (~200), transact (~100), capture (~60). Key patterns: global epoch for change detection, lazy computed with 3-condition cache-hit, transact with rollback via initialAtomValues snapshot. Source-backed from tldraw main.
- [Research: tldraw HistoryManager + RecordsDiff](#) — Resolved. RecordsDiff = {added,updated,removed} + reverseRecordsDiff + squashRecordDiffsMutable. HistoryManager = 2-stack mark-based system (mark/bailToMark/squashToMark/batch, 3 modes). Maps cleanly to Archie: undo stack on top of append-only log as UI projection layer. Source-backed from tldraw main + docs.

## Fog

- **Manager decomposition boundaries** — when session.ts exceeds ~800 LOC, which concerns to extract into managers and what the manager interface looks like. Depends on signals + undo decisions.
- **Geometry objects with behavior** — when Archie adds a 3rd annotation shape type (maps, audio regions), adopt Geometry2d-style classes with hitTest/nearestPoint. Premature to spec now.
- **Self-contained export pipeline** — tldraw's StyleEmbedder + FontEmbedder + embedMedia pattern for single-file HTML. Research ticket Archie-5582 still open.

title: Grilling: schema version in archie.json marker
description:
## Question

Should Archie embed a schema version in `archie.json` (the .archie.zip self-ID marker) so loaders can auto-migrate old data? What would the migration runner look like?

## Context

tldraw embeds `schema: SerializedSchema` in every `StoreSnapshot` — old data loads cleanly after schema changes because the loader runs migrations automatically. Archie's migration system (`migrate/`) works but doesn't version the artifact itself.

Currently `archie.json` identifies the archive as Archie's format but carries no version number. Adding one would be ~20 lines.

## Open questions

1. What's the current schema version? Is there an implicit version number anywhere?
2. Where would the migration runner live — in `@render/core/migrate/`? In `@render/core/publish/open.ts`?
3. Should we add it now (preemptively) or wait for the next schema-breaking change?
4. Does this interact with the existing `migrate/object-ids.ts` engine?

## Acceptance

A close reason recording the decision + any resulting task tickets.

---

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (C1 · yes, version-stamp now)

Add the version stamp to `archie.json` now. ~20 lines, and tldraw's precedent shows old files then
load cleanly forever after. This has the worst regret curve on the whole board: it is cheap today and
impossible to retrofit onto files already in the wild.
closeReason:
DECIDED + FOUND STALE. The decision (yes, version-stamp now) is recorded on the ticket, but its premise was wrong: archie.json HAS carried a version since ADR-0020. marker.ts:29 writes 'version: SCHEMA_VERSION' and :67 gates on it. Nothing to add.

Answers to the four open questions, from the code:
1. Current schema version: SCHEMA_VERSION = 1, explicit in migrate/migrate.ts:11 — not implicit, and already stamped into every published tree.
2. Where the runner lives: it already exists at @render/core/migrate/migrate.ts — migrate(doc, migrations) over a MIGRATIONS registry, deliberately empty at v1.
3. Now or wait: moot; the stamp is already there.
4. object-ids.ts: a separate engine, untouched by this.

THE REAL GAP, which the ticket's tldraw framing was actually about: migrate() has NO production caller. Grep its importers — only stamp, foldLayersIntoTags and SCHEMA_VERSION are wired anywhere. So 'old data loads cleanly, the loader migrates automatically' is not true here. Worse, the runner is per-annotation-doc and cannot bring a v(n-1) exhibits.json/collection.json forward at all. Filed as Archie-69f9 (P1) with the design work spelled out.

SHIPPED HERE (d265282): the one safe half. validateArchieMarker had a single 'version !== SCHEMA_VERSION' check telling every mismatch to 'Re-publish it from a current Archie' — advice that is impossible to act on when the READER is the one behind. Split into malformed / newer ('Update Archie') / older ('Re-publish'), each with a test asserting the ADVICE rather than merely that it threw. Red-green proven on both halves, including isolating the not.toThrow assertion (message keeping 'Update Archie' but gaining 're-publish' -> 'expected [Function] to throw error not matching /re-publish/i'). The gate was NOT loosened: 1260 render-core tests green, typecheck clean.

title: Research: tldraw signals internals
description:
## Question

What is the minimal signals API Archie needs from tldraw's @tldraw/state? Study the source to extract the core primitives (Atom, Computed, transactions) and identify what's essential vs what's tldraw-specific.

## Scope

Read from https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw:
- `packages/state/src/lib/Atom.ts` — atom implementation
- `packages/state/src/lib/Computed.ts` — computed/derived signals
- `packages/state/src/lib/transactions.ts` — batching
- `packages/state/src/lib/capture.ts` — dependency tracking
- `packages/state/src/lib/EffectScheduler.ts` — reactions
- `packages/state-react/src/` — the React bridge (to understand what the framework adapter looks like)

## Acceptance

A markdown summary in ledgers/ covering:
1. The core API surface (atom, computed, react, transact, unsafe__withoutCapture)
2. The dependency tracking mechanism (capture parents, global epoch)
3. What a Svelte 5 bridge would look like (analogous to state-react)
4. What tldraw does that Archie does NOT need (diff history, WhyAmIRunning debug)
5. Estimated LOC for a minimal Archie signals layer
closeReason: Resolved: source-scouted tldraw signals layer from GitHub main. Minimal Archie API: atom (~140 LOC) + computed core (~200 LOC) + transact (~100 LOC) + capture (~60 LOC) = ~500 LOC. Key patterns: global epoch for change detection, lazy computed with 3-condition cache-hit, transact with rollback via initialAtomValues snapshot. Full findings: ledgers/RESEARCH-tldraw-source-scout-2026-07-22.md §1.

title: Research: tldraw HistoryManager + RecordsDiff
description:
## Question

How does tldraw's HistoryManager use RecordsDiff for undo/redo, and how would this pattern compose with Archie's append-only annotation log?

## Scope

Read from https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw:
- `packages/editor/src/lib/editor/managers/HistoryManager/HistoryManager.ts` — the full implementation
- `packages/store/src/lib/RecordsDiff.ts` — the diff primitives (reverseRecordsDiff, squashRecordDiffsMutable)
- `packages/store/src/lib/Store.ts` — how the store emits diffs to subscribers

## Acceptance

A markdown summary in ledgers/ covering:
1. The RecordsDiff data structure and its operations
2. How HistoryManager accumulates diffs, creates marks, and replays
3. The batch/transact integration
4. How this would compose with Archie's immutable log (diff stack for UI undo, log stays append-only)
5. Estimated LOC for a minimal AnnotationUndoManager
closeReason: Resolved: scouted RecordsDiff (181 LOC) + HistoryManager pattern. Core: {added,updated,removed} + reverseRecordsDiff + squashRecordDiffsMutable (perf: for-in, in-place tuple mutation, no Object.entries allocation). History: 2-stack mark-based — mark, bailToMark, squashToMark, batch, 3 modes (Recording/RecordingPreserveRedoStack/Paused). Maps cleanly to Archie: undo stack sits ON TOP of append-only log as UI projection layer. Full findings: ledgers/RESEARCH-tldraw-source-scout-2026-07-22.md §2.

title: Task: embed schema version in archie.json marker
description:
## Question

Add a version field to the .archie.zip marker so loaders can auto-migrate old data.

## What to do

Based on the grilling ticket (Archie-fc75) decision:

1. Add `"version": <N>` to the `archie.json` marker structure
2. Update `validateArchieMarker` in `@render/core/publish/marker.ts` to read the version
3. Update `ZipFilesystem.fromZip` in `@render/core/publish/open.ts` to check version and run migrations
4. Wire the existing migration runner (`migrate/migrate.ts`) to the version check
5. Update tests for marker validation and version-gated loading

## Acceptance

- `archie.json` carries a version number
- Loading an older `.archie.zip` runs migrations automatically
- Loading a future version produces a clear error (not silent corruption)
- Tests cover: current version loads, older version migrates, future version errors
closeReason:
SUPERSEDED. Half of this was already built before the ticket was written; the other half is Archie-69f9, filed today from the same finding. Item by item:

1. Add version to archie.json — ALREADY DONE. marker.ts:29 (ARCHIE_LIBRARY_MARKER) has carried 'version: SCHEMA_VERSION' since ADR-0020.
2. validateArchieMarker reads the version — ALREADY DONE, marker.ts:67. IMPROVED today (d265282): the single '!==' check became malformed / newer ('Update Archie') / older ('Re-publish'), because one message told an author to re-publish a file in the one direction where re-publishing cannot help.
3. ZipFilesystem.fromZip checks version and runs migrations — NOT DONE -> Archie-69f9.
4. Wire the migration runner to the version check — NOT DONE -> Archie-69f9. Note WHY this is not a small wiring job: migrate() is per-annotation-DOC and cannot bring a v(n-1) exhibits.json / collection.json forward. A tree-level migration shape has to be designed first. That is 69f9's acceptance.
5. Tests for marker validation and version-gated loading — DONE for the marker (marker.test.ts, 13 tests incl. three added today, red-green proven). The 'older version migrates' case cannot be tested until 3/4 exist; it is in 69f9's acceptance.

Acceptance status: 'carries a version number' met; 'future version produces a clear error' met and sharpened; 'older .archie.zip runs migrations automatically' NOT met and tracked in Archie-69f9.

title: Research: tldraw self-contained export pipeline
description:
## Question

How does tldraw's SVG/PNG export pipeline produce a fully self-contained artifact (no external fonts, images, or stylesheets)? What would a single-file HTML export look like for an Archie exhibit?

## Scope

Read from https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw:
- `packages/editor/src/lib/exports/exportToSvg.tsx` — the main pipeline
- `packages/editor/src/lib/exports/getSvgJsx.tsx` — JSX → SVG conversion
- `packages/editor/src/lib/exports/StyleEmbedder.ts` — computed style inlining
- `packages/editor/src/lib/exports/FontEmbedder.ts` — @font-face → base64 embedding
- `packages/editor/src/lib/exports/embedMedia.ts` — image/video → data URI
- `packages/editor/src/lib/exports/getSvgAsImage.ts` — SVG → PNG rasterization

## Acceptance

A markdown summary in ledgers/ covering:
1. The full pipeline: render-to-real-DOM → read computed styles → inline fonts/media → extract
2. How StyleEmbedder reads computed styles and writes inline attributes
3. How FontEmbedder discovers and embeds @font-face declarations
4. What a single-file Archie exhibit export would look like (HTML page with all CSS/JS/fonts inlined, annotations burned into the image)
5. What's transferable vs what's tldraw-specific (React-based rendering)
6. Estimated effort for a minimal single-file Archie export
closeReason:
ANSWERED 2026-07-27. Findings in docs/research/tldraw-self-contained-export-2026-07-27.md, read at source from tldraw/tldraw@main rather than summarised.

THE PIPELINE'S LOAD-BEARING IDEA: exportToSvg builds a JSX SVG, then renders it into the LIVE document hidden (inert, tabIndex -1, opacity 0) BEFORE harvesting — 'we have to add the element to the document as otherwise styles won't be computed correctly'. A self-contained export is not produced by serialising a model; it is produced by rendering the real thing and photographing everything it depended on, because you cannot know which fonts or url() references matter until the browser resolves them.

Three embedders: StyleEmbedder records computed styles plus ::before/::after (which naive serialisers drop), with two economies — skip a child property equal to the tag default, skip anything that would inherit — and the ROOT exempted since it has no parent. FontEmbedder is three-phase and starts fetching the moment StyleEmbedder reports a font-family, so walk and network overlap. embedMedia replaces by kind: canvas->toDataURL, video->frame grab then poster then data:, img->currentSrc (so a srcset-resolved variant embeds the one actually chosen), each awaiting image.decode() with failure swallowed; it also fixes DOM-only form state.

THE ARCHIE CONCLUSION, and it is a de-scoping one: the published static page is ALREADY structurally self-contained — one HTML file, no script, one inlined STYLE constant, no external stylesheet. VERIFIED: it uses system-ui and contains ZERO @font-face, so tldraw's most intricate machinery (the font embedder) has nothing to do here. And the render-then-photograph step is unnecessary too — Archie's page is generated from the model with one known STYLE constant, so a computed-style harvest has no work. Porting this pipeline would import a solution to a problem this codebase does not have. Only IMAGES stand between the current page and one file.

WORTH TAKING: embedMedia's currentSrc rule (Archie's grid emits sized IIIF derivatives); the decode-before-snapshot discipline; and the observation that tldraw gets self-containment VERIFIED for free (an SVG referencing an external font renders wrong) where Archie would not — so a single-file export needs a gate that loads the artifact with the network cut, the same shape as the viewer's existing goOffline specs.

COST, stated: base64 inflates ~33% and is unstreamable, so this is a small-exhibit affordance only — exactly how Archie-c34f scopes it. This research does not recommend building it; it removes the unknowns so c34f can be a half-day rather than an investigation.

title: Flatpak sandbox: does tauri-plugin-opener survive?
description:
Does tauri-plugin-opener actually open URLs via the xdg-desktop-portal OpenURI inside the Flatpak sandbox, or does it need a portal talk-name too? Couples to the keyring-manifest issue. Answer: test in Flatpak build or audit the plugin source.

Source: Archie-51ff Fog item 1.

--- ORGANISED 2026-07-26: batch:packaged-drive ---
Answer this in the same packaged/Flatpak session as Archie-9ece (native-store verification rows),
Archie-e47d (external links from Publish.svelte) and Archie-a09d's undriven dialog flows. One build, four answers.
closeReason:
ANSWERED 2026-07-27 by audit + an empirical check inside the real runtime. NO --talk-name is needed; tauri-plugin-opener survives the Flatpak sandbox as configured.

The chain, verified end to end rather than assumed:
1. Archie grants only opener:allow-open-url (src-tauri/capabilities/default.json:37).
2. tauri-plugin-opener 2.5.4 open_url() -> open(url, None) -> ::open::that_detached (src/open.rs:9-15, :33-36) — no D-Bus of its own.
3. open 5.3.6 on UNIX tries xdg-open FIRST (src/unix.rs:13, ahead of gio/gnome-open/kde-open).
4. In the GNOME 49 runtime /usr/bin/xdg-open is NOT the xdg-utils shell script — it is an ELF binary (the flatpak-xdg-utils shim). Ran it inside a real sandbox (flatpak run --runtime=org.gnome.Platform//49 org.gnome.Sdk//49) and grepped the binary: it carries org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop, /org/freedesktop/portal/desktop, org.freedesktop.portal.OpenURI and OpenURI. So it calls the OpenURI portal.
5. The portal bus name org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop is permitted by Flatpak by default — portal access is exactly the case that needs no talk-name.

Also verified the manifest's second claim: revealItemInDir / reveal_item_in_dir is called NOWHERE in apps/, packages/ or src-tauri/src, so --talk-name=org.freedesktop.FileManager1 is genuinely unnecessary rather than merely unused-so-far.

The comment already in src-tauri/flatpak/digital.compost.archie.yml:29-35 stated this conclusion; this ticket confirms it against the plugin source, the open crate source and the installed runtime, so it is now measured rather than asserted. It does NOT couple to the keyring issue: org.freedesktop.secrets genuinely needs its talk-name (a daemon, not a portal); OpenURI genuinely does not.

title: Security grilling: http:default CSP over-grant in Tauri
description:
http:default allows http://** (cleartext) though every caller uses https:. Over-grant worth tightening, or is a plain-http IIIF/asset host a real case? Grill → decision record → either tighten or document the exception.

Source: Archie-51ff Fog item 2.

---

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (C3 · tighten to https:)

Drop plain `http://**` from the desktop CSP — every caller already uses `https:`. Confirmed by the
maintainer rather than inferred; the sector caveat (institutions serving IIIF over plain http) was
raised explicitly and the decision stands. If such a host ever appears, the native-http bridge
(tauri-fs.ts) is the escape hatch, not a CSP relaxation.
closeReason:
DECIDED (C3) and SHIPPED. Tightened to https: only.

CORRECTION to the ticket's framing: the over-grant was not in the CSP. tauri.conf.json's csp has no http wildcard — only Tauri's required http://asset.localhost and http://ipc.localhost, which are webview protocols and unaffected. The grant was the 'http:default' capability in src-tauri/capabilities/default.json, allow: [https://**, http://**]. Removed the second entry.

Callers checked before tightening: fetchRemoteAsBlobUrl / fetchRemoteJson in apps/studio/src/tauri-fs.ts (remote IIIF images, info.json, remote AV) — all https in practice. The failure mode for a cleartext URL is clean rather than mysterious, which is what makes this safe: the plugin refuses, tauriFetch throws, the caller falls back to the webview path, and that CSP is https-only, so the user sees the ordinary 'couldn't load this media item'.

The escape hatch if a plain-http institutional IIIF host ever appears is a NARROW per-host entry in this capability — never restoring the wildcard, and never a CSP relaxation. Recorded as a comment on the permission itself.

Verified: cargo check clean (build.rs validates and regenerates the schema); regenerated capabilities.json carries allow=[{url: https://**}] and 0 occurrences of http://**.

title: Tauri webview: do Publish.svelte external links open?
description:
Under --base ./ in the combined frontend, do the secondary <a target=_blank> links in Publish.svelte (commit / Pages settings / docs) open externally at all, or navigate/no-op inside the webview? Answer: test in real Tauri build.

Source: Archie-51ff Fog item 3.

--- ORGANISED 2026-07-26: batch:packaged-drive ---
Answer this in the same packaged/Flatpak session as Archie-9ece (native-store verification rows),
Archie-7e2e (opener under the sandbox) and Archie-a09d's undriven dialog flows. One build, four answers.
closeReason: ANSWERED 2026-07-27 by audit of the shipped code. The ticket's premise is already handled — and its worry was correct, which is why it was handled. Archie-2139 established that a plain target=_blank anchor in the Tauri webview is unreliable (no window.open handler, so the link is silently dead), and EVERY external anchor in Publish.svelte now carries onclick={(e) => externalAnchor(e, url)}. Verified all 9 of them (lines 808, 821, 827, 843, 850, 902, 904, 907 x2) — there is no bare target=_blank anchor left in the file. externalAnchor (Publish.svelte:164) is a no-op on web (the anchor opens a tab normally) and on desktop preventDefaults the click and routes it through machine.openExternal, which hostname-allowlists via isAllowedExternalUrl (publish-machine.svelte.ts:168, :335) and then calls the opener plugin's openUrl. A refusal is visible, not silent: the openUrlFailed note renders. So the answer to 'do they open externally at all, or navigate/no-op inside the webview' is: they no longer depend on the webview's target=_blank behaviour at all. The opener path they DO depend on is verified end to end in Archie-7e2e (plugin -> open crate -> xdg-open -> OpenURI portal, confirmed inside a real GNOME 49 sandbox). NOT done: a click-by-click drive of the packaged binary. It would need a completed GitHub publish to reach most of these anchors, and the two facts it could add (the intercept fires; openUrl succeeds) are the two this audit and 7e2e establish separately. Left in Archie-9ece/a09d's packaged-drive batch if a belt-and-braces confirmation is wanted.

title: Import-validation depth: validate .archie.zip beyond marker?
description:
Freecut Zod-gates its .freecut.zip on import. Whether .archie.zip should validate beyond the marker sits in tension with render-core's per-item-tolerant read policy (docs/research/freecut-unverified-claims.md item 18). Grill scope: which validation depth (marker-only, structural, full-content), what's the cost (perf, false-reject risk), when does it pay off (malformed third-party zips? upgrade-forward compat?)

Source: Archie-5b06 Fog item 3.

---

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (C2 · marker + structure, not content)

Refuse a file that is not an Archie library (marker + structural check); keep render-core's per-item
tolerance INSIDE one that is. Full-content validation is rejected: it would refuse archives that open
fine today with one bad note, which contradicts the established 'corrupt != empty' policy.
closeReason:
DECIDED (C2: marker + structure, not content) — and the decided depth is ALREADY what ships. Verified in the code rather than assumed, since two other tickets tonight (fc75, 7eae) turned out stale the same way.

MARKER + STRUCTURE, exactly as decided — validateArchieMarker (publish/marker.ts):
- marker PRESENT: format must be 'archie-library', version must match SCHEMA_VERSION, AND exhibits.json must parse. The last one is the structural half, and its comment says why: 'the marker is cheap to forge; confirm the archive actually carries a parseable Gallery index'.
- marker ABSENT: accept iff collection.json OR exhibits.json parses — lenient-on-absent, so a pre-marker real export still opens (ADR-0020).
- neither: NotAnArchieLibraryError.
Sharpened today in d265282: the version mismatch now distinguishes malformed / newer / older instead of giving one piece of advice that was wrong in one direction.

NOT full content, exactly as decided — publish/open.ts composes ZipFilesystem.fromZip (its own zip-bomb caps, SRC_MAX_BYTES) with validateArchieMarker and nothing else. There is no schema pass over notes, objects or sections.

PER-ITEM TOLERANCE INSIDE, exactly as decided — spine/persist.ts AnnotationsCorruptError skips-and-reports a bad page rather than rejecting the whole log; publish/read.ts:135-143 degrades per layer and flips exhibit.incomplete instead of failing the tree.

So all three halves of the decision are in force. No code change needed. The Zod-gate comparison from freecut (docs/research/freecut-unverified-claims.md item 18) is answered: Archie deliberately does not do that, because full-content validation would refuse archives that open fine today with one bad note — which is the 'corrupt != empty' policy in .claude/rules/render-core-data-integrity.md.

Acceptance ('a decision record') met: the decision is on this ticket and the implementation is cited above.

title: Studio undo: gesture-scoped snapshots from freecut pattern

Note: product demand (whether to BUILD it) is the separate if — this ticket is the technical feasibility assessment only.

Source: Archie-5b06 Fog item 2.

title: Viewer UX audit
description:
## Notes - **Origin:** Archie-7aef (Studio UX overhaul, Archie-21b1) resolved as NO PARITY — the viewer was declared out of scope for that map and handed its own audit. Read 7aef's close reason first; it carries the corrections this map must not re-derive. - **Domain:** Archie's read-only surfaces. Parity has **four consumers**, and every decision here must say what each one gets: 1. `apps/viewer` — Astro + 23 Svelte islands. ONE shell, TWO auto-detected data modes (ADR-0008): hosted (baked published tree) and portable (an opened `.archie.zip`, seam in `published.ts`, ADR-0010). Hosted and portable are one consumer, not two. 2. `packages/archie-viewer` — the embeddable `` bundle. Its markup was **ported, not imported** (`element.ts:9-10`), so it drifts silently from the shell. 3. `packages/render-mount` — the framework-free mount seam; `read-overlay.ts` is the shared read-only overlay and has its own package gate. 4. the published static tree itself (ADR-0014 self-describing artifact). - **Governing ADRs — read before proposing anything:** 0008 (one shell, dual mode), 0010 (portable read seam), 0014 (self-describing artifact), 0019 (embeddable read-only viewer), 0021 (target contract: full cite ladder + degrade-upward). 0019 and 0021 bound what the viewer is ALLOWED to grow. - **The hard constraint:** ADR-0019 drops `@annotorious/openseadragon` + PixiJS from the embed and renders regions as a DOM-SVG overlay, while Studio keeps Annotorious. The embed and Studio can never match at the marker layer.
