An IntersectionObserver over the beats drives the camera (root = the scrolling column, rootMargin -50%/-50%, threshold 0); activating a beat scrolls the column and moves the camera. The observer watches the same box the activation scrolls, so the re-entry is real, and NO corpus system solves it: scrollama never scrolls at all (`grep scrollIntoView src/` is empty, it only reads scrollTop), quire's canvas-panel.js:259 calls goToFigureState (:68) and scrollToHash (:118) from inside an IO callback with no suppression but is structurally immune because its root is not what scrollToHash scrolls and an observer measures geometry RELATIVE TO ITS ROOT, and annomea/anvil have no scroll-coupled surface. The guard is ORIGINAL DESIGN and claims no precedent. Two review rounds, each finding the same class of error. (1) Ending the intent when the column went QUIET (last scroll + 150ms) was measured FULLY DEFEATED: every scroll re-armed the settle, so a zero-distance click plus continuous scrolling froze the highlight 1546ms while the reader passed 2760px and 15 sections; it was also load-sensitive, since one natural 160ms frame stall fires a 150ms timer mid-animation — which is why it flaked only under CPU contention. Replaced by ARRIVAL at a computed scrollTop, reached-OR-PASSED rather than equals because a dragged scrollbar steps ~58px and would straddle any tolerance window. (2) That fix then shipped the very defect the guard exists to prevent: pointerdown dropped the intent TOKEN but not the scroll MACHINE, so the animation ran on with the observer un-muted — TEN spurious section changes in ~300ms, each closing the open note and swapping the canvas object; wheel/touchstart had looked fine only because Chromium cancels a smooth scroll on a real gesture, so three paths were lucky rather than correct. Two claims were disproven, both originally stated in the author's favour: INTENT_MAX_MS was read only inside the observer callback, so it could not bound a wedge whose definition is that the callback stopped arriving (measured frozen 3500ms with no recovery), and ARRIVE_PX is load-bearing by two independent mechanisms (Chromium rounds scrollTo to whole pixels against a fractional getBoundingClientRect target — 20 of 21 beats land up to 0.48px short, stable DPR 1 to 2.4 — and the same constant gates the nothing-to-do branch in scrollToBeat), the suite being green at 0 was a coverage gap because every probe overshoots by hundreds of pixels. - [Hiding the narrative spine is per-exhibit and plainly reversible](Archie-c5cb) — V83 fixed, merged WITH 0d6c deliberately: once the spine is an input device, hiding it silently removes the interaction the mode is named for, so the two could not ship apart. The state is scoped by exhibit in `apps/viewer/src/aside-persistence.ts` rather than under one flat global key. Prior art BOUNDS the claim rather than supporting it — anvil's read/Sidebar.svelte and editor/Sidebar.svelte persist WIDTH only, flat global key, no collapse at all — so the corpus says nothing about persisting a hidden panel and the decision is stated as ours. V80 re-measured, since the earlier figures mixed two states: the canvas chrome clears the spine by 30px in BOTH (expanded chromeRight 840.41 vs spineLeft 870.41; collapsed chromeRight 1250 vs viewport 1280 with spineWidth 0). One injection on this ticket's own key came back GREEN and forced a better test — the first unscoped-key injection unscoped only the READ, not the write, so the global key was never written and the test passed against deliberately broken code. - [ADR-0019 gains a capability contract, and smoke enforces it](Archie-f90d) — one row per capability in ADR-0019 with a verdict, an obligation and the gate that holds it. Vocabulary and shape are annomea's (EMBED-AUDIT.md:21, :23-33), including DONE-differently, which is what the DOM-SVG overlay actually is and which a bare DROP would misreport. The diagnosis is annomea's too (:15): its Channel-3 Web Component evaporated because the audit was FILE-driven, so with no embed/ directory every embed file had zero counterpart and was invisible by construction — exactly how Archie lost nav, the note list, readings, the narrative and its visual language with every suite green. What is NOT annomea's, and the ADR says so: the GATE. annomea proposed a one-time audit and manual recovery order (:53-62); nothing in the corpus gates embed parity (clover-iiif documents an options table plus a named unsupported list, canvas-panel scopes by framing sentence, anvil ADR-0006 files follow-ups) — all documents. recipes/smoke.mjs asserts every MUST row against the BUILT bundle in real Chromium, 15 to 33 assertions at merge and 42 now, each comparing against an INDEPENDENT truth so a rendering of the WRONG data fails too. This ticket's own post-review fix then shipped the defect that produced two rules: five CONTRACTED_LABELS entries spliced into a record() argument list 135 lines away, silently covering 35 labels rather than 40 — all four AV labels missing, so the one capability with no coverage was still uncovered by the commit whose message said it was covered — found ONLY because a reported 41/41 did not reconcile with the completeness line's 35/35. Hence `post-review-fixes-are-unreviewed.md`, and the principle that a gate's reference must not be writable by the thing it gates (two instances here: bundle-size.json rewritten by a mandatory build, and CONTRACTED_LABELS lowered by moving its own entries). With the splice reproduced the completeness check PASSED at 40/40 while auditOwnSource FAILED — which is what proves the invariant load-bearing. - [Embed parity: object nav, note list, readings, narrative, shared tokens](Archie-c314) — all restored and gated in real Chromium against the built bundle; V55, found orphaned between Archie-9a81 and this ticket, folded in. The ADR-0019 constraint held and was not re-litigated: the embed drops @annotorious/openseadragon + PixiJS for a DOM-SVG overlay, so it and Studio can never match at the MARKER layer — only contracts (what is selectable, what a select does, what is keyboard-reachable) are held in common, never pixels. That is DONE-differently, not DROP. Verified on the merged tree: smoke PASS at 41/41 labels with bookkeeping intact, eager 38.9KB / total 274.9KB gz inside the ratchet allowance, and dist/ byte-identical to a fresh build after sync-dist. - [The seed corpus has no polygon region, so the path is never seen](Archie-f4fb) — SHIPPED `8683b02`. Polygon fixture + assertions in `fixture-reach.test.ts`. Its first assertion selected by `.find(… === "Polygon")` — whichever is first — so a fixture reorder would have retargeted it; now keyed on `objectId`, both sides sorted. The sibling in `seed-carry.test.ts` had the same shape and WAS flaky, 9-in-20 against a correct tree. Earned `.claude/rules/a-green-run-is-one-sample.md`. - [The seed has no local audio/video, so the AV surface has no offline gate](Archie-b135) — SHIPPED `8683b02` + gate `9a64974`. Local AV in the seed; `av-surface.spec.ts` can run offline. Its own red-green was found to be a NO-OP (a `box-sizing` assertion that could not fail) by the review at `ledgers/REVIEW-ux-fixture-slice-2026-07-26.md` — 17 injections, 15 red — and a prior-art citation was corrected in place. - [The sheet’s media-route modal guard is correct but unfalsifiable](Archie-0cc6) — SHIPPED `8683b02`. Fixture reaches the media route out of the sheet; guard pair in `note-surface.spec.ts`, third guard site added at review. Two of this slice’s new e2e tests were silently VACUOUS when written — a bare `Locator.count()` after `goto()` reads 0 against an unhydrated island — earning `.claude/rules/playwright-count-does-not-wait.md`. - **The canvas chrome docks** (`de08`/`c30a`/`9838`, merged `dfe7ab4`) — chrome sits beside the canvas, not over it. V49 fixed (`min-height: 100dvh` → `height` + `overflow: auto`; 720/720 at 8 viewports). Dismissing a note now reflows the canvas by the note row’s height, and that is a RULING, not an accident: option 3 (`preserveImageSizeOnResize`) was measured and made it worse, 17/20 → 9/20. Pinned by an assertion. ADR-0019’s corpus claim was narrowed to *structural chrome docks, instrument chrome floats* against a 7-system sweep (`ledgers/PRIORART-chrome-placement-2026-07-26.md`). - [A single-object exhibit drops its exhibit-level credit, licence and metadata](Archie-36e6) — FILED, not resolved. Spawned by `Archie-a5b1`; a IIIF MUST-display violation for the whole `single` layout and the narrative reader. Needs one placement decision in reader chrome, taken at the TOP of a slice. - [Studio and Viewer token files have already drifted — unify onto one floor](Archie-ecf4) — SHIPPED, wave 2. **There was no genuine divergence at all**: 100 tokens byte-identical in the same order, plus identical `*`/`body`/`.eyebrow` rules — one file and a stale copy, never two design systems. Studio consumes the floor with **no local layer** (its app-local properties are per-component *runtime* channels declared at their use sites). The ticket's measurement was stale (`--topbar-h` et al. retired by the dock) and missed the one that mattered: `.eyebrow` differed **by value**, studio `0.55` vs floor `0.70` — a contrast fix that reached the reader and never the author. Artifact: `#1a3c23b3` = 0.702 in the built CSS. **Strongest prior-art result is an absence** — nothing in the corpus documents at the token why a token is app-local, so that rule is original; tldraw is explicitly *not* a donor (build-time concatenation, not import-time sharing). - [The finder says what it found, not where it is](Archie-9eeb) — SHIPPED, wave 2. A hit now leads with **where it lives** — object label, plus section title in a narrative — built as a pure projection (`locateNotes`), with **no second address writer**: activation still routes through `ExhibitView`'s one `locus`. Took mirador's per-row shape (`SearchHit.jsx:120-125`) over clover's group headers (`ContentSearch.tsx:50-58`) on a real axis: clover's results arrive in *document order from the server*, ours are a MiniSearch **ranking**, so grouping would reorder by place instead of match quality. Two judgement calls chose an honest gap over a plausible answer — a section is named only when exactly one activates the object, and an unlabelled object yields no locus rather than a row reading `o17`. - [The finder's facet row starves the results list off-screen](Archie-8e73) — FOUND BY DRIVING IT, fixed same slice. On `screenshots`, **every finder result was off-screen and unclickable**: 132 tag chips → a 668px facet block in a 547px panel collapsed `.finder-results` to `clientHeight: 0`, first row at y=883 in a 720px viewport. Proven pre-existing. **A third detection family**: text, counts, *and Playwright's own `toBeVisible()`* all returned true — a non-empty box outside the viewport is still "visible" — while no mouse could reach it. Only the driven click caught it. - [The cite trigger occludes the first tag chip on the AV note card](Archie-d37d) — CLOSED AS **OBVIATED BY THE DOCK**, not fixed. The overlap did not go away, it **grew 62px → 78px** — it stopped mattering, because the card and the bar are now flow siblings. Confirmed by injection: re-floating `.cite-trigger` to its pre-dock box reproduces this ticket's exact symptom from geometry alone, which validates both the original measurement and the dock as its cure. - [V23 re-measured: two object-stepping affordances remain](Archie-d6e9) — CLOSED, **no fix**; the pairing is correct. Remainder unchanged post-dock. Corpus: universalviewer ships both by default, mirador makes the stepper unconditional and the strip opt-in, clover is the stated absence. **Nothing ships a strip *instead of* a stepper** — so the intuitive fix was the one arrangement no corpus system uses. - [The AV surface has no reading legend](Archie-4524) — SHIPPED, wave 2, fixture verified before the control was built. Two deliberate omissions: `styleOf` not taken (returns a `MarkerStyle`; this surface has no marker canvas), and **hide-all withheld** — gated on `onhiddenchange` so an unwired host gets an honest absence rather than a dead door. - **`Archie-7b86` NARROWED, not closed** — V49 confirmed closed by measurement (a spec marked `⚠ KNOWINGLY RED` is green), V53 landed via `4524`, V51/V29 already done. **V50 is the whole remainder and needs its own slice**: wavesurfer decodes the entire file without precomputed peaks and the seed is a 296s remote MP3 that streams today, so the fix is a publish-time bake in Studio/render-core — a different package and a different gate. - **`Archie-3e2d` FILED** — `element.test.ts` waits by draining a fixed count of event-loop turns (four sites at 8/20/20/60 — the spread is the tell). CI red on one branch, green on a sibling with the same base, 24/24 locally, and `rerun --failed` green on the identical commit. A false red trains everyone to re-run until green, which is the habit that hides the next real failure. ## Fog - **What each decision's implementation looks like.** Meta-planning: graduates into impl tickets as `Archie-52a9` / `d5cd` / `ed50` / `e902` close. Deliberately unwritten — the Studio map's pattern was decision-then-impl-ticket, and inventing the impl before the decision inverts it. - **Whether the Studio side needs the mirror of any of this.** `route.ts` and `marker-style.ts` are shared, so two of the four decisions can propagate INTO Studio — the reverse direction from the one `Archie-7aef` refused. That's a real question and it can't be phrased sharply until the decisions land. - **V54 — not one polygon region exists in the whole corpus**, so `SvgSelector` handling in BOTH overlays (Annotorious in the shell, DOM-SVG in the embed) is content-untested. ADR-0019 explicitly requires the embed overlay to reproduce *both* `xywh` Fragment AND `SvgSelector` polygon regions. This is a fixture / showroom gap, not a UX defect: the fix is authoring a polygon into the seed so the path is exercised at all. Belongs with whoever owns the showroom corpus (`ledgers/SHOWROOM.md`). - **V12 — arrival states nothing about what the collection is or who assembled it.** Recorded in the ledger as judgment rather than defect, and left here on purpose: the library-level description field may simply be unset in the seed, so it needs verifying against a library that sets one before anyone designs an orientation surface. If it turns out the field exists and is rendered, this patch dissolves. - **Whether the read surface's a11y subset folds into `Archie-eec7`** (screen-reader walk, open-backlog map) or eec7 narrows to Studio. Named in `Archie-c831`'s body as a resolution-time call; kept here so it isn't lost if that ticket is reshaped.

title: Audit vertical 1 — Arrival
description:
## Question

What does a first-time visitor meet in the first ten seconds, across every way of arriving, and where
does it fail them?

## Surfaces

`apps/viewer/src/pages/index.astro`, `ViewerShell.svelte` (427 lines — the shell that auto-detects its
data mode), `EmptyHall.svelte` (the portable drop screen), `Gallery.svelte`. On the embed side: `src=`
boot, the no-`src` local-drop screen, and `offline` (ADR-0019's attribute set, frozen by ADR-0021).

## Also in scope for this vertical specifically

- **Degrade-upward messaging.** ADR-0021 mandates that an unresolvable `target` degrades upward and
  NEVER errors — missing note → its exhibit, missing exhibit → the gallery. What the reader is TOLD
  when that happens is unspecified, and silent redirection is its own usability problem.
- **Failure states.** TEND-EXPLORE I-V2: a corrupt deployment surfaces to the reader as "check your
  connection" — a wrong diagnosis pointing at the wrong fixer.
- **The swap affordance.** ADR-0008's "Open another library" is shown in BOTH modes (2026-05-27 user
  override of the portable-only rule) so a single-exhibit collapse can't trap the reader.

## This ticket also establishes the apparatus for the other five

It is first because it is what the reader meets first — the conventions fall out of doing it, they are
not invented in the abstract. By closing, it must leave behind: the `archie-viewer-wireframes` board,
the roll-up index `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer.md` with the V-number ranges recorded, and the drive recipe
for all four consumers written down where the next five can follow it.

## Ledger

Findings file: `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-arrival.md`. Reserved finding numbers: **V1–V19**.

## Method (same for every vertical on this map)

Drive the RUNNING app in a real browser, then wireframe what the drive shows and judge it. Not
markup-reading: the four consumers drift silently (the embed's markup was PORTED, not imported —
`packages/archie-viewer/src/element.ts:9-10`), and only a drive catches that.

- **Consumers, all four, in this vertical's terms:** `apps/viewer` in BOTH data modes (hosted baked
  tree and portable dropped `.archie.zip` — ADR-0008's two auto-detected sources); the embed via the
  existing `recipes/*.html` driver pages (`recipes/smoke.mjs` shows the Chromium harness CI already
  uses); `packages/render-mount`'s read seam where this vertical touches it; the published static tree
  where it is this vertical's substrate.
- **Harness:** the `run-app` skill is the repo's verified launch path. Reuse it; don't rediscover the
  commands.
- **Judging standard — already ratified, do not re-litigate.** `docs/GOAL.md:11-13` defines the reader:
  *a first-time visitor opening a published Archie exhibit*. `:15-18` sets the evidence bar — there are
  no users, so success is an agent driving a real browser and producing NUMBERS ("heuristic-violation
  count fell 6 → 3"), never "I think it looks nicer". `:20-24` ranks Look > Feel > Performance >
  Features.
- **Finding shape:** mirror `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-studio-wireframes.md` — each finding names the SURFACE,
  the WEAKNESS, and the PRINCIPLE it strains, numbered, grouped by screen.
- **Output:** findings to `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-{slug}.md`, plus ONE line in the roll-up index
  `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer.md` linking it. Separate files so the five parallel verticals don't collide;
  the index is the only shared write. Wireframes go on the tldraw board `archie-viewer-wireframes`, one
  frame per vertical.
- **Do not re-derive:** `ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-viewer-2026-07-20.md` already holds evidence-backed
  findings (I-V1 route-set disagreement + sitemap 404s, I-V2 corrupt-deployment reads as "check your
  connection", I-V3 untested modal focus-trap) and two surplus directions. Cite and extend them.
- **Prior art is mandatory** (`Annotators/Image/CLAUDE.md`): cite it per finding. The read-side donors
  sit beside this repo — `annomea`, `anvil`, `quire`, `juncture`, `tropy`, `canvases-annotations-sharing`,
  `iiif-demo`. Use `fff`.
- **Gate after any edit:** `pnpm --filter @archie/viewer run check:svelte` (svelte-check
  `--fail-on-warnings`, baseline 0/0). `astro check` covers `.astro` pages ONLY and proves nothing about
  an island.
closeReason:
DONE. 12 findings (V1–V12) in ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-arrival.md; roll-up index + drive recipe + standing corrections in ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer.md; wireframes on tldraw board archie-viewer-wireframes (7 screens, 2 flows) at http://localhost:3002/?board=archie-viewer-wireframes.

All four consumers driven in real Chromium at 1280x800: apps/viewer hosted (V1–V7, V12), apps/viewer portable via setInputFiles of a real .archie.zip (V8; V1/V2 confirmed in both modes), the embed against the LOCAL dist/ build (V9, V10, V11). render-mount is not reachable at arrival — its surface is the object canvas, so it belongs to vertical 3.

HIGH-SEVERITY:
- V1 The empty hall is a one-way door. OPEN ANOTHER LIBRARY sits top-right (highest-value real estate, rarest need); clicking it from inside an exhibit replaces the app with the drop screen, whose ONLY app control — measured in light DOM with astro-dev-toolbar filtered — is "Open a library…". Escape inert, no cancel. ADR-0008 added this affordance to both modes so a single-exhibit collapse "can't trap the reader"; as built the mitigation IS the trap.
- V2 Browser Back restores the address but not the view: hash returns to #/{slug} while the hall stays on screen. Only a reload recovers (hall state is session-only, not persisted). Separate from V1 because the fix differs — V1 wants an exit control, V2 is a router not re-rendering on popstate.
- V3 Degrade-upward announces itself on 2 of 3 rungs. Object and note rungs show a dismissible notice; the SLUG rung is silent — follow a colleague's link to one exhibit, land on a gallery of six, told nothing. The notice component exists and works; one rung doesn't use it. Studio's ADR-0024 paired fallback WITH notice; the viewer took the fallback only.
- V9 The embed and the shell are visually unrelated products (green gradient + display face + warm-paper cards vs white + system-ui + orange + square). ADR-0019 sanctions divergence at the MARKER layer only; typography/palette/cards are not that. Cause is recorded in element.ts:9-10 — markup ported, not imported. GOAL.md ranks Look first.

MEDIUM: V4 dead address persists after degrading on 2 rungs but is rewritten on the third (opposite policies). V6 mode-dependent search shipped on the read side — EXHIBITS/ALL IMAGES silently changes the corpus, only the placeholder signals it; this is Studio's W7 verbatim, fixed in Studio by Archie-2308 (merged 2c47bdb) and never propagated — direct measured evidence for the thesis this map exists to test. V7 no cover fallback: the uncovered exhibit renders title-only AND sits first, top-left; Studio's LibraryHome does "explicit cover else first object's thumb via readThumbUrl" (Archie-2308 / SCALE-GALLERY-PLAN P3b). V8 shell chrome changes with data mode — portable loses the EXHIBITS/ALL IMAGES toggle, contradicting ADR-0008's one-shell contract. V11 embed gallery resolves no thumbnails at all from a zip source (distinct path from V7; ADR-0010's portable rewrite may not cover covers).

LOW: V5 "That note isn't here anymore" asserts deletion it cannot know (the object rung's wording is accurate for the same failure class). V12 arrival states nothing about what the collection is or who published it — recorded as judgment, not defect.

SURPLUS, and it matters: V10 — the embed's failed-src handling is BETTER than the shell's failed-target handling ("Couldn't open the library. The link may be broken or the file unavailable.", in place, beside the recovery control). The fix for V1 and V3 already exists in this repo; the fix tickets don't start from a blank page.

TWO OVERCLAIMS CAUGHT AND CLEARED (recorded so no vertical re-reports them):
- The "assets" card in the zip-sourced gallery is NOT an internal directory leaking into the reader's view. exhibits.json genuinely declares {"slug":"assets","title":"assets","order":0} with a 2-item manifest — the viewer faithfully renders what was published. What survives is V7, not a leak.
- "Report a Bug" / "Feedback" / "Inspect" / "Audit" are Astro's DEV TOOLBAR (hrefs point at withastro repos), not app chrome. They do not ship. Every vertical must filter e.closest('astro-dev-toolbar') from DOM queries or it will report dev-only affordances as shipped ones.

APPARATUS ESTABLISHED for the five now-unblocked verticals: the board; the index with its V-range table (append ONE row, nothing else — it is the only shared write); the four-consumer drive recipe, including the trap that recipes/*.html pin a jsDelivr CDN build (@v1.1) so driving them audits a release rather than the working tree — script the local dist/ instead; and the test library at Annotators/Image/archie-library.archie.zip.

No code was changed, so no gate was owed or run.

title: Audit vertical 2 — Browsing an exhibit
description:
## Question

Once inside an exhibit, how does a reader find their way among its objects — and does the structure
they're shown match the one the author built?

## Surfaces

`apps/viewer/src/pages/[slug].astro`, `ExhibitView.svelte` (643 lines — the largest island),
`ObjectGrid.svelte`, `Filmstrip.svelte`, `SidebarObjectNav.svelte`, `MediaThumbnail.svelte`.

## Known threads to pull

- **Object navigation has no keyboard model.** The viewer's `Filmstrip.svelte` is a plain `<ul>` of
  buttons with `aria-current`; Studio adopted APG grid + roving-tabindex under Archie-f260. Deliberate
  difference or gap? Judge it against `docs/research/a11y-interactions.md`, which is the repo's own
  ratified research on exactly this.
- **Two disagreeing enumerations of the exhibit route-set** (TEND-EXPLORE I-V1) — sitemap 404s, and
  third-party exhibits get no page at all. Where does that land on the reader?
- Three nav affordances coexist (grid, filmstrip, sidebar). Do they agree about where the reader is?

Findings file: `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-browse.md`. Reserved finding numbers: **V20–V39**.

- **Prior art is mandatory** (`Annotators/Image/CLAUDE.md`): cite it per finding. The read-side donors

closeReason:
12 findings (V20-V31) in ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-browse.md; index row + 3 board frames (v2-grid / v2-reader / v2-embed). All four consumers driven in real Chromium (hosted #/voynich 12 objects, portable archie-library.archie.zip, embed via recipes/try.html against local dist @ 2026-07-24 19:52, render-mount reached only as the embed canvas).

HIGH: V24 the viewer READS an object address it never WRITES - '#/voynich/o/o5' resolves to 'Object 5 of 12', yet browsing 12 objects leaves hash at '#/voynich' with history.length 2, Back EXITS the exhibit, reload returns to the overview; the whole viewer has exactly 2 hash writes (ViewerShell.svelte:79,156), both 'reset to #/'. title: Audit vertical 3 — Reading an object
description:
## Question

At the deep-zoom canvas — the product's centre of gravity — what does the reader see, what can they
reach, and how far do the shell and the embed diverge?

## Surfaces

`Reader.svelte` (536 lines), the deep-zoom canvas, `ReadingLegend.svelte`, `ReadingSheet.svelte`,
`MediaPlayer.svelte` (318 lines, AV). Overlay on BOTH sides: Annotorious/PixiJS in the shell vs the
DOM-SVG `packages/render-mount/src/read-overlay.ts` in the embed.

## This is where the drift lives

ADR-0019 drops Annotorious + PixiJS from the embed and rebuilds region rendering as a geometry-only
DOM-SVG overlay. The two CANNOT look identical, by design. The audit's job is to find where they differ
in ways that change what the reader can DO — hit-testing, `fitBounds`-on-select (the ADR-0006 nav
contract), marker labels, both `xywh` Fragment and `SvgSelector` polygon regions.

## Two corrections this ticket must not undo

- The marker's colour-only coding IS a real WCAG 1.4.1 gap
  (`docs/research/a11y-interactions.md:97-133`) — but it lives in SHARED code,
  `packages/render-core/src/query/marker-style.ts` `readingMarkerStyle`, called by both
  `apps/studio/src/App.svelte:1482` and `apps/viewer/src/components/ExhibitView.svelte:277`. Fixing it
  lands on both apps at once. It is not a viewer-parity question.
- `ReadingLegend`'s swatch+name pairing ALREADY satisfies 1.4.1 (`a11y-interactions.md:102-104`), and
  `:128-129` says explicitly: don't touch it.
- The embed overlay keyboard/AT dead end is CLOSED (Archie-9413, merged `4178a7b`) —
  `read-overlay.ts:184-191` sets `role`, `aria-label`, `tabindex="0"` and a keydown handler.

## AV

ADR-0021 requires `t=` to seek PAUSED at an offset and must not reuse the play-coupled `seekTo`.
Whether that reads correctly to a visitor is this vertical's call.

## Ledger

Findings file: `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-read-object.md`. Reserved finding numbers: **V40–V59**.

## Method (same for every vertical on this map)

Drive the RUNNING app in a real browser, then wireframe what the drive shows and judge it. Not
markup-reading: the four consumers drift silently (the embed's markup was PORTED, not imported —
`packages/archie-viewer/src/element.ts:9-10`), and only a drive catches that.

- **Consumers, all four, in this vertical's terms:** `apps/viewer` in BOTH data modes (hosted baked
  tree and portable dropped `.archie.zip` — ADR-0008's two auto-detected sources); the embed via the
  existing `recipes/*.html` driver pages (`recipes/smoke.mjs` shows the Chromium harness CI already
  uses); `packages/render-mount`'s read seam where this vertical touches it; the published static tree
  where it is this vertical's substrate.
- **Harness:** the `run-app` skill is the repo's verified launch path. Reuse it; don't rediscover the
  commands.
- **Judging standard — already ratified, do not re-litigate.** `docs/GOAL.md:11-13` defines the reader:
  *a first-time visitor opening a published Archie exhibit*. `:15-18` sets the evidence bar — there are
  no users, so success is an agent driving a real browser and producing NUMBERS ("heuristic-violation
  count fell 6 → 3"), never "I think it looks nicer". `:20-24` ranks Look > Feel > Performance >
  Features.
- **Finding shape:** mirror `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-studio-wireframes.md` — each finding names the SURFACE,
  the WEAKNESS, and the PRINCIPLE it strains, numbered, grouped by screen.
- **Output:** findings to `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-{slug}.md`, plus ONE line in the roll-up index

  the index is the only shared write. Wireframes go on the tldraw board `archie-viewer-wireframes`, one
  frame per vertical.

  findings (I-V1 route-set disagreement + sitemap 404s, I-V2 corrupt-deployment reads as "check your

NOT REACHED: the portable .archie.zip shell mode at the canvas (needs a zip with regions AND a narrative; neither available zip has both); viewport widths other than 1280x800/900 (V40/V48/V49 are geometry findings that will move, and a narrow pass would likely find more); the SvgSelector polygon path in either consumer (no content exists -- V54); the embed's deep-link fitBounds branch in isolation (source-verified only: onSelect shows the card and never moves the camera, so ADR-0006's select->camera contract is present in the shell and absent from the embed's only working selection path).

Audit only -- no app code changed, nothing committed. Wireframes on archie-viewer-wireframes as v3-reader-canvas / v3-reader-selected / v3-av-audio / v3-embed-canvas. Drive scripts and the embed host page deleted; the port-5199 static server killed.

title: Audit vertical 4 — The note

Vertical 5 (The narrative) audited across all four consumers; findings V80-V91 in ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-narrative.md, wireframes v5-* on board archie-viewer-wireframes. It isn't: the note never resolves at all (both the bare ULID and the percent-encoded full IRI produce 'That note isn't here anymore'), and the in-app search jump - same seam, same resolver - lands correctly on section 6 with the note open. The defect is the cite ladder's note rung and is handed to vertical 6 as V100. Also cleared: the collapsed-spine stepper (works well, per-direction labels, carries the reading across a step - the model the expanded spine should copy), the broken-reference guard, and the ADR-0016 index escape itself (the door exists; V84 is about state and address).

NOT REACHED: (a) the narrative in PORTABLE mode - archie-library.archie.zip holds only 'assets' and 'screenshots'; no narrative exists in any droppable fixture, so NarrativeReader cannot be exercised from a zip without new fixture data. (b) the spine's AV branch - none of voynich-reading's 6 sections points at the exhibit's sound object, and unlike the index-AV branch (guarded structurally by narrative-escape.test.ts) the spine-AV branch has neither test nor fixture. Both are fixture gaps, not drive gaps.

title: Audit vertical 6 — Leaving with something
description:
## Question

A reader found something worth keeping. Can they cite it, credit it, search back to it, or hand it to
someone else — and does the wider web see it at all?

## Surfaces

`CiteCard.svelte`, `ExhibitCiteCard.svelte`, `Credit.svelte`, `MetadataList.svelte`,
`MetadataRun.svelte`, `ProseCites.svelte`, `SearchOverlay.svelte`, plus the published tree's own
surfaces: `sitemap.xml.ts`, `robots.txt.ts`, and the deep-link `target` grammar.

## Anchors

- The cite-target ladder has five rungs (CONTEXT §244): Exhibit / Object / Note / sub-region `xywh` /
  Section. ADR-0021 freezes the address grammar as public API. `packages/render-core/src/url/route.ts`
  is the single definition and PREDATES `apps/studio/src/place.ts`, which mirrors it (`place.ts:27-31`).
- TEND-EXPLORE I-V1 is squarely this vertical: the sitemap and the route-set disagree, so some exhibits
  are unreachable to anything that isn't already inside the app.
- ADR-0014 (self-describing published artifact) and ADR-0022 (IIIF Content State interop) bound what
  leaving-with-something is allowed to mean.
- Metadata/rights display is the read half of the Dublin Core work (map Archie-c6bf) — cross-reference,
  don't fork.

## Overlap to declare, not resolve

`Archie-33bf` (Published-site deep links: should viewer URLs mirror Studio place grammar?) currently
lives on the Studio UX map and covers the URL-grammar decision. This vertical AUDITS what the reader
experiences; it must not pre-empt 33bf's decision. If the finding set argues 33bf should move under
this map, say so in the resolution.

## Ledger

Findings file: `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-leaving.md`. Reserved finding numbers: **V100–V119**.

## Method (same for every vertical on this map)

Drive the RUNNING app in a real browser, then wireframe what the drive shows and judge it. Not
markup-reading: the four consumers drift silently (the embed's markup was PORTED, not imported —
`packages/archie-viewer/src/element.ts:9-10`), and only a drive catches that.

- **Consumers, all four, in this vertical's terms:** `apps/viewer` in BOTH data modes (hosted baked
  tree and portable dropped `.archie.zip` — ADR-0008's two auto-detected sources); the embed via the
  existing `recipes/*.html` driver pages (`recipes/smoke.mjs` shows the Chromium harness CI already
  uses); `packages/render-mount`'s read seam where this vertical touches it; the published static tree
  where it is this vertical's substrate.
- **Harness:** the `run-app` skill is the repo's verified launch path. Reuse it; don't rediscover the
  commands.
- **Judging standard — already ratified, do not re-litigate.** `docs/GOAL.md:11-13` defines the reader:
  *a first-time visitor opening a published Archie exhibit*. `:15-18` sets the evidence bar — there are
  no users, so success is an agent driving a real browser and producing NUMBERS ("heuristic-violation
  count fell 6 → 3"), never "I think it looks nicer". `:20-24` ranks Look > Feel > Performance >
  Features.
- **Finding shape:** mirror `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-studio-wireframes.md` — each finding names the SURFACE,
  the WEAKNESS, and the PRINCIPLE it strains, numbered, grouped by screen.
- **Output:** findings to `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-{slug}.md`, plus ONE line in the roll-up index
  `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer.md` linking it. Separate files so the five parallel verticals don't collide;
  the index is the only shared write. Wireframes go on the tldraw board `archie-viewer-wireframes`, one
  frame per vertical.
- **Do not re-derive:** `ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-viewer-2026-07-20.md` already holds evidence-backed
  findings (I-V1 route-set disagreement + sitemap 404s, I-V2 corrupt-deployment reads as "check your
  connection", I-V3 untested modal focus-trap) and two surplus directions. Cite and extend them.
- **Prior art is mandatory** (`Annotators/Image/CLAUDE.md`): cite it per finding. The read-side donors
  sit beside this repo — `annomea`, `anvil`, `quire`, `juncture`, `tropy`, `canvases-annotations-sharing`,
  `iiif-demo`. Use `fff`.
- **Gate after any edit:** `pnpm --filter @archie/viewer run check:svelte` (svelte-check
  `--fail-on-warnings`, baseline 0/0). `astro check` covers `.astro` pages ONLY and proves nothing about
  an island.
closeReason:
Vertical 6 (Leaving with something) audited across all four consumers plus the published static tree; findings V100-V110 in ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-leaving.md, wireframes v6-* on board archie-viewer-wireframes. Drive 2026-07-24, real Chromium 1280x800 plus request-level probes of robots/sitemap/OG.

ANSWER TO THE QUESTION: no, mostly - and not because a capability is broken. The address grammar is built, parsed and frozen as public API; the rights and metadata components are built and correct; the archival tree is built and crawlable. What is missing is every CONNECTION between them and the reader.

THE LADDER, DRIVEN TWICE PER RUNG (hand-built URL, then trying to make the app produce it): exhibit resolves+produced; object resolves, never produced; note CANNOT BE EXPRESSED; region falls with the note rung; section resolves, never produced. Three of five resolve, ZERO of five are ever produced by the reading UI.

HIGH (5): V100 the note rung is unsatisfiable - every published note id is an absolute IRI with seven slashes and parseRoute splits the path on '/'; both candidate forms (bare ULID, percent-encoded IRI) return 'That note isn't here anymore', and the same id shape appears in the portable library, so it is universal to anything publish/site.ts writes. recipes/04-deep-link.html:62-75 already ships its note example COMMENTED OUT with the reason inline. V101 the address bar stops at the exhibit: opening an object, selecting a note, switching reading layer and deep-zooming all leave the hash at #/voynich - six reader states, two addresses. V102 there is nothing to copy it with: exhaustive grep for clipboard/navigator.share/copy across apps/viewer, packages/archie-viewer and packages/render-mount returns ZERO outside comments, while Studio has five; the open-note surface's full control set was enumerated by drive and contains no cite, no copy link, no permalink. Prior art quire ships MLA/Chicago CSL citations at page AND publication scope. V105 the embed displays no attribution, licence or metadata at all (credit:[] metadata:0 search:false in the shadow root at both gallery and object level) - the one consumer that renders on someone else's site, dropping a IIIF MUST-display value it has in hand. V107 the page robots.txt sends crawlers to ships 31 crawlable body characters (geo-map 45, sampler 25) because ExhibitView is client:only - correct and load-bearing, but six sections of prose, 22 notes and every object label are invisible to crawlers, reader-mode and archival ingestion. V110 the ADR-0014 archival page has no concept of a section (grep sections static-pages.ts = nothing): published/voynich-reading/index.html carries 13,491 body chars and zero of the six sections' prose, so the narrative exists in exactly ONE reachable place - the live shell's spine.

MEDIUM (4): V103 the licence ladder is inverted - object shows 'License: Public Domain Mark 1.0', the exhibit (the unit anyone would cite) shows Source only, the gallery has no credit line and no info button at all; measured in data, every manifest has requiredStatement and no rights, collection.json has neither. V104 metadata surfaces render 0/0/0 at all three levels; zero Dublin Core entries on any exhibit, any of 35 objects, or collection.json - 131 lines of MetadataList/MetadataRun have never been exercised against real published data (cross-ref Archie-c6bf, don't fork). V106 the finder returns text with no locus: across a 12-folio exhibit with four reading layers, no result names its folio, its layer or its section, and there is no result count. V108 every exhibit has two live web faces (/viewer/<slug>/ at 31 chars with NO rel=canonical, and /viewer/published/<slug>/index.html at 13,491 chars with rel=canonical pointing at itself) and neither points at the other. V109 the published tree's own sitemap lists 2 of its 7 exhibit index.html files - static-pages.ts:102-114 is correct; the cause is the repo's two seed sources writing one tree, which is I-V1's lesson recurring in the layer a curator self-hosts.

CLEARED AS OVERCLAIMS: (1) I-V1 itself is FIXED and I verified it rather than citing it forward - robots.txt to sitemap to all seven <loc>s return 200 including geo-map/; [slug].astro now enumerates ALL exhibit cards and its header documents the remaining sitemap split as the deliberate Archie-77b2 'unlisted' lever, so sampler's absence from the sitemap beside a live /viewer/sampler/ is that lever working. V109 is a DIFFERENT sitemap in a DIFFERENT tree; do not merge them. (2) robots.txt is correct (derives its Sitemap line from CANONICAL_BASE). (3) ProseCites/CiteCard/ExhibitCiteCard work - an author's archie: cite renders as a typed card and routes in-app to the right folio; citation in Archie is a thing authors do, never a thing readers do. (4) OG tags and JSON-LD are present, correct and guarded by a build-time HEAD probe against level-0 IIIF hosts - the healthiest part of this vertical.

NOT REACHED: metadata display under real Dublin Core data and a licensed exhibit/library (no such data exists in the corpus - fixture gaps, V103/V104); the region rung (composes on the note rung, so not separately reportable until V100 moves); the portable library's cite surfaces beyond id form (its test zip has two thin exhibits, but its note ids were inspected and match the hosted form, which was the finding that mattered).

ON Archie-33bf: it SHOULD move under this map. Its current framing would decide the URL grammar from Studio's place.ts with none of the read-side evidence. Two inputs it needs first: (a) V100 is a PUBLISH-STEP question, not a routing one - the note rung needs site.ts to emit a slash-free logicalId alongside the IRI, or the grammar needs a rung addressing what the tree actually contains; route.ts cannot be fixed alone. (b) V108 forces a canonicality choice between the app page and the archival page that 33bf's framing doesn't include and that ADR-0013/ADR-0014 together imply but don't settle. If the map owners keep it where it is, it should at minimum take V100/V101/V108 as its primary evidence.
