- **V64** — the expanded sheet carries LESS context than the card it came from, so "expand to read"
  loses information at the exact moment the reader asked for more.
- **V65** — the note card grows a stepper that steps something other than notes, and only in a state
  the reader must first discover.
- **V23** — the four nav affordances agree about where you are and disagree about what you are
  looking at.

## Why this is a decision, not a fix

Each finding alone reads as a bug. Together they say the note has no single home: the card, the
sheet, the canvas mark and the rail each hold a partial copy with different content and different
controls. You cannot dedupe without first saying which surface is canonical and what the others are
FOR — and V64 proves the current answer is inconsistent, since the "more" surface carries less.

## Now unblocked

Archie-ed50 settled the canvas half: the selected mark is a contrasting halo, so the CANVAS now has
a real answer to "which one" that it did not have before. That removes one reason a text surface had
to duplicate the identifying context — which is exactly the pressure that produced the triplication.

## Constraints

- The standalone note card is ONE shared component (`NotePopup.svelte`) used by Reader (grid /
  steps-objects) and NarrativeReader (narrative / steps-sections). A decision that splits its
  behaviour by mode splits that component — say so explicitly if that is the answer.
- V65's stepper is the concrete instance of the general question: a control that appears in one
  state and acts on a different noun than its container.

## Follow-on tickets (filed)

- Archie-dbbc — One note surface: NotePopup is the note, the sheet is it at a larger size (V60, V64)
- Archie-01a6 — Object/section nav belongs in the canvas chrome, not inside a note card (V65; reduces V23)
closeReason:
DECIDED: the note has ONE home, and the sheet is that home at a larger size.

THE MODEL — three surfaces, three distinct jobs, no duplicated content:
1. Sidebar list = INDEX. It locates and identifies (truncated preview, reading colour, tags, position). It is never a reading of the note. When its note is open it marks position; it does not restate the text.
2. NotePopup = THE NOTE. Full text, identity eyebrow, media, tags, actions. This is the canonical content renderer, and the ONLY one.
3. ReadingSheet = the SAME NotePopup at a larger size. It becomes a shell (scrim + focus-trapped dialog) that renders NotePopup inside it, with size='sheet'. It is not a second content surface.
4. Canvas mark = WHICH ONE (settled by Archie-ed50/52a0, the halo). This is what removed the pressure that produced the triplication: no text surface has to carry identifying context to answer 'which one' any more.

WHY THIS SHAPE:
- V64 (the sheet carries LESS than the card it came from) dies BY CONSTRUCTION, not by patching. One content renderer cannot have two different headers. Any future field added to the note card is in the sheet the same day.
- V60's count goes 2→2 on select and 3→2 on expand: index + note, in both states. The sheet does not add a copy; it resizes the one that exists.
- The NotePopup-is-shared constraint is SATISFIED, not split: Reader and NarrativeReader keep the same component, and so does the sheet. The mode difference stays where it already is — the eyebrow's content (object vs section·object) — which is data, not behaviour.

PRIOR ART (cited, decisive): annomea's NarrativePane (ADR-0021) is ONE pane at mini/half/full — a reader-controlled size slider, not three surfaces. Its ADR-0007 is explicit that the popup IS the note surface, popup OR drawer, one at a time. Archie had drifted to 'popup AND drawer AND list'. quire's expanded views leading with the work's identity is the V64 half.

V65 — DECIDED SEPARATELY: the stepper leaves the note card. It steps objects (Reader) or sections (NarrativeReader), never notes, so it does not belong inside a note. It only migrated there because collapsing the aside took the real object nav away with it. Object/section nav moves to the CANVAS CHROME, visible in BOTH sidebar states, with its noun spoken visibly ('Object 2 of 12' — matching what SidebarObjectNav already reads aloud). This fixes both halves of V65: the label AND the discoverability. NotePopup loses its 'step' prop entirely.

Follow-on: Archie-<impl> (one note surface) and Archie-<nav> (object/section nav to the canvas chrome). V23 (four nav affordances disagree about what you're looking at) is materially reduced by the nav move and should be re-measured after, not fixed blind.

title: The embed resolves tree-relative asset refs against the host page (V11)
description:
## Question

Measured 2026-07-25 while fixing Archie-64ef, in a real drive of `recipes/try.html`:

```
HTTP 404 http://127.0.0.1:PORT/recipes/screenshots/assets/o1-e1-embed.png
```

The library base is `/apps/viewer/public/published/`, and the asset ref in the tree is the
tree-relative `screenshots/assets/o1-e1-embed.png`. The embed resolved it against the HOST
PAGE's directory (`/recipes/`) instead of the library base, so it 404s.

## Why this matters more in the embed than in the app

This is the portable twin of **V7**, which `Archie-a897` fixed on the gallery side with
`publishedAssetUrl` (apps/viewer/src/published.ts) — the audit flagged it as "plausibly the
portable twin" and it is now measured rather than suspected.

But the embed's exposure is strictly worse: `<archie-viewer src="...">` is loaded from an
ARBITRARY host page at an arbitrary path, so the host's directory is never the library base.
In the app the two happened to coincide often enough to hide the bug.

## Shape of the fix

Resolve asset refs against the library base the loader already holds, not against
`document.baseURI`. `publishedAssetUrl`'s rule is the right one (absolute / protocol-relative /
root-anchored pass through; anything else anchors to the base) — check whether it can be shared
from `@render/core` rather than reimplemented, since a second copy is exactly how V7 and V11
drifted apart in the first place.

## Verify

`recipes/smoke.mjs` — assert ZERO 404s on asset requests during the gallery + object-open
drive. The 404 above was visible in that exact flow and nothing was watching for it.
closeReason:
Merged 6feebdd. Reproduced exactly as filed: `404 /recipes/screenshots/assets/o1-e1-embed.png`.

FIX: the rule moved to @render/core as `assetUrlAgainst(base, ref)`, and apps/viewer's `publishedAssetUrl` is now a thin binding of it to the app's base rather than a parallel implementation. The ticket asked whether it could be shared instead of reimplemented — it can, and a second copy is exactly how V7 and V11 drifted apart. One definition, two bases.

Applied at the READ boundary (openLibraryFromTree's openExhibit), mirroring the ZIP path's blob rewrite in loadPortableExhibit (ADR-0010) — same seam, same moment, different destination. One place to be right, and no way for a future consumer of `object.source` to forget. Covers: object source, thumbnail, a baked DZI's filesPath (which would 404 every TILE, and only at deep zoom — worse than the reported symptom), and the gallery covers.

Note bodies deliberately left alone: the app rewrites those for a DIFFERENT problem (absolute canonical BASE → serving origin), and a blind rewrite of note markup here would be a second, unmeasured behaviour riding on a bug fix.

GATE, and it caught me first. recipes/smoke.mjs now fails on any same-origin 404 during the drive. My first version asserted MID-drive and passed against the unfixed code — covers are `loading="lazy"`, so the request that exposes V11 had not been made yet. Verified by a standalone probe that the 404 was real the whole time. Moved to the end of the drive it goes red with the exact V11 signature and green with the fix. That red-green mattered more than usual here: a missing image degrades to a blank box and never reaches the console, which is why nothing was watching.

NOTE FOR THE PARITY TICKETS (Archie-c314): while measuring this I found the embed also has NO equivalent of the app's `toServingOrigin` rebase — published object sources are baked as ABSOLUTE canonical URLs (https://micahchoo.github.io/...), so a locally-served or re-hosted tree loads its images from the canonical host rather than from where it is actually served. Out of scope here (V11 is the tree-relative half), real, and worth folding into the embed-parity work.

Gates: render-core 1159, archie-viewer 138, viewer 149, studio 925, render-mount 207, e2e 44, smoke 11/11, svelte-check 1507 0/0, bundle +0KB eager.

title: The rights and metadata surfaces render nothing on the read side (V103/V104)
description:
## Question

Two findings deferred INTO this map by the Viewer UX audit (Archie-c405, 2026-07-25), because this
map owns read-side rights and metadata display. They were named at resolution but never filed —
this ticket closes that gap.

- **V103 — the license ladder is inverted.** The object is licensed, the exhibit is not, and the
  library has nothing at all. Rights should get MORE general as you go up, not vanish: a reader
  arriving at the library sees no licensing, then finds it only by opening a specific object.
- **V104 — the Dublin Core metadata surfaces render nothing, anywhere in the corpus.** Not "render
  wrong" — render nothing, across every exhibit. Determine first whether this is a SEED gap (no
  exhibit sets the fields) or a RENDER gap (the fields are set and the surface drops them). The two
  have opposite fixes and the audit did not separate them.

## Why here and not on the viewer map

`Archie-c6bf` owns Dublin Core metadata end to end, including the `RightsFields` write-back
contract (`.claude/rules/metadata-rights-keyed-writebacks.md`). Fixing display on the viewer map
would have split that ownership.

## Do V104's triage first

It gates V103's framing: if no seed exhibit carries metadata, then "renders nothing" is a showroom
problem and belongs with `ledgers/SHOWROOM.md`, and the render path is untested rather than broken.
Check `apps/viewer/fixtures/sample-data.ts` (voynichExhibitMetadata is referenced there) against
what `MetadataRun.svelte` actually receives.

## Related

`Archie-aafd` decides whether the read boundary REJECTS excluded dcterms properties or displays
them — that decision changes what V104's surface is supposed to show, so land aafd first if the
triage says the render path is at fault.
closeReason:
SHIPPED — merged to main at ead0ad7. Full separation evidence: ledgers/FIX-a5b1-rights-metadata-2026-07-26.md.

THE TICKET'S PREMISE WAS HALF WRONG, and the correction is the point. V104's 'renders nothing, anywhere' is FALSE for the SPA — driven against the built viewer, the voynich grid header renders 3 exhibit rows and the reader's Details tab renders 9 object rows. It is TRUE for the archival published page, which is the surface the originating audit (Archie-c405) was actually looking at: grep -n metadata static-pages.ts returned zero hits. Anyone re-reading V104 should look at the published tree, not the app.

V104 also had a real seed half: 4 of 7 exhibits carried no metadata at any level.

V103 fired on BOTH halves at once. Seed: no exhibit and no library set rights anywhere in the corpus, and three exhibits lifted only the credit half of a rights object while dropping the licence. Render: even where rights was set, the archival page emitted it only into JSON-LD.

FIX: one rightsHtml block in packages/render-core/src/publish/static-pages.ts used at all three levels, carrying credit, the licence as visible rel=license text, and the metadataRows projection as a dl.

ARTIFACT MEASUREMENT (counted independently on both sides, not taken from the report) across the 8 published pages:
  dl class="meta"   0 -> 26
  <dt> rows          0 -> 216
  rel="license"      0 -> 40

Three levels left DELIBERATELY unlicensed with the reason stated: their contents carry two or three licences and a blanket claim would be false.

Gates: render-core 1202, viewer e2e 138/138, smoke 42/42 + 41/41 labels, eagerGzKB delta +0KB with the baseline unmoved. Eight new assertions red-greened across 7 injections; 20/20 repeat runs.

LEFT ALONE, PINNED BY A TEST: six seed licence URIs resolve to no human label — a vocabulary gap in Studio's approved-URI picker. Nine others were a one-character https:/http: mismatch and are fixed.

SPAWNED: the single-object-exhibit IIIF MUST-display violation, filed separately.

title: One note surface: NotePopup is the note, the sheet is it at a larger size
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-c982's decision. Covers V60, V64.

## The work

1. **NotePopup gains `size: "card" | "sheet"`** (default `"card"`). Sheet size = wider measure,
   larger type, no anchoring to the mark. SAME markup, same header, same media/tags/actions.

2. **ReadingSheet becomes a SHELL, not a content surface.** It keeps what it uniquely owns — the
   scrim, `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`, and `use:dialog` (the focus trap V63 installed; do NOT
   regress it) — and renders `<NotePopup size="sheet" ... />` inside. It stops rendering `text`
   itself. Its `aria-label` comes from the same eyebrow NotePopup already builds, so the sheet
   finally says what you are reading (V64).

3. **The sidebar card stops restating the note while it is open.** It is the INDEX: preview, reading
   colour, tags, position. Selected state marks position — it must not read as a second copy of the
   text. (Judgement call on exactly how it de-emphasises; the constraint is that a reader never sees
   the same sentence twice in two type treatments 900px apart, which is what V60 measured.)

4. **Only ONE note-content element on screen at a time.** With the sheet open the floating card must
   not remain behind the scrim — measured, `.note-pop` is still in the DOM and legible there today,
   which is V60's third copy. Either the popup renders INTO the sheet, or it hides while the sheet
   is open. Assert whichever you choose.

## Constraints

- `NotePopup.svelte` is shared by Reader (grid / steps-objects) and NarrativeReader (narrative /
  steps-sections). This decision deliberately does NOT split it — the mode difference stays in the
  eyebrow's CONTENT (object vs section·object), which is data. Keep it that way.
- The `step` prop is being removed by the sibling nav ticket. Coordinate: do not build sheet support
  for a control that is leaving.

## Verify

- `apps/viewer/e2e/note.spec.ts` already guards V61/V62/V63 — those must stay green (especially the
  focus trap; the sheet is still a real dialog).
- Add: with the sheet open, exactly ONE element renders the note's body text.
- Add: the sheet's header carries the same identity string as the card it came from (V64) — assert
  they are EQUAL, not merely both non-empty, or the class comes back.

## Prior art

annomea `NarrativePane` (ADR-0021): one pane at mini/half/full, reader-controlled — not three
surfaces. ADR-0007: popup OR drawer, one at a time. quire: expanded views lead with identity.
---

## Resolution (2026-07-26) — merged `273bea7`

**The defect was real and worse than "styling".** Expanding a note and then clicking a tag chip put
**two `aria-modal="true"` dialogs on screen at once** (the reading sheet plus the finder). The old
sheet also took only `text`, so a note's media and tags *vanished* on expand — the larger size was
strictly lossier than the card it replaced.

**The rule the three separate judgements collapse to**, which is what makes this one decision rather
than three:

> A card affordance is withheld at sheet size **only when it is meaningless there** (the expand glyph
> offers to expand what is already expanded). Everything meaningful at any size is **kept**, and
> anything modal it opens **replaces** the sheet rather than stacking on it.

So: media and tags are carried into the sheet; the expand glyph is not; `onopenfinder` and `onmedia`
both clear `readingSheet` in both readers.

The hide mechanism is `display: contents` → `display: none` on `.note-slot`, so the card is not
unmounted while the sheet is up — state survives the round trip.

`NotePopup.svelte` remains the ONE shared standalone note card (Reader grid/steps-objects and
NarrativeReader narrative/steps-sections both use it), so this fix reached every surface at once.

### Gates
svelte-check 1518 files 0/0 · typecheck 7/7 · vitest 176 · **e2e 85 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped**.

The skipped count going to zero matters: two of this slice's *own* new tests were silently vacuous
via `Locator.count()` after `goto` (one skipped on `n < 2`, one reported "no AV object in the
sampler") — **both while the fixture was perfectly fine**. Filed as
`.claude/rules/playwright-count-does-not-wait.md`.

### Follow-up filed
- **Archie-0cc6** — the `onmedia` half of the guard is correct, **unfalsifiable, and on a route no
  fixture can reach**: reverting `readingSheet = false` from `onmedia` in both readers leaves 18/18
  passing, because no fixture note is both expandable and media-bearing (a note needs `text` to show
  the expand glyph at all). The guard is right; the fixture is thin. Do not close that one by
  deleting the guard.
closeReason: Merged 273bea7 — the sheet keeps every meaningful affordance and modals replace it rather than stacking. Follow-up Archie-0cc6 filed for the unfalsifiable media route.

title: Object/section nav belongs in the canvas chrome, not inside a note card
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-c982's second decision. Covers V65; materially reduces V23.

## The work

1. **Remove the `step` prop from `NotePopup.svelte`** (`:58-74`) and its two wirings
   (`Reader.svelte:413`, `NarrativeReader.svelte:350`). A note card carries the note. It must not
   carry a control that acts on a different noun.

2. **Put object/section nav in the CANVAS CHROME, visible in BOTH sidebar states.** Today the aside
   holds `SidebarObjectNav` and the stepper only appears when the aside is COLLAPSED — a primary nav
   affordance that exists only in a state most visitors never enter. That is the discoverability half
   of V65 and it is the more serious half.

3. **Speak the noun VISIBLY.** `‹ Object 2 of 12 ›`, not `‹ Prev 1 / 12 Next ›`. The aria side is
   already honest (`SidebarObjectNav` reads "Object 2 of 12"); the visible text should match it.
   In the narrative the same control says `Section 3 of 6`. Route the wording through `product-copy`.

## Why this is the fix and not the label alone

The stepper migrated into the note card because collapsing the aside took the real nav with it. Fix
the cause — nav that lives where the thing it navigates lives — and the symptom has nowhere to
reappear. Relabelling alone leaves a primary affordance hidden behind a state toggle.

## Watch

- `V80`/`Archie-40fe` is the floating-chrome occlusion ticket. Adding chrome to the canvas is
  adding to exactly the surface 40fe is about — coordinate, or the nav lands on top of the scale cue.
  Doing 40fe FIRST is defensible if its reservation model is what this should slot into.
- `V23` says the four nav affordances agree about WHERE you are and disagree about WHAT you are
  looking at. This ticket changes one of the four. RE-MEASURE V23 after, do not fix it blind.

## Verify

Drive both modes with the sidebar OPEN and COLLAPSED — four states. The nav must be present and
correct in all four, and the note card must carry no stepper in any of them.
---

## Resolution (2026-07-26) — merged `273bea7`

Object nav now lives in the canvas chrome. The reasoning that settled it is **structural, not
aesthetic**, and worth keeping because it also explains a side effect nobody asked for.

`stepIntoReading` existed **because the stepper lived inside the note card**. Stepping had to keep a
note selected or the card would unmount — pulling the button out from under the reader's cursor
mid-gesture. The carry was never a reading feature; it was the machinery keeping the control mounted
while it was being used. Moving nav to the canvas chrome, where it neither moves nor unmounts,
dissolved the justification along with the structure that needed it.

**`MediaPlayer.svelte` deliberately keeps the sidebar stepper** — an AV object has no canvas chrome
to move object nav to. It is byte-identical to base (`8a7a8344`), because `MediaPlayer.svelte:54`
already computed the identical opt-in condition and `ExhibitView.svelte:575-578` already fed all four
props. The opt-in gate is at `SidebarObjectNav.svelte:32`. That "no change needed" is pinned by a
wiring test rather than left to look like an oversight.

### One measurement error worth recording, because it nearly shipped a false gate

The coordinator asked for a landmark assertion on the opted-out path. As specified it was **green
before the fix**: two different `<nav>`s carry the identical accessible name `"Objects in this
exhibit"` (this component's old root, and the canvas-chrome stepper via `navRegionName("object")`),
so `getByRole('navigation', {name: 'Objects in this exhibit'})` could never fail. Measured: image
path 1 → GREEN, AV path 1 → GREEN. The container-scoped form
(`Back-to-Exhibit.closest('nav')`) goes **null → RED** on both. The landmark was never actually
lost — the name migrated with the control.

### Gates
svelte-check 1518 files 0/0 · typecheck 7/7 · vitest 176 · e2e 85 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped.

### Follow-ups filed
- **Archie-5185** — flip-and-read disappeared as a consequence of removing `stepIntoReading`, and
  **neither this ticket nor Archie-dbbc asked for that.** Recorded as a decision rather than a side
  effect. The argument above is structural; whether a reader working through a sequence of annotated
  objects *wants* the note to follow them is a reading question, and only the first has been
  answered. `object-nav.spec.ts` pins the current behaviour explicitly, with a comment naming it as
  the test to invert if the project restores the carry.
- **Archie-d6e9** — V23 re-measured: two object-stepping affordances remain, named.
closeReason: Merged 273bea7 — object nav moved to the canvas chrome; MediaPlayer keeps the sidebar stepper by design. Follow-ups Archie-5185 (flip-and-read decision) and Archie-d6e9 filed.

title: The note rung resolves: match by logicalId, not by full IRI
description:
## Question

Fix V100. The cite ladder's note rung has NEVER resolved — but the grammar is fine and must not change.

## The actual defect

`route.ts` parses `#/<slug>/a/<id>` into one path segment. Published note ids are
`{baseUrl}{slug}/annotations/{ULID}/v{n}` (site.ts:510 `citeBase`). `note-arrival.ts:29,33`
compares that single segment to the WHOLE IRI with `===`. Nothing can satisfy it.

`buildNoteDeepLink(logicalId)` (deeplink.ts:76) already builds `#/a/<logicalId>`, and `brand.ts`
already owns the split (`mintLogicalId`, `versionId`, `parseVersionId`, `VERSION_ID_RE`). The
intended design was always "the URL carries the ULID". Only the comparison is wrong.

## The work

1. **A pure helper in `@render/core`** — `logicalIdOf(publishedAnnotationId): LogicalId | null`.
   Reuse `brand.ts`'s `VERSION_ID_RE` against the IRI tail; do NOT hand-roll a second regex, and do
   NOT split on "/" and take `[-2]` (a base path containing `/annotations/` would break it silently).
   Returns null for anything that is not `{...}/annotations/{ULID}/v{n}`.

2. **`resolveNoteArrival` matches on logicalId.** Accept EITHER form for the incoming id (a bare
   ULID from the address bar, or a full IRI from an internal caller) by normalising both sides
   through the helper.

3. **Audit every other `a.id === ` comparison** against a URL-supplied id. `resolveNoteArrival` is
   the one the audit measured; grep for siblings (`narrative-landing.ts` `ownerObjectOf`,
   `arrivalSectionIndex`, the search-jump path) before calling this done.

## Verify

- **Drive a REAL published id end to end**: take a ULID out of
  `apps/viewer/public/published/voynich/manifest.json`, visit `#/voynich/a/<ULID>`, assert the note
  opens and the camera fits it. The audit drove five spellings and all five degraded; this must be
  the sixth that does not.
- A tombstoned/unknown id must STILL degrade honestly (ADR-0003) — do not turn a miss into a throw.
- e2e, not a unit test alone: the bug lived in the seam between a parser and a comparison, and both
  halves were individually correct.
closeReason:
Done — merged as 4e21416 (commit ed40a42).

`logicalIdOf` lives in `brand.ts` (which already owned the split) and normalises BOTH
sides. The `{ULID}/v{n}` pattern now has ONE source, composed from `ULID_RE`; the IRI
matcher is anchored on `/annotations/` AND on end-of-string, so a deploy path containing
`/annotations/` cannot shift the match — the silent failure the forbidden
`split("/").at(-2)` would have had. Version-agnostic by construction, which is what
ADR-0003 needs: a cite minted at v1 still names the note at v9.

THE AUDIT (step 3) FOUND TWO MORE SHIPPING HALVES — this ticket was bigger than one
comparison:

1. `narrative-landing.ts` `ownerObjectOf` carried the identical raw-`===` defect, so it
   always returned null and `arrivalSectionIndex` fell back to section 0. Every
   deep-linked note in a narrative exhibit landed at the TOP of the spine instead of its
   own beat — a plausible-looking wrong answer, which is why nobody caught it.
2. `ExhibitView` set `arrivedNote = targetNote` (the raw URL segment), which feeds
   Reader's `initialSelected` and is matched against `annotation.id`. That re-opened the
   same gap one layer down: the object would open and the note still never select.
   `resolveNoteArrival` now returns the note's PUBLISHED id and callers carry that —
   hence the new `noteId` field on `NoteArrival`.

WHY THE OLD TESTS WERE GREEN, which is the part worth remembering: both fixtures used the
same synthetic string (`"n-base"`) for the queried id AND the annotation id. With both
sides identical, raw `===` passes — the suite was structurally incapable of modelling the
bug. Rewritten to the real shapes (published IRI in the data, bare ULID in the query).

VERIFIED with a REAL published id, read out of the committed manifest AT RUNTIME rather
than hard-coded — a literal would rot on the next regen and then assert the degrade path
while looking like the happy one. Drives `screenshots`: the one seed exhibit with local
images (so it runs in the hermetic offline suite), and whose notes live only on READING
pages, so arrival must flip the reading on rather than merely find the object.

Red-green proven: both happy-path e2e tests fail against the restored raw `===`; the two
degrade tests pass either way, correctly.

Gates: 2605 unit (+34), 48 e2e (+4), smoke 15/15, svelte-check 0/0, TS7 clean.

title: The address bar writes every rung the grammar already reads
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-d5cd's address decision. Covers V101, V24, V84, V52.

## The work

`route.ts` parses `/o/`, `/a/`, `/s/`, `?xywh` and `?t`; the viewer honours all of them on arrival
and writes NONE. Make the address track the DEEPEST rung currently open:

| reader state | address |
| --- | --- |
| exhibit | `#/<slug>` |
| object open | `#/<slug>/o/<objectId>` |
| note open | `#/<slug>/a/<logicalId>` |
| section active | `#/<slug>/s/<sectionId>` |
| note + region / offset | `…?xywh=…` / `…?t=…` |

- **`replaceState`, not `pushState`.** Selecting notes must not fill the back stack — Escape and the
  browser Back button both already mean "up a level", and a per-selection history entry would make
  Back mean "the previous note" instead. (If a case for pushState appears, it is arrival, not
  selection.)
- **Use `routeToHash`** (route.ts) — the inverse already exists. Do not hand-build strings.
- **Depends on Archie-67b6**: writing `#/<slug>/a/<ULID>` is only honest once that address resolves.

## What this unblocks, and why they are the same ticket

- **V84** — the narrative section index has no address, so stepping out and back loses your place.
  Writing `/s/<id>` fixes it with the rung that already exists.
- **V52** — ADR-0021's `t=` landing seek (seek PAUSED at an offset, deliberately not the play-coupled
  `seekTo`) is correctly built and structurally UNREACHABLE: no address ever carried `t=`. Working
  code, no way in. Writing the param is the whole fix.
- **V106** — the finder returns text with no address or locus. Once every result HAS an address, the
  finder can show one.

## Verify

`apps/viewer/e2e`. Assert the round trip, which is the property that matters: drive to a state, read
`location.hash`, reload, and assert the SAME state. A test that only checks the string is written
would pass against an address nothing can parse — which is exactly how V100 survived.
closeReason:
Done — merged as c903371 (commit 110cc53).

ONE writer, in ExhibitView, fed by an `onlocus` seam the three reader islands report
through (Reader, NarrativeReader, MediaPlayer). The islands stay ignorant of the address
grammar — they report the raw note id, the active section, the region, the cue offset —
and ExhibitView alone decides precedence and builds the string via `routeToHash`. A second
writer is how the writer and the parser drift apart.

Precedence is the ladder's own, with one refinement the ticket's table didn't cover: an
object opened from the NARRATIVE INDEX (ADR-0016's escape-out) is deeper than the section
behind it, so it takes the rung. Otherwise the section is the narrative's rung — an object
id would be the wrong grain there, since the spine may revisit one object across several
sections.

`replaceState`, never `pushState`, as decided.

V52 detail: the AV rung reports the CUE'S START, not `currentTime`. A link must land at the
beginning of the moment it names, and a per-frame value would rewrite the bar continuously
while citing an arbitrary instant. Fires on cue boundaries.

One interaction worth recording: the writer YIELDS to V4's honest-degrade path. While the
arrival chrome is explaining that a cited target was missing, `normalizeAddressToExhibit`
owns the bar; re-asserting a locus would race it and could restore the dead address the
reader was just rescued from.

VERIFIED as the round trip, not the string — drive, read `location.hash`, RELOAD, assert
the same state. Red-green: 4 of 5 fail with the writer disabled. The fifth (Back doesn't
walk notes) passes either way by construction; it guards a future `pushState` regression
rather than today's bug, and its comment says so rather than implying broader coverage.

Gates: 2605 unit, 53 e2e (+5), smoke 15/15, svelte-check 0/0, TS7 clean.

UNBLOCKED, as the ticket predicted: V106 (the finder can now show each result's address)
and Archie-3ea1's link grain, which must READ `location.hash` rather than re-derive it.

title: Cite panel: link, formatted citation, and IIIF Content State at equal weight
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-d5cd's taking-away decision. Covers V102 (the audit's headline finding), V106.

There is currently NO clipboard or share affordance anywhere in the read surface. For a tool whose
purpose is citable annotation, that is the finding the whole audit points at.

## The work

A **cite panel** offering three grains SIDE BY SIDE — not a menu behind a default, because the three
serve different readers and hiding two answers only the easiest case:

1. **Link** — the address for the current rung. Comes free once Archie-99b1 writes it; this panel
   must READ that address, never re-derive it, or the two drift and one of them is wrong.
2. **Citation** — a formatted, copyable reference. Prior art donor: `quire`
   (`packages/11ty/_includes/components/citation/`) builds CSL-JSON and renders MLA/Chicago. Read it
   before designing the fields; the exhibit already carries `requiredStatement` + Dublin Core
   `metadata` (Archie-c6bf), which is most of what CSL needs.
3. **IIIF Content State** — `encodeContentState` / `decodeContentState` ALREADY EXIST, unused, in
   `packages/render-core/src/url/deeplink.ts` (ADR-0022). Wire the existing codec; do not write a
   second one. Prior art: `canvases-annotations-sharing`.

Offer it at the grains the ladder has: note, object, section, exhibit.

## Constraint — do not undo Archie-40fe

`Archie-40fe` just spent a whole ticket getting floating chrome OFF the canvas (V22/V48/V71/V87).
This panel must be a **dialog** — the `ReadingSheet` shape: scrim, `use:dialog` focus trap, Escape,
focus returned to the trigger — NOT a new persistent floating surface. A cite panel parked over the
canvas is V48 again with a different name.

Reuse `dialog-a11y.ts`. `apps/viewer/e2e/note.spec.ts` has the assertions that shape must satisfy
(focus moves in, Tab is trapped, Escape returns focus); the panel gets the same.

## Verify

- Each grain's copied text is asserted from the CLIPBOARD, not from the DOM node that displays it.
- The link grain must equal `location.hash` at that moment — assert equality, not both-non-empty.
- The Content State grain must round-trip through `decodeContentState`.
closeReason:
Done — merged as 532ebdc (commit 7a45198).

Three grains side by side, as decided. The LINK grain READS `location.href`, never
re-derives it. CONTENT STATE wires the EXISTING `encodeContentState` codec (ADR-0022), which
had sat unused since it was written — no second encoding.

CITATION: prior art read first, as instructed. quire's `citation/page.js` adapts page data to
a CSL-JSON item (author / container-title / issued.date-parts / publisher / title / type /
URL) and hands it to a formatter plugin for MLA or Chicago. `render-core/cite/citation.ts`
copies quire's FIELD MAPPING and deliberately stops short of its formatter: real MLA/Chicago
means citation-js or citeproc — a new runtime dependency in the viewer island graph, which is
exactly the shape `.claude/rules/viewer-optimizedeps-bare-includes.md` records biting three
times, and it would land on the embed's eager budget too. So it emits the CSL-JSON (the
interchange format — paste into Zotero and it IS a real citation) plus one plainly formatted
line built FROM that item, so the two cannot drift.

Dublin Core supplies author/publisher/issued; `requiredStatement` rides CSL `note` so the
MUST-display credit survives being pasted.

TWO HEURISTICS PINNED HONESTLY rather than hidden:
- `cslName` keeps an institution whole (splitting "Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library"
  family-last would cite an author named "Library"), but a two-word non-personal name like
  "Unknown scribe" still splits. Nothing in the string distinguishes it from a personal name,
  and guessing harder would misfile real people. The test says so and names the real fix (an
  authored `literal` flag on the metadata entry), rather than implying coverage it lacks.
- `yearOf` returns undefined rather than guessing — a wrong year is worse than an absent one.

Content State is ABSENT at object/section/exhibit grain, not fabricated: it names an
annotation on a canvas, so those rungs genuinely have none, and a payload decoding to a
non-existent target is worse than no payload.

DID NOT UNDO Archie-40fe: the panel is a dialog in the ReadingSheet shape (scrim + sheet
siblings, `use:dialog`, Escape, focus returned), and the trigger sits in the SAME chrome row
as the finder pill — the one strip whose geometric tests already hold it clear of the
filmstrip and the note card, inheriting the same `--strip-h` reservation.

VERIFIED as required: every grain asserted from the CLIPBOARD, not the textarea that displays
it. Link asserts EQUALITY with `location.href`. Content State is decoded and checked to be a
real Annotation/highlighting payload. Red-green: re-deriving the link instead of reading the
address fails both the link and citation tests.

Gates: 2621 unit (+16), 59 e2e (+6), smoke 15/15, svelte-check 0/0, TS7 clean, eager +0.1KB.

V106's other half (the finder showing each result's address) is now trivially available —
every result has an address and the panel proves the grain works.

title: Embed ships rights, attribution and licence (V105) — legal, do this first
description:
## Question

Implement the non-negotiable half of Archie-52a9. Covers V105.

`<archie-viewer>` shows NO attribution, licence or metadata at gallery OR object level, against a
published tree whose manifests DO carry `requiredStatement` — the shell renders it on the same
object, from the same bytes. An embed that strips a required statement is legal exposure, not a
missing feature, and it is the reason this is filed separately and first.

## The work

- Render the exhibit-level and object-level `requiredStatement` (label + value) and `rights` (licence
  URI) wherever the embed shows an exhibit or an object.
- Read them from the SAME already-resolved published values the shell reads (`readExhibitTree` →
  `PortableExhibit`). Do NOT re-run the opt-in cascade — it collapsed at publish time (the Q5 note in
  ExhibitView.svelte), and re-deriving here would let the two consumers disagree about what a work is
  credited to.
- Dublin Core `metadata` (Archie-c6bf) rides the same already-resolved path; include it.

## Weight

~0KB. The bytes are already fetched — this is rendering data the embed downloads and discards.
Assert it: `node build.mjs --check` must show eagerGzKB unmoved.

## Verify

`recipes/smoke.mjs`, against the BUILT bundle: open an object whose manifest carries a
`requiredStatement` and assert the statement's VALUE appears in the shadow DOM. Not that a rights
element exists — that its text matches the manifest, or the two can drift exactly as they did before.
closeReason:
Done — merged as 4df71ee (feat commit 309dd67).

The credit line renders at all three view-levels from the already-resolved published
values: the gallery's on `ExhibitsJson.library`, the exhibit's spread onto
`PortableExhibit` by `rightsFromIIIF`, the object's on `AObject`. The reader shows the
OBJECT's own credit with NO display-time inheritance — matching ExhibitView.svelte's Q5
rule. Markup follows Credit.svelte, with `<details>` instead of a wired button so the
open/close and a11y semantics are the platform's. The credit VALUE is never behind the
disclosure; licence and Dublin Core rows ride it.

WEIGHT — the ticket's "~0KB" was wrong, and this is the one thing worth carrying forward.
Eager page-load payload moved 33.1KB -> 36KB gz (+2.9KB, ~9%). Isolated by measurement:
markup+CSS +0.8KB, `licenseLabel` +0.3KB, `metadataRows` +1.8KB (it pulls the dcterms
vocabulary table). The estimate was reasoning about DATA — those bytes genuinely were
already fetched and discarded — and didn't account for the display helpers' CODE. Inside
the ratchet's +10KB allowance; baseline re-recorded at 36KB.

VERIFIED as the ticket asked: `recipes/smoke.mjs` against the BUILT bundle, comparing the
shadow DOM against the MANIFEST's own values, not merely that a rights element exists.
Four new hard assertions (exhibit statement, object statement, licence href, every Dublin
Core label present), 11/11 -> 15/15, proven red-green — all four fail against the pre-fix
bundle.

One trap worth recording: `recipes/try.html` loads `/dist/archie-viewer.js` (the ROOT
mirror), not `packages/archie-viewer/dist/`. Rebuilding the package alone leaves the smoke
driving the OLD bundle — it reported this fix as still-broken until `node
scripts/sync-dist.mjs` ran. Same shape as the stale-generated-artifact class in
.claude/rules/svelte-no-typecheck-net.md.

title: ADR-0019 gains a capability contract, and smoke enforces it
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-52a9's enforcement decision: make the embed's obligations explicit and gated.

## Why convention failed

`element.ts:9-10` records the mechanism: the markup was **ported, not imported**. Ported markup
drifts silently, and nothing was watching.

Prior art is decisive, and it is a cautionary tale about the AUDIT as much as the code. annomea's
`EMBED-AUDIT.md` found its whole Channel-3 Web Component had "evaporated silently" — and explains
why the previous audit missed it: that audit was **file-driven**, annomea had no `embed/` directory,
so every counterpart file "had zero counterpart to compare against and was **invisible by
construction**." Archie lost readings, navigation, rights and the narrative the same way, with every
test green throughout.

So the gate must be **capability-driven**. A capability with no file cannot go missing quietly.

## The work

1. **A contract table in `docs/adr/0019`**, one row per capability, using annomea's own verdict
   vocabulary — `PORT` / `ADAPT` / `DROP-justified` / `DEFER-tracked` / `ABSENT`:

   | capability | verdict | gate |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | rights / attribution / licence | MUST | smoke |
   | object navigation | MUST | smoke |
   | note list | MUST | smoke |
   | readings + legend | MUST | smoke |
   | narrative | MUST | smoke |
   | authoring / drawing | DROP-justified | — |
   | Annotorious + PixiJS | DROP-justified | eagerGzKB |

2. **`recipes/smoke.mjs` asserts every MUST row** against the BUILT bundle. It is already the gate
   that drives real Chromium and already the only thing that catches this class.

3. Adding a `DROP` row becomes a deliberate, reviewable act with a written reason — which is the
   whole point. A silent drop becomes a failing build.

## Watch

Scope this to a CONTRACT plus assertions. A shared framework-free component layer was considered and
REJECTED in Archie-52a9: the embed is framework-free by design and the shell is Svelte, so it means
shipping a framework in the embed or rewriting the shell's UI. Don't reopen it here.
closeReason:
Implemented and merged (26c2a59, merge 39e2902 + follow-ups eadf50e / 5530b99 / cc49ee0). docs/adr/0019 gains a capability table: one row per capability with a verdict, an obligation and the gate that holds it.

PRIOR ART: the vocabulary and the one-row-per-capability shape are annomea's (EMBED-AUDIT.md:21, :23-33), including DONE-differently — which is what this ADR's DOM-SVG overlay actually is and which a bare DROP would misreport. The DIAGNOSIS is annomea's too and is quoted at :15: its whole Channel-3 Web Component evaporated because the prior audit was FILE-driven, so with no embed/ directory every embed file had zero counterpart and was invisible by construction. Archie lost nav, the note list, readings, the narrative and its visual language exactly that way, every suite green throughout.

What is NOT annomea's, and the ADR says so: the GATE. annomea proposed a one-time audit plus a manual recovery order (:53-62) and no automated enforcement. Nothing in the surveyed corpus gates embed parity — clover-iiif documents its surface as an options table plus a named unsupported list, canvas-panel scopes by framing sentence, anvil ADR-0006 weighs costs in prose and files follow-ups. All documents. recipes/smoke.mjs is ours.

smoke.mjs asserts every MUST row against the BUILT bundle in real Chromium: 15 to 33 hard assertions at merge, 42 now. Each new assertion compares against an INDEPENDENT truth (the manifest's own annotation pages, readings.json, the Ranges, tokens.css fetched from the same tree) rather than the embed's own output, so a rendering of the WRONG data fails too.

THE DEFECT THIS TICKET'S OWN FIX SHIPPED, because it is the reason two rules now exist. A post-review commit spliced five CONTRACTED_LABELS entries into the middle of a record() argument list ~135 lines away. Consequences, both silent: the completeness check covered 35 labels rather than 40 — all four AV labels missing, so the one capability with no coverage was still uncovered by the commit whose message said it was now covered — and record(ok,label,detail) bound the first stray as `detail`, replacing a diagnostic with a label. Every gate green, RESULT: PASS either way. It was found ONLY because a reported "41/41" did not reconcile with the completeness line's "35/35".

Two rules came out of it: .claude/rules/post-review-fixes-are-unreviewed.md (a fix made after the review is unreviewed; probes with an implicit scope; reconcile every number against one you actually read; read the DETAIL line) and the gate-reference principle — a gate's reference point must not be writable by the thing it gates, which had TWO independent instances here (bundle-size.json rewritten by the build that mandatorily runs, and CONTRACTED_LABELS lowered by moving its own entries). auditOwnSource() now asserts no phantoms, no duplicates, no strays; with the historical splice reproduced the completeness check PASSED at 40/40 while that invariant FAILED — which is what proves it load-bearing.

Current: smoke RESULT PASS, 41 labels, 41/41 present, bookkeeping intact, verified on the merged tree.

title: Embed parity: object nav, note list, readings, narrative, shared tokens
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-52a9's parity decision. Covers V30, V56, V70, V88, and V9/V31/V69.

The audit's clearest pattern: the embed did not lose polish, it lost FUNCTION. ADR-0019 sanctions
dropping Annotorious/PixiJS for a geometry-only DOM-SVG overlay. It sanctions nothing else.

## The work, each behind the EXISTING lazy boundary

The weight argument mostly dissolves: ADR-0019's budget is enforced on `eagerGzKB` (32.9 today), and
every one of these rides behind the same `await import("./reader.js")` boundary the canvas already
uses. Measured expectation — confirm each with `node build.mjs --check`, and treat any eager
movement as the bug:

- **V30 object navigation** (~1KB) — a 12-object exhibit's entire visible control set is
  `["← The Whole Manuscript"]`. There is no way to move between objects at all.
- **V70 note list** (~2KB) — with no list, the marker is the only door to a note, and V69 makes the
  marker near-invisible. Per Archie-c982 the list is the INDEX; that role is what is missing here.
- **V56 readings + legend** (~2KB) — three readings in the library, zero coloured marks, no legend.
  Colour the marks through `readingMarkerStyle` (render-core), the same call the shell and the
  legend swatch use — do not hand-roll a third copy of those numbers.
- **V88 narrative** (~8KB, and only downloaded for exhibits that HAVE sections) — `voynich-reading`
  renders 12 thumbnails, zero prose, no sections, no spine. The one exhibit whose entire subject is
  the narrative.

## V9 / V31 / V69 — share the tokens, do not copy them

Decided in Archie-52a9: the duplicated `markers.css` / `tokens.css` / `atmosphere.css` copies are
NOT the right boundary, because they are precisely what produced the drift the audit saw — white +
system-ui + orange + square cards + a 1.5px near-black hairline marker, against the shell's green
atmosphere, display face and reading colours. Share the token layer.

## Order

`Archie-b681` (rights) ships first — it is legal exposure. `Archie-f90d` (the contract + smoke gate)
should land BEFORE or WITH this, so each capability is asserted as it arrives rather than after.
closeReason:
Implemented and merged (26c2a59, merge 39e2902). The embed had silently lost object nav, the note list, readings, the narrative and the shared visual language — every suite green throughout, because the prior audit was file-driven and the embed had no files to compare against (annomea EMBED-AUDIT.md:15 names that exact mechanism; see Archie-f90d).

Restored and gated in real Chromium against the built bundle. V55, found orphaned between Archie-9a81 and this ticket during reconciliation, is folded in.

The hard constraint held and was not re-litigated: ADR-0019 drops @annotorious/openseadragon + PixiJS and renders regions as a DOM-SVG overlay, so the embed and Studio can never match at the marker layer. Only CONTRACTS are held in common — what is selectable, what a select does, what is reachable by keyboard — never pixels. That is DONE-differently, not DROP.

Verified on the merged tree: smoke RESULT PASS with 41/41 contracted labels present and the label bookkeeping intact, eager 38.9KB / total 274.9KB gz within ratchet allowance, dist/ byte-identical to a fresh build after sync-dist.

title: The image follows along: couple the spine and the camera, both directions
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-e902's decision: the image follows along. Covers V81, V82, V85.

## The state you are starting from

Better than the audit implies. All beats are ALREADY rendered in one scrollable column — measured,
the spine aside has `scrollHeight` 2255 against `clientHeight` 720, six `<li>` present, each with its
own `<div class="prose">`. Nothing hides the non-active beats. The mode is one observer away from
its own stated premise.

## The work

1. **Scroll → camera (V81).** An `IntersectionObserver` over the beat `<li>`s drives `activeIndex`;
   the camera follows through the existing `fitRegion(section.start)` path.
   Prior art, in the corpus and exact: **scrollama**, explicitly built on "IntersectionObserver in
   favor of scroll events" — same choice, same reason. Do not hand-roll scroll math or listen to
   `scroll` directly.

2. **Activate → scroll (V82).** This is the SAME coupling run backwards, not a second feature. A
   section cite currently lands the camera and strands the prose off-screen because activation only
   ever drove one half. `activate(i)` must also scroll that beat into view. One coupling, two
   directions, so both halves of the mode arrive together whichever door the reader came in by.

3. **Number the beats (V85).** Once the active beat moves under the reader, "where am I" needs an
   answer that is not just typographic emphasis. `Section 3 of 6`, matching the noun-and-position
   idiom `SidebarObjectNav` and Archie-01a6 already use.

## The hazard this creates

The two directions will fight if you let them. A programmatic scroll from `activate()` re-enters the
observer and can bounce the reader to a neighbouring beat. Either suppress the observer for the
duration of a programmatic scroll, or ignore observer callbacks that disagree with an intended
target. Whichever you choose, TEST IT: drive a section cite and assert the spine settles on the cited
beat, not its neighbour.

## Verify

`apps/viewer/e2e`, offline — the spine and its prose render from the local manifest, so this whole
interaction is testable with the network cut (unlike anything needing a painted canvas; see
selection.spec.ts's header). Assert: scrolling the spine changes the active beat; activating a beat
scrolls it into view; a section cite lands on the CITED beat and stays there.
closeReason:
Implemented and merged (37783df, branch ux/narrative-coupling: 87b4bd1 + 8cbe399). V81 — the mode's central promise, "read down the page and the image follows along" — now holds in both directions.

MECHANISM. IntersectionObserver over the beats (root = the scrolling column, rootMargin -50%/-50%, threshold 0) drives the camera; activating a beat scrolls the column and moves the camera. The difficulty is that the observer watches the same box the activation scrolls, so a programmatic scroll re-enters its own callback and reports every beat it sweeps past.

PRIOR ART: no donor, and the ticket's premise was wrong. scrollama supports the API choice ONLY (use IntersectionObserver, don't hand-roll scroll math) and has NO reentrancy guard — verified, `grep scrollIntoView src/` is empty and it only ever reads scrollTop, so it has no two-directions problem. quire's canvas-panel.js:259 calls goToFigureState (:68) and its scrollToHash (:118) straight from an IO callback with NO suppression — but its observer root is .quire-entry__content (intersection-observer-factory.js:12) while scroll-to-hash.js:21-28 scrolls the DOCUMENT, and an observer measures geometry relative to its root, so a document scroll translates root and target by the same delta and the measurement is invariant. Structurally immune, not solved. annomea/anvil have no scroll-coupled surface. The guard is ORIGINAL DESIGN and claims no precedent.

THE GUARD, after two review rounds that each found the same class of error.

Design 1 — end the intent when the column goes QUIET (last scroll + 150ms). Measured FULLY DEFEATED: every scroll re-armed the settle, so a zero-distance click followed by continuous scrolling froze the highlight 1546ms while the reader passed 2760px and 15 sections, released only by the ceiling. A scrollbar drag is the realistic path. It was also load-sensitive: a single natural 160ms frame stall fires a 150ms timer mid-animation, which is why the flake appeared only under CPU contention.

Design 2 — ARRIVAL. scrollToBeat computes the destination as a NUMBER and the intent ends when the column reaches or passes it. Reached-or-PASSED, not equals: a dragged scrollbar steps ~58px and would straddle any tolerance window. A stalled frame moves nothing, so it cannot release an arrival.

Round 2 then found design 2's own fix shipped the defect the guard exists to prevent: adding pointerdown to the cancel list dropped the intent TOKEN but not the scroll MACHINE, so the animation kept running with the observer un-muted — TEN spurious section changes in ~300ms on one activation, each closing the open note and swapping the canvas object. wheel/touchstart looked fine only because Chromium cancels a smooth scroll on a real scroll gesture; three paths were lucky, not correct. onColumnInput now stops the scroll itself.

TWO CLAIMS DISPROVEN, both originally stated in the author's favour:
- INTENT_MAX_MS was not a backstop at all on the scroll path — the deadline was read only inside intentActive(), whose only caller is the observer callback. Where crossings continued it did fire (1491ms measured); where they stopped, nothing consulted it and the highlight stayed frozen 3500ms with NO recovery. A deadline only a callback can notice cannot bound a wedge defined by that callback not arriving. Now a timer armed WITH the intent that ends it and re-observes. endIntent() is the single exit so it can never fire against a later intent; it only ever ENDS suppression, which is what separates it from the quiet timer.
- ARRIVE_PX was called "not pinned from below, by design". It is load-bearing, by two independent mechanisms: Chromium rounds scrollTo to whole pixels while the target comes from getBoundingClientRect() and is fractional (20 of 21 beats land up to 0.48px short, stable DPR 1 to 2.4), and the same constant gates the nothing-to-do branch in scrollToBeat. The suite was green at 0 only because its probes overshoot by hundreds of pixels — a coverage gap, not redundancy. Now pinned by a test.

Also corrected: a post-sign-off comment claiming beatAtColumnEnd does not pin the cite test. It reddens three tests including that one; the injection had disabled only the head branch while the test cites the last section, resolved by the foot branch — the same incomplete-injection error that had already produced one false green on this branch.

GATES: svelte-check 1521 files 0/0, typecheck 6 packages, vitest 176 (viewer) / 2690 total, e2e 122 passed 0 skipped over two full runs incl. one under 28-way CPU contention. Twelve injections redden; four documented non-claims. The injection battery hard-fails unless `astro build` appears in the run and asserts every anchor is still present — that assert caught two stale anchors that would previously have been silent green.

title: Hiding the narrative spine is per-exhibit and plainly reversible
description:
## Question

Fix V83, which Archie-e902's decision makes more urgent than the audit rated it.

## Why it got worse

Hiding the spine is sticky, global and near-irreversible. Under the OLD behaviour that cost the
reader a panel. Under Archie-0d6c's scroll coupling the spine becomes the mode's INPUT DEVICE — the
thing that drives the camera — so hiding it does not merely hide prose, it silently removes the
interaction the mode is named for, and leaves an image that no longer follows anything.

## The work

- **Per-exhibit, not global.** Collapsing the spine on one narrative must not collapse it on the
  next. The persistence idiom is already here: `aside-persistence.ts` + the `archie.*.v1` metadata
  keys; scope the key by exhibit slug.
- **Plainly reversible.** Whatever the collapsed state renders must carry a visible, named way back —
  the same discipline `Archie-3d55` applied to the canvas (`ResizeDivider` stays a sibling of the
  collapsed aside precisely so un-collapsing stays reachable; check that idiom before inventing one).
- Consider whether "hidden" should even survive a reload for a scroll-coupled mode. A reader who
  returns to a narrative and finds its driving surface gone has no way to know what they are missing.

## Watch

`Archie-40fe` already fixed V80 (canvas chrome rendering over the spine) via the `--strip-h` /
`--finder-h` reservation. RE-MEASURE rather than re-fixing it.

## Verify

`apps/viewer/e2e`, offline. Collapse the spine on one exhibit, open another, assert its spine is
present. Then assert the collapsed state still offers a named control that restores it.
closeReason:
Implemented and merged with Archie-0d6c (37783df). Landed together deliberately: once the spine is an INPUT DEVICE, hiding it silently removes the interaction the mode is named for — so the two could not ship apart without a window in which the mode's promise was unreachable and unexplained.

V83 was: hiding the narrative spine is sticky, GLOBAL and near-irreversible. Now per-exhibit and plainly reversible — the state is scoped by exhibit in apps/viewer/src/aside-persistence.ts rather than under one flat key, so hiding the spine in one exhibit does not silently hide it in every other.

PRIOR ART, with what it does and does not support: anvil's read/Sidebar.svelte and editor/Sidebar.svelte persist WIDTH only, under a flat global key, with no collapse at all. The corpus therefore says nothing about persisting a HIDDEN panel, and the sessionStorage-and-per-exhibit decision is stated as ours rather than dressed as precedent.

A measurement worth keeping (V80, re-measured during this work — the earlier figures mixed two states): the canvas chrome clears the spine by 30px in BOTH states — expanded chromeRight 840.41 vs spineLeft 870.41; collapsed chromeRight 1250 vs viewport 1280 with spineWidth 0. Independently verified by review.

One injection on this ticket's own key came back GREEN and forced a better test: the first unscoped-key injection unscoped only the READ, not the write, so the global key was never written and the test passed against deliberately broken code.

Gates as for Archie-0d6c: svelte-check 1521 files 0/0, typecheck 6 packages, e2e 132 passed 0 skipped on the merged tree.

title: The finder says what it found, not where it is
description:
## Question

Fix **V106** — the finder's results don't show where a hit lives. Orphaned by an audit
reconciliation on 2026-07-26: no ticket has ever owned it.

## Why it was missed, and this is the instructive part

`Archie-3ea1` (the cite panel) and `Archie-99b1` (the address writes every rung) both record V106's
capability as now "available" / "unblocked" — and both are telling the truth about the *substrate*.
The address grammar exists, `routeToHash` builds every rung, and `logicalIdOf` resolves a note id
from either form.

Neither ticket touched `SearchOverlay.svelte`. **A capability being reachable is not the same as a
surface using it**, and both closures read as if it were. That is the same epistemic shape as
`.claude/rules/svelte-no-typecheck-net.md`'s "a gate proves the code COMPILED, never that the output
CARRIES anything" — here, the plumbing landed and nothing consumed it.

## The work

A finder result should say where it is, in the same noun-and-position idiom the rest of the viewer
now uses. At minimum a hit should name its object (and its section, in a narrative); ideally the
result carries the locus so activating it lands on the exact rung rather than the object's top.

Read `ExhibitView.svelte`'s `locus` derivation first — it is the ONE address writer and already
computes precedence across noteId / objectId / sectionId / xywh / t. The finder should read from
that vocabulary, not re-derive an address of its own. Do not add a second address writer.

## Verify

`apps/viewer/e2e`, offline. Open the finder, assert a result displays its locus, and assert that
activating it lands on that locus rather than the object's default view. Inject the bug (strip the
locus from the result) and confirm the test fails before trusting it.

---

## Prior art swept 2026-07-26 — clover-iiif is a fully worked donor

`IIIF/clover-iiif/src/components/.../ContentSearch.tsx` and `Annotation/Item.tsx`:

- **Canvas name is a GROUP header, not a per-row field.** `ContentSearch.tsx:50-58` groups hits by
  `target.source.id`; `:83-88` renders each group under `<header><Label label={canvas.label}/></header>`.
  Avoids repeating the same canvas name down every row.
- **The thumbnail IS the locus.** `Item.tsx:41-52` builds each row's thumbnail from the hit's own
  `FragmentSelector` xywh, requesting a IIIF image crop AT THAT REGION
  (`${targetResource}/${xywh}/!${w},${h}/0/default.jpg`) — not a generic canvas cover. A result shows
  *where* it is by showing what is there.
- **Activation lands on the exact region — ONLY when the canvas is already visible.** `handleClick`
  (`Item.tsx:134-155`): if the hit's canvas is visible, `handleOverlayZoom()` (`:101-117`) fits the
  viewport to the annotation's own overlay bounds with padding. If not, it dispatches
  `updateActiveCanvas` — **and nothing else happens.**

  **CORRECTED 2026-07-27.** This ticket previously claimed a `useEffect` at `:119-132` polls until the
  annotation's overlay exists and then runs the same zoom, so "the cross-canvas path still ends at the
  exact region." **It does not, for search hits.** That effect is gated
  `if (!openSeadragonViewer || !isContentState) return;` and `ContentSearch.tsx` never passes
  `isContentState` — it passes `isContentSearch`. So for a content-search hit on a not-yet-visible
  canvas the poll never fires and the reader lands on the canvas, not the region.

  The line numbers were right and the causal sentence was wrong — habit 1b in
  `.claude/rules/prior-art-citation-discipline.md`, *cited correctly, read past*. It survived two
  relays and was caught only by the third reader, who was about to build on it. **Do not treat clover
  as a donor for the cross-canvas case; it has the same gap.**

  (Also corrected: the thumbnail template at `:41-52` is `!${computeSize(w, h)}`, not a raw `!${w},${h}`.
  The concept — crop at the hit's own xywh rather than a generic canvas cover — is unaffected.)
- Position count ("3 of 12") is **not** shown per result. clover-iiif has that idiom
  (`Slider/Items/Items.tsx:127`) but does not wire it to search.

**Two other strategy families, for contrast:**

- **universalviewer — hits as a spatial minimap, not a list.** `uv-searchfooterpanel-module/FooterPanel.ts`
  places each hit as a tick on a page-position ruler (`:520-523`, `:713-729`). Hover
  (`onPlacemarkerMouseEnter`, `:594-673`) shows canvas identity (`"Page {label}"` / `"Image {N+1}"`,
  `:617-635`) plus a match count from `result.rects.length` and the ellipsized terms (`:644-667`), and
  publishes `SEARCH_PREVIEW_START` (`:603-606`) — a live preview-pan before any click.
- **quire — the fragment is baked at index time.** `_plugins/search/search.js:100-101` indexes each unit
  with its own `canonicalURL + '#' + id`, so "land on the exact locus" is a plain anchor, not app logic.
- **tropy — filter-in-place.** Search filters the existing item grid; there is no result row to carry a
  locus at all.

Checked and not comparable: immarkus (structured knowledge-graph query builder, not full-text over
image content).

**One gap worth knowing:** clover-iiif appears to render only the Content Search `resources`, not the
Search API 2 `hits` array (match-context objects). If Archie ever consumes a real Content Search
response, that distinction is unresolved in the corpus.
closeReason: Closed on the SURFACE, not the substrate. apps/viewer/src/components/SearchOverlay.svelte now renders a locus line per result: the object's authored label, plus the section title in a narrative (locateNotes in search-index.ts). No second address writer — activation still routes choose -> onselect -> arriveAtNote -> ExhibitView's one locus derivation; ExhibitView touched at exactly two mount-site lines. Proven by driving the built app offline: apps/viewer/e2e/finder-locus.spec.ts 4/4, five injections red-green'd, 20/20 independent repeat invocations (80/80 test runs). Prior art: mirador SearchHit.jsx:120-125 (per-row, chosen — our list is a MiniSearch ranking, so clover's ContentSearch.tsx:83-88 group header would reorder by place not match quality), quire index.js:108-109 (the only corpus system naming a hit by narrative unit). Ledger: ledgers/FIX-finder-locus-2026-07-27.md. Filed and closed Archie-8e73 along the way — driving this surface revealed every finder result was off-screen and unclickable on the seed narrative.

title: Canvas chrome needs a contrast floor against an arbitrary image
description:
## Question

Fix **V42** — the canvas chrome has no contrast floor against the image beneath it. Orphaned by an
audit reconciliation on 2026-07-26.

## Provenance

`Archie-c831` deferred V42 by name into `Archie-9a81`. `Archie-9a81` closed having fixed V40 and V80
without touching V42, and nothing has owned it since. A deferral that names its destination is only
as good as the destination's memory of it — this one was dropped in the handoff.

## The work

Canvas chrome (scale cue, locator, finder pill, nav) sits over an arbitrary image. A photograph can
be any luminance at any point, so chrome that relies on the image being light — or dark — is
unreadable against half the corpus. `screenshots` is the useful adversarial exhibit here: it is full
of near-white UI captures.

Establish a contrast floor that holds regardless of what is beneath. Prior art in the corpus should
be checked before inventing one — how do clover-iiif / canvas-panel / universalviewer keep overlay
chrome legible over unknown imagery (scrim, backdrop-filter, outline, plate)? Cite what you find.

## Watch

`Archie-40fe` established the `--strip-h` / `--finder-h` reservation model for WHERE chrome sits.
This ticket is about LEGIBILITY once it is there — a different axis, same elements. Don't disturb
the reservation while fixing the contrast.

Note also that V80's fix was `Archie-9a81`'s, not `Archie-40fe`'s — several tickets carry that
attribution wrongly. Cite 9a81 for the V80 fix and 40fe for the reservation idiom.

## Verify

Measure, don't eyeball: compute the actual contrast ratio of chrome text/glyphs against the sampled
pixels beneath it, on a light exhibit and a dark one. `screenshots` (light) and a Voynich folio
(dark parchment) are the two poles. State the ratio achieved and the floor targeted.

---

## Prior art swept 2026-07-26 — and it complicates the ticket's premise

**The corpus default is: don't float chrome over the image at all.**

- `IIIF/clover-iiif/src/components/Viewer/Viewer/Viewer.tsx:180-184` — `<ViewerHeader>` and
  `<ViewerContent>` are SIBLINGS in normal flex flow (`Viewer.styled.tsx:15-22`). The header can be
  `background-color: transparent !important` (`Header.styled.ts:57-73`) precisely because it never
  sits over the image. Its one over-canvas control, `PanelToggle`, is an **opaque plate**
  (`background: $primary` + `boxShadow: 2px 2px 5px #0003`) — contrast sidestepped, not solved.
- `tropy/src/components/esper/container.js:11,39` — overlay toolbar is opt-in (`hasOverlayToolbar`
  default `false`); the default lives outside the canvas. Even in overlay mode it is hidden
  (`translate3d(0,-100%,0)`) until hover/focus (`_toolbar.scss:139-158`).
- `canvas-panel` paints no chrome over the image. `cozy-iiif` is headless.

Archie has already committed the other way — `Archie-40fe`'s `--strip-h`/`--finder-h` reservation
model, plus scale cue, finder pill, locator, and (in flight) object nav. That commitment is not
re-opened by this ticket, but **whoever takes this should know it is the minority posture**, and
should say why it stands rather than treating it as given.

## When chrome DOES float, five mechanisms with real values

| technique | donor | values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| opaque plate | clover-iiif `Viewer.styled.tsx:41-82` | solid theme colour + `2px 2px 5px #0003` |
| scrim + backdrop-filter, solid fallback FIRST | universalviewer `center-panel.less:79-83` | `background: @gray-dark` (fallback, commented `// ie8`) → `fadeout(@gray-dark, 30%)` → `blur(5px)` |
| theme-adaptive scrim + heavy blur, transient | tropy `_tropy.scss:429`, `_variables.scss:263` | 80% opacity, swaps light/dark **by UI theme, not by sampling the image**; `blur(20px)` |
| token-routed scrim + hairline border | anvil `Toolbar.svelte:80-93` | `var(--surface-floating)` + `blur(8px)` + `1px solid var(--border-floating)` |
| gradient scrim + doubled text-shadow halo | immarkus `Images.css:22-30` | directional gradient only under the label + `text-shadow: 0 0 2px rgba(0,0,0,.5), 0 0 6px rgba(0,0,0,.35)`, same recipe as `drop-shadow()` for SVG |

Cascade order is UV's guard for non-supporting browsers, not `@supports`. anvil's border substitutes
for contrast when fill and blur fall short. immarkus doubles gradient AND halo rather than trusting
either.

**Nobody samples the underlying pixels.** Tropy adapts to UI theme; no one adapts to the image.

## The measured-ratio ask is ORIGINAL, not a port

All seven repos grepped for `4.5:1`, `3:1`, "contrast ratio", "WCAG" — **zero real hits**. Every
technique above was chosen by eye. The measurement discipline this ticket asks for has no corpus
precedent; keep it, but label it as Archie's own rather than implying a donor.
closeReason:
OBVIATED, not fixed — the human ruled on 2026-07-26 that canvas chrome DOCKS out of the canvas.

There is no contrast floor to establish because nothing floats. Every element this ticket named —
scale cue, locator aside, finder pill, object nav, the reading legend — is now a flow sibling of the
canvas box (ADR-0019's layout row): ViewerShell's top bar, the readers' `.canvas-dock`, ExhibitView's
`.chrome-dock`, and on the embed side `.reader-dock` / `.reader-note`. Chrome and image do not share
pixels, so "legible over an arbitrary image" is not a question this app asks any more.

This is exactly the outcome the ticket's own prior-art sweep pointed at and flagged as complicating
its premise: clover-iiif's header is transparent BECAUSE it is a flex sibling of the content
(`Viewer/Viewer.tsx:180-184`, `Viewer.styled.tsx:15-22`, `Header.styled.ts:57-73`), and tropy's
overlay toolbar is opt-in with `hasOverlayToolbar` defaulting false (`esper/container.js:11,39`). The
sweep said Archie's floating posture was the minority one; the ruling moved us to the corpus default.

The measured-ratio discipline the ticket asked for is NOT lost, it is unneeded: the five floating
techniques it catalogued all exist to rescue legibility over unknown pixels, and there are none. If a
future surface genuinely must float, that table is still the right starting point.

ONE NAMED EXCEPTION, recorded in ADR-0019 rather than left implicit: the OSD locator mini-map still
sits over the image. It is OpenSeadragon's own `navigator` (`read-mount.ts:245`), a map OF the image
rather than chrome on it, every viewer in the corpus floats it, and docking it needs `navigatorId`
plumbing through @render/mount. The smoke gate is scoped to a NAMED SET of docked elements so that
exclusion is visible instead of silently baked in.

Gate: `recipes/smoke.mjs` — three new CONTRACTED_LABELS entries (docked chrome is on screen; no
docked chrome overlaps the canvas box; the canvas centre hit-tests to the canvas). Proven red-green
by injection against the built bundle.

title: The seed corpus has no polygon region, so the path is never seen
description:
## Question

**V54** — the seed corpus contains zero polygon regions, so the polygon path is never exercised by
anything a reader or a developer actually looks at. Orphaned by an audit reconciliation on
2026-07-26: never named outside the map epic and its own audit ledger.

## Why this is filed low, and honestly

This is a **showroom gap, not a viewer defect**. The polygon selector is implemented; nothing in the
shipped seed data uses it. So every screenshot, every demo, every manual drive and every e2e run
exercises rectangles only — and a polygon regression would surface in front of a user rather than in
front of us.

It is scoped as content work, which is why it sat unowned: it does not look like a bug in any file.

## The work

Add at least one polygon region to the seed corpus, on an object where a polygon is the *right*
shape rather than a demonstration of the feature (an irregular illustration, a marginal figure —
the Voynich rosettes are the obvious candidate).

Two seed sources exist and they are not the same thing — check which one this belongs in before
editing: studio `seed-data` versus viewer `sample-data` → `gen-published.mts`. Shared content lives
in `apps/viewer/fixtures`.

Then assert it: a polygon region should appear in the offline e2e suite, so the path has a gate and
not just a presence.

## Watch

Do NOT change an existing fixture to make it a polygon — the project rule is that a shared fixture
is never modified to serve one need; add a new one. Changing one requires checking every consumer.
closeReason:
SHIPPED — merged to main in the fixture slice at 8683b02 (authored 5252f69, 1cdf706; review-fixed 1d3e33a).

The seed corpus now carries a polygon region, so the polygon path is exercised rather than merely implemented. Assertions live in apps/viewer/fixtures/fixture-reach.test.ts.

Carried forward, and it is the reason this ticket's own review was worth doing: the first version of the polygon assertion selected its subject with .find(s => shapeLabel(s) === 'Polygon') — 'whichever is first' — so reordering the fixture would have silently retargeted a twelve-vertex assertion at the ten-vertex polygon. Fixed to key on objectId with both sides sorted (a440721, 95787d4). The sibling assertion in seed-carry.test.ts had the same shape and WAS flaky: 9 failures in 20 against a correct tree. Both are now 20/20 across 20 independent vitest processes.

Rule earned: .claude/rules/a-green-run-is-one-sample.md — a red-green proves an assertion CAN fail and says nothing about whether it passes reliably.

title: Studio and Viewer token files have already drifted — unify onto one floor
description:
## Question

Studio and Viewer each carry their own `tokens.css`, and the two have **already drifted**. Unify
them onto one source, or record why they must stay separate.

## The measurement (2026-07-26, found while landing the embed's shared token layer)

- `apps/studio/src/tokens.css` has `--text-lede` and `--text-note`; the viewer's copy does not.
- `apps/viewer/src/tokens.css` has `--topbar-h`, `--scrim-top`, `--pane-top`; studio's copy does not.

Neither divergence was decided. They accumulated, which is the entire failure mode `Archie-52a9`
named when it rejected copied `markers.css` / `tokens.css` / `atmosphere.css` for the embed:
duplicated token files are *precisely* what produced the visual drift the viewer UX audit measured
(white + system-ui + orange + square cards against the shell's green atmosphere, display face and
reading colours).

The embed work (`Archie-c314`) moved the **viewer's** copy down into a shared package so the embed
and the shell consume one floor. **Studio was deliberately left out of that change** — it is a
bigger fish than the embed ticket, and folding it in would have made a scoped slice unreviewable.
This ticket is that fish.

## The work

1. Diff the two files properly. Separate genuine divergence (a token only one app can meaningfully
   have) from accidental divergence (a token both want, added to one).
2. For accidental divergence: promote to the shared token package the embed work created.
3. For genuine divergence: keep it app-local, and say in a comment WHY it is app-local. An
   unexplained app-local token is how this recurs.
4. Decide whether studio consumes the shared floor plus a local layer, or stays wholly separate.
   Consuming plus layering is the obvious default; argue it down if it doesn't hold.

## Watch

- The shared floor now has THREE consumers once studio joins: `apps/viewer`, `packages/archie-viewer`
  (the embed), and `apps/studio`. A token added to the floor lands in the published embed bundle —
  check the `eagerGzKB` ratchet (`cd packages/archie-viewer && node build.mjs --check`) after, since
  the embed inlines the token text into its entry.
- Studio is an authoring surface and the viewer is a reading surface. Some divergence is legitimate
  — authoring chrome has no reason to exist in a reader. Don't unify for symmetry's sake.
- `recipes/smoke.mjs` now asserts the embed's computed token values AGREE with the shared source
  (not merely that tokens exist). If you change the floor, that assertion is the thing that tells
  you whether the embed followed.

## Verify

`pnpm --filter @archie/studio run check` and `pnpm --filter @archie/viewer run check:svelte` both at
0/0, `pnpm -r run typecheck`, and a driven look at both apps — a token move that typechecks and
silently changes a colour is the failure this ticket exists to prevent. Screenshot both surfaces
before and after and compare.
closeReason:
SHIPPED — merged in wave 2. Ledger: ledgers/FIX-token-unify-2026-07-27.md.

THE HEADLINE IS THAT THERE WAS NOTHING TO DECIDE. 100 tokens, identical values, identical order, plus identical */body/.eyebrow rules. These were never two design systems — one file and a stale copy. main carried TWO tokens.css; the branch carries ONE, at packages/render-core/src/tokens.css, which tokens-source.mjs already pointed at.

Studio now consumes the floor with NO local layer. Its only app-local custom properties (--studio-aside-w, --plate-w) are per-component RUNTIME channels written by style: bindings and already declared at their use sites. Creating an empty local file would be scaffolding that invites filling; the rule for when one is genuinely needed is written into the floor's header instead.

THE TICKET'S MEASUREMENT WAS STALE, AND IT MISSED THE ONE THAT MATTERED. --topbar-h/--scrim-top/--pane-top were retired from BOTH files by the dock (dfe7ab4). Not in the ticket: --scrim-dim (studio inlined the value as a var() fallback because the token was missing), and the .eyebrow rule differed BY VALUE — studio 0.55, floor 0.70. A contrast fix reached the reader and never reached the author.

SEPARATION: --text-lede accidental (viewer hardcodes 1.0625rem at 7 prose sites) · --text-note accidental (2 viewer prose sites) · --scrim-dim accidental · .eyebrow colour = drift, not divergence · the other 100 identical. GENUINE DIVERGENCE: NONE.

ARTIFACT, not exit code: apps/studio/dist/assets/index-*.css emits .eyebrow{…color:#1a3c23b3} — 0xb3/255 = 0.702, the fix; the old copy emitted #1a3c238c = 0.549. The embed bundle carries all three promoted tokens.

GATES: studio 968/968 · viewer 184/184 · render-core 1202/1202 · embed 185/185 · studio check 1184 0/0 · viewer check:svelte 1523 0/0 · typecheck 6/6 · smoke 45/45 + 44/44 labels · viewer e2e 142/142 · eagerGzKB 38.9→39.3 (Δ+0.4, allowed +10.0) · sync-dist matches. 5/5 injections red, each taking down exactly one assertion; 20/20 stable.

PRIOR ART — and the strongest result is an absence.
