title: Run the a09d packaged verification for the native folder-canonical store (7 rows still pending)
description:
Desktop folder-canonical (Archie-623e) is IMPLEMENTED in the tree at d2e4f63 — resident-store.ts mounts TauriFilesystem(defaultLibraryRoot()), store.ts + asset-store.ts both route through residentProjectDir, the seam carries lazy getFile/size/resolveUrl, AV goes through convertFileSrc, peaks live in a hidden .archie-cache, single-instance plugin + mirror-stamp token guard are in. What is missing is EVIDENCE, not code.

All seven 'only the packaged app proves' rows in docs/plans/native-canonical-store.md:316-326 are still marked pending build:

  P1-a  multi-GB AV streams in BOUNDED memory via plugin-fs open() under WebKitGTK
  P1-b  copyTree over a REAL OPFS FsaFilesystem source round-trips a real library
  P2-a  a session authors to {appDataDir}/library and SURVIVES RELAUNCH
  P2-b  migration of a REAL pre-existing OPFS library; marker LAST; OPFS retained
  P3-a  storage chip hidden and persist() skipped on desktop
  P4-a  folder-resident AV plays via asset:// with byte-range seeking; images stay blob:; OSD unaffected
  P5-a  a second launch FOCUSES rather than opening a second writer
  P5-b  the generation-token guard pauses+warns on an out-of-band writer

Also confirm the abort-not-skip migration posture end-to-end (native-canonical-store.md:330-340): a deliberately interrupted copy must leave migrated.json ABSENT and the session must REFUSE to boot against the partial folder — no silent skip back to OPFS.

Needs a tauri build + Flatpak. None of this is observable in vitest, and none of it should be claimed done on headless gates.

Source: ledgers/EXPLORE-studio-folder-export-settings-2026-07-26.md §1.

--- RELEASE GATE (decided by grill, 2026-07-26) ---

BLOCKER on the next DESKTOP build. Cut so it is actually doable — only two rows gate a ship:

  P2-a  author -> relaunch -> the work is still there
  P2-b  migrate a REAL pre-existing OPFS library (marker LAST, OPFS retained)

Those two cover the catastrophic cases. The other five (bounded-memory multi-GB write,
convertFileSrc AV, single-instance focus, token guard, desktop deep-zoom) are DEGRADATIONS, not
bricks, and may ride a later build.

Why blocker: resident-store.ts is on MAIN (981be88), not a branch. If defaultLibraryRoot() resolves
wrong under Flatpak — a path nothing headless exercises — the abort-not-skip posture means the app
REFUSES TO BOOT for 100% of existing desktop users, not an edge case. The posture is right (copy
never moves, OPFS retained, so no data loss) but 'refuses to boot' is still the outcome.

Not reverting the flip on main: it is a large coherent change and reverting costs more than gating
the release. The risk is entirely in SHIPPING it.

--- ENVIRONMENT RE-MEASURED (2026-07-26, studio-explore lane) ---

This ticket was recorded as needing "your machine or CI" on the strength of ONE probe: flatpak-builder
is missing. That probe was of the FLATPAK path only, and the claim it was taken to support was wider.
Re-measured in this checkout:

  flatpak-builder                              MISSING
  flatpak / cargo / rustc                      present
  webkit2gtk-4.1, javascriptcoregtk-4.1        present (pkg-config OK)
  cargo check in repo-root src-tauri/          Finished dev profile in 32.50s
  @tauri-apps/cli ^2.11.3, .bin/tauri          present

So a NATIVE (non-Flatpak) desktop build is buildable here, and the two ship-gating rows are about the
storage spine under a real webview -- which a native build exercises exactly as well as a packaged one:

  P2-a  author -> relaunch -> the work is still there
  P2-b  migrate a REAL pre-existing OPFS library (marker LAST, OPFS retained)

What a native run does NOT cover, and must not be reported as covering: the Flatpak sandbox itself --
defaultLibraryRoot() path mapping under the sandbox, portals, tauri-plugin-opener survival. That is the
exact variable this ticket calls catastrophic ("refuses to boot for 100% of existing desktop users"),
and it has its own ticket, Archie-7e2e. A green native run is a PARTIAL pass: it retires the spine
risk and leaves the sandbox risk untouched. Do not close 9ece on it.

--- NATIVE RUN EXECUTED (2026-07-26) ---

Built native debug (cargo, --no-bundle, 47.75s) and drove the real window via xdotool + import
screenshots on Xwayland. NOT Flatpak; the sandbox variable remains untested (Archie-7e2e).

FIRST BOOT FOUND A P0, unrelated to the risk this ticket predicted: every file write failed because
the capability manifest omits fs:allow-rename, and TauriFilesystem commits via temp-then-rename.
100% of authored work lost, with the app looking healthy. Filed as Archie-91e7 with red-green
evidence and a suggested derived gate. defaultLibraryRoot() itself resolved CORRECTLY natively
({appDataDir}/library) — the predicted failure mode was not the one that fired.

P2-a  author -> relaunch -> work survives           PASS (after the Archie-91e7 fix)
      An exhibit authored before quitting (slug 0accebf6883150506f6ce8587d7fa7bd735a472b, no
      seedVersion = user-owned) was present after a full relaunch: 7 exhibits before, 8 after (the
      extra is a replayed queued ingest, see below). All 4 files on disk non-empty, ZERO 0-byte
      files, so no torn writes. The object-id migration also ran and left pre-migration/library.json
      + pre-migration/snapshot-complete.json, i.e. snapshot-then-marker behaved.

P2-b  migrate a REAL pre-existing OPFS library      NOT RUN — precondition absent
      This machine has an app-data dir from an earlier build (Jul 5), but its WebKit storage/ holds
      only "salt" and there is no library.json anywhere beneath it: that install booted and cached
      pages but never authored. So there is no real OPFS library here to migrate, and no
      migrated.json was written on any boot — correct per opfs-to-folder.ts:64 (no source => no
      marker, so a later-appearing OPFS library can still migrate). Creating the precondition
      honestly needs a build with the pre-flip OPFS-canonical store; hand-crafting the WebKit OPFS
      backing store is not a safe substitute.

SIDE FINDINGS
  - Media ingest never completes ("Adding <file> 1 of 1", no asset reaches disk) and replays a
    different queued file each launch. Persisted stale ingest state is the likely cause, not the
    write path. Recorded in Archie-91e7 as explicitly separate.
  - The library home reads "Living in this browser" on desktop — wrong surface copy for
    folder-canonical.

The app-data dir was backed up before the first boot to /tmp/archie-9ece/appdata-backup-preboot
(11M) and nothing was deleted; the test library remains in place at {appDataDir}/library.


--- CORRECTION 2026-07-26: part of the first evidence set was measured against ANOTHER CHECKOUT ---

`tauri build --debug --no-bundle` bakes `frontendDist` (the packaged origin). A plain `cargo build`
does NOT — it bakes `devUrl`, i.e. http://localhost:5174. After the first build I rebuilt twice with
plain `cargo build` to pick up the capability edits, and those binaries loaded the dev server that was
already listening on 5174 — running from /mnt/Ghar/.../Archie/apps/studio, the MAIN checkout, not this
worktree. I was driving someone else's frontend without knowing it. This is exactly the hazard in
.claude/rules/viewer-e2e-shared-port.md ("a run whose port ownership you cannot establish is
unverified, not passed"), reached by a different route: not a reused server, but a build flag that
silently selects one.

The tell, and it is unambiguous — WebKit names its localStorage file after the ORIGIN:

  profile used for boot 1 + later boots   tauri_localhost_0.localstorage  AND  http_localhost_5174.localstorage
  profile used for the "clean" run        http_localhost_5174.localstorage ONLY

WHAT STANDS:
  - The total write failure. Boot 1 ran on the properly packaged binary (tauri_localhost_0 origin):
    18 directories, 4 files, ZERO bytes of content. Valid.
  - The fix. Re-measured on a REBUILT packaged binary (origin confirmed tauri_localhost_0) against a
    freshly deleted profile: library.json 21,606 bytes, 0 zero-byte files. Both sides of the A/B are
    now packaged builds of THIS worktree, differing only in the permission.
  - The capability audit itself is Rust-side and origin-independent, and it is now gated in CI by
    scripts/check-tauri-capabilities.mjs (red-greened: removing fs:allow-rename exits 1).

WHAT DOES NOT STAND, AND WAS WITHDRAWN:
  - The "stale ingest queue replaying on every boot" and the mystery BHC006_GMT_PN_* exhibits. Those
    were the MAIN checkout's live dev-session state reached through the dev server, not a defect in
    this tree, and not stale state. The real ingest defect is Archie-ce7a (webkitdirectory picks a
    file under WebKitGTK).
  - The "blank window on relaunch". That was a SCREENSHOT artifact: `import` captures the X window,
    and WebKit composites to a GPU surface it cannot read. Booting with
    WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1 renders correctly every time. No app defect.
  - The P2-a author -> relaunch -> survives cycle. The authoring and the relaunch both happened on a
    cargo-build binary, so the frontend serving them was the main checkout's. The STORE path is the
    same code, and writes are re-proven packaged, but the author->relaunch cycle itself has NOT been
    re-run end to end on a packaged binary. Treat P2-a as: writes verified packaged, persistence
    cycle pending a re-run.

METHOD NOTE for whoever picks this up: build with `tauri build --debug --no-bundle`, never plain
`cargo build`, and confirm the origin before trusting any result:

  ls ~/.local/share/digital.compost.archie/localstorage    # must be tauri_localhost_0.*
  ss -ltnp | grep 5174                                     # must be nothing, or a port you own

--- STATUS 2026-07-26: P2-a PASSES, Flatpak PASSES, P2-b is UNREACHABLE on Linux ---

P2-a (author -> relaunch -> work survives): PASSES on a packaged debug build, clean profile, origin
confirmed tauri_localhost_0. Imported a 3-image folder into 2 exhibits, relaunched, both survive with
media and thumbnails intact. (An earlier claim of this was WITHDRAWN — it had been measured against a
cargo-build binary loading another checkout's dev server.)

FLATPAK (was Archie-7e2e's variable, the one this ticket calls catastrophic): PASSES. Built with
org.flatpak.Builder against GNOME 49, installed --user, booted under Xvfb. defaultLibraryRoot()
resolves correctly inside the sandbox to
~/.var/app/digital.compost.archie/data/digital.compost.archie/library. All store assertions pass, and
it wrote .archie-mirror.json (a dot-path), so the Archie-7b48 scope fix holds under the sandbox too.
The recorded blocker ("flatpak-builder MISSING") was stale — the Builder and both GNOME 49 runtimes
were already installed; the only real gap was that the manifest packages a RELEASE binary.

P2-b (migrate a real OPFS library): RUN, and it CANNOT BE COMPLETED ON LINUX. Method: build the
pre-flip binary (61d070a, the commit before b7a747e "mount the native folder as the resident store"),
author a distinctive exhibit, then boot current and watch the migration.

  pre-flip boots clean          window up, 6 exhibits, "Living in this browser", NO library/ folder
  create P2B-CANARY-OPFS        created, exhibit view opens
  RELAUNCH pre-flip             CANARY GONE. Only "New exhibit" + the 6 examples.
  storage/ throughout           8.0K — `salt` only. Never grew, before or after authoring.
  then boot current             library/ written; migrated.json ABSENT

opfs-to-folder.ts writes the marker ONLY on a real copy (no-source writes nothing), so the absent
marker is CORRECT — there was nothing to migrate. The pre-flip build never persisted to OPFS on this
WebKitGTK at all.

So: the migration's no-source path is verified; its COPY path is unexercised and unreachable here.
Completing P2-b needs a webview where OPFS actually persists (macOS/Windows). RECOMMEND SPLITTING:
close the Linux scope of this ticket on P2-a + Flatpak, and carry P2-b as its own platform-specific
ticket rather than leaving a release gate blocked on something this platform cannot produce.

The corollary is the strongest result of the exercise: the folder flip fixed a REAL Linux data-loss
bug. Pre-flip, authored work did not survive a relaunch at all. Post-flip it does. Same machine, same
webview, same profile path.

NEW GATES, both red-greened: scripts/desktop-smoke.sh (assertions: packaged origin, no 0-byte files,
no leftover .tmp-*, library.json parses, optional MIN_ASSETS), scripts/desktop-boot.sh
(orchestration), and .github/workflows/desktop.yml. NOTE THE SCOPE: it BOOTS, it does not DRIVE — so
it covers the write-path class and NOT ingest.


--- ORGANISED 2026-07-26 ---
Was mapless. Now labelled map:tend-tauri and carries batch:packaged-drive — the shared label for every
question that can only be answered by booting ONE packaged/Flatpak build (this ticket's 7 rows, Archie-e47d
target=_blank behaviour, Archie-7e2e tauri-plugin-opener under the Flatpak sandbox, and the undriven native
dialog flows still open on Archie-a09d). Do them in one session, not four. Archie-623e (the desktop release
gate) now DEPENDS on this ticket — 623e says close-when-a09d-signs-off, and this is the run that signs it off.

title: The cite trigger occludes the first tag chip on the AV note card
description:
## Question

The cite trigger sits on top of the AV note card's FIRST tag chip, so that tag cannot be clicked with a mouse. Found 2026-07-26 by the driven test that landed `onopenfinder` on the AV surface — the click timed out with `<button aria-label="Cite this view" class="cite-trigger"> subtree intercepts pointer events`.

## The measurement (sampler → audio object → cue t=180,220, 1280x720)

| element | box x | box y | elementFromPoint at its centre |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.cite-trigger` | 20 – 100 | 556 – 588 | — |
| `#cadence` chip | 38 – 122 | 560 – 572 | **SPAN.lbl** (the cite label) — OCCLUDED |
| `#transcript` chip | 134 – 245 | 560 – 572 | BUTTON.tag, isSelf true — clickable |

**62px of horizontal overlap.** The second chip clears the trigger only because it happens to start at x=134; a shorter first tag, or a third chip wrapping to a second row, changes which tags are reachable. This is not one unlucky fixture — it is a layering fault whose visible extent depends on tag text length.

## Why nothing caught it

The same reason `.claude/rules/osd-overlay-wrapper.md` exists: the control RENDERS, it is visible, enabled and stable, and every synthetic click on it works. Only a real driven `click()` hit-tests. svelte-check sees a correctly typed, correctly bound prop. The chip was reachable by keyboard throughout.

Note the shape: this was found by the FIRST test ever to drive that path. The chips only started rendering when `ExhibitView` threaded `onopenfinder` (MediaPlayer gates them on the handler rather than shipping inert chips), so the occlusion has been latent behind an absent control rather than shipped-and-unnoticed.

## Relationship to the dock ruling — check before fixing

The human ruled 2026-07-26 that canvas chrome DOCKS out of the canvas (see Archie-de08 / Archie-c30a). Establish first whether `.cite-trigger` is inside the scope of that work:

- If the cite trigger is part of the chrome being docked, this defect **disappears with it** and this ticket closes as obviated — do not fix it twice.
- If the cite trigger is scoped as note-card chrome rather than canvas chrome, it needs its own answer, and the AV surface is the case that proves it: an AV object has **no canvas chrome at all** (that is why Archie-7b86 withheld collapse on its aside), so whatever positions the trigger here is not the canvas chrome layer.

The second is the likelier reading and is why this is filed separately rather than folded into de08.

## Verify

A real driven click on EVERY tag chip on the AV note card opens the finder pre-scoped to that tag, and `elementFromPoint` at each chip's centre returns the chip. Not a synthetic click — it passes against the broken code.

The existing test (`apps/viewer/e2e/av-surface.spec.ts`, "a tag chip on a time-ranged note opens the finder ALREADY SCOPED to that tag") deliberately drives the SECOND chip, with the measurement above recorded at the call site, so it proves the wire without being blocked by this. When this is fixed, move it to the first chip and assert both.
closeReason:
CLOSES AS OBVIATED BY THE DOCK — not fixed, and the distinction matters. Merged in wave 2. Ledger: ledgers/FIX-av-surface-2026-07-27.md.

RE-MEASURED ON A CLEAN TREE BEFORE ANY EDIT, on this ticket's exact route (#/sampler → audio → cue t=180,220, 1280x720):

  .cite-trigger   y 556-588  →  y 641-673
  .note-pop ends at y 592; .chrome-dock begins at y 592
  elementFromPoint at BOTH chip centres now returns BUTTON.tag tag-btn (was SPAN.lbl on the first)
  a real driven click() on the FIRST chip opens the finder with #cadence pressed

THE OVERLAP DID NOT GO AWAY — IT GREW, 62px → 78px. It stopped MATTERING, because the card and the bar are now flow siblings rather than one floating over the other. A fix aimed at the overlap would have been solving a non-problem, which is exactly why the ticket said re-measure before fixing.

THE TICKET'S SECOND READING IS FALSE. It proposed the defect might be note-card chrome needing its own fix independent of layout. It is not; the layering was the whole cause.

INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED BY INJECTION. Re-floating .cite-trigger to its pre-dock box reproduced '#cadence is covered by SPAN.lbl' — THE SAME ELEMENT THIS TICKET RECORDED, from geometry alone. That one probe confirms two things at once: the original measurement was right, and the dock is what removed it.

The spec now hit-tests EVERY chip and drives both, with the before/after table at the call site — so a regression in the dock's flow-sibling arrangement will surface here rather than silently restoring the occlusion.

title: Deposit copy has no within-exhibit search (narrative IS present — original claim was wrong)
description:
CORRECTION (2026-07-26): the original filing claimed the embed drops NARRATIVE reading. That was wrong — it was measured against a branch base 82 commits behind main. Main's packages/archie-viewer HAS narrative: narrative.ts + narrative.test.ts, mounted lazily from element.ts (commit 26c2a59, 'embed parity', Archie-f90d/c314). Deposit copies render narrative readings correctly.

What IS genuinely absent from the embed: within-exhibit SEARCH (no minisearch, no SearchOverlay equivalent). archie-ux Q-3 states search is a built-in feature of the published Viewer, so an offline deposit copy is missing a documented capability.

Priority LOWERED to Low. Unlike the narrative claim, this understates the artifact rather than misrepresenting the author's work — a reader without search still sees everything that was authored, they just cannot query it. Weigh against the cost: minisearch in a bundle already at ~932KB raw / 274KB gz.

If taken: the index must sit behind the same lazy boundary as the reader — eagerGzKB (the CDN entry's page-load closure) must not move. Gate: node build.mjs --check.

Shipped mitigation: the Publish card names the limit — 'Search isn't in it — that needs the full Viewer.'
closeReason: MERGED into Archie-1820 (the embed's four DEFER-tracked capabilities — note media, reading sheet, cite hovercards, SEARCH). This ticket had narrowed to exactly 1820's search row, so two tickets tracked one work item. Its full content — the narrative-claim correction (the original filing was measured 82 commits behind main; narrative IS present), the severity argument, the shipped Publish-card mitigation, and the eagerGzKB constraint — is now carried in 1820's body under 'MERGED IN'. Nothing lost.

title: Make the Astro viewer exportable (Q-3 revisit)
description:
User-gated 2026-07-26 to REVISIT Q-3 (docs/decisions/archie-linkability.md), against the
recommendation to accept it. Q-3 as shipped says a self-contained export ships <archie-viewer>,
never the Astro viewer app.

WHY IT IS THAT WAY TODAY
apps/viewer's [slug].astro derives its routes at BUILD time from public/published/exhibits.json
(getStaticPaths). A built viewer therefore only knows the exhibits that existed when it was built,
so it cannot travel with an arbitrary library. packages/archie-viewer (the embed) has no such
coupling, which is why the deposit copy uses it.

WHAT REVISITING ACTUALLY REQUIRES
1. A RUNTIME route source for apps/viewer, replacing build-time baking. This is the load-bearing
   change; everything else follows from it.
2. A decision about the SECOND reader. The embed and the Astro viewer are two independent readers
   of the same tree. Putting the Astro app on the export path means both must stay behaviourally
   equivalent, or the deposit copy and the hosted site diverge.
3. Size: the deposit copy is currently ~274.5KB gz for the whole reader. An Astro build is a
   multi-file tree, so a single-file export would need a different inlining strategy entirely
   (the current one base64s ONE bundle into ONE html).

WHAT IS UNAFFECTED MEANWHILE
The shipped deposit copy keeps working; the embed remains the export vehicle until this lands.
Nothing is blocked on this ticket.

NOT SCHEDULED. Sized before starting — item 3 in particular may make the single-file form
impossible, in which case the honest outcome is to re-accept Q-3 with that measurement attached.

--- ORGANISED 2026-07-26 ---
Was mapless (labels viewer/export/decision only). Filed under map:published-tree as a grilling: the Q-3
revisit is the same question Archie-e09d prototypes from the other side — e09d Candidate A ships the
<archie-viewer> element into the tree, this ticket asks whether the Astro viewer could be the exported
thing instead. Now DEPENDS on e09d deliberately: the revisit should be judged against e09d's real numbers
(bundle, build shape, what a static host actually needs), not re-argued from first principles.
closeReason: DECIDED 2026-07-27 (A4): no — keep the <archie-viewer> embed as the self-contained export artifact. Maintainer-gated explicitly ('babe - no full viewer export'). The Astro app derives its routes at BUILD time from public/published/exhibits.json, so exporting it means shipping a build step; the embed is the portable artifact and the Astro app is the HOSTED experience. Q-3 as originally shipped stands.

title: Desktop writes ALL fail: capability manifest omits fs:allow-rename (TauriFilesystem commits via rename)
description:
The desktop capability manifest (src-tauri/capabilities/default.json) does not grant
fs:allow-rename. TauriFilesystem commits EVERY durable write with a same-directory temp-then-rename
(packages/render-core/src/fs/tauri.ts:182 — bridge.rename(tmp, this.path), the atomicity guarantee
.claude/rules/tauri-fs-seam.md exists to preserve). Tauri v2 denies any command not granted by a
capability, so the rename is refused and every file write fails at its commit point.

MEASURED on a native debug build (2026-07-26, first boot, clean {appDataDir}/library):

  18 directories created   (mkdir IS granted)
   4 files, 0 with content (every file 0 bytes, incl. ingested .jpg assets)
  library.json             0 bytes
  library.json.corrupt     0 bytes  <- snapshotIfUnparseable fired on the empty file it just wrote
  no .tmp-N leftovers      <- close() cleaned up after the rename threw

The UI surfaced it honestly but non-fatally: header showed "Retry save" and "Library details
couldn't be stored. Try again, or save your library as a new copy to be safe." The app looks alive
and loses 100% of authored work.

RED-GREEN, one line, nothing else changed:
  before  library.json = 0 bytes,      header "Retry save" + error banner
  after   library.json = 21,606 bytes, header "Saved", banner gone
Adding only "fs:allow-rename" flipped it. Cause, not correlation.

Also added: fs:allow-stat. apps/studio/src/tauri-fs.ts:42 calls fs.stat (backing FsFile.size and the
stat-sized lazy getFile). Required by code inspection; NOT independently red-greened — the asset path
that would exercise it is blocked behind a separate stuck-ingest symptom (see below). Both identifiers
are validated by the build: tauri errors at compile time on an unknown permission identifier, and both
cargo builds succeeded.

WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT — worth recording, it is the repo's own recurring shape:
fs/tauri.test.ts proves TauriFilesystem over a node:fs conformance bridge. node:fs has no permission
system, so rename always succeeds there. The suite answers "are the filesystem semantics right" and
never "is the command permitted in the packaged app". Same family as .claude/rules/bound-fetch-defaults.md
(Node more permissive than the browser) and svelte-no-typecheck-net (a gate proves it compiled, never
that the output carries anything). NOTHING headless can see this class — it needs the real webview.

SUGGESTED GATE: a check that every method on TauriFsBridge has a matching fs:allow-* in
capabilities/default.json. The bridge surface is a closed set (readFile, writeFile, open, rename,
mkdir, readDir, remove, exists, stat) and the manifest is JSON — this is a cheap, derived,
non-hand-maintained check, so it cannot rot the way a hand-listed reference does.

STILL OPEN (separate symptom, do not fold in): media ingest sits at "Adding <file> 1 of 1" and no
asset ever reaches disk, across boots and after both permissions were added. It replays a DIFFERENT
queued file each launch, which points at stale pending-ingest state persisted from an older session
rather than the write path. Needs its own look.

--- CORRECTION 2026-07-26: part of the first evidence set was measured against ANOTHER CHECKOUT ---

`tauri build --debug --no-bundle` bakes `frontendDist` (the packaged origin). A plain `cargo build`
does NOT — it bakes `devUrl`, i.e. http://localhost:5174. After the first build I rebuilt twice with
plain `cargo build` to pick up the capability edits, and those binaries loaded the dev server that was
already listening on 5174 — running from /mnt/Ghar/.../Archie/apps/studio, the MAIN checkout, not this
worktree. I was driving someone else's frontend without knowing it. This is exactly the hazard in
.claude/rules/viewer-e2e-shared-port.md ("a run whose port ownership you cannot establish is
unverified, not passed"), reached by a different route: not a reused server, but a build flag that
silently selects one.

The tell, and it is unambiguous — WebKit names its localStorage file after the ORIGIN:

  profile used for boot 1 + later boots   tauri_localhost_0.localstorage  AND  http_localhost_5174.localstorage
  profile used for the "clean" run        http_localhost_5174.localstorage ONLY

WHAT STANDS:
  - The total write failure. Boot 1 ran on the properly packaged binary (tauri_localhost_0 origin):
    18 directories, 4 files, ZERO bytes of content. Valid.
  - The fix. Re-measured on a REBUILT packaged binary (origin confirmed tauri_localhost_0) against a
    freshly deleted profile: library.json 21,606 bytes, 0 zero-byte files. Both sides of the A/B are
    now packaged builds of THIS worktree, differing only in the permission.
  - The capability audit itself is Rust-side and origin-independent, and it is now gated in CI by
    scripts/check-tauri-capabilities.mjs (red-greened: removing fs:allow-rename exits 1).

WHAT DOES NOT STAND, AND WAS WITHDRAWN:
  - The "stale ingest queue replaying on every boot" and the mystery BHC006_GMT_PN_* exhibits. Those
    were the MAIN checkout's live dev-session state reached through the dev server, not a defect in
    this tree, and not stale state. The real ingest defect is Archie-ce7a (webkitdirectory picks a
    file under WebKitGTK).
  - The "blank window on relaunch". That was a SCREENSHOT artifact: `import` captures the X window,
    and WebKit composites to a GPU surface it cannot read. Booting with
    WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1 renders correctly every time. No app defect.
  - The P2-a author -> relaunch -> survives cycle. The authoring and the relaunch both happened on a
    cargo-build binary, so the frontend serving them was the main checkout's. The STORE path is the
    same code, and writes are re-proven packaged, but the author->relaunch cycle itself has NOT been
    re-run end to end on a packaged binary. Treat P2-a as: writes verified packaged, persistence
    cycle pending a re-run.

METHOD NOTE for whoever picks this up: build with `tauri build --debug --no-bundle`, never plain
`cargo build`, and confirm the origin before trusting any result:

  ls ~/.local/share/digital.compost.archie/localstorage    # must be tauri_localhost_0.*
  ss -ltnp | grep 5174                                     # must be nothing, or a port you own
closeReason: FIXED and on origin/main. fs:allow-rename (+ fs:allow-stat) granted in src-tauri/capabilities/default.json. Red-green proven on packaged builds both sides: library.json 0 bytes -> 21,606 bytes, header 'Retry save' -> 'Saved'. Gated two ways so it cannot regress: scripts/check-tauri-capabilities.mjs derives the required permission list from the TauriFsBridge interface (CI unit-scripts), and .github/workflows/desktop.yml boots the packaged binary and asserts what it wrote (red-greened: permission removed => 'library.json never became non-empty', exit 1).

title: Desktop: the media-folder picker selects a FILE, not a folder (webkitdirectory is unsupported in WebKitGTK)
description:
USER-REPORTED 2026-07-26: "the folder picker only picks a file in the desktop build".

ROOT CAUSE (read, not guessed). CreateExhibitDialog.svelte:716 `pickFolder()` does `dirEl?.click()`,
and `dirEl` is `<input type="file" webkitdirectory>` (CreateExhibitDialog.svelte:903). `webkitdirectory`
is a Chromium/WebKit-browser affordance; WebKitGTK's file chooser does NOT implement directory
selection on it, so the control degrades to an ordinary single-FILE picker. The desktop user picks a
file where the flow expects a folder.

This is very likely the same defect as the "stuck ingest" symptom recorded on Archie-91e7: the media
add sits at `Adding "<file>" 1 of 1` forever with 0 media items and no asset on disk. One file where a
folder tree was expected is exactly the shape that produces "1 of 1".

THE APP ALREADY HAS THE RIGHT DOOR, and this path does not use it. `tauri-fs.ts:58 pickTauriFolder()`
wraps `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog` `open({ directory: true })` — the native directory dialog — and
`folder-backend.ts:38-42 pickFolderBinding()` is the in-repo precedent for branching on it:

    if (isTauri()) { const path = await pickTauriFolder(); ... }
    const handle = await pickFolder();   // browser FSA fallback

So the fix is to give the ingest picker the same isTauri() branch the project-binding picker already
has. Two surfaces picking folders by two different mechanisms is the actual defect; one of them was
simply never taught about the desktop.

THE WRINKLE, AND ITS DONOR. `applyFolderFiles(files: File[])` (CreateExhibitDialog.svelte:469) consumes
browser `File` objects, and the grouping/naming logic reads `webkitRelativePath || name` to know which
first-level subfolder each file came from. A native path walk yields no `File` objects. This is already
solved in this repo for the drag-and-drop path: folder-drop.ts:42-45 notes that `webkitRelativePath` is
a plain own property (not prototype-locked) and does
`Object.assign(new File(...), { webkitRelativePath })`. The desktop implementation should follow
folder-drop.ts exactly — walk the directory over the TauriFsBridge, construct Files, assign the
relative path — rather than inventing a third shape.

Memory cost is the open design question: folder-drop already materialises whole files in memory, so a
native walk is at parity with an existing shipped path, but a large media folder is the case to think
about before writing it.

GATE. jsdom cannot see this (no file chooser, no WebKitGTK), and neither can svelte-check or the unit
suites — the failure is a platform capability difference in the packaged webview. It needs the same
kind of driven check as the rest of the desktop surface. At minimum, a unit-level assertion that the
desktop branch calls pickTauriFolder() and never touches `dirEl`.

Found while driving the native build for Archie-9ece. NOT yet fixed.
closeReason: FIXED and on origin/main, verified by driving the packaged app. Desktop now takes the native directory dialog via the same isTauri() branch folder-backend.ts:39 uses; folder-native.ts walks the tree into the File[] the existing pure planner consumes, filtering with folder-import.ts's own predicates BEFORE reading bytes (a browser File is a lazy disk reference, bridge.readFile is not). Driving it exposed a SECOND defect fixed with it: Object.assign on webkitRelativePath throws in JavaScriptCore, which had also been breaking drag-and-drop folder import and the flatten path — see webkit-relative-path.ts. Measured on the packaged build: 'Added 3 files to 2 exhibits', correct subfolder grouping, and both exhibits survive a relaunch.

title: Published tree as the product
description:
## Notes

Charting decisions (2026-07-26): ONE map covers the broken GitHub-push publish AND the next-level program — shared spine: the published tree is the product. The /test/ fix commits to FULL self-replicating publish (rank 8), not a minimal link fix. All four idea clusters ticketed: publish trust, citation wedge, pull-merge probe, institutional pack.

Source material: docs/research/next-level-2026-07-26.md — 12 ranked ideas with verified file evidence, four themes, and five anti-ideas (standing guidance: no general IIIF-viewer mode for the embed, no in-browser Whisper, no auto-deposit, no mirror failover, no CSV round-trip as the lock-in proof).

Skills each session should consult: /prototype (prototype tickets), /grilling + /domain-modeling (grilling tickets), run-app (browser verification). Binding repo rules: perf-measure-the-flow (publish-pipeline changes must move scripts/perf/publishrun.mjs; ratchet wins), archie-viewer-eager-closure (embed eagerGzKB gate), render-core-data-integrity (marker-last multi-file writes), untrusted-archive-open-seam, metadata-rights-keyed-writebacks. CI reader-payload budget guards published-page weight. Grep with -a (NUL-byte hazard); .claude/worktrees/ holds ~35 stale checkouts whose grep hits are noise.

Standing constraints: static/no-server/open-standards identity is load-bearing; solo maintainer — first steps sized days, not months; citation grammar strictly additive (#note-<logicalId> is frozen by test, decision P-1); Issue 13 (identity read-only → "anonymous") degrades the who-dimension everywhere — ship without it, never block on it.

## Decisions so far

- Trace the GitHub-push base URL: why archie.demo shipped (Archie-d6ad) — Studio hands publishLibrary the AUTHORING namespace as if it were a deploy origin (App.svelte:1932 → seed-data.ts:33 → working.ts:38 WORKING_IRI_BASE); the real Pages URL is computed and shown on screen but only AFTER the tree is baked (deploy-flows.svelte.ts:158 projects, :174 computes) — and baseUrl double-duties as the annotation-target namespace, so a naive swap silently drops every annotation (site-geo.test.ts). All three sinks affected (GH/zip/folder). 51 URL emitters inventoried in three tiers. Four independent defects found and ticketed. Full evidence: ledgers/TRACE-publish-base-url-2026-07-26.md

## Fog

- Open in Archie (rank 5): inbound URL grammar + the button on other people's pages — sharpens once self-replicating publish decides what a tree contains.
- HTR last mile (rank 6): ALTO adapter → parallel-text edition.
- Succession proof (rank 7): versioned format spec + independent reference reader.
- Overlay Readings (rank 9): publish a Reading targeting an institution's canvases, not Archie's.
- Bilingual editions (rank 12): WADM Choice bodies, language-aware reading.
- Published-id registry (citations.json carried through merges) — the hard tail of version-anchored citation.
- Pull-merge productization (Studio UI over MergeReview, per-host CORS strategy, Tauri native-http fallback) — pending the probe's verdict.
- History-sidecar growth on heavily-edited notes: lazy-fetch vs budget; watch the CI payload ratchet.
- Issue 13 identity capture — unlocks "who" in citation surfaces, Zotero authors, attributed classroom merges.
- Zenodo round-trip: prefill zenodo.json from DC metadata; stamp the returned DOI back into JSON-LD on the next publish.
- Republish hygiene: what a SECOND publish to the same repo must do about ids minted under a previous base (rewrite? redirect? refuse?) — sharpens once the destination-URL decision lands.
- Orphaned history page seen live in micahchoo/test: annotations/history/01KYFYYBSC….json targets a canvas absent from the manifest — unexplained; may be a publish-time filter bug or stale working state.
- Whether the working IRI namespace should be per-library/opaque (urn:) rather than a fake https origin, now that the two roles are being split.

title: Trace the GitHub-push base URL: why archie.demo shipped
description:
## Question

The Studio GitHub push to micahchoo/test baked https://archie.demo into canonical, og:url, JSON-LD, and IIIF manifest ids, and linked micahchoo.github.io/Archie/viewer/ with no ?src=. Trace the pipeline (packages/render-core/src/publish/site.ts, static-pages.ts, serialize.ts; the Studio publish dialog/flows): where does baseUrl enter, what defaults when unset, and inventory EVERY baked URL as absolute-vs-relative (canonical, og, JSON-LD, manifest/canvas/annotation ids, asset+tile refs, the viewer link). For each: what it needs to be destination-aware (https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/) or relative-first. Asset: a markdown trace with file:line refs, linked from the close reason.
closeReason:

title: Prototype self-replicating publish: the tree carries its own viewer
description:
## Question

Cheapest working shape for a pushed tree that serves its own interactive viewer. Candidate A: emit viewer.html + the archie-viewer Web Component bundle (packages/archie-viewer/dist) into the tree, src pointing at its own base — ADR-0021 says the embed already accepts a published-tree base URL; check bundle weight (archie-viewer-eager-closure rule / eagerGzKB), fully-local operation (no CDN), and hash-route deep links. Candidate B: build the Astro viewer app base-configurable/relative and copy it in. Prototype both far enough to compare weight, build coupling, and deep-link behavior; serve locally AND from a scratch GitHub Pages repo. Decide the shape — feeds the /test/ republish.

CONSTRAINT from the base-URL trace (Archie-d6ad, 2026-07-26): the static pages' viewer links are emitted from viewerBase with NO back-reference — static-pages.ts:133 (library), :202 (exhibit, `{viewerBase}#/{slug}` — which resolves against the CANONICAL library's slugs, not the pushed tree's), :217 (section), :192 (note), plus in-prose cites via link.ts:84-91. Under self-replicating publish these must point at the tree's OWN viewer. Decide what viewerBase becomes for a self-contained tree (relative "viewer.html"? still absolute for the hosted fallback? both?) as part of this prototype.
---

## FINDINGS (2026-07-27, branch `proto/self-replicating-publish` off d15b928)

**Candidate A works. Decided. Candidate B not built — and the prototype produced the argument against it rather than a preference.**

Commits: `c6214e0` emission + 11 tests · `81ad0fb` Chromium drive · `c6deb52` ledger.
Full evidence: `ledgers/PROTO-self-replicating-publish-2026-07-27.md`.

### What ships

`publishLibrary` gained one injected option, `getViewerBundle` (same shape as `getAsset`/`tileObject` — core cannot read the embed's dist). Given it, the tree gains `_viewer/` (the 9-file esbuild output), a `viewer.html` shell, and `.nojekyll`; every page's viewer link is re-pointed TREE-RELATIVELY (`viewer.html` from the root, `../viewer.html#/{slug}` from an exhibit page). Absent = byte-identical output, pinned by a test; every existing caller omits it, so the committed published tree is unchanged.

### Drive (bare static server, own port, killed on exit)

10/10 PASS, repeated 4/4. Gallery renders from the tree's own bundle · deep-zoom canvas mounts from the tree's own tiles · a REAL `page.mouse.click()` on a region opens its note · `viewer.html#/{slug}` deep-links · the archival page's relative link, followed by clicking it, reaches the viewer · zero external SCRIPT requests.

RED (`--no-viewer`, same tree, bundle omitted): **5/10** — gallery, canvas, note-click, deep link and archival link all go dark.

### viewerBase decision (the ticket's open question)

**Tree-relative, computed per page depth, and it OVERRIDES a hosted `viewerBase` when both are given** — a self-contained tree that still links out is not self-contained. The shell computes its library base from `new URL(".", location.href)` and its route from `location.hash` at runtime, so nothing is baked and the tree survives being moved, mirrored, renamed, or served from a subpath.

**DEFERRED, structurally:** in-prose cites keep the hosted `viewerBase`. A cite is rewritten ONCE into the note body, and that body is served to two documents at different depths (the exhibit page AND `viewer.html`, which reads it out of `annotations.json`) — no single relative string is correct for both. Closing it needs a root-absolute path derived from `baseUrl`'s pathname, which reintroduces the base coupling this design removes. Stated at the call site in `site.ts`.

### file:// — NO, on two independent measured grounds

1. Opaque origin: the ES **module** script is CORS-refused, so the element never upgrades.
2. Switching to the IIFE build (`dist-single`) fixes (1) and **does not help** — a classic script's `fetch("./exhibits.json")` is also refused ("URL scheme file is not supported"). A published tree is inherently multi-file.

So a self-replicating tree **requires an HTTP origin, always**. That case belongs to the single-file export (`apps/studio/src/single-file-export.ts`), which inlines everything. Two artifacts, not one gap.

### Weight (exact bytes, green vs --no-viewer on the same fixture)

21,112,539 B / 544 files → 22,094,510 B / 555 files = **+981,971 B (+959 KB), +11 files**. **950,118 B (96.8%) is `_viewer/`**; `viewer.html` is 1,168 B; `.nojekyll` is 0. The residual ~31 KB is the 275 per-note/per-section viewer links the `--no-viewer` baseline omits (it is given no `viewerBase` at all).

Wire: `_viewer/` 927.8 KB raw / **275.5 KB gz** total — but **page load is 38.9 KB gz**, because the OSD reader chunk (228.4 KB gz) stays behind `element.ts`'s lazy boundary. That is the strongest argument for A over B.

### Gates

- CI **reader-payload budget: UNAFFECTED, structurally** — emission is opt-in, nothing in the repo passes `getViewerBundle`, `apps/viewer/public/published/` byte-unchanged, no Astro route references `_viewer/`. Nothing loosened.
- `node build.mjs --check`: ok eager 38.9→39.4, total 274.9→275.5, single 274.5→275.1 (pre-existing drift; the prototype consumes `dist`, it does not change the embed).
- `pnpm -r run typecheck` → `Scope: 6 of 7`, all Done, 0 errors. render-core vitest 98 files / **1271** tests (1260 before, +11). New suites repeated 5/5.

### Prior art correction (the first draft was wrong, and the correction is the useful part)

"No corpus system ships a viewer into its data tree" is **false**. quire does: `packages/11ty/_includes/components/head.js:62` loads a canvas-panel 1.0.68 bundle vendored at `packages/11ty/content/_assets/javascript/application/canvas-panel-web-components-1.0.68.js`. It is direct precedent for the bundle-in-the-tree move, and useful mainly for the DIVERGENCE: quire's path is ROOT-ABSOLUTE, pinning the built site to a deploy root — the exact coupling this design removes. So quire supports the bundle decision and **not** the tree-relative one. (quire also ships no `.nojekyll` while emitting `_assets/`; its docs point at Netlify, where Jekyll never runs.) clover-iiif and universalviewer were NOT opened for this question — an absence there is unestablished.

### NOT DONE — the one environment claim reasoned rather than measured

**No scratch GitHub Pages deploy.** Local only; the ticket asked for both. The `.nojekyll` reasoning (Pages runs Jekyll; Jekyll owns `_`-prefixed top-level directories) is documented platform behaviour plus a 0-byte guard, not a measurement. Cheap to close: push the baked tree to a scratch repo and load `viewer.html` — **with `.nojekyll` deliberately removed first**, so the trap is observed rather than assumed.

### Recommendation

Ship A; default it for the GitHub-push and folder sinks, probably **not** for `.archie.zip` (which is opened BY a viewer, so carrying one is a megabyte of redundancy). Order: (0) close the Pages hole; (1) wire `getViewerBundle` in Studio's publish flow as a LAZY import beside the existing `import("@render/archie-viewer/single?raw")` (`publish-flows.svelte.ts:418`) and check it against the root bundle ratchet; (2) decide the default per sink; (3) only then revisit the cite tension.


---

## CLOSED 2026-07-27 — prototype proven and merged; the live deploy belongs to Archie-8d3d

Merged c2f1ade. The tree carries its own viewer via opt-in getViewerBundle: 10/10 drive assertions
off a bare static server (repeated 4/4), red-green 5/10 with the bundle omitted, +959 KB tree weight
(96.8% = _viewer/), page-load wire unchanged at 38.9 KB gz. file:// is a structural NO (opaque-origin
CORS on module scripts AND on fetch of tree JSON) — that case stays with the single-file export.
Remainders → Archie-8d3d: Studio/script wiring of getViewerBundle at a real publish, the scratch
Pages deploy (.nojekyll behaviour measured, not documented), and the in-prose-cite depth tension.

title: Decide how publish learns its destination URL
description:
## Question

GitHub push can DERIVE its URL (owner/repo → https://owner.github.io/repo/). Folder and zip publishes have no URL at publish time. Decide per target: derive vs ask vs archie.config — and whether tree outputs go relative-first so one tree works at any base (what genuinely needs absolutes: og:url, JSON-LD, IIIF ids?). Depends on the base-URL trace ticket's inventory.

---

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (A1 · relative-first)

The tree uses RELATIVE paths everywhere except the four things that genuinely need an
absolute URL: `og:url`, JSON-LD `url`, IIIF ids, and the canonical link. A GitHub push derives its
base from `owner/repo`; folder and zip publishes leave it relative unless the author types one in.

WHY: one published tree then works at any base — served from a laptop, a USB stick, or a university
subdirectory — without republishing. The rejected alternative (always ask) puts a URL prompt in front
of someone who only wants a folder.

---

## IMPLEMENTATION NOTE 2026-07-27 — render-core already does this; the work is in Studio

Verified while re-reading Archie-19c5:

- `publishLibrary` already defaults `baseUrl` to `""` (`publish/site.ts:313`) and mints ids by raw
  concatenation, so **relative-first is already render-core's behaviour**. No change needed there.
- The annotation-drop that used to make a base change unsafe is **fixed** — `rebaseCanvasId`
  (`iiif/canvasid.ts:42`) re-mints head targets onto the publish base, tested at
  `site-geo.test.ts:48` and `site.test.ts:636-675`. So changing the base no longer costs annotations.

**The work is Studio's wiring, and it has two halves:**

1. Stop passing `BASE` (= `WORKING_IRI_BASE`, the authoring namespace) as the publish base —
   `App.svelte:203`, `:294`, `:1956`.
2. **Fix the projection ordering.** `openPublish` (`publish-flows.svelte.ts:377-397`) bakes the tree
   and caches it in `cachedSiteFs` BEFORE the user types a repo name; nothing re-projects afterwards.
   A correctly derived GitHub base would still arrive too late to reach the artifact. See
   `ledgers/TRACE-publish-base-url-2026-07-26.md`.

Archie-19c5 carries the same two halves — treat them as one change.

Archie-19c5 carries the same two halves — treat them as one change.


---

## IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-27 — branch `fix/publish-base-wiring` (e473b9e test, fac00f1 fix)

**H1 was already closed at `b240a0e`, by `7fafd2a` — do not re-do it.** `App.svelte:2035` passes
`publishBase: () => publishBaseFor(DEPLOY_LIBRARY_ID)` into `createPublishFlows`, and
`deploy/remembered.ts` resolves it to the library's live URL if it has ever deployed, else `""`.
Verified by test: a destination-less folder publish and a destination-less zip export both emit
relative ids with **zero** `archie.demo` anywhere in the artifact.

**The three surviving `baseUrl: BASE` call sites are CORRECT and were deliberately left alone.**
`App.svelte:203` (`createViewState`), `:294` (`createExhibitSession`), `:1956` (`createIngestFlows`)
are the AUTHORING identifier namespace — `view-state.svelte.ts:67,112` mint `target.source`,
`exhibit-session.svelte.ts:69` / `ingest-flows.ts:1157` pass it to `AnnotationSession.save`. That is
exactly `WORKING_IRI_BASE`'s stated contract, and it is the namespace `rebaseCanvasId` rebases FROM.
Changing them would break the grouping premise the annotation-drop fix rests on.

**H2 (the ordering) was real and is now fixed.** The path was the browser paste-a-PAT form —
`Publish.svelte:434` `onpublish` -> `publish-flows` `publish()` -> `collectSiteFiles()` ->
`cachedSiteFs`, the tree `openPublish()` baked before any repo name existed. (The desktop deploy path
was already correct: `deploy-flows.svelte.ts:150` computes `pagesUrlFor` before staging.) Now:

- `collectSiteFiles(withOriginals, baseOverride?)` keys the cache on `cachedSiteBase`, the base the
  cached tree was projected at — reuse only when the bases agree.
- `publish()` derives `pagesUrlFor(target.owner, target.repo)` and hands it in, so the projection runs
  at the destination. A same-base repeat push still reuses the warm tree (a retry does not re-tile).

**Red-green (`apps/studio/src/publish-base-wiring.test.ts`, 6 assertions over the REAL projection):**

| tree | result |
| --- | --- |
| `e473b9e` (test only, fix absent) | **3 failed / 3 passed** — pushed tree carried `voynich/manifest.json`, expected `https://micahchoo.github.io/test/voynich/manifest.json` |
| `fac00f1` (fix present) | **6/6 passed**, and **20/20** on repeat |
| `baseFor` forced back to `"https://archie.demo/"` | **6/6 failed** — so the relative-first assertions are not vacuous |

The push assertions read the ARTIFACT, not the exit code: the IIIF manifest `id`, the
`<link rel="canonical">`, the `og:url`, and the JSON-LD `url` all carry the derived Pages base, and no
file in the tree contains `archie.demo`.

**Gates:** `apps/studio` vitest **78 files / 993 tests passed**; `pnpm typecheck` (typescript-native)
exit 0; `svelte-check` **1190 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings**.

**Deliberately not done:** no author-typed base prompt (3504 A1 rejects it); no change to render-core;
`preflight.ts`'s "NOT CHECKED: base-path shape" note still stands (it names 3504 as the blocker — a
base-shape check is now writable, but it is a separate ticket).

title: Publish preflight: refuse to ship a broken tree
description:
## Question

Pre-push walk of the publish tree: Git LFS pointer files (Pages serves pointers — instant broken site), total size vs GitHub's 1 GB soft limit, 404.html presence, base-path shape. Hard-stop with a plain explanation. Start with LFS alone as the hard block — highest damage-to-effort. Lives in the studio publish flow over a shared walk in render-core publish.

--- ORGANISED 2026-07-26 ---
batch:publish-gates — this (pre-push refusal), Archie-fde8 (post-push verification) and Archie-8772
(rights-coverage report) are three gates on ONE surface: the publish dialog. Design the surface once —
what blocks, what warns, what merely reports — instead of bolting on three independent panels.
closeReason: Implemented in 83141b8. Pre-push walk lives in render-core/publish/preflight.ts (pure, Filesystem-only): LFS pointer files BLOCK (Pages serves the ~130-byte pointer text where a JPEG belongs — every image broken, nothing in the publish path errors), tree size over GitHub's 1 GB SOFT limit WARNS (the push still works and GitHub emails the owner, so blocking would refuse a publish that would have succeeded), missing 404.html WARNS. Findings render into the advisory surface the Publish dialog already has, not a new panel, and blocksPublish is the single predicate canPublish consults. The severity model is stated once at the top of preflight.ts and covers this ticket, Archie-8772 and (when it unblocks) Archie-fde8 — the batch's requirement that the call be made once. Base-path shape is deliberately NOT checked: it depends on Archie-3504's undecided answer, and the ticket's own 'start with LFS alone as the hard block' is this shape. Two tests were rewritten before shipping because they could not fail (a tautological severity filter; a size warn that never crossed its threshold). render-core 1243/1243, studio 977/977, studio e2e 12/12, svelte-check 0/0, tsc clean. NOT browser-driven: no fixture produces an LFS-pointer library, so the blocker's rendered path is unverified in a real browser — the prop chain was hand-verified through all five hops instead.

title: Post-publish verification: fetch the live site back
description:
## Question

After push: fetch {base}/archie.json (marker + generation match), one manifest, one asset/tile, index.html; report per-item pass/fail in the publish dialog. Converts "publish said success, site is broken" from discovered-by-a-colleague-in-3-weeks to discovered-in-10-seconds. Needs the destination URL (blocked on that decision). Desktop note: webview CSP/CORS may require the Tauri native-http bridge (tauri-csp rule).

--- ORGANISED 2026-07-26 ---
batch:publish-gates — the after half of the pair with Archie-0cd6 (before/preflight), plus Archie-8772
(rights coverage). One publish-dialog surface, one decision about block-vs-warn-vs-report.

--- IMPLEMENTATION NOTE 2026-07-27 ---
Shipped: `scripts/verify-publish.mjs <baseUrl-or-dir> [--generation <id>]` — fetches a published
tree back through the REAL render-core readers (readExhibitTree, HttpFilesystem/fsJsonSource — the
exact code path `<archie-viewer src=...>` and apps/viewer's hosted mode use, not a re-implementation)
and checks: archie.json marker present+valid (format/SCHEMA_VERSION), generation matches when
--generation is given, every gallery slug's manifest+annotations parse (readExhibitTree, with its
own incomplete-layer detection), per-slug annotation head counts, each exhibit's + the library's
index.html non-empty and carrying the right <h1> title, and a scan for the leaked `archie.demo`
authoring namespace across marker/gallery/manifests/index.html pages (regression net for the
Archie-3504 base-URL fix). Per-item tolerant (every check runs and prints, exit 1 on any failure)
and works against both a local directory and an http(s) base — same script, two byte sources.

Two files: verify-publish.mjs (plain node, resolves the target path + spawns vite-node) and
verify-publish-run.mts (the real logic; needs vite-node because @render/core's TS source and its
isomorphic-dompurify dep need a bundler present — plain node can't resolve either). vite-node is
already a workspace devDependency; apps/viewer's own gen-published.mts boots identically.

Red-green proven manually (not yet an automated test in this ticket): against a freshly generated
apps/viewer/public/published tree, in both directory and local-http-server mode, the unmodified tree
passes 27/27; a truncated manifest.json, a truncated exhibits.json, a deleted archie.json, an emptied
index.html, an injected "archie.demo" string, and a --generation mismatch each fail exactly the one
check they should, restored via `git restore --source=HEAD` between trials (tree was clean/committed
throughout — nothing lost). An unreachable http base degrades per-item rather than crashing.

NOT done, left for a follow-up: wiring this into the Studio publish dialog as a visible surface
(the batch:publish-gates note's "one publish-dialog surface" — Archie-0cd6/8772 already have their
severity model there; this ticket only delivers the standalone CLI gate) and running it against the
live micahchoo/test site (explicitly out of scope here — deferred to Archie-8d3d, which is blocked on
the site's own known breakage, not on this script).

---

## CLOSED 2026-07-27 — script merged; the two remainders have owners

`scripts/verify-publish.mjs` is on main (merge 7fbd87d), red-green proven across 8 injection classes
in both dir and http modes. The two flagged gaps are not this ticket's to hold open:
- Studio publish-surface wiring → Archie-c367 (the export surface owns what publish shows the user).
- Running it against the live micahchoo/test site → Archie-8d3d (it IS that ticket's acceptance gate).

title: Republish micahchoo/test as a self-contained working site
description:
## Question

Acceptance test for the publish-trust cluster. With the trace, the self-replication shape, and the destination-URL decision landed: republish the same library to micahchoo/test. The live site must serve its OWN interactive viewer of its OWN data — correct base URLs, working deep zoom, one working deep link — verified in a real browser (adapt the run-app recipe; link a screenshot). Record before/after in the close reason.

---

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (batch grill)

**REPUBLISH IS PRE-APPROVED WHEN GREEN.** Whoever lands the self-contained publish fix republishes
micahchoo/test WITHOUT a fresh ask — gated on post-publish verification (Archie-fde8's fetch-back)
passing locally first. It is a test repo and the current live tree is broken anyway. No fresh
go-ahead needed at the moment of push.


---

## DONE 2026-07-27 — republished, verified live (`d710f64`)

`https://micahchoo.github.io/test/` serves its own viewer of its own data. Ledger:
`ledgers/PUBLISH-test-republish-2026-07-27.md`. Repo commit `dadb030`.

**Before** (`f971414`): 1 exhibit `documents-d`, 1 object, 0 published heads, generation `36anb9`;
every absolute id at `https://archie.demo/` (canonical, og:url, IIIF canvas ids, collection);
`viewer.html`, `_viewer/`, `.nojekyll` all 404. Archival-only and unresolvable.

**No content substitution.** The brief allowed publishing seed content since the Studio OPFS library
is unreachable — unnecessary, because the published tree round-trips through `loadLibrary`
(`site.ts:857`). The user's own library went in and came out: 1 exhibit, 1 object, 412 DZI tiles,
4 annotation revisions.

**Live gates.** `verify-publish https://micahchoo.github.io/test/ --generation 1dj4fhz` -> **9/9,
exit 0**. Browser drive against the real host -> **6/6**, including deep zoom TILED (32 tiles served
2xx) and **0 external requests of any kind**. Pages served the new generation ~20 s after push.

**Local gates before pushing.** Bake 438 files / 8511272 bytes, generation `1dj4fhz`, no missing
assets or broken links. `verify-publish <dir>` 9/9. Drive 10/10, repeated **6/6** unchanged.
Red-greened both ways: pyramid deleted -> FAIL 9/10; `--no-viewer` -> FAIL 1/10.

**Two traps this hit, both caught by red-greening rather than by reading:**
- `loadLibrary` DROPS `tileSource` and `thumbnail` on the round trip (`site.ts:846-847`). Left
  dropped, the republish ships no deep zoom (5.4 MB flat master) and a dangling gallery cover — with
  every gate green. `scripts/republish-tree.mts` hands both back, re-using the existing pyramid.
- The drive's first "TILED" assertion counted tile REQUESTS and passed against a deleted pyramid;
  and serving the tree at 127.0.0.1 left its absolute IIIF ids pointing at production, so an early
  green was measured off the live broken site. Both fixed; see the ledger.

**`archie.demo` scan is 4, not 0** — all four in one file, all `target.source` on the four revisions
of `01KYFYYBSC9R42PBEK0HY0GQVP`, whose head carries `archie:deleted: true`. A tombstone, targeting an
object (`01KXZPZ55DVMB2DNHCKFWKFS4A`) that exists nowhere in the library at any origin. `rebaseCanvasId`
refuses it by its documented non-fuzzy contract, correctly: rewriting would forge a live-looking
pointer for a deleted note; deleting would destroy merge data. 0 occurrences on any served surface.

**`.nojekyll` — half measured.** WITH it present, Pages serves `_viewer/` (200, 31059 + 822106 bytes)
and the embed boots. The counterfactual e09d asked for (remove it, watch `_viewer/` disappear) is
**still open**: the probe push was denied by the permission system, correctly — republishing is not
licence to deliberately break the site. Needs an explicit go-ahead, ~2 min of degraded site, or a
scratch repo.

**Follow-up for Archie-fde8:** `verify-publish` check 7 is labelled "no occurrences anywhere in the
served tree" while its own detail says "scanned 5 file(s)" of 438 — it is scoped to the four
absolute-URL surfaces (good scope, overclaiming label) and did not see the tombstone's four.
