title: Pull-merge probe: is a published tree a mergeable remote?
description:
## Question

scripts/probe/pull-merge.mjs — publish the Voynich seed to a temp dir (reuse the scripts/perf/publishrun.mjs harness), serve it statically, construct new HttpFilesystem(base), run readAnnotations on {slug}/annotations, and print classifyLogical(local, remote, id) per logicalId against the local log. If merge classifications print, the whole feature is a dialog over MergeReview. Also test CORS against a real live tree (https://micahchoo.github.io/test/ works as a target). Deliver a verdict + findings doc.

## FINDINGS (2026-07-27, probe/pull-merge, d19043121347fa81b7445f9e20e6c74232a2f6cc)

Probe built and run end-to-end: scripts/probe/pull-merge.mjs (committed). Full output + analysis:
ledgers/PROBE-pull-merge-2026-07-27.md.

Publishes the Voynich seed (publishLibrary, pure — no browser needed) to a MemoryFilesystem, flattens
it to a real temp dir on disk, serves it with a plain node:http static server (deliberately no
Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, mimicking "most static hosts don't send one"), reads it back with
`new HttpFilesystem(base)` + `readAnnotations`, and classifies all 55 logicalIds against the local log
with `classifyLogical`.

PASS 1 (echo, unmutated local log): 55/55 "identical" — exact match against the tree it was published
from.
PASS 2 (one local note edited with appendEdit before reclassifying, same 55 ids, same remote log):
54/55 "identical", 1 "fast-forward" (local ahead) — proves the probe's output actually changes when
the input changes, not just prints a plausible classification regardless.

CORS: the local server sent NO ACAO header and the probe succeeded anyway — this is NOT evidence CORS
doesn't matter, it's because Node's fetch performs no CORS enforcement at all (browser-only policy).
Live check against https://micahchoo.github.io/test/ confirms the research doc's claim: GitHub Pages
sends `access-control-allow-origin: *` unconditionally. A browser-hosted Studio can pull-merge from
any GH-Pages-published tree with zero extra work; a non-ACAO static host blocks the browser fetch
outright, with the Tauri native-http bridge (Archie-fada, already used for images/info.json) as the
only known desktop-only escape hatch — same shape, not yet extended to this fetch.

VERDICT: Confirmed — the whole feature is a dialog over MergeReview. `HttpFilesystem` +
`readAnnotations` already read a real published tree over real HTTP with zero new code;
`classifyLogical(local, incoming, logicalId)` doesn't care that "incoming" came from `fetch` instead
of a dropped zip; and the classification output (`LogicalMergeResult` — identical / fast-forward /
conflict / only-local / only-incoming) is exactly the shape MergeReview's existing conflict-card UI
already consumes. What's NOT yet built: (1) a Studio UI surface that pastes a URL and feeds this
probe's steps into MergeReview instead of a zip's mergeLogs input, (2) the CORS edge for non-ACAO
hosts (real, confirmed above, GH Pages unaffected), (3) Issue 13 identity capture for attributed
classroom merges (already flagged in the research doc as a hard dependency, out of scope for this
probe). None of the three is a research question.

title: BagIt-shaped deposit export with fixity
description:
## Question

Emit a BagIt bag (bagit.txt, manifest-sha256.txt, bag-info.txt) from a published tree; validate with bagit-python (external validator as the test). Decide where hashing lives (publish-time vs export-time) and measure the cost at library scale via scripts/perf/publishrun.mjs — per the perf-measure-the-flow rule, the end-to-end number is the headline. Verified starting fact: zero hashing exists anywhere in the repo today.

## Findings (prototype, 2026-07-27) — branch `proto/bagit-fixity`, `3565a56` + `306372d`

**Answer to "where does hashing live": PUBLISH time, at the Filesystem seam.** `publishLibrary`
gains an opt-in `PublishOptions.fixity`; a `HashingFilesystem` decorator wraps the sink, so every
write site is covered without knowing it — including `writeStructure`'s, which lives in another
module. Export-time hashing was rejected on two grounds: it would mean a second full read of every
asset and tile, and `ZipStreamFilesystem` (the bounded-memory export sink) streams media straight
out and cannot be read back at all, so the bytes are only in hand DURING the write. The bag
consequently re-hashes nothing of the payload — it prefixes the tree's own manifest with `data/`
and hashes exactly two files publish could not cover (its own manifest, and the marker written
after it).

**Write ordering, proven by a test that records `close()` order:** `… → manifest-sha256.txt →
archie.json`, i.e. second-to-last and last. The marker stays the sole commit point
(render-core-data-integrity rule 1), so a tree torn between the two reads as having no marker and
is refused, rather than presenting as complete with a short manifest.

**Incremental correctness was designed in, and it is the part that would have shipped broken.**
`mergeFixity` carries the prior manifest's lines forward for files a scoped republish did not
rewrite (an out-of-scope exhibit; the skipped ~1 MB `_viewer/` bundle) and drops lines under paths
removed through the seam — which `HashingFilesystem` observes directly, so the removal list is not
re-derived from `PublishOptions`. The gate is an oracle that re-hashes the entire finished tree with
`node:crypto`: the manifest must equal that walk exactly, on the full path AND after an incremental
republish. Evidence the incremental path was really taken rather than a full rewrite sneaking in:
`a/index.html` changed, `b/index.html` and `_viewer/archie-viewer.js` did not.

**ADR-0020 agrees, it is not reversed.** That ADR rejected a hash or signature ON the marker (L2/L3)
because sealing and hand-editability are mutually exclusive and key distribution needs a server. A
separate file makes neither claim: it authenticates nothing (an attacker who can rewrite a payload
can rewrite the manifest beside it — same forgery cost as the marker), it catches ACCIDENTS (bit rot,
truncated transfer, a partial rsync, a file a static host dropped), and a legitimate hand-edit
invalidates one line rather than the artifact.

**Deposit shape: a separate EXPORT arrangement, per the charting.** A bag root would either break
every relative link in the published site or make the bag a second differently-shaped tree
maintained beside the first. `publish/bag.ts` writes payload under `data/` plus `bagit.txt`,
`manifest-sha256.txt`, `bag-info.txt` and `tagmanifest-sha256.txt` (that last written LAST — the
bag's own commit point). `bag-info.txt` derives `Source-Organization` from `dcterms:publisher`
falling back to the attribution credit, `Contact-Name` from `dcterms:creator`, and omits any field
it has no source for rather than inventing one. `Bagging-Date` is an injected parameter, never
`Date.now()` — two bags of the same library are byte-identical, asserted.

### External validator: bagit-python 1.9.0, VERDICT VALID

`pipx install bagit` succeeded in this environment, so this is an external verdict rather than a
hand-written claim. `scripts/bag-validate.mjs` is red-green by construction — every check runs
against the clean artifact, then the corrupted one, then the restored one:

```
built: tree 24 files / 22 manifest lines · bag 28 files, Payload-Oxum 30110.24
PASS  verify-publish: the published tree verifies — exit 0 · 22/22 verified, 0 bad
PASS  verify-publish: one truncated payload byte makes it FAIL, naming the file — exit 1
PASS  verify-publish: restoring the byte makes it PASS again
external validator: bagit-python version 1.9.0
PASS  bagit.py --validate: the deposit bag is a valid BagIt bag — exit 0 · "bag is valid"
PASS  bagit.py --validate: one FLIPPED payload bit (same size) makes it FAIL on the sha256, not the Oxum
PASS  bagit.py --validate: restoring the byte makes it valid again
6/6 checks passed
```

The bag tamper is a same-size BIT FLIP, not a truncation, and that distinction is load-bearing:
`bagit.py` validates `Payload-Oxum` first, so a truncation fails on the octet count and never
reaches a checksum — a green/red pair on a truncation would prove only that the byte total is
watched. The flip makes the SHA-256 in our manifest the only thing that can catch it, and
bagit-python's error names that file and both hashes. Note the file it names carries a SPACE in its
path (`data/quire-1/assets/folio 1r.jpg`), which is the RFC 8493 §2.1.3 encoding rules being
exercised rather than assumed. Counts reconcile: tree 24 files = 22 manifest lines + the manifest +
the marker; bag 28 files = 24 payload + 4 tag files; `payloadFiles` 24 matches the Oxum's stream
count.

### Perf — END-TO-END, N=3 per cell, attributed by DIFFERENCE

`node scripts/perf/publishrun.mjs` (a fixity axis was added to the existing bench rather than a new
microbenchmark, per perf-measure-the-flow). Totals in ms, `pooled` = the shipping tiling path:

| corpus | sink | fixity off (3 runs) | fixity on (3 runs) | delta (median) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 objects / 2 exhibits | opfs | 2224 · 2112 · 2234 | 2163 · 2153 · 2160 | **−1%** (below noise) |
| 10 objects / 2 exhibits | zip-stream | 1703 · 1679 · 1755 | 1799 · 1806 · 1739 | **+4%** |
| 70 objects / 10 exhibits | opfs | 13105 · 13024 · 13162 | 13522 · 13293 · 13437 | **+2.4%** (≈320 ms) |
| 70 objects / 10 exhibits | zip-stream | 10859 · 10881 · 11438 | 10937 · 11102 · 11379 | **+0.6%** (≈80 ms) |

Three of the twelve fixity runs came out FASTER than their paired baseline (−74, −60, −59 ms), which
is the honest reading of the result: the effect is at or below this bench's run-to-run noise. The
reason is structural rather than lucky — publish over a tileable corpus is ~99% tile encode (the
existing rows measure exactly that), so a SHA-256 over the same bytes is a rounding error against
work already being done. The headline is **fixity costs 0–4% end-to-end at library scale**, and the
sub-second corpus is where the relative cost is largest because there is less tiling to hide behind.

The one real cost is not time but memory, and it is recorded in `fs/hashing.ts`: WebCrypto has no
streaming digest, so a file's chunks are held until `close()`. Publish writes each file once, with
bytes the caller already holds, so this is one extra reference rather than a copy of the tree — but
a single multi-GB asset is momentarily referenced twice. A streaming digest would need a hand-rolled
SHA-256, which is a bigger claim than this buys.

### What shipped

- `packages/render-core/src/fs/hashing.ts` + test — the seam decorator, `sha256Hex` (WebCrypto,
  no import, verified on Node 24 against RFC 6234 vectors and `node:crypto`).
- `packages/render-core/src/publish/fixity.ts` + test — RFC 8493 line format, the LF/CR/% encoding
  rules, and `mergeFixity`.
- `packages/render-core/src/publish/bag.ts` + test — `writeBag` / `libraryToBagZip`.
- `packages/render-core/src/publish/site.ts` — `PublishOptions.fixity`, `PublishResult.fixity`.
- `packages/render-core/src/publish/site-fixity.test.ts` — the re-hash oracle, ordering, incremental.
- `scripts/verify-publish-run.mts` — the fixity check, extending the existing gate rather than a
  second verifier.
- `scripts/deposit-fixture.mts` + `scripts/bag-validate.mjs` — the red-green external gate.

Gates: render-core vitest **1342 passed** (baseline 1299 + 43 new), `pnpm -r run typecheck`
**Scope: 6 of 7 workspace projects**, 6 done, 0 errors.

### Not done / next

- Nothing wires this into Studio yet — no "Deposit a copy" button, no `fixity: true` at any app call
  site. The primitive and its gate exist; the UI affordance is a separate slice.
- `scripts/bag-validate.mjs` is not in CI. It needs bagit-python on the runner and exits 2 when the
  validator is absent (deliberately not 0 — an unrun gate is not a passed one), so adding it means
  adding a `pipx install bagit` step.
- A bag from an ALREADY-PUBLISHED tree on disk is not implemented — only library → bag. A tree → bag
  path would need a Filesystem walk that re-reads bytes, which is the export-time hashing this
  design avoided.


---

## CLOSED 2026-07-27 — fixity + bag merged and externally validated

Merged (render-core 1358/1358 on the combined tree). manifest-sha256.txt written at the sink seam
(HashingFilesystem) second-to-last, marker last (order-pinned by test); incremental republish gated
by a node:crypto whole-tree oracle; bag validated by bagit-python 1.9.0 red-green 6/6 including a
same-size bit flip only the checksum can catch; fixity time cost at or below bench noise (N=3/cell,
attributed by difference). Remainders with owners: Studio "Deposit a copy" wiring + fixity flag at
app call sites → Archie-c367 (export surface); bag-validate.mjs in CI needs a pipx install step —
left as a note, not silently added.

title: Rights coverage as a computed publish gate
description:
## Question

At publish, compute which exhibits/objects lack rights / requiredStatement (keyed RightsFields only — metadata-rights-keyed-writebacks rule) and surface a coverage report in the publish dialog (and into the tree?). Decide warn vs hard gate inside the ticket.

--- ORGANISED 2026-07-26 ---
batch:publish-gates — the warn-vs-hard-gate call here is the SAME call Archie-0cd6 (preflight) and
Archie-fde8 (post-publish verification) make. Decide it once for the publish dialog, not three times.
closeReason: Implemented in 83141b8 alongside Archie-0cd6, per the batch requirement to decide the surface once. DECISION: rights coverage is a REPORT, never a gate — which items carry a licence is a curatorial decision, and a tool that blocked on it would assert an editorial policy it has no standing to assert. rightsCoverage() reads the two KEYED rights properties only and never metadata (metadata-rights-keyed-writebacks): descriptive metadata describes a work, it does not licence it, and counting it would report coverage the library does not have. EITHER field covers a level — a credit alone is a real if partial rights statement, so requiring both would report gaps on libraries that made a deliberate choice. Gaps name WHERE they are (library title / exhibit slug / slug+object label) so the report is actionable. Surfaced in the Publish dialog's existing advisory surface with a neutral rule rather than a warning stripe, since nothing is wrong. Covered by 19 unit tests including the keyed-read rule and the never-gates property.

title: Accessibility as a measured build output
description:
## Question

axe-core pass over the published static pages (and the viewer shell, once self-replicating publish lands) in CI: record a baseline, fail on regression — same ratchet discipline as the payload budget. Decide which pages, which ruleset, and where in checks.yml.
closeReason: Implemented in 99b937a. scripts/a11y-check.mjs runs axe-core over the COMMITTED published static pages with a per-page baseline in scripts/a11y-baseline.json, wired into checks.yml beside the bundle ratchets as 'pnpm a11y:check'. THE THREE DECISIONS: (1) WHICH PAGES — the published tree (landing + every exhibit index.html), because that is the artifact in question and it is checked in, so the gate needs no build and is deterministic; the viewer shell stays out until self-replicating publish lands, since its e2e already carries a11y specs and two sources for one fact is how they drift. (2) WHICH RULESET — WCAG 2.1 A+AA, what procurement actually names; axe's best-practice tag deliberately EXCLUDED because it is advice not a standard, and a gate failing for unagreed reasons gets switched off rather than fixed. (3) WHERE — its own checks.yml step. IT FOUND A REAL DEFECT ON THE FIRST RUN: 676 violating nodes across all 8 pages, all color-contrast, from exactly two tokens in static-pages.ts's STYLE — #6B7D6A at 4.01:1 and #9A7B39 at 3.63:1 against AA's 4.5:1 for normal text. FIXED rather than baselined (enshrining a real defect makes a ratchet a rubber stamp): #5C6B5B and #846829 clear AA on both grounds the page uses. 676 -> 0, baseline committed at zero. Ratchet proven red — reverting the muted token alone fails all 8 pages (0 -> 502) and exits 1. Per-page rather than a total, so one page improving cannot mask another regressing, and a NEW page must start clean. Baseline written ONLY by 'pnpm a11y:baseline', never as a side effect of the check.

title: Desktop: asset persist reports failure while the bytes land correctly
description:
FOUND 2026-07-26 by driving the packaged desktop build under Xvfb (during the Archie-ce7a fix).
NOT yet diagnosed. Do NOT assume it was introduced by the folder-picker work — see ATTRIBUTION.

SYMPTOM. Creating an exhibit from a media folder on desktop reports:

  Added 0 files to 1 exhibit. Couldn't store "page-2.jpg" on this device — check the save
  indicator, and free some space. The remaining 2 files were not attempted.

The library header flips to "⚠ Retry save" and the library home shows "Media couldn't be stored."
The exhibit is created with 0 MEDIA ITEMS.

THE CONTRADICTION, and it is the whole finding. The asset IS on disk, at its FINAL name, correct:

  library/exhibits/voynichtest/assets/01KYGEMTJ9Y372J5QH39GSWM0Y-page-2.jpg   7159 bytes, valid JPEG

and the whole tree is clean: no 0-byte files anywhere, no leftover *.tmp-* entries, library.json
parses at 21728 bytes with the new exhibit present. So TauriFilesystem's temp-then-rename commit
COMPLETED, and the job that wrapped it still rejected.

THE SEAM. ingest-flows.ts persistAsset -> enqueueSave(`assets:${slug}`, "Media", write). enqueueSave
(save-queue.svelte.ts:67) resolves false only when `job()` rejects; it records
s.errors[key] and console.error(`Save failed for "${key}" (${label}):`, err). persistAsset false ->
the ingest classifies the refusal as "storage" and STOPS EARLY by design (the STOPPED_EARLY comment
explains why there is no quota preflight), which is why the other 2 files were never attempted.
The "storage" classification is by PHASE, not by sniffing the error — so the copy naming disk space
is a phase-accurate guess, not evidence of an actual quota problem. Here it is misleading: there is
~1 TB free.

ALREADY RULED OUT (checked, not assumed):
  - requestPersistence() — storage-quota.svelte.ts:72 early-returns on isTauri(), and is
    try/caught besides.
  - the single-writer gate — that branch returns false WITHOUT running the job, and it would have
    surfaced the read-only message instead. Also library.json persists fine through the same queue,
    so the queue itself works on desktop.

NEXT STEP, concretely. The real error is in `console.error("Save failed for ...")`, which goes to the
WEBVIEW console — it does NOT appear in the process stderr (measured: app stderr held only libEGL and
Gtk-CRITICAL noise). Build a probe that surfaces it (the ce7a diagnosis did exactly this: temporarily
widen a user-facing alert to include String(err) + err.stack, rebuild with `tauri build --debug
--no-bundle`, re-drive, then revert). That named the JavaScriptCore TypeError in one cycle and will
name this one too. Suspect the steps AFTER the bytes land in the asset job.

ATTRIBUTION — deliberately open. The failing seam is asset persistence, which the drag-and-drop
folder path and single-file add share. It plausibly predates both 2026-07-26 desktop fixes. Two
independent desktop defects were already found the same day (fs:allow-rename ungranted, Archie-91e7;
Object.assign on webkitRelativePath throwing in JSC, Archie-ce7a), each invisible to every headless
gate. Establish attribution by driving a single-file add and a drag-drop add on desktop BEFORE
concluding anything about the picker.

REPRO. Xvfb recipe — the Wayland session cannot drive this app (blank capture, refused root capture,
synthetic clicks never arrive), see the session-4 section of
ledgers/HANDOFF-studio-preview-export-2026-07-26.md:

  Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1600x1000x24 &
  pnpm exec tauri build --debug --no-bundle        # NEVER plain cargo build — that bakes devUrl
  DISPLAY=:99 GDK_BACKEND=x11 WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1 ./src-tauri/target/debug/archie

Then: New exhibit -> From a media folder -> Choose a folder -> a folder of images under $HOME
(GTK: ctrl+l, paste with xclip — xdotool type is corrupted by inline autocompletion — then click
Open; Enter does not commit) -> Create exhibit.
--- DIAGNOSED AND FIXED 2026-07-26 (same day), commit 7cdf1fa ---

CAUSE. Not storage, not quota, not the picker. `fs.exists()` on the `.bake-schema` marker was
refused by the capability SCOPE:

  forbidden path: /home/micah/.local/share/digital.compost.archie/library/exhibits/voynichtest/
  assets/.bake-schema, maybe it is not allowed on the scope for `allow-exists` permission in
  your capability file

Tauri matches fs scope globs with a leading-dot rule: a `**` wildcard does NOT match a path
component that begins with a dot. `$APPDATA/**` covers library.json only because `$APPDATA` expands
to a LITERAL path (so the dots in `.local` are never matched by a wildcard) — it is exclusively the
TRAILING dot-components that fall outside the scope. Archie writes two of them:
`.bake-schema` (asset-store.ts:26, one per assets dir) and `.archie-cache/` (resident-store.ts:146,
the desktop-only hidden peaks cache).

FIX. Four entries added to fs:scope — `$APPDATA/**/.*`, `$APPDATA/**/.*/**`, and the `$HOME`
equivalents (the dir form is needed for `.archie-cache`'s children). Commented in the manifest as
load-bearing so nobody prunes them as defensive.

WHY THE COPY BLAMED DISK SPACE. `AddFileRefusal` is classified by WHICH PHASE failed, never by
sniffing the error — a deliberate design (the header comment explains that sniffing `createImageBitmap`
DOMExceptions across engines would be "a guess wearing the costume of a diagnosis"). That is right in
general, and here it meant a PERMISSION failure inside the persist phase was reported to the user as
"free some space" on a disk with ~1 TB free. Worth revisiting whether the storage refusal should
distinguish a scope/permission rejection, which is knowable on desktop — NOT done, no ticket yet.

ATTRIBUTION, now settled: NOT caused by the folder-picker work. The failing call is
`fs.exists(.bake-schema)` in the shared asset-persist path, which every ingest route uses. Any
desktop media add — folder pick, drag-drop, single file — hit it. It predates both 2026-07-26
picker fixes.

VERIFIED on a packaged debug build (clean profile, origin tauri_localhost_0, no probe in the
binary): "Added 3 files to 2 exhibits", 3 assets + 2 .bake-schema markers on disk, no 0-byte files,
no leftover .tmp-*, library.json parses at 22475 bytes with both new exhibits. Relaunched: both
survive with media and thumbnails intact — which also clears Archie-9ece row P2-a on a packaged
binary for the first time.

GATE GAP, still open. scripts/check-tauri-capabilities.mjs derives the required PERMISSION list from
the TauriFsBridge interface and would have caught the fs:allow-rename P0 (Archie-91e7). It says
nothing about SCOPE, so it could not have caught this one — `fs:allow-exists` WAS granted; the path
was out of scope. A scope-side check is derivable (scan the source for dot-path literals handed to
getFile/getDirectory, assert the manifest carries matching dot-globs) and is not yet written.


--- GATE GAP CLOSED 2026-07-26 ---

scripts/check-tauri-capabilities.mjs now runs a SECOND, independent audit for scope. Dot-segments are
DERIVED from the app's own getFile/getDirectory call sites (following one level of const indirection,
which is how .bake-schema is written); every wildcarded scope root must admit both a hidden file
(<root>/**/.*) and a hidden directory's contents (<root>/**/.*/**). Finds three today: .archie-cache,
.archie-mirror.json, .bake-schema.

Red-greened at BOTH levels: a unit test reproduces the shipped manifest with the dot-globs stripped and
asserts all four missing globs; the CLI against the same stripped manifest exits 1 with 4 MISSING lines,
and exits 0 restored.

Gate bug worth knowing: the first version read $APPDATA/**/.*/** as a wildcard ROOT (it also ends in
/**) and demanded $APPDATA/**/.*/**/.*, regressing forever. A root must be a LITERAL prefix. It was
caught by the new gate failing against a manifest that was already correct — run a new gate against
known-good input before trusting its first red.

Deliberately NOT flagged: file extensions (".json") and the temp-write suffix (".tmp-"). Those are
dot-strings, not leading-dot path COMPONENTS, and the rule is about a component's first character.
Pinned by a test so the derivation is not "fixed" into noise.

STILL OPEN from this ticket: the refusal copy blames disk space for a permission failure
("free some space" on a disk with ~1 TB free). AddFileRefusal classifies by PHASE by design; whether a
scope/permission rejection should be distinguished on desktop is undecided and unticketed.
closeReason: FIXED and on origin/main. Cause was scope, not storage: Tauri scope globs do not match a path component starting with a dot, so fs.exists('.bake-schema') was refused while the command itself was granted. Four dot-globs added to fs:scope. Verified on a packaged build with no probe in the binary: 'Added 3 files to 2 exhibits', 3 assets + 2 markers on disk, surviving a relaunch. The gate gap it exposed is closed — check-tauri-capabilities.mjs now runs a second SCOPE audit deriving dot-segments from the app's own getFile/getDirectory call sites, red-greened at lib and CLI level. STILL OPEN, deliberately unticketed: the refusal copy blames disk space for a permission failure.

title: Separate the publish base from the annotation-target namespace
description:
## Question

baseUrl does double duty: it mints every published id AND is the namespace publish groups annotations by — site.ts:575-578 matches targetSource(h) === ${baseUrl}${slug}/canvas/${objId}, while stored target.source was minted at authoring time against WORKING_IRI_BASE (view-state.svelte.ts:67,112; written through unchanged at serialize.ts:159). Swapping in the real Pages URL alone silently DROPS every annotation — pinned by publish/site-geo.test.ts:1-3,41. Section targets are built from baseUrl at publish (manifest.ts:310) and do NOT have this problem; that asymmetry means a fix can look right on a narrative exhibit and be empty on an object grid.

Decide the shape: (a) a target-remap pass at projection time (working IRI -> publish IRI), or (b) a publishBase distinct from the grouping base — mint ids from publishBase, keep comparing against WORKING_IRI_BASE. Include the tier-3 relativisation question (asset source / filesPath / thumbnail / history refs, which the codebase already documents as relative — iiif/resolve.ts:54-56). Evidence: ledgers/TRACE-publish-base-url-2026-07-26.md.

---

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (A2 · split the two jobs)

`baseUrl` currently BOTH mints published ids AND is the namespace annotations are grouped by, so
setting a real Pages URL silently drops every annotation. Fix: keep an internal authoring namespace
for grouping, and rebase to the public base at publish time. Annotations get found; ids stay citable;
stored data is untouched.

This is a correctness bug, not a preference — the only open question was which shape of fix.

---

## RE-READ 2026-07-27 — the shape question is ANSWERED, and the blocking premise is GONE

**"Decide the shape: (a) a target-remap pass at projection time, or (b) a publishBase distinct from
the grouping base" — (a) is already built and shipped.**

- `rebaseCanvasId` (`packages/render-core/src/iiif/canvasid.ts:42`) re-mints a head's canvas IRI onto
  the base being published to, but ONLY when the slug segment and the object-id tail both match this
  exhibit exactly — not a suffix match. Its docblock cites the prior art (cozy-iiif
  `importAnnotationsToManifest`, clover `Painting.tsx`) for why identity, not fuzziness.
- `rebaseHeadTarget` (`publish/site.ts:241`) applies it per head; wired at `site.ts:564`.
- Idempotent, and projection-only: `site.test.ts:674` pins that the history sidecar stays canonical.

**So this ticket's premise no longer holds.** It says "Swapping in the real Pages URL alone silently
DROPS every annotation — pinned by `publish/site-geo.test.ts:1-3,41`". That test was UPDATED on
2026-07-25: the case that used to pin the drop now reads *"SURVIVES a baseUrl != the target base — the
geo note rebases onto the published canvas"* (`site-geo.test.ts:48`). Verified green today, 34 tests
across the two files.

The base can now be changed safely. That was the whole reason this was blocking.

## What is ACTUALLY left, and it is not in render-core

`publishLibrary` already defaults `baseUrl` to `""` — relative (`site.ts:313`). That IS
Archie-3504's decided relative-first behaviour. render-core needs no change.

The defect is Studio's wiring, exactly as `ledgers/TRACE-publish-base-url-2026-07-26.md` traces it:
`BASE` (`seed-data.ts:33`, re-exporting `WORKING_IRI_BASE = "https://archie.demo/"`) is handed to the
publisher as if it were a deploy origin. Three call sites: `App.svelte:203`, `:294`, `:1956`. The
constant's own docblock (`working.ts:29-37`) states the contract that wiring breaks — *"an internal
IDENTIFIER namespace only — never fetched, never published"*.

## An ORDERING defect that survives any base decision — do not miss this

From the same ledger, and it would defeat a correct base computation silently:

`openPublish` (`publish-flows.svelte.ts:377-397`) starts the projection **the moment the user enters
the GitHub step — before any repo name is typed** — and caches it in `cachedSiteFs` (`:385`);
`collectSiteFiles` (`:248-251`) reuses that cache. The real URL IS computed
(`publish-machine.svelte.ts:599-608` → `pagesUrlFor`) and even shown on screen, but only at
`deploy-flows.svelte.ts:174`, after the push — used for the success link, never fed back.

So the tree is baked strictly before owner/repo exist, and nothing re-projects once they do. Fixing
the base without fixing this yields the same wrong ids.

## Consequence: this is now ONE implementation with Archie-3504

3504 decided relative-first; render-core already behaves that way; this ticket's remaining work is
the Studio wiring + the re-projection ordering that 3504 also needs. Do them together.

## IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-27 — branch `fix/publish-base-wiring` (e473b9e test, fac00f1 fix)

**H1 was already closed at `b240a0e`, by `7fafd2a` — do not re-do it.** `App.svelte:2035` passes
`publishBase: () => publishBaseFor(DEPLOY_LIBRARY_ID)` into `createPublishFlows`, and
`deploy/remembered.ts` resolves it to the library's live URL if it has ever deployed, else `""`.
Verified by test: a destination-less folder publish and a destination-less zip export both emit
relative ids with **zero** `archie.demo` anywhere in the artifact.

**The three surviving `baseUrl: BASE` call sites are CORRECT and were deliberately left alone.**
`App.svelte:203` (`createViewState`), `:294` (`createExhibitSession`), `:1956` (`createIngestFlows`)
are the AUTHORING identifier namespace — `view-state.svelte.ts:67,112` mint `target.source`,
`exhibit-session.svelte.ts:69` / `ingest-flows.ts:1157` pass it to `AnnotationSession.save`. That is
exactly `WORKING_IRI_BASE`'s stated contract, and it is the namespace `rebaseCanvasId` rebases FROM.

`Publish.svelte:434` `onpublish` -> `publish-flows` `publish()` -> `collectSiteFiles()` ->

was already correct: `deploy-flows.svelte.ts:150` computes `pagesUrlFor` before staging.) Now:

- `collectSiteFiles(withOriginals, baseOverride?)` keys the cache on `cachedSiteBase`, the base the
  cached tree was projected at — reuse only when the bases agree.
- `publish()` derives `pagesUrlFor(target.owner, target.repo)` and hands it in, so the projection runs
  at the destination. A same-base repeat push still reuses the warm tree (a retry does not re-tile).

| tree | result |
| --- | --- |
| `e473b9e` (test only, fix absent) | **3 failed / 3 passed** — pushed tree carried `voynich/manifest.json`, expected `https://micahchoo.github.io/test/voynich/manifest.json` |
| `fac00f1` (fix present) | **6/6 passed**, and **20/20** on repeat |
| `baseFor` forced back to `"https://archie.demo/"` | **6/6 failed** — so the relative-first assertions are not vacuous |

The push assertions read the ARTIFACT, not the exit code: the IIIF manifest `id`, the
`<link rel="canonical">`, the `og:url`, and the JSON-LD `url` all carry the derived Pages base, and no
file in the tree contains `archie.demo`.

exit 0; `svelte-check` **1190 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings**.

**Deliberately not done:** no author-typed base prompt (3504 A1 rejects it); no change to render-core;
`preflight.ts`'s "NOT CHECKED: base-path shape" note still stands (it names 3504 as the blocker — a
base-shape check is now writable, but it is a separate ticket).

title: Fix the ?src= grammar drift: Studio mints a dead query param
description:
## Question

Publish.svelte:198 mints ${CANONICAL_VIEWER}?src=${encodeURIComponent(u)} — a real query param — but the viewer parses the HASH query only (ViewerShell.svelte:55 -> route.ts:28-33); location.search is read nowhere in apps/viewer/src. ADR-0009 and route.ts:8-11 both specify #/?src=. Every share link and iframe snippet Studio has ever minted (including the embed snippet at Publish.svelte:216) opens the canonical viewer's own Voynich gallery instead of the shared zip.

Fix the minting site, and add the test that was missing: route.test.ts covers the PARSER (correct all along) — nothing covers the minted string. Assert the round trip mint -> parseRoute.
closeReason: FIXED. Publish.svelte minted ${CANONICAL_VIEWER}?src=<url> — a real query param — while the viewer reads location.hash and nothing else (ViewerShell.svelte:55,136; location.search appears nowhere in apps/viewer/src). Every share link AND every iframe snippet (embedSnippet derives from shareLink) opened the bare Library Gallery instead of the shared library. Now minted by apps/studio/src/share-link.ts as #/?src=, the grammar url/route.ts:8-11 and ADR-0009 both specify. Extracted to a module rather than fixed in place because a $derived.by inside a component is untestable — vitest does not render it and svelte-check cannot tell a working URL grammar from a broken one. The test ROUND-TRIPS through the viewer's own parseRoute: mint a link, parse its hash, assert the src comes back. Red-greened: the shipped form fails 4 of 9 including the round trip. Swept for other mint sites — Publish.svelte:212 was the only one; every remaining '?src=' in the tree is prose or a test name.

title: Teach the hosted viewer to open a published tree by URL
description:
## Question

apps/viewer's ?src= accepts only zip bytes (published.ts:282-284 -> open.ts:109-113) and its hosted-tree read is pinned to its own deploy (published.ts:22 `${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}published`). So NO url exists today that opens https://micahchoo.github.io/test/ in the hosted viewer. The dispatch already exists and is tested in the embed: packages/archie-viewer/src/load.ts:120-128 (non-.zip -> openLibraryFromTree, with the looksLikeZip fallback at :142-160).

Port that dispatch into apps/viewer so #/?src=<tree base> works. Note the interaction with self-replicating publish (Archie-e09d): if a tree ships its own viewer, its OWN links point locally — but this is still what makes a tree openable in someone ELSE's hosted viewer, and what the exhibit-page links (static-pages.ts:202, which today resolve against the CANONICAL library's slugs) need. Watch: the embed's tree path applies NO url transform (load.ts:204), so a mis-based tree still 404s its images — this ticket does not fix that; the base fix does.
closeReason: Implemented in 836517c. openLibraryFromSrc now dispatches on the extension exactly as the embed does (archie-viewer/src/load.ts:120-128): a non-.zip src is a published tree base read lazily over HTTP, with the looksLikeZip fallback for a .zip-less zip link — ported, including the documented reason the sniff is not core's fetchArchieLibraryBytes (it must swallow to null so the original TREE error surfaces). The repoint is one variable: genUrl and toServingOrigin are the single URL-construction and asset-rebase points, so both read PUBLISHED live; setHostedTreeBase clears the slug-keyed session caches, which would otherwise collide across two trees. A foreign tree is validated (ADR-0020 marker gate, then exhibits.json) before being committed to, so a mere website fails loudly instead of rendering an empty hall; on failure the previous base is restored rather than stranding the viewer on a dead tree. Two independent injections proved the gates red. Explicitly NOT fixed, per the ticket: a mis-based tree still 404s its images (no url transform, same as the embed) — that is the base ticket. viewer 190/190, svelte-check 0/0, tsc clean. Separately filed Archie-06fb for a PRE-EXISTING full-suite-only failure in selection.spec.ts:96, verified on clean main in a separate worktree.

title: Static-page URL defects: JSON-LD contentUrl and the missing og-card
description:
## Question

Two defects independent of the base, both in the published static pages:
1. JSON-LD ImageObject contentUrl is the raw WORKING path (live: "/assets/01KX....JPG"). site.ts:616 hands exhibitPageHtml the pre-rewrite `exhibit` while site.ts:485 builds the manifest from `manifestExhibit`. Fix is one identifier at site.ts:616 — verify nothing else on the page depends on pre-rewrite sources.
2. og-card.png is advertised by both static pages (static-pages.ts:47,160) and never written into a tree (grep -rn og-card packages/ hits only static-pages.ts; verified 404 live). Either generate it at publish or stop emitting the meta tag when it will not exist.
Evidence: ledgers/TRACE-publish-base-url-2026-07-26.md.

--- ORGANISED 2026-07-26 ---
batch:static-pages — same file as Archie-321c and Archie-a1d4. These two defects are independent of the
base decision (Archie-3504) and can ship in the same static-pages.ts pass as the citation work.
closeReason: Fixed in deaadbb. Defect 1: site.ts now hands exhibitPageHtml the manifestExhibit (published asset triple) instead of the pre-rewrite working model, so JSON-LD contentUrl and og:image resolve to published URLs and the page agrees with the manifest by construction; verified nothing else the page reads changes (title/summary/rights/requiredStatement/readings/object labels+ids copy through, sections additionally arrive with archie: cites resolved). Defect 2: the og-card.png fallback is deleted rather than generated — og:image/twitter:image are emitted only when a real image exists (cover, else first object's absolute source), and twitter:card degrades to 'summary' since summary_large_image over a missing image renders nothing. Library landing gains the same derivation. Both gates proven red-green by reverting each defect independently. Worth noting the pre-existing ImageObject test asserted typeof contentUrl === 'string', which the broken value satisfies — that is why it shipped. render-core 1208/1208, tsc clean.

title: A single-object exhibit drops its exhibit-level credit, licence and metadata — a IIIF MUST-display violation
description:
## Question

Found by Archie-a5b1 (2026-07-26) while fixing V103/V104, deliberately NOT fixed there because the fix needs a placement decision in reader chrome — territory the dock slice held at the time. That slice has since merged (dfe7ab4), so this is unblocked.

**A single-object exhibit never renders its exhibit-level credit, licence or metadata anywhere in the SPA.** Measured: `dl.run .pair count=0` against data carrying 3 rows, and the credit visible on screen belongs to the OBJECT, not the exhibit.

**Mechanism.** `MetadataRun` is mounted only at `apps/viewer/src/components/ObjectGrid.svelte:50`. A `single` layout routes straight past the grid to the Reader, so nothing on that path ever mounts it. Same boundary for the narrative reader: `NarrativeReader.svelte:778` shows the exhibit credit but has no metadata run.

**Why this is a bug and not a nicety:** a IIIF `requiredStatement` is MUST-display. Silently dropping it for an entire layout is a spec violation, and the failure is invisible — the page looks complete, and the object-level credit sitting nearby makes it look correct.

## What this ticket must decide, not just implement

The fix threads a new prop through `Reader` / `MediaPlayer`, but the load-bearing part is **where the exhibit-level block goes in reader chrome** — and it must be decided ONCE, for the image reader, the AV surface and the narrative reader together. Deciding it per-surface is how the three drifted in the first place.

**Prior art already identified:** universalviewer's `CenterPanel.ts:170-174` (from the a5b1 sweep). Read it at the line before citing it — see `.claude/rules/prior-art-citation-discipline.md`; seven plausible-reading citations were caught wrong in one session.

**Sequence it at the TOP of a slice, not the tail.** That is the explicit recommendation from a5b1's author and from the dock's, both of whom paid for a placement decision made late.

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (human) — placement, and the echo rule

**Placement: beside the object credit, on all three readers.** Extend the existing `.credit-row` to carry both levels with the level named. The three call sites already exist — `Reader.svelte:366`, `MediaPlayer.svelte:206`, `NarrativeReader.svelte:303` — each rendering `<Credit {rights} tone="paper"/>`. One component, three existing sites, **always on screen**, so the IIIF MUST-display obligation is satisfied without argument.

```
Exhibit · Beinecke Rare Book Library · CC BY 4.0
This folio · MS 408 f.1r · CC BY-NC
Creator  Anonymous
Date     c. 1404-1438
```

**Rejected: docking it.** Exhibit-level attribution is arguably structural chrome by the ADR-0019 distinction the corpus sweep landed on, but the dock slice fought to keep the chrome tax proportional (the `:empty` gating, the 141px reflow ruling) and this would add permanent height to every reader.

**Rejected: a UV-style attribution panel.** `CenterPanel.ts:170-174` calls `openAttribution()` unconditionally whenever a `requiredStatement` exists, so that panel is open by default and the precedent is sound. But it is a new surface built three times — the largest option, and the one most likely to drift again. Drift is why this ticket exists.

**The echo rule: on an EXACT folded match, the OBJECT row yields to the EXHIBIT row.** A single-object exhibit very often carries the identical sentence at both levels, and stacking them prints it twice in two voices — indistinguishable from a data bug, which is exactly what `metadataRows` rule 3 already exists to prevent. This follows rule 3's shape: the more-general MUST-display slot wins and the narrower row yields.

**A NEAR-match keeps BOTH**, unchanged from rule 3's reasoning — we cannot know which is the fuller statement, and silently hiding authored data is the worse error:

```
Exhibit · Beinecke Rare Book Library
This folio · Beinecke, gift of J. Voynich
```

Reuse rule 3's existing fold/compare rather than writing a second comparison. A second one will drift, and this map already carries `markers.css` / `tokens.css` as the standing example of what duplicated sources do.

## Gate

Not a unit test. The proof is the rendered artifact: count the exhibit-level credit/licence/metadata elements on a single-object exhibit in the driven app, and in the published tree. A green suite over a tree that carries nothing is this repo's most-repeated failure — `.claude/rules/svelte-no-typecheck-net.md` has the table.
closeReason: Fixed in a44436b. Credit.svelte gained an optional exhibitRights prop (its presence switches the component to a named two-level stack); Reader/MediaPlayer gained the prop plus an exhibit MetadataRun; NarrativeReader gained the run it was missing; ExhibitView threads exhibitRights to all four object-reader mounts; MetadataRun gained a paper/canvas tone since the same run now appears on both grounds. The echo rule reuses metadataRows rule 3's fold/compare, exported as isExactEcho with 4 new unit cases, rather than a second comparison that could drift — and the licence must agree too, since same-sentence/different-licence is differing authored data. Gate is the rendered artifact: e2e/exhibit-rights.spec.ts, driven against pnpm build output, proven red-green per half independently (revert Reader's mount -> tests 1+2 fail; revert Narrative's -> test 3 fails; both in place -> 4/4). Test 4 pins that the grid path stays one unnamed level. Static pages were never affected: publish/static-pages.ts already emits exhibit.requiredStatement and runs the same metadataRows projection (verified). viewer 184/184, render-core 1206/1206, svelte-check 0/0, tsc clean.

title: Implement the dcterms exclusion policy: demote to verbatim, preserve source property, drop it on edit
description:
## Question

Implement the policy decided in `Archie-aafd` (2026-07-27). That ticket carries the full reasoning and the measurement that reframed it — **read its close reason first**, and do not re-derive the decision.

## The defect being closed

A foreign `.archie.zip` carrying `dcterms:title` currently becomes **an editable Studio row that renders nowhere**:

1. `isMetadataEntry` (`model.ts:86`) accepts it — it validates only the `dcterms:` prefix
2. `seedRows` (`metadata-rows.ts:88`) maps it into an editable row
3. `metadataRows` rule 1 (`metadata-display.ts:99`) drops it on display

The curator types into a field and nothing appears anywhere.

## The four rulings to implement

1. **Demote at deserialize.** `model.ts:104` is the single call site. An entry whose `property` is in `METADATA_EXCLUDED_PROPERTIES` becomes verbatim: strip `property`, keep `value`, label via `dctermsLabel`. Same rule `iiif-import.ts:85` already applies to IIIF imports — make them one rule, not two.
2. **Preserve `sourceProperty`** on the entry so serialize writes back what came in. An untouched foreign tree round-trips byte-faithful.
3. **Drop `sourceProperty` on edit.** It is a provenance record about *that value*; once the curator changes the value it no longer applies and the row becomes an ordinary verbatim entry. This is what stops Archie publishing a typed `dcterms:title` carrying a value its source never had.
4. **No publish preflight.** Considered and rejected in `aafd`.

## What will bite

- `sourceProperty` is a **new model field**, so it needs a carry sentinel — `.claude/rules/render-core-data-integrity.md` rule 3: every boundary that hand-maps model fields carries a co-located `satisfies Record<keyof Source, CarryDisposition>`. That rule exists precisely to make "added a field, forgot a copy site" a compile error rather than the recurring bug class it was.
- **Assert the round trip, not just the demotion.** A test that only checks the demoted row renders will pass against code that silently loses `sourceProperty`. Assert: foreign entry in → byte-identical entry out; and edited entry → `sourceProperty` gone.
- `isMetadataEntry` is a type *guard* and cannot transform. The demotion is a normalization step beside it, not inside it.

## Territory

`packages/render-core/src/model/**` and `apps/studio/src/metadata-rows.ts`. **Not** the viewer components — `Archie-36e6` holds those.
closeReason: Implemented in c23cf48, all four rulings from Archie-aafd. (1) sanitizeMetadataEntries demotes an excluded dcterms property to verbatim — property stripped, value kept under the third party's own label if present else the vocabulary's; same rule iiif-import.ts already applied, now one rule not two. Demotion sits BESIDE isMetadataEntry, since a type guard cannot transform. (2) sourceProperty preserved on the entry; it rides archieMetadata through IIIF and sanitize carries an existing one through, so the 2nd save round-trips too. (3) Dropped on a VALUE edit (the Studio row carries the arrival value to make that decidable); a relabel is deliberately not an edit. (4) No publish preflight. New model field => carry sentinel at the sanitize boundary per render-core-data-integrity rule 3; sameEntries compares it so re-seeding can't eat it. Both halves gated and proven red by independent injection: dropping sourceProperty at demotion fails 3 core tests including the round trip; letting provenance survive a value edit fails the studio test. render-core 1213/1213, studio 977/977, tsc clean both.

title: The finder's facet row starves the results list off-screen
description:
## What shipped

On the `screenshots` seed exhibit, **every finder result was off-screen and unclickable**. Opening
the finder and clicking a result — the whole point of the surface — did nothing a reader could reach.

Measured on the BUILT app (`astro preview`, Chromium, 1280x720 viewport), with the finder open:

| what | measured |
| --- | --- |
| `.finder-facets` height | **668px** (132 tag chips) |
| `.finder` `max-height` | 76vh = **547px** |
| `.finder-results` `clientHeight` | **0** |
| `.finder-results` `scrollHeight` | **9930px** (79 rows of real content) |
| first `.result` bounding top | **y=883** in a 720px viewport |
| `.finder` `overflow-y` | `visible` |

## Why

`allTags` (`SearchOverlay.svelte`) is the exhibit's WHOLE tag vocabulary — 132 chips here. The facet
block is a flex item with `overflow: visible`, so its `min-height: auto` resolves to its **content
height** and it refuses to shrink. It therefore consumed the entire panel before the results list
began. `.finder-results` DOES have `overflow-y: auto`, which resolves its own `min-height: auto` to
0, so it obediently collapsed to nothing — the list was the only thing in the panel that could yield,
and it yielded everything.

The panel's `overflow-y: visible` is what turned "clipped" into "off-screen below the fold": the
content spilled past the panel's bottom edge rather than being contained.

## Proven pre-existing

Re-measured with the (unrelated, Archie-9eeb) locus line forced to `display: none` via an injected
style tag. Geometry **identical**:

```
WITH locus line  : {"facetsH":668,"listClientH":0,"firstRowTop":883,"viewportH":720}
locus line HIDDEN: {"facetsH":668,"listClientH":0,"firstRowTop":883,"viewportH":720}
```

The starvation is caused entirely by the facet block; nothing in the result row participates.

## Fix (landed on `fix/finder-locus`, commit `8efa137`)

`SearchOverlay.svelte` styles only:

- `.finder-facets` — `flex: 0 1 auto; max-height: 20vh; overflow-y: auto;` (cap the facets and let
  THEM scroll, so they can no longer take the panel whole)
- `.finder-results` — `flex: 1 1 auto;` (claim the remaining height rather than sit at its own zero
  minimum)

Red-green proven: with those two declarations reverted to their pre-fix form and everything else
untouched, the driven-click spec fails with Playwright's `element is outside of the viewport`
retrying until timeout; restored, it passes. Gate: `apps/viewer/e2e/finder-locus.spec.ts`, the
`activating a hit lands on that note's own rung` test.

## The transferable part — a THIRD member of a family this repo already documents

> The three text/count assertions stayed **green** throughout, because text and counts do not imply
> **reachability**. Only the driven click caught it.

`[[osd-overlay-wrapper]]` covers *something on top eats the click*. `[[playwright-count-does-not-wait]]`
covers *the count is zero because nothing has hydrated yet*. This is neither:

**the element is present, correct, and pushed out of the viewport by a sibling that ate the height.**

Every assertion about its content passes — it is in the DOM, its text is right, `toHaveCount` finds
all 87 of them, and Playwright's own `toBeVisible()` returns true (a non-empty bounding box outside
the viewport is still "visible" by that definition). No human can reach it. The only probe that
distinguishes the two worlds is a **real driven click**, which reports `element is outside of the
viewport` after scrolling into view fails.

So the detection question for this family is *"could a reader's mouse get to it?"*, and neither
presence, nor text, nor count, nor `toBeVisible` answers it.

Worth folding into the rules beside its two siblings.

## Found-not-fixed, adjacent

- The facet row still offers all 132 chips with no search/filter of its own. Capped and scrollable is
  correct-but-blunt; a 132-chip scroll box is not a usable facet affordance. A tag filter, or showing
  the top-N by frequency with a "more" affordance, is the real answer.
- No test asserts a panel child stays within the viewport in general. The driven click covers the
  results list only because that list happens to be clicked. A sibling that grows (a long exhibit
  title, a future toolbar) could re-starve it and only that one spec would notice.
closeReason: Fixed on fix/finder-locus (8efa137): .finder-facets capped at 20vh with its own scroll, .finder-results flex:1 1 auto. Red-green proven as injection 5 in ledgers/FIX-finder-locus-2026-07-27.md — reverting the two declarations makes the driven-click spec fail with 'element is outside of the viewport'. Gate: apps/viewer/e2e/finder-locus.spec.ts. Follow-ups (facet affordance for 132 chips, a general in-viewport invariant) are recorded in the ticket body as found-not-fixed.

title: Small-institution archive: folders to website, end to end
description:
## Notes

Goal (Micah, 2026-07-26): a small institution with a **10–30 GB archive** in folders can go
end-to-end in Archie — ingest → annotate → publish → a viewable website. Standing stance:
"if Archie can't do all the things it should facilitate most of the things" — Archie may hand
off a step (an upload command, HandBrake) rather than owning it, but it must never leave the
user without a route.

Skills each session should consult: /grilling + /domain-modeling (grilling tickets), /prototype
(prototype tickets), run-app (browser verification), /research (research tickets). Repo rules that
bind here: perf-measure-the-flow (any publish-pipeline change must move scripts/perf/publishrun.mjs),
archie-viewer-eager-closure (embed eagerGzKB gate), render-core-data-integrity (marker-last writes),
untrusted-archive-open-seam, tauri-fs-seam, two-typescript-compilers, svelte-no-typecheck-net.
Grep with -a (NUL-byte hazard); .claude/worktrees/ holds stale checkouts whose hits are noise.

CROSS-MAP CONTRACTS — feed these, never fork them:
- "Published tree as the product" (Archie-c268) owns what a published tree CONTAINS. This map owns
  how BIG it can be and how it GETS OUT. Bundling the viewer is Archie-e09d there, not a ticket here.
- The destination-URL decision is Archie-3504 (in c268). It BLOCKS object-storage publish here —
  upload 19 GB under a wrong base URL and every link in it is dead. Trace: Archie-d6ad /
  ledgers/TRACE-publish-base-url-2026-07-26.md.
- Native folder as canonical desktop store is Archie-623e — CODE ALL MERGED, open only as the
  packaged-release gate (Archie-a09d). Annotating 10–30 GB already works on desktop; don't re-plan it.
- Freecut optimization program (Archie-5b06) holds the WebCodecs/AV templates in its Fog.

CHARTING DECISIONS (2026-07-26) — settled in the grilling, do not re-litigate without new evidence:
1. TILES ARE CONDITIONAL. site.ts:420 tiles every asset unconditionally today. Tile only above a
   size threshold. The seam already supports it: tileObject → null leaves a plain `source`, and
   resolve.ts:107 classifies that as kind:"image", which OSD renders natively. The change is a
   `return null` in the slicer; nothing downstream moves. Threshold VALUE is ticketed, not decided.
2. EVERY EXPORT BUNDLES THE VIEWER (~33 KB eager; OSD ~231 KB lazy behind it). An extracted zip
   opened by double-click runs on file:// where fetch of local JSON is blocked — it shows an honest
   "open in Archie, or serve this folder" page, never a broken screen. Feeds Archie-e09d.
3. THE ZIP CARRIES ORIGINALS (assets-original/ — the ONLY non-regenerable bytes, asset-store.ts:86);
   publish and folder stay lean. Limits are surfaced BEFORE the wall, not after a long publish fails.
   Accepted limitations: the 65,535-file cap binds before the 4 GiB cap for tiled images (~63 large
   images); Firefox/Safari have no folder escape hatch behind it; zip→Archie round-trip of originals
   is unproven, an assumption until something tests it.
4. KEEP FIREFOX. Sacrificing it buys nothing for export: streaming save already works there via OPFS
   staging (binding.ts:105), the folder sink is already Chromium+Tauri only, and the 4 GiB/65,535 caps
   are fflate's writer, not the browser. freecut goes Chromium-only for WebGPU/WebCodecs — COMPUTE,
   not file size. Revisit ONLY if video transcode becomes a product decision.
5. NO DATABASE. library.json is monolithic (Library{exhibits:Exhibit[]}, read whole store.ts:182,
   written whole store.ts:217) but ~6 MB at 20k objects — not the wall. A DB is opaque to a text
   editor and to git, is a SECOND format beside the JSON the published tree must keep anyway
   (IIIF/WADM), and breaks the static/no-server/open-standards identity c268 calls load-bearing.
   If it hurts, split per-exhibit plain JSON first.
6. OBJECT STORAGE IS CONDITIONAL, NOT MANDATORY — this is the map's pivot. Images-only archives fit
   FREE hosting at web quality; video makes object storage unavoidable at any quality tier.

UI/UX DECISIONS (grilling 2026-07-26, second pass) — each is written in full on its ticket:
7.  THE PROBE EXTENDS AN EXISTING SURFACE. CreateExhibitDialog's folder path already previews via
    summarizeFolderFiles → {name,total,images,audio,video}; the probe adds bytes, sampled dimensions
    and the two costed routes to that same panel. No new scrimmed surface (single-scrim invariant).
    [Archie-7280]
8.  THE PROBE IS THE WALKTHROUGH. No first-run guided flow; teaching attaches to a real decision at
    the moment of import, plus one "Preparing your archive" slide in the existing TutorialModal deck.
    [Archie-7280]
9.  LIMITS SURFACE TWICE: up front in the probe, and persistently — StorageBar grows a second
    dimension (which destinations are still reachable), so the ceiling is visible for weeks rather
    than discovered on publish day. [Archie-7280]
10. TIER: the probe RECOMMENDS at ingest (library default); PUBLISH DECIDES (pre-checked, changeable).
    Ingest is never lossy, so a tier change just re-derives. [Archie-4b0a]
11. ARCHIE NEVER HANDLES CREDENTIALS, on any platform — no S3 client, no keyring, no direct upload
    even on desktop. It writes the folder and hands over a copyable `rclone sync` command. Two
    consequences: (a) incremental sync becomes rclone's job, and is REPLACED by a requirement that
    Archie's folder output be BYTE-DETERMINISTIC across publishes (known suspect:
    StaticPageOptions.publishedAt); (b) THE ARCHIVAL TIER IS DESKTOP-OR-CHROME — Firefox/Safari have
    no showDirectoryPicker, so with credentials declined they have NO object-storage route at all,
    only GitHub Pages or a capped zip. Accepted as honest; must be STATED in the greyed-out
    destination, never hidden. [Archie-c85f, surfaced by Archie-c367]
12. METADATA IMPORT GETS A COLUMN-MAPPING STEP — a deliberate divergence from csv-import.ts's
    fixed-dialect precedent, because a catalogue export comes from someone else's collections system
    and cannot be reshaped on demand. Matching key is a user choice, not a fixed rule. The
    export-fill-reimport round trip (extending App.svelte:1193) is kept as the fallback on-ramp.
    [Archie-3754]
13. EXPORT IS ONE FLOW WITH THE PROBE'S RECOMMENDATION PRE-SELECTED — it confirms a decision rather
    than posing a fresh one. Unavailable destinations are greyed WITH THEIR REASON, never silently
    swapped (this is what kills the folder→zip fallback collision). [Archie-c367]
14. LONG JOBS: background ingest/bake behind a status-bar indicator (app stays usable, pause+cancel,
    real estimate); publish stays BLOCKING (library state must be stable while the tree is projected)
    but gains cancel and an estimate. [Archie-c74e]

MEASURED FACTS (this session — arithmetic, not estimates):
- 1,000 images @4000×6000 full fidelity: ~19 GB tree, **521,000 tile files**.
- Same library at web quality (WebP @2000px, no tiles, no originals): **~400 MB, ~2,000 files**
  — 54× smaller, 260× fewer files, fits GitHub Pages' 1 GB free tier.
- Dead at target scale: GitHub Pages (1 GB), Cloudflare Pages (20,000 files), .archie.zip
  (4 GiB / 65,535). Alive: object storage (R2/S3/B2 ~$0.30/mo for 20 GB), a plain web server.
- GitHub publish is O(tiles): one POST /git/blobs per binary at BLOB_CONCURRENCY=6, and
  ghpages.ts:202 uses NO base_tree, so every republish re-uploads everything. Four 6000×8000 scans
  = 4,132 uploads ≈ 52-minute floor against GitHub's ~80 content-writes/min secondary limit.
  This is the measured cause of the user-reported "could barely publish a four image exhibit".
- Media types diverge sharply: basemaps (XyzTileSource) publish as REMOTE REFS — zero bytes, free.
  Images are capped at MAX_MASTER_DIM=6000 and tiled. Audio and video are stored AS-IS
  (ingest-flows.ts:461-467) with NO transcode and NO size cap — MAX_MASTER_DIM is images-only.
- 50 hrs of video ≈ 100–200 GB source, still ~45 GB at 720p. No quality tier puts video on free
  hosting. Audio is borderline (100 hrs ≈ 1.4 GB as Opus).
- tiff-transcode.ts ALREADY does TIFF→WebP at (maxDim, quality): 8–15× smaller at visually
  equivalent quality, proven on the Gawan Museum import of 375 files. The quality-tier work is an
  extension of proven code, not new machinery.

## Decisions so far

- [Desktop: the media-folder picker selects a FILE, not a folder](Archie-ce7a) — FIXED on origin/main
  by a concurrent session 2026-07-27, verified by driving the packaged app. Desktop now takes the
  native directory dialog via the same isTauri() branch folder-backend.ts:39 uses; folder-native.ts
  walks the tree into the File[] the existing pure planner consumes, filtering with folder-import.ts's
  predicates BEFORE reading bytes. Exposed and fixed a SECOND defect: Object.assign on
  webkitRelativePath throws in JavaScriptCore (webkit-relative-path.ts), which had also been breaking
  drag-and-drop folder import and the flatten path. Step 1 of the pipeline now works on the only
  platform that can hold 10-30 GB. Unblocks Archie-c74e.

## Fog

- VIDEO TRANSCODE is the deferred fork. Browser video transcode needs WebCodecs (Chromium-only) —
  exactly what freecut sacrifices Firefox for, and exactly what Archie-5b06's Fog parks. Current
  stance is the cheap side: Archie does NOT transcode video; it MEASURES and TELLS ("your video is
  180 GB — transcode with HandBrake first, or budget ~$2.70/month"). Graduates to a ticket only if
  an institution's video makes hand-off unacceptable. Decision 4 (keep Firefox) is downstream of this.
- Ingest resumability at scale: 1,000+ files, what happens when it dies at #800 — no progress model,
  no resume, unproven. Sharpens once "Prove 1,000 images end to end" reports where it actually breaks.
- The BAKE step has no home in the user's mental model: derivatives are split across two moments
  (thumbnails at ingest, tiles at publish) and at 1,000 images it is where the hours go. Whether it
  becomes one visible, resumable, cancellable job is a product question the scale proof will force.
- Multi-person annotation at a small institution (2–3 staff): MergeReview exists, the pull-merge
  story is still a probe in c268 (Archie-30ff). Revisit after that probe reports.
- Custom domain + bucket CORS: an object-storage site needs CORS headers or the bundled viewer cannot
  fetch its own JSON, and a raw bucket URL is not a citable home. Sharpens once the storage target lands.
- Folder → exhibit structure mapping: how nested institutional folder trees become exhibits/sections
  is unspecified. May graduate out of the probe ticket once real folder shapes are seen.
- Succession/handoff for a small institution (the person who ran Archie leaves) — relates to c268's
  succession-proof fog; deliberately not this map's problem yet.
- Whether "web quality" is a one-way door or re-derivable from the retained originals. Assumed
  re-derivable (the working store keeps assets-original/), unverified.
- Publish-output DETERMINISM is now load-bearing (decision 11): if unchanged input does not produce
  byte-identical output, `rclone sync` re-uploads gigabytes on every republish. Only one suspect is
  identified so far (StaticPageOptions.publishedAt). A real audit of the DZI slicer, the bake path
  and the manifest serializers has not been done and may graduate into its own ticket.
- Integrity under a third-party sync tool: rclone does not know archie.json is the commit point, so
  an interrupted sync can land content without its marker, or a marker without its content —
  inverting render-core-data-integrity contract #1. Sharpens once the rclone handoff is specified.
- Whether Firefox/Safari ever get an archival route at all, or whether "desktop-or-Chrome for large
  archives" is the permanent, stated answer. Currently the latter — revisit only if a credential-free
  browser upload path appears.

title: Probe the folder, then recommend a quality tier and a destination
description:
## Question

Before a single file is ingested, can Archie READ the institution's folder and tell them which
routes are open — with their own numbers, not generic advice?

A small institution cannot answer "do you need object storage?". They CAN answer "free and good,
or paid and archival?". So this is a PROBE, not a questionnaire: walk the folder, count files, sum
bytes, sample dimensions and formats, classify media (image / audio / video / basemap), then show
the two routes costed for THEIR archive:

    2,400 files, 31 GB, mostly 6000x8000 TIFFs, plus 12 hrs of video.
    Full fidelity  — ~74 GB published. Needs object storage (~$1.10/month).
    Web quality    — ~900 MB published. Free on GitHub Pages.
    Your video (12 hrs) forces object storage either way.
    Originals stay on your disk in both cases.

Open sub-questions:
- BEFORE or AFTER ingest? Before is far better (decide once, ingest once) but means reading a folder
  that hasn't been imported — cheap on desktop via the native dialog, awkward on web.
- What does the probe need to sample to be accurate without reading 31 GB? (dimension probe on a
  sample; extension+size for the rest?)
- Does this become the on-ramp for a first-run walkthrough, or a standalone "check my archive" tool?
- What does it say when the answer is "your archive is too big for anything Archie facilitates"?

The size arithmetic this must encode lives in the map's MEASURED FACTS block (Archie-34a2) — reuse
it, don't re-derive it. Media types diverge sharply and the probe is where that becomes visible to
the user: basemaps cost zero published bytes, images shrink 54x at web quality, video shrinks but
never enough to reach free hosting.

Blocked on nothing; this is the map's spine. Its output is what makes the destination and quality-tier
decisions concrete rather than abstract.

## UI/UX decided (grilling 2026-07-26)

SURFACE: extend the EXISTING folder preview inside CreateExhibitDialog's folder path — do NOT build a
new scrimmed surface. summarizeFolderFiles (folder-import.ts:115) already returns {name, total, images,
audio, video}; the probe adds total bytes, sampled dimensions/formats, and the two costed routes to that
same panel. This honors the single-scrim invariant (CONTEXT.md -> Surfaces) and the dialog's established
"three in-surface expanding paths with < Back" shape. A parallel wizard would have to REPLACE the create
dialog and duplicate its folder path.

    My Archive/
    2,400 files - 31 GB
    images 2,380   audio 20   video 0
    mostly 6000x8000 TIFF
    ----------------------------------
    Full fidelity   ~74 GB -> needs object storage
    Web quality     ~900 MB -> free on GitHub Pages
    Originals stay on your disk.
    [< Back]                        [Import]

TEACHING: the probe IS the walkthrough. No separate first-run guided flow — teaching attaches to a real
decision at the moment of import. Add ONE "Preparing your archive" slide to the existing TutorialModal
deck (docs/learn -> public/learn) for people who want to prepare beforehand.

LIMITS: stated up front here AND persistently — StorageBar.svelte grows a second dimension: not just
disk used, but which destinations are still reachable. The author watches the ceiling approach over
weeks instead of discovering it on publish day. REJECTED: export-time preflight only (still late news);
inline per-import warnings (nag risk once permanently past a threshold).

RECOMMENDATION, NOT DECISION: the probe recommends a tier and stores it as a library default; the actual
choice happens at publish (Archie-4b0a). Nothing here is lossy — originals always land.

## FINDINGS 2026-07-27 (prototype run, branch `proto/folder-probe`)

**Shipped:** `apps/studio/src/archive-probe.ts` + 51 tests, and the measurement harness
`scripts/perf/webptier{.html,bench.ts}` / `webptierrun.mjs`. No UI (that is Archie-c367).
Full write-up with the measured tables: `ledgers/PROTO-folder-probe-2026-07-27.md`.

**WEB TIER PINNED: 2400 px / quality 0.80.** Measured through `canvas.toBlob(…, "image/webp", q)`
in real Chromium — the encoder Archie ships (`bake.ts:45`, `tiff-transcode.ts:72`), not cwebp —
over SIX REAL digitization masters (Yale IIIF Voynich folios, an LOC film scan, a Google Art Project
painting, a letterpress incunabulum page, a herbarium sheet). This CONFIRMS Archie-4b0a's starting
point rather than moving it; what is new is the criterion and what breaks if either value moves.

- Bytes-per-pixel is essentially FLAT across output dimension at fixed quality (q0.8: 0.1496 /
  0.1500 / 0.1432 bpp at 1600 / 2400 / 3200 px), so maxDim and quality are SEPARABLE levers.
- Pooled bpp / mean SSIM: q0.7 = 0.1092 / 0.9317 · **q0.8 = 0.1476 / 0.9555** · q0.9 = 0.2445 /
  0.9839. SSIM is against a same-dimension lossless reference, so it isolates encoder loss.
- The deciding boundary is GitHub Pages' 1 GB, costed on this map's own 1,000-image reference
  library: 2400/q0.8 = **0.54 GB**, against 0.89 GB at q0.9 and 0.91 GB at 3200 px — both of which
  lose the free destination once thumbnails and pages are counted. (2400, 0.80) is the LARGEST swept
  pair that fits with headroom.
- Corpus sanity check: raw RGB over the archival WebP master came out **7.7-15.0x**, which brackets
  `tiff-transcode.ts`'s own 8-15x from the 375-file Gawan import. Independent corpora, same range.

**ANSWERS TO THIS TICKET'S OPEN SUB-QUESTIONS**

- *Before or after ingest?* **BEFORE, structurally.** `ProbedFile` carries only what a
  `webkitdirectory` pick or a Tauri directory walk already yields (name, path, MIME, size) plus
  optional samples. Nothing is ingested. Whether the create dialog can afford the dimension sampling
  on a 10,000-file folder is untested — flagged, not solved.
- *What must it sample?* Dimensions on a SUBSET; derive pixels-per-source-byte from the subset and
  apply it to each unsampled file's OWN byte count, so a folder mixing 2 MB and 20 MB scans keeps its
  spread. With no sample at all the fallback is the ingest cap, which over-states — deliberate, since
  over-stating refuses a route the archive might have squeaked into, and under-stating promises one
  that does not exist. `ArchiveProbe.confidence.imagesSampledFraction` reports how much was real.
- *What when nothing fits?* Reachable and reported. Object storage is gated on the SAME capability as
  the folder (decision 11: Archie writes a folder and hands over an rclone command, never credentials),
  so on Firefox/Safari a large archive has GitHub Pages and a capped zip and nothing else. The probe
  returns `blockers` naming the desktop-or-Chrome reason rather than silently recommending nothing.

**RECOMMENDATION RULE.** Destinations best-first — **GitHub Pages -> object storage -> folder -> zip**
(object storage above the folder because the goal is a viewable website, and a folder on your own disk
is a staging step, not one). At the first destination where any tier fits, prefer ARCHIVAL, with two
exceptions, both found by printing the probe's real output rather than by reading assertions:
1. archival costs >10x the FILES (today's tiling threshold makes a 10k-master archive 5.96M files vs
   30k — that is the DZI tax, not fidelity). Goes inert once Archie-53e3 lands.
2. archival turns a FREE route into a paid one (200 hrs of WAV is $1.64/mo where Opus is free) —
   "free and good, or paid and archival?" is the question the institution CAN answer, so silently
   answering "paid" answers the wrong one. Where both tiers cost the same (video) archival still wins.

**OUTPUT SHAPE FOR Archie-c367** — `probeArchive()` returns `folder` (counts/bytes),
`sample` (median long edge, dominant MIME, hours of AV), `tiers.{archival,web}` (publishedBytes,
publishedFiles, originalBytes, bytesByMedia, driver, tileFiles), `destinations[]` = every
(destination x tier) pair with `{fits, reason, estimatedBytes, estimatedFiles,
estimatedMonthlyCostUsd?, estimatedUploadMinutes?, carriesOriginals}`, plus `recommendation`
and `blockers`. EVERY row carries a reason whether it fits or not — that is c367's greyed-with-reason
contract. Worked examples for four inventories are in the ledger.

**LIMITS ARE THE PUBLISHED ONES**, read from source 2026-07-27: GitHub Pages 1 GB site / 100 MiB per
file / 10-min deploy timeout; Cloudflare R2 $0.015 per GB-month over a 10 GB free tier, usage rounded
up. Zip caps and the tiling threshold are PARAMETERS, so Archie-1cf0 and Archie-53e3 are each one
argument away rather than a code edit.

**GATES:** apps/studio `pnpm exec vitest run` **1044 tests / 79 files green**; `pnpm typecheck`
clean. Red-green found a real hole first: injecting bytesPerPixel 0.1476 -> 0.30 left all 46 tests
GREEN, because every estimator assertion computed its expectation FROM the constant it was checking.
Four non-tautological assertions were added (measured literals, range invariant, the 1 GB decision
criterion, an absolute Opus byte count); re-proven at 3 / 2 / 4 failures for the bpp, Opus and maxDim
injections respectively.

**STILL OPEN:** Opus is arithmetic on a bitrate, never an actual encode (no transcode path exists to
measure). The viewer bundle is not yet in the file-count model (Archie-e09d). `practicalFileCeiling`
= 4,800 is derived from the ~80 writes/min rate, not a published GitHub limit. The probe has never
been driven in a browser.

title: Quality tiers: generalize transcode beyond TIFF
description:
## Question

What exactly is a "quality tier", and how far does transcode generalize beyond TIFF?

`tiff-transcode.ts` already does TIFF -> WebP at (maxDim, quality), measured 8-15x smaller at
visually equivalent quality on the Gawan Museum import of 375 real digitization masters. Images are
already capped at MAX_MASTER_DIM = 6000 (geometry/downscale.ts:8). Audio and video are stored AS-IS
(ingest-flows.ts:461-467) with no transcode and no cap.

Decide:
- The tier SET. Two ("archival" / "web") or three? What maxDim + quality does each pin?
- Does a tier apply at INGEST (smaller working store, lossy up front) or at PUBLISH (originals
  retained, derived per publish)? Publish-time is re-derivable and matches decision 3's "originals
  are the only non-regenerable bytes" — confirm that is the choice and record why.
- AUDIO: Opus/MP3 transcode is well-trodden and doesn't need WebCodecs. In or out of this ticket?
  100 hrs lands ~1.4 GB as Opus vs ~60 GB as WAV, which is the difference between borderline and dead.
- VIDEO is explicitly OUT (map Fog): it needs WebCodecs, i.e. Chromium-only, which decision 4 declined.
  Record the refusal and what Archie does INSTEAD (measure and tell: "180 GB - run HandBrake, or
  budget ~$2.70/month"). If this ticket concludes the hand-off is unacceptable, say so and graduate
  the video fork out of Fog rather than quietly widening scope here.
- Is "web quality" a one-way door? Assumed re-derivable from retained originals; verify.

Prior art rule applies: cite tiff-transcode.ts's own header (UTIF chosen over wasm-vips for
footprint; Tropy uses sharp/libvips) before proposing a different decoder.

## UI/UX decided (grilling 2026-07-26)

WHEN THE TIER IS CHOSEN: the probe RECOMMENDS at ingest (stored as a library default); PUBLISH DECIDES
(pre-checked, changeable). Two touchpoints, one remembered answer.

This settles this ticket's own "ingest or publish?" sub-question: PUBLISH-TIME. The reason is
reversibility — originals always land at ingest, so switching tiers later just re-derives.

REJECTED: decide-at-ingest (a one-way door whose only benefit, a smaller working store, is illusory once
decision 3 keeps originals anyway); library-setting-only (invisible at the moment it matters, and a user
who never opens settings never learns the tradeoff exists).

The publish-side control is specified in Archie-c367.

---

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (batch grill — remaining sub-questions)

**TIER SET: TWO.** Archival = as-ingested bytes (assets-original/ + the ≤6000px masters). Web = WebP
re-encode; params (starting point ~2400px / q0.8) are PINNED BY MEASUREMENT in the Archie-7280 probe
on the Gawan corpus, not chosen here. Rejected: a third "print" tier (turns c367's one-line quality
control into a menu nobody asked for).

**AUDIO: IN.** The web tier transcodes audio to Opus at publish; archival keeps bytes as-is. No
WebCodecs needed. The 40× factor (100 hrs ≈ 60 GB WAV → ~1.4 GB Opus) is the difference between
"GitHub Pages works" and "dead on arrival" for AV archives. c367's size estimates must account for it.

**VIDEO: GRADUATED OUT OF FOG** — see the new video-transcode ticket. Decided BOTH paths: a native
ffmpeg/gstreamer sidecar on desktop (WebKitGTK has no WebCodecs) AND WebCodecs on Chromium web;
Firefox/Safari keep the measure-and-tell hand-off, greyed with reason per c367's rules.

**ONE-WAY DOOR: verified NO** (from code, not decided): originals are retained at ingest
(saveOriginalFile → assets-original/, ingest-flows.ts:522), so the web tier is always re-derivable.


## WEB-TIER PARAMS PINNED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-07-27 (Archie-7280)

This ticket deferred the web tier's numbers to the Archie-7280 probe ("params (starting point
~2400px / q0.8) are PINNED BY MEASUREMENT in the Archie-7280 probe on the Gawan corpus, not chosen
here"). They are now pinned, and the starting point is **CONFIRMED, not moved**:

    WEB TIER = 2400 px longer edge, canvas.toBlob quality 0.80
    apps/studio/src/archive-probe.ts -> WEB_TIER  (measured bpp 0.1476)

**Instrument:** `scripts/perf/webptierbench.ts` + `webptierrun.mjs` — real Chromium, driving
`canvas.toBlob(…, "image/webp", q)`, i.e. the encoder this codebase actually ships
(`bake.ts:45`, `tiff-transcode.ts:72`). Deliberately NOT cwebp: Chromium's canvas encoder is
libwebp with its own method/segment defaults, so a CLI `-q 80` is a different number and pinning
against it would pin the wrong parameter.

**Corpus:** six REAL digitization masters, not synthetic — two Yale IIIF Voynich folios (this repo's
own seed material), an LOC large-format B&W film scan, a Google Art Project oil painting, a
letterpress incunabulum page, and a 10175 px herbarium sheet that exercises MAX_MASTER_DIM. The Gawan
corpus itself was not available to this run; see the independent cross-check below for why the
substitute is defensible.

**Measured (pooled, 6 masters x 3 output dimensions per quality, n=18):**

| quality | bytes/px | SSIM mean | SSIM worst master |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.70 | 0.1092 | 0.9317 | 0.8813 |
| **0.80** | **0.1476** | **0.9555** | **0.9182** |
| 0.90 | 0.2445 | 0.9839 | 0.9634 |
