| 0.92 (= bakeDisplayMaster default) | 0.2742 | 0.9887 | — |

SSIM is against a SAME-DIMENSION lossless reference, so it measures encoder loss alone rather than
conflating it with downscale loss.

**The finding that let each parameter be pinned independently:** bytes-per-pixel is essentially FLAT
across output dimension at fixed quality — q0.8 gives 0.1496 / 0.1500 / 0.1432 bpp at 1600 / 2400 /
3200 px. So maxDim is purely a total-bytes lever and quality is purely a per-pixel lever; they do not
trade against each other.

**The criterion both were pinned against** — Archie-34a2's own 1,000-image reference library at
4000x6000, versus GitHub Pages' published 1 GB site limit:

| | q0.70 | q0.80 | q0.90 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1600 px | 0.18 GB | 0.24 GB | 0.39 GB |
| **2400 px** | 0.40 GB | **0.54 GB** | 0.89 GB |
| 3200 px | 0.67 GB | 0.91 GB | 1.52 GB |

**(2400, 0.80) is the largest swept pair that leaves that library under 1 GB with real headroom.**
q0.9 (0.89 GB) and 3200 px (0.91 GB) each leave under 12% of the ceiling, which thumbnails, static
pages and the bundled viewer consume — so both LOSE THE FREE DESTINATION, which is this map's whole
pivot. Going the other way, 1600 px gives up half the linear resolution to buy headroom nobody needs.
Fidelity price of stopping at 0.80: +0.028 mean SSIM for +66% bytes.

Worth knowing about the fidelity distribution: the hardest class is FINE-GRAINED TEXTURE, not text.
Worst master at q0.8 is the B&W film scan (0.9190 — grain is the first thing a lossy encoder
discards), parchment folios sit at 0.936-0.937, and the letterpress page scores **0.9961** because
flat paper with sharp black text is easy for WebP.

**Independent cross-check that the substitute corpus is representative of the Gawan-class material:**
raw RGB (3 bytes/px, an uncompressed TIFF) over the archival WebP master at q0.92 came out at
**7.7-15.0x** across the five within-cap masters. `tiff-transcode.ts`'s header records **8-15x**
from the real Gawan Museum import of 375 digitization masters. Two independent corpora, same range.

**AUDIO, for the record:** the Opus figure this ticket decided (~40x) is carried in the probe as
`WEB_TIER_OPUS_KBPS = 32` — the spoken-word bitrate Archie-34a2's own arithmetic implies (100 hrs
= 60 GB WAV -> ~1.4 GB Opus). The exact ratio is 1411/32 = **44x**; the map's "~40x" is that rounded.
A music-heavy collection wants ~96 kbps and lands ~3x larger, so it is a parameter. **NOTE: this is
arithmetic on a bitrate — no Opus encode has been measured, because no transcode path exists yet.**

**What this does NOT settle:** SSIM is a proxy; nobody has compared q0.8 and q0.9 renders side by
side at viewing size. The 0.9190 worst case is inside the conventional "good" band and outside the
>=0.95 "visually near-identical" one. That is an accepted trade rather than an unnoticed one — the
web tier is a derivative and originals are always retained (`ingest-flows.ts:522`, this ticket's own
verified no-one-way-door finding), so it is re-derivable at any quality later.

Full working: `ledgers/PROTO-folder-probe-2026-07-27.md`.
---

## ENGINE SHIPPED 2026-07-27 — `feat/tier-engine`, studio-side (surface is Archie-c367)

`apps/studio/src/publish-tier.ts` + the wiring in `publish-flows.svelte.ts`. Default is **archival**,
so nothing changes for any author until c367 supplies a tier.

**No render-core change was needed, and the reason is worth recording.** `publish/site.ts` derives an
asset's published file name from the model's own `source` (`:514`), writes whatever `getAsset` returns
under that name (`:523`) and points the manifest at it (`:527`); the baked thumbnail reuses the same
name (`:545`,`:549`). So handing `publishLibrary` a library that already says `folio.webp`, plus a
`getAsset` that maps the published name back to the stored one, re-tiers an entire publish at the
studio seam. Dimensions are computed with the same `fitWithin` the encoder uses, so the manifest's
width/height are exactly what the re-encode produces rather than a value awaited from it.

- Renaming is **collision-safe over the exhibit's asset set**: `plate.jpg` and `plate.png` both want
  `plate.webp` into one flat `assets/` dir, which would silently overwrite one object's bytes. First
  wins, later ones get `-2`, `-3`.
- Fallbacks are **counted, never silent** — `tierFallbackCount()` / `tierFallbacksByReason()`,
  following `bake-async.ts:38`. Capability is "an encoder is wired" and is part of the DECISION, so a
  platform with no encoder degrades cleanly (archival bytes under their OWN name and MIME) instead of
  publishing JPEG called `.webp`.
- Tier joins `cachedSiteBase` in the projection cache key.
- Tiling stays inert at the web tier as `PROBE-tiling-threshold-2026-07-27.md` expects: `tileObject`
  receives the transformed bytes, which are ≤2400 px against `TILE_MIN_EDGE` 4096.

### BLOCKER — the web tier misplaces every annotation, and this must be closed before c367 offers it

Selectors are stored as **absolute image pixels** (`xywh=pixel:x,y,w,h`, `spine/serialize.test.ts:20`;
SvgSelector polygons in the same space) and the viewer maps them off the **loaded image's content
size** — `viewport.imageToViewportRectangle` at `render-mount/src/read-overlay.ts:295` and
`mount.ts:233`, with `item.getContentSize()` at `mount.ts:405`. Nothing rescales a selector between
the manifest's canvas dimensions and the image actually served. A 6000 px master published at 2400 px
therefore puts every region **2.5x out of place**.

The engine reports it rather than hiding it: `projectLibraryForTier` returns every object whose pixel
space moved, `flows.tierRescaled` exposes it, and a console warning names the objects on every sink.
Closing it means either rescaling selectors in the published annotation projection or teaching the
viewer a canvas→image transform — both outside this ticket's studio-side fence (render-core /
render-mount), so it wants its own ticket. **Until then the web tier is correct for an unannotated
library and wrong for an annotated one**, which is why the engine default is archival and why c367
must not pre-check "web".

### AUDIO — this ticket's premise is out of date, and the real blocker is a muxer

Read from `mdn/browser-compat-data` `api/AudioEncoder.json` on 2026-07-27 (fetched, not recalled):

| path | Chrome | Firefox | Safari | faster than realtime? | container? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WebCodecs `AudioEncoder` | 94 | 130 | 26 | YES | **NO** |
| `MediaRecorder` `audio/webm;codecs=opus` | yes | yes | no | **NO** | yes |

So "WebCodecs is Chromium-only" no longer holds — all three engines ship `AudioEncoder`. But
**MediaRecorder is structurally unusable for a publish-time transcode**: `createMediaStreamDestination`
is defined on `AudioContext`, not `BaseAudioContext` (`api/AudioContext.json`; webaudio
`#dom-audiocontext-createmediastreamdestination`), so an `OfflineAudioContext` — the only thing that
renders faster than realtime — cannot feed one. A 90-minute oral history would take 90 minutes of wall
clock.

What is missing is a **container**. `AudioEncoder` emits `EncodedAudioChunk`s — raw Opus packets — and
something must mux them into Ogg (RFC 7845) or WebM before anything will play the file. This repo has
no muxer and no dependency that provides one, and a muxer written without a real-browser decode check
is exactly the artifact `.claude/rules/svelte-no-typecheck-net.md` says not to trust. So the seam,
the probe (`audioEncodeAvailable`) and the counter ship; every audio asset at the web tier currently
takes the **counted** archival passthrough. Follow-up: add an Ogg-Opus muxer and gate it on the probe.

### Gates
vitest 1130 passed / 83 files (baseline 1093 + 37 new), `pnpm typecheck` 0 errors,
`svelte-check` 1201 files 0 errors 0 warnings. Red-green proven on three assertions: tier removed
from the cache key, reverse name map defeated, degraded passthrough left uncounted — each went red.
The cache-key assertion was itself found vacuous first (it measured the BASE key, because the base
changed too) and rewritten to hold the base fixed.

---

## BLOCKER CLOSED 2026-07-27 — `fix/web-tier-selector-rescale` (`a447af1`, `317274e`, `6c18c94`)

The web tier's selector fence is down. The ENGINE SHIPPED section's BLOCKER subsection above is
superseded by this one: the defect it describes is real and is fixed; the fence on Archie-c367's
surface pre-checking "web" is lifted, subject to the one residue named at the end.

**The seam.** `publishLibrary` takes `scaleSelectors(slug, objectId) → {sx, sy} | null`
(`render-core/src/publish/site.ts`), and the studio's `tierRun` supplies it from
`projectLibraryForTier`'s `rescaled` report. That report was already exact — `fitWithin` computes the
served dimensions purely, before any encode runs — so the fix is the report being CONSUMED rather
than only warned about. render-core deliberately cannot re-derive the factor: by the time it is
handed the library, the object already carries the SERVED dimensions and the master's are gone.

**Projection-only, the `rebaseCanvasId` posture.** Scaled: the per-canvas heads pages and the
manifest's Range `start` (plus the ADR-0017 narrative AnnotationCollection, which must agree with the
Range or a IIIF viewer and a WADM tool would put the same beat in two places). NOT scaled: the
authored log and `annotations/history/`, so a load→publish round trip rescales from canonical instead
of compounding.

**Selector-shape coverage, and the three spaces that must NOT move.** `xywh=pixel:` / bare `xywh=`
scale; `<polygon>`/`<polyline>` point lists scale; `<rect>`/`<circle>`/`<ellipse>`/`<line>`
attributes scale. Untouched, each pinned by a test: **`xywh=percent:`** (frame-size-independent by
construction — video), **`t=start,end`** (time, not space), and **`archie:geo`** (WGS84 lng/lat per
`wadm/types.ts:279` — verified by reading the type, not assumed; a geographic anchor is not in the
image's pixel space at all). A spatiotemporal `t=…&xywh=…` has only its spatial half moved, with
dimension order preserved.

**Rounding, documented and pinned from both sides.** `xywh` → integer pixels, half-up, scaling the
EDGES rather than (origin, extent) so the far edge cannot drift by a pixel; SVG → two decimals,
trailing zeros dropped (Annotorious emits fractional vertices; integer-snapping would visibly move a
small polygon).

**Never silent.** A selector the scaler cannot move exactly ships UNCHANGED and is reported per note
in `PublishResult.unscaledSelectors`, which `warnTier` surfaces. Two cases only, both outside the v1
shape vocabulary Archie authors or draws (`isV1Shape`): a `<path>` (arc flags and elliptical-arc
radii do not survive attribute rewriting) and any SVG carrying a `transform` (it re-parents the
coordinate system). An imported-WADM edge, counted rather than shipped wrong-and-quiet.

**One finding recorded rather than fixed:** a BARE-STRING target carrying a `#xywh=` fragment is not
scaled, and cannot be. `publishLibrary` groups heads by exact canvas-IRI equality and `targetSource`
returns the whole string for a bare target, so `{canvasId}#xywh=…` matches no canvas and never
reaches a per-canvas page at all. Scaling it would be code no published tree can exercise. The bare
targets that DO reach a page are ADR-0018 whole-object notes, which carry no fragment.

### The gate that can actually fail

`scripts/probe/web-tier-selector-rescale.mts` bakes a real tree (a real PNG drawn in Node, real
`publishLibrary`, the real embed bundle from `packages/archie-viewer/dist`), serves it from a bare
static server and drives Chromium. The measurement is zoom/pan-independent: the region overlay's
centre as a FRACTION of the object frame's rendered box. The fixture's marker sits at master pixels
`3000,2000,600,400` on a 6000x4000 master — 0.55/0.55 of the image — published at 2400x1600.

| run | measured fraction | authored | size fraction | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rescale ON | **(0.5500, 0.5500)** | (0.5500, 0.5500) | (0.1000, 0.1000) vs (0.1000, 0.1000) | PASS 5/5 |
| `--no-rescale` | **(1.3750, 1.3750)** | (0.5500, 0.5500) | (0.2500, 0.2500) vs (0.1000, 0.1000) | FAIL 3/5, exit 1 |

The red case is the defect exactly as it shipped: 2.5x, Δ 0.8250, with the region rendering entirely
off the image (`left` 1039 against a frame right edge of 850).

### Consumers updated

`flows.tierRescaled` is now INFORMATIONAL — its console line is `console.info` and says the
selectors were rescaled to match. The correctness warning moved to the new `flows.unscaledSelectors`.
The `publish-tier.ts` header's BLOCKER block is rewritten as a closed-defect record.

### Gates

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| render-core vitest | **1394 passed / 106 files** (baseline 1358 + 36 new) |
| studio vitest | **1177 passed / 84 files** (baseline 1173 + 4 new) |
| `pnpm -r run typecheck` | 6 of 7 projects, 0 errors |
| studio svelte-check | 1208 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings |
| order-sensitivity | new render-core suites 20/20 green; studio wiring suite 20/20 green |

One defect was caught by the typecheck that vitest is structurally blind to: a fixture object typed
`mediaType: "audio"` where the model says `"sound"` (`6c18c94`).

### Still fenced

Only `unscaledSelectors` — a `<path>` or transform-bearing SVG imported from another WADM tool onto
a re-encoded object still lands in the authored pixel space, and says so. Nothing Archie itself
authors can produce one.


---

## CLOSED 2026-07-27 — engine + rescale merged; the web tier is real

Engine merged 1074795 (publish-time, archival default, 2400/q0.80 imported from archive-probe,
fallbacks counted). The annotation-misplacement blocker is fixed and merged 10c82ab: publishLibrary
scaleSelectors projection (all authored shapes + Section.start; percent/time/geo pinned unscaled),
drive-proven — 2.5x displacement red, exact-fraction green. Remaining fenced surface is only
unscaledSelectors (imported <path>/transform SVG — nothing Archie authors can produce one).
Audio Opus stays a counted passthrough pending an Ogg/WebM muxer decision (recorded in the note);
the tier engine is honest about it. Surface control → Archie-c367.

title: Where the tiling threshold sits
description:
## Question

Above what size should an image be tiled — and what does the reader actually lose below it?

Decision 1 (Archie-34a2) settled that tiling becomes conditional. This ticket sets the number, and
the leverage is enormous: at 4000x6000, a 4000px threshold still tiles everything (521,000 files for
1,000 images); a 6000px threshold ships ~1,000 files for the same library. Same content, 500x fewer
objects to write and upload.

The change itself is small and the seam already exists: site.ts:420 tiles unconditionally today, but
`tileObject` returning null leaves a plain `source`, which resolve.ts:107 classifies as kind:"image"
and OSD renders natively. So this is a `return null` under threshold inside the slicer.

What needs MEASURING, not guessing:
- Perceived load/zoom cost of an untiled image at 2000 / 4000 / 6000 px on a slow connection and on
  a phone. A 6000px WebP is several MB delivered as one blob before anything appears.
- Interaction with the quality tier: if web quality caps the master at 2000px, the threshold may
  never fire at all on that tier, and tiling becomes an archival-tier-only concern. Confirm or refute.
- Whether the threshold is one constant or a function of the chosen tier.

perf-measure-the-flow binds: report the END-TO-END number from scripts/perf/publishrun.mjs, not a
single-image primitive benchmark. That rule exists because a 19-37x per-image tiling win was only
1.9-4.7x across a library.

## UI/UX note (grilling 2026-07-26)

The threshold is INVISIBLE to the user — it is not a control. The user-facing choice is the quality tier
(Archie-4b0a: recommended by the probe at ingest, chosen at publish), and the threshold is an
implementation constant underneath it, possibly a function of the chosen tier rather than one number.

That sharpens this ticket's third sub-question: if web quality caps the master below the threshold, the
threshold never fires on that tier and tiling becomes an archival-tier-only concern. Confirm or refute
that FIRST — it may collapse this ticket into "pick the archival-tier constant".

## FINDINGS 2026-07-27 (Archie-86ff probe — measured, not guessed)

Full table, reasoning, and instrument: ledgers/PROBE-tiling-threshold-2026-07-27.md · branch
probe/tiling-threshold · scripts/perf/tilingthresholdbench.ts (+ .html + run.mjs), donor
publishbench.ts. N=3 runs/config, two independent full sweeps (tile counts identical, times within
2-8% run-to-run).

**Web-tier collapse CONFIRMED first, per this ticket's own instruction.** Archie-4b0a pins the web
tier at ~2400px; every threshold candidate measured (800-6000px) sits at or above that, so tiling
never fires on the web tier for ANY plausible threshold. Tiling is archival-tier (+ remote-IIIF)
only — confirmed structurally, not assumed.

**Measured (longer-edge / tiles-per-object / file multiple / byte multiple / publish-time cost per
object / first-paint-byte ratio, N=3, MemoryFilesystem, real sliceToDziAuto):**
800px: 25 tiles, 5.8x files, 2.74x bytes, +30.6ms/obj, 101x first-paint win.
1200px: 37 tiles, 8.2x, 2.87x, +33.9ms/obj, 142x.
1600px: 60 tiles, 12.6x, 3.00x, +37.6ms/obj, 178x.
2400px: 117 tiles, 23.6x, 2.98x, +55.5ms/obj, 439x.
3200px: 190 tiles, 37.8x, 2.97x, +80.7ms/obj, 760x.
4096px (today's TILE_MIN_EDGE): 320 tiles, 62.9x, 2.99x, +114.9ms/obj, 1114x.
6000px (= MAX_MASTER_DIM): 592 tiles, 115.6x, 2.95x, +205.9ms/obj, 2689x.
Every measured tile count matched the analytic dziPyramid() count exactly at every dimension.

**Byte overhead is a STABLE ~2.7-3.0x regardless of size** — not threshold-diagnostic on its own.
**File count and publish time grow steeply with size, and first-paint benefit grows EVEN FASTER** —
so nothing in reader-experience data argues for an upper bound; larger images benefit MORE from
tiling, not less. The real constraint is hosting FILE-COUNT caps (Cloudflare Pages 20,000, zip
65,535 — Archie-34a2's own MEASURED FACTS), which a bulk-import archive blows through in the
thousands of objects if every image over ~4096px tiles. Reconciles with the map's own
'521,000 files for 1,000 images at a 4000px threshold' estimate: at this probe's own reference
point (near MAX_MASTER_DIM, 6000x4500), 592 tiles/object x 1,000 objects = ~592,000 — same order of
magnitude (aspect-ratio difference from the map's 4000x6000 explains the gap). The map's arithmetic
is now measured, not guessed.

**RECOMMENDATION: split the shared TILE_MIN_EDGE constant; derive the local-import one from
MAX_MASTER_DIM instead of hand-picking a sibling number.**
- tileObject (local imports, site.ts:437): threshold = MAX_MASTER_DIM (currently 6000,
  geometry/downscale.ts:8 — import it, don't restate it). A capped local import can never exceed
  its own cap, so this makes local-import tiling structurally inert for the common bulk-import
  case — ~1,000 files instead of ~592,000 for a 1,000-object archival library. Answers the
  ticket's 'one constant or a function of the tier?' sub-question: neither — it's a function of
  MAX_MASTER_DIM (the import cap), which is also why it's moot on the web tier (2400 < 6000).
- tileRemote (remote IIIF, site.ts:468): LEAVE AT today's 4096px. No population data exists on how
  many remote-sourced objects a realistic library carries (out of this ticket's scope to gather),
  and moving it needs the same kind of evidence the map cites for local imports before it should
  change.

**Caveats:** viewer load was measured via a first-paint-bytes PROXY (whole master vs level-0 tile
bytes), not a throttled-network real-OSD drive — the ticket's 'on a slow connection and on a phone'
ask is not fully closed; flagged as follow-up. Synthetic JPEG masters, not real scans (byte figures
could shift on real corpora; file counts are pure geometry and won't). Extrapolation to 1,000
objects is arithmetic on a measured per-object number (file/byte counts scale linearly by
construction), not a separately-run large-library sweep. No product code changed by this probe.

title: Publish to object storage, with incremental sync
description:
## Question

How does a published tree get to object storage — and how does the SECOND publish avoid re-uploading
everything?

This is the archival route. Every git-based host and every "deploy a site" service is dead at target
scale (GitHub Pages 1 GB; Cloudflare Pages 20,000 files; .archie.zip 4 GiB / 65,535 entries). Object
storage has no such caps and costs roughly $0.30/month for 20 GB on R2/S3/B2.

The fork, and the map's stance ("facilitate most of the things") leans cheap:
- FACILITATE: Archie produces the folder (already works, no caps) and hands over the exact command
  (`rclone sync ...`). No credentials in the app, no CORS fight, robust, tiny to maintain.
- OWN IT: Archie uploads directly. On DESKTOP this is genuinely easier than it sounds — Tauri has
  native HTTP with no CORS (the tauri-fs.ts bridge precedent), so S3/R2 from the desktop app avoids
  the browser's whole problem. On web it means credential handling in a browser app.

Either way, decide:
- INCREMENTAL SYNC is not optional. Add 10 images to a 1,000-image archive and you must not re-upload
  19 GB. `IncrementalScope` already exists for folder writes — does it carry, or does object storage
  need its own manifest-diff? Note the cautionary precedent: ghpages.ts:202 uses NO base_tree, which
  is why every GitHub republish re-uploads everything.
- Bucket CORS headers, or the bundled viewer cannot fetch its own JSON.
- What a partial/failed upload leaves behind — the marker-last discipline in
  .claude/rules/render-core-data-integrity.md applies to any multi-file write, including this one.

BLOCKED ON Archie-3504 (destination URL, in map Archie-c268). Publishing 19 GB under a wrong base URL
makes every link in it dead, and the trace (Archie-d6ad) shows Studio currently ships the AUTHORING
namespace as if it were a deploy origin. Do not start the upload path before that lands.

## UI/UX decided (grilling 2026-07-26) — SCOPE CUT, read before planning

ARCHIE NEVER HANDLES CREDENTIALS, on any platform. The fork in the Question above is settled on the
FACILITATE side, and harder than it was drafted: no S3 client, no keyring entry, no direct upload even
on desktop where Tauri's native HTTP would have made it easy. Archie writes the folder and hands over a
copyable command:

    rclone sync ./out r2:my-archive        [copy]   [what is rclone?]

CONSEQUENCE 1 — INCREMENTAL SYNC IS NO LONGER OURS. `rclone sync` diffs source against bucket itself, so
that half of this ticket largely evaporates. What REPLACES it is a sharper constraint: Archie's folder
output must be BYTE-DETERMINISTIC across publishes, or rclone sees churn and re-uploads gigabytes.
Known violator to check first: StaticPageOptions.publishedAt stamps datePublished/dateModified and the
sitemap lastmod on every publish (static-pages.ts) — small files, likely harmless, VERIFY rather than
assume. Then confirm the DZI slicer and the bake path emit byte-stable output for unchanged input.

CONSEQUENCE 2 — THE ARCHIVAL TIER IS DESKTOP-OR-CHROME. folderSinkSupported() = isTauri() ||
supportsFolderPicker(), and showDirectoryPicker is Chromium-only. Firefox and Safari cannot write the
folder, and with credentials declined they cannot upload either — so they have NO object-storage route
at all, only GitHub Pages (small archives) or a capped zip. ACCEPTED as honest: it matches where the
native store already lives (Archie-623e), and the alternative is precisely the credential surface that
was declined. Archie-c367 must state this reason in the greyed-out destination, never hide it.

STILL IN SCOPE: bucket CORS — the bundled viewer cannot fetch its own JSON without it — but as
DOCUMENTATION beside the command, not as an API call Archie makes. And the integrity question changes
shape: what a partial/interrupted rclone run leaves behind, and whether marker-last ordering
(render-core-data-integrity contract #1) survives a third-party sync tool that does not know
archie.json is the commit point. That is now the main risk on this ticket.

The "what is rclone?" affordance is load-bearing, not decoration — this choice puts a CLI in the path of
the audience least likely to have one. /product-copy applies.

## FINDINGS 2026-07-27 — prototype run (branch proto/object-storage)

Full detail: ledgers/PROTO-object-storage-2026-07-27.md. Summary:

**Mechanism.** Confirmed against REAL infra (docker MinIO, S3-compatible SigV4; real `rclone`), not a
stub — Archie facilitates via `rclone sync`, never uploads directly (per this ticket's own 2026-07-26
grilling). An unauthenticated PUT against the bucket returns 403 — concretely why credentials-in-
browser was declined; rclone signs locally from the user's own config, Archie never sees a key.

**Byte-determinism (the constraint that replaced "does Archie own the diff").** Measured, not assumed:
Studio's current wiring (`STATIC_PAGE_OPTS`, publish-flows.svelte.ts:26) never sets `publishedAt` —
grepped, zero hits — so the "known violator to check first" this ticket flagged is NOT currently a
violator. Two identical publishes of a 3-exhibit fixture come back 22/22 files byte-IDENTICAL. One
exhibit edited + full republish: 18/22 unchanged, exactly the touched exhibit's files (+1 new history
page) differ; library-global projections stay byte-identical when untouched.

**What rclone actually transfers, same sequence.** Sync 1 (empty bucket): 22 files, 22.8 KiB. Sync 2
(edited full republish over an existing bucket): only 5/23 files actually transfer bytes (7.8 KiB) —
matches the computed delta exactly. The other 18 get a metadata-only mtime touch, not a re-upload.
Confirms the ticket's "rclone diffs source against bucket itself" claim against real transfer logs.

**Marker-last risk — the ticket's stated main risk — reproduced, not just discussed.** A plain
`rclone sync` uploaded `archie.json` FIRST in this run (transfer order has no ordering guarantee — 
rclone runs several transfers concurrently). A viewer fetching mid-sync could see a valid-looking
marker over an incomplete tree — fails OPEN, worse than the local torn-write case the existing
marker-last discipline guards (which fails closed). Verified mitigation: two-pass
`rclone sync --exclude archie.json` then `rclone copyto` the marker alone, last. Should replace the
ticket's illustrative one-line `rclone sync` command in the Archie-c367 copy-paste snippet for every
publish after the first.

**Cost table (10/30/74 GB, cites + fetch dates in the ledger).** S3 Standard $0.023/GB-mo (secondary
sources — AWS's own pricing page renders its table via client-side JS, not captured by the fetch); R2
$0.015/GB-mo, egress unconditionally free (Cloudflare's own page, verified — "no charges for egress
bandwidth for any storage class"); B2 ≈$0.00695/GB-mo, egress free up to 3x storage then $0.01/GB
(Backblaze's own page). At 74 GB: S3 $1.70/mo, R2 $1.11/mo, B2 $0.51/mo. Citation-consistency finding:
this ticket's own "~$0.30/mo for 20GB" and Archie-c367's "~$1.10/mo for 74GB" both match R2's rate
almost exactly (20×$0.015=$0.30, 74×$0.015=$1.11) and neither matches S3 or B2 — the product's
existing estimates were evidently built assuming R2, worth making explicit given R2's free-egress
property is the strongest reason to actually default there.

**Bucket CORS** (still in scope per this ticket, as documentation beside the rclone command, not code):
minimum config is GET/HEAD + AllowedOrigins — full JSON snippet in the ledger.

**Delivered:** `packages/render-core/src/publish/delta.ts` + `delta.test.ts` (6 tests, pure delta
computation, no fs) — wired into the `@render/core` barrel.
`scripts/probe/object-storage-publish.mts` — the runnable probe (needs a booted S3-compatible target;
bootstrap commands in the ledger). Gates: render-core vitest 99 files/1266 tests pass, typecheck clean.

**Open follow-ups** (not shipped — prototype scope): (1) a permanent byte-stability regression test in
`site.test.ts` so a future `publishedAt`-threading change can't silently reintroduce full-tree churn;
(2) land the two-pass rclone sequence in the Archie-c367 UI copy; (3) a draft grey-out reason string
for c367 ("Needs a folder this browser can write to — open Archie on desktop, or use Chrome or Edge"),
not decided here — c367's call.


---

## CLOSED 2026-07-27 — prototype answered; surface work is Archie-c367's

Merged d7ae26f. Mechanism proven against real MinIO+rclone: folder output is byte-deterministic
(22/22 identical on republish; one edit → 5/23 files transfer), so rclone's own diff IS the
incremental sync. Marker-first hazard reproduced and mitigated: the hand-off command must be the
TWO-PASS form (`rclone sync --exclude archie.json` then `rclone copyto` the marker) — c367's surface
copy must emit exactly that. Pricing pinned (R2 $1.11/74GB, free egress) — c367's estimates match R2.

title: Bulk metadata import: the catalogue-spreadsheet door
description:
## Question

How does an institution's catalogue spreadsheet get into Archie?

The gap: `csv-import.ts` is ANNOTATIONS only — a fixed dialect of `object,comment[,x,y,w,h][,tags]
[,reading]`. There is no door for OBJECT-LEVEL metadata: title, date, creator, identifier, rights.
Dublin Core support exists (Archie-c6bf) but per-object and by hand. A small institution arrives with
half its archive in folders and half in a spreadsheet, and Archie only has a door for the folders. At
1,000 objects, typing is not a plan.

Decide:
- The MATCHING key: filename? relative path? a column of identifiers? Institutional exports rarely
  match Archie's object ids, and folder ingest mints its own.
- Fixed dialect (csv-import.ts's precedent: "one fixed, documented dialect, no column-mapping UI")
  or a mapping step? The existing choice was deliberate and its reasoning is in that file's header —
  cite it before departing from it. A catalogue export is much less predictable than an annotation
  sheet, which is the argument FOR mapping.
- Which fields land where: DC metadata (Archie-c6bf), the RightsFields trio, plain object label?
  .claude/rules/metadata-rights-keyed-writebacks.md binds — any write-back must be a KEYED PARTIAL
  patch, never a reconstructed whole RightsFields object.
- Partial/failed rows: per-item tolerance per render-core-data-integrity contract #2 (corrupt is not
  empty), matching how csv-import already skips-and-reports.
- Does this also cover UPDATE (re-import a corrected sheet), or import-once only?

## UI/UX decided (grilling 2026-07-26)

A COLUMN MAPPING STEP — a deliberate DIVERGENCE from csv-import.ts's "one fixed, documented dialect (no
column-mapping UI)". The reason, recorded so it is not re-litigated: an annotation sheet is authored TO
Archie's spec, but a catalogue export is produced by someone else's collections system and cannot be
reshaped on demand. A fixed dialect pushes the reshaping onto the institution — the audience least
equipped to do it.

    Import metadata
      Your column        ->   Archie field
      Accession No.      ->   [identifier v]
      Object Title       ->   [title      v]
      Date Made          ->   [date       v]
      Match on:          ->   [filename   v]
      [Preview 5 rows]   [Import]

This also answers the ticket's first sub-question: the MATCHING KEY is a user choice (filename /
relative path / an identifier column), not a fixed rule.

CONSIDERED, NOT CHOSEN AS PRIMARY: the export-fill-reimport round trip — extend App.svelte:1193's
"starter CSV seeded with THIS exhibit's items" to metadata so the file carries Archie's own ids and
matching becomes trivial. Cheaper, and it has in-repo precedent. KEEP IT as the fallback on-ramp for an
institution with no existing catalogue, and consider shipping both doors. It lost as the primary because
it requires copy-pasting columns between two spreadsheets, which is exactly where institutional data
gets mangled.

Preview-before-commit is required. Per-row tolerance per render-core-data-integrity contract #2 (a bad
row is skipped and reported, never a whole-file refusal); keyed partial patches per
metadata-rights-keyed-writebacks (never reconstruct a whole RightsFields object).

---

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (D1 · build it)

Build spreadsheet catalogue import: map columns to Dublin Core, match rows to objects by filename.
CSV import today is annotations-only, so an institution arriving with a spreadsheet of titles, dates,
creators, identifiers and rights has no way in except typing. This is the biggest single gap between
Archie and 'a small museum can actually use this'. Not a small job.

Per Archie-34a2 decision 12, this gets a COLUMN-MAPPING step — a deliberate divergence from
csv-import.ts's fixed-dialect precedent, because a catalogue export comes from someone else's
collections system and cannot be reshaped on demand.


---

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (batch grill — remaining sub-questions)

**RE-IMPORT UPDATES.** Same mapping + same matching key = idempotent update of MAPPED FIELDS ONLY,
via keyed partial patches (metadata-rights-keyed-writebacks binds). Institutions always fix sheets;
import-once turns every typo into a dead end. Unmapped fields are never touched; skip-and-report
semantics apply per row exactly as on first import.

**BOTH DOORS SHIP IN V1.** Column mapping is the primary (institutions with an existing catalogue);
the export-fill-reimport starter CSV (extend App.svelte:1193's template to metadata so the file
carries Archie's own ids and matching is trivial) ships alongside as the on-ramp for the
no-catalogue case. Two import paths to build and verify — accepted knowingly.

---

## IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-27 (`feat/bulk-metadata-import`, base `b240a0e`)

Both decided doors ship. Four commits: `7a76313` (planner) · `70c5c8b` (an invariant found while
red-greening) · `a9c3b64` (copy) · `f4cf946` (dialog + wiring + e2e).

**`apps/studio/src/metadata-import.ts`** — pure, 44 unit tests. Column mapping (`targets` index-aligned
with the header, so a repeated header stays separately mappable), four match keys, and one keyed partial
patch per row. Its header records the divergence from `csv-import.ts`'s fixed dialect and the four
contracts it holds: keyed partial patches, idempotent re-import, a blank cell says nothing, per-row
tolerance. A whole-file refusal is reserved for the two cases where no row could be read either way.

**The filename key is TIERED, and this was the one real discovery.** Studio does not store the user's
filename: an import becomes `source = /assets/{id}-{safe}` and the TIFF and EXIF paths rewrite the
extension (`ingest-flows.ts:511,517`). The only field holding what the curator typed into their sheet is
`label` (`ingest-flows.ts:563`). So a filename match considers the label, the source basename and the
preserved-original name, exact tier first across all objects, then extension- and prefix-stripped — which
is what keeps `plate.tif` and `plate.jpg` in one exhibit resolving exactly instead of collapsing into an
ambiguity. Four keys total: `archieId` / `filename` / `path` / `identifier`.

**Metadata merge.** A mapped property replaces the first matching entry IN PLACE and drops later repeats
of it (otherwise every re-import appends another Creator and run two is not idempotent). An unmapped
entry — including a verbatim IIIF import with no property — is carried through untouched, in order.

**Door 2** is `buildMetadataCsvTemplate`: this exhibit's items with their current values and Archie's own
ids. Deliberately a SEPARATE file from `buildCsvTemplate`, not more columns on it — the notes template's
rows are annotations, one per note; these are one per media item, and folding them together would make a
sheet whose rows mean two things depending on which cells are filled.

**Gates.** vitest 78 files / 1031 tests · `pnpm typecheck` clean · svelte-check 1192 files 0/0 ·
studio e2e 14 passed (12 + 2 new), each new spec run 5x unchanged.

**Red-green, three injections, each restored from `/tmp`:**
- a `rights` key written by the label branch (the whole-RightsFields clobber the rule forbids) → 2 patch-
  shape assertions red, naming the injected key.
- `mergeMetadata`'s no-op return removed → its own assertion red. It did NOT redden the idempotence
  test, which exposed a real hole: a row whose only effect was collapsing a pre-existing duplicate
  produced a non-empty patch with an empty change list — previewed as a blank row and silently
  discarded. Fixed in `70c5c8b` so an empty change list means an empty patch, structurally.
- the toolbar control made unreachable → e2e red on `Import metadata…` not visible, with the overview
  itself still rendering. A first attempt (dropping the prop from the destructuring pattern) crashed the
  component and reddened the PRECONDITION instead — a red for the wrong reason, so it was redone.

Worth recording: dropping the prop from `$props()`'s destructuring while leaving it in the type
annotation IS caught by svelte-check here (2 errors), unlike the `EmptyHall`/`oncancel` case
`.claude/rules/svelte-no-typecheck-net.md` documents. The e2e is still the only thing that catches a
control that renders nothing for any other reason.

**Deferred, deliberately:**
- **Exhibit- and library-level import.** This is object-level only. The same planner would serve, but the
  match-key question is different (there is one exhibit, not N objects) and nobody asked for it.
- **Clearing a field from the sheet.** A blank cell never clears (contract 3). A sheet cannot currently
  say "remove this value"; that stays a deliberate act in the object's own editor. A future explicit
  sentinel would be the way in, and it needs its own decision.
- **Saved mappings.** A second import of the same institution's export re-does the mapping. The starter-
  spreadsheet door sidesteps it entirely, so this is cheap to live without until someone hits it.
- **A non-URI rights value.** Refused per row, naming both accepted forms. Storing "Public domain, we
  think" in an IIIF `rights` slot would publish a broken rights statement.

title: Prove 1,000 images end to end
description:
## Question

Does the whole pipeline actually survive 1,000 images end to end — and where does it break first?

Every other ticket on this map assumes a scale nobody has driven. This is the honest test: a real
1,000-image folder through ingest -> annotate -> bake -> publish -> served website, with numbers at
each stage.

What it must report, not assume:
- INGEST: wall-clock, memory, and what happens when it dies at file #800. There is no progress model
  and no resume today. The map's Fog flags this; this ticket is what sharpens it.
- BAKE: derivatives are split across two moments (thumbnails at ingest, tiles at publish). At 1,000
  images this is where the hours go. Is it resumable? Cancellable? Does the UI survive it?
- PUBLISH: the folder sink writing ~521,000 files (full fidelity) or ~2,000 (web quality). Both.
- SERVE: the bundled viewer against the published tree, gallery and search at 1,000 objects.
- The monolithic library.json (read whole store.ts:182, written whole store.ts:217) under 1,000
  objects with frequent saves. Decision 5 predicts this is fine; prove or refute it.

Run on DESKTOP — the native folder store (Archie-623e, code merged) is the only place 10-30 GB can
live. Note that desktop folder ingest is broken until Archie-ce7a lands, which is why that blocks this.

perf-measure-the-flow binds: end-to-end via scripts/perf/publishrun.mjs, attribute by DIFFERENCE
against a run with a stage disabled (concurrent stages mean summing per-call times double-counts),
and ratchet anything won. Record what BROKE as findings; new tickets graduate from them.

## UI/UX decided (grilling 2026-07-26) — the progress model this must validate

BACKGROUND INGEST/BAKE, BLOCKING PUBLISH.

- INGEST and BAKE run in the BACKGROUND behind a status-bar job indicator; the app stays usable and the
  author keeps annotating what has already landed. Needs pause/cancel and a trustworthy time estimate.
- PUBLISH stays BLOCKING — library state must be stable while the tree is projected — but gains cancel
  and an estimate. Today's model (PUBLISH_STEPS, publish-machine.svelte.ts:106) is a stepped checklist
  with no cancel, no resume and no estimate: fine for 4 images, brutal for 1,000.

    Status bar (app usable)          Publish (blocking)
      Baking 340/1000 ~12 min          Uploading 12,400/521,000
      [pause] [cancel]                 ~41 min left    [cancel]

REJECTED: everything-background (edits during a publish land in a half-projected tree — marker-last
ordering protects the commit point, not the projection); everything-blocking (locks the app for the
~hour a 1,000-image bake runs, the worst possible moment to lock someone out).

So this ticket now reports on TWO axes: does the pipeline survive 1,000 images, AND is the model above
sufficient at that scale — is the estimate trustworthy, does cancel leave a clean resumable state, does
a status-bar indicator still feel alive after an hour.

---

## ABSORBS Archie-b9c4 (heap-aware cache eviction budgets) — user decision 2026-07-27

b9c4 asked whether studio/viewer's in-memory caches (masters-on-demand, lightbox, OSD tiles) need
byte-budgeted LRUs with heap-scaled concurrency, on freecut's precedent (128 MB waveform / 200 MB gif,
`filmstrip-cache.ts:416-459`). It is folded here rather than measured separately, because THIS drill
exercises the real pipeline at real scale and a synthetic probe does not.

**Why the separate probe was abandoned, specifically.** `scripts/perf/heaprun.mjs` was written for
b9c4 and its own header states the disqualifying limit: `Runtime.getHeapUsage` reports the V8 heap,
which does **not** include decoded image surfaces, OSD tile textures, or GPU memory — *exactly* the
things a cache budget would be about. It could honestly answer "does JS-side retention grow without
bound", and that is not b9c4's question. The script is left in the tree, unrun; if anyone revives it,
read that caveat first.

Also worth carrying: freecut's 128/200 MB constants are freecut's, measured on freecut's workload.
Copying them here without our own numbers would be the speculative elaboration CLAUDE.md warns about.

### Added to this ticket's acceptance

Alongside the per-stage numbers already required, the run must report:

- **Peak memory** across the walk, by whatever instrument actually sees decoded surfaces and GPU
  memory (CDP `Memory` domain / per-process reporting — NOT `Runtime.getHeapUsage`).
- **Whether retention grows across a full walk** (open N objects, return home, repeat) or is bounded.
- **A verdict, stated either way:** does anything here need a byte-budgeted LRU, and if so which cache
  and at what budget — derived from these numbers, not from freecut's.

If the answer is "bounded, no LRU needed", that is a real result and closes the question for good.


---

If the answer is "bounded, no LRU needed", that is a real result and closes the question for good.

title: GitHub publish is O(tiles) with no incremental push
description:
## Question

Make the GitHub publish stop being O(tiles) — is incremental push enough, or is git simply the wrong
transport for a published tree?

MEASURED (Archie-34a2): publishToGitHub uploads one POST /git/blobs per binary file at
BLOB_CONCURRENCY = 6 (ghpages.ts:189), and ghpages.ts:202 creates the tree with NO base_tree —
"replace-this-tree" — so every republish re-uploads every tile. Four 6000x8000 scans = 4,132 blob
POSTs, a ~52-minute floor against GitHub's ~80 content-writes/min secondary limit. This is the
measured cause of the user-reported "could barely publish a four image exhibit", and it is
arithmetic, not a rough edge.

Two fixes, and they are not alternatives:
- base_tree + skip unchanged blobs. Makes REPUBLISH cheap. Does nothing for the first publish.
- The tiling threshold (separate ticket). Cuts the file count ~500x, which fixes BOTH.

So this ticket is narrower than it looks: with the threshold landed, is incremental push still worth
building? Decide with the threshold's measured numbers in hand, not before.

Also settle what GitHub Pages is FOR now that it cannot hold a target-scale archive (1 GB cap). The
map's position is that it stays the FREE route for web-quality, images-mostly archives (~400 MB for
1,000 images) — which is most small institutions. If that holds, this path stays first-class and
must be fast; if not, say so and demote it.

Blocked on the tiling threshold. Do not optimize a transport for a file count you are about to
delete 99.8% of.

## UI/UX note (grilling 2026-07-26)

Publish stays BLOCKING with cancel + a real time estimate (decided on Archie-c74e). PublishProgress
already carries {phase, done, total} during upload (ghpages.ts:69) — the gap is cancel and estimate, not
instrumentation. If this ticket concludes incremental push is worth building, the progress model must
distinguish "uploading 300 changed files" from "uploading 4,132" or the user cannot tell an incremental
republish from a full one.

## IMPLEMENTED — browser transport only (2026-07-27, branch `feat/incremental-push`)

Commits `facbded` + `58abcc6` off `c800a83`. render-core 1282 pass (was 1261+ baseline), typecheck
clean; studio 1037 pass, typecheck clean, svelte-check 1194 files 0 errors 0 warnings.

**Design.** `publish/push-delta.ts` is the pure half: `gitBlobSha` (sha1 of `"blob <len>\0<bytes>"`,
verified against `git hash-object` itself, not a hand-written constant) and `planPush(local, remote)
-> {toUpload, toReference, toDelete, truncated}`. `ghpages.ts` reads the base commit's tree once
(`GET /git/commits/{sha}` then `GET /git/trees/{sha}?recursive=1`), plans, and uploads only
`toUpload`; everything else contributes a `sha` reference to a blob GitHub already stores.

**Still no `base_tree`.** The tree is emitted COMPLETE, so a removed exhibit drops out by omission —
structural, not bookkeeping. A `base_tree` + `sha: null` design would have to get the delete list
exactly right, because create-tree "Returns an error if you try to delete a file that does not exist".

**Cited API limits.** Recursive tree read caps at **100,000 entries / 7 MB** and sets `truncated: true`
(docs.github.com/en/rest/git/trees). A truncated OR unreadable listing degrades to a full re-upload,
never to a skip — every failure direction is "slow", none is "corrupt". Note the cap sits below the
map's own 592k-file reference point, so an un-thresholded archival library gets no benefit at all;
this optimization is for libraries under ~100k files, which is exactly the post-threshold world.

**Measured from tests.** Unchanged republish: **0** blob POSTs (was one per binary). One re-rendered
tile out of 5 files: **1** blob POST, and the assertion checks it carries that tile's bytes, not merely
that one upload happened. Truncated/unreadable: 3 of 3 binaries re-upload.

**Red-green, 5 injections.** Inverting the sha match → 13 red. Dropping the `planPush` truncation guard
→ 2 red. Dropping the *transport's* truncation guard → 1 red (a SECOND, independent guard — the first
injection had left the transport tests green, so "the truncation guard is proven" would have been a
false claim from one probe). Removing the listing-failure swallow → 1 red. Breaking the blob framing →
**only** the `git hash-object` test red, because the transport tests build their mock remote with the
same `localBlobShas` under test; that one test is the sole tie between our sha and git's object id, and
that is now written into the test file so nobody deletes it as redundant. Plus 20/20 unchanged-tree
runs (a-green-run-is-one-sample).

**Progress model** (the UI/UX note's requirement): new `comparing` phase and `uploading.unchanged`, so
Publish.svelte renders "Uploading media — 1 of 1… (4 already up to date)".

**DESKTOP PARITY GAP — stated, not closed.** The one-motion desktop deploy does not use this transport
and gets nothing from it. `src-tauri/src/github.rs:339-341` stages into a **throwaway**
`Repository::init` and `:392` writes a **root commit** (no parents), so push negotiation has no base
and the pack carries every blob on every deploy — O(tiles) in BYTES. But it is ONE request, so the
~80-content-writes/min secondary limit and the ~52-minute floor that motivated this ticket do not apply
there. Closing it means fetching the remote branch into the staging repo and committing on top; that is
a Rust change and a separate ticket.

**What this does NOT settle** — the ticket's actual question, which is still open. The spec asks
whether incremental push is worth building *given the tiling threshold* (Archie-86ff), and says not to
decide before that lands. `ledgers/PROBE-tiling-threshold-2026-07-27.md` recommends deriving the local
threshold from `MAX_MASTER_DIM`, which makes local-import tiling inert and cuts ~592,000 files to
~1,000 for a 1,000-object library. **With that landed, the first publish is already cheap and this
change buys much less than the 4,132-POST measurement suggests** — its remaining value is republish
cost for libraries that still tile (remote IIIF at the 4096px bar) and for the ordinary case of
re-publishing after editing one object. Nothing here re-answers "is GitHub Pages still first-class",
which the spec also asks for and which needs the 1 GB-cap arithmetic, not this transport.


---

## CLOSED 2026-07-27 — browser transport is delta-based; two flagged remainders have homes

Merged ec4c763. Unchanged republish = 0 blob POSTs; one-tile edit = 1 POST; truncated/unreadable
listing degrades to full re-upload, never a skip. Desktop parity (Rust gh_push_tree root-commit pack
carries every blob, but in ONE request so the rate-limit motivation doesn't bite) → follow-up ticket.
The strategic "is GitHub Pages still first-class at archival scale" question belongs to the map-level
destination story (Archie-c367 presents the honest per-destination verdicts from the probe).

title: Zip64 writer: kill the 4 GiB and 65,535-entry caps
description:
## Question

Swap the zip WRITER for one with Zip64, killing the 4 GiB and 65,535-entry caps — without dropping
Firefox?

fflate 0.8.3 has no Zip64 writer. fs/zip.ts:83-101 documents the consequence precisely: its EOCD
writer stores the entry count in 2 bytes and offsets in 4, with NO overflow check, so both serializers
(`ZipFilesystem.toZip`, `ZipStreamFilesystem`) enforce ZIP_FORMAT_LIMITS and throw an actionable
refusal rather than emit a silently corrupt archive.

Those caps are the LIBRARY's, not the browser's — which is what made decision 4 (keep Firefox) safe.
`@zip.js/zip.js` supports Zip64 and works everywhere. Confirm that before committing.

Decide:
- Is the swap write-side only, or does the READ side move too? The read path has its own caps
  (ZIP_LIMITS zip-bomb guards, SRC_MAX_BYTES = 1 GiB in limits.ts) and its own trust boundary
  (.claude/rules/untrusted-archive-open-seam.md — openArchieLibrary is the ONE composition point;
  do not grow a second).
- Does SRC_MAX_BYTES rise with it? A valid 3 GB zip is currently unopenable via ?src= regardless of
  whether it can be written. Raising a hostile-input cap is a security decision, not a bug fix.
- Streaming: openStreamingZipSave's ZipStreamFilesystem is the path that matters (binding.ts:105 —
  streaming works on Chromium, Tauri, AND Firefox/Safari via OPFS staging). The eager path's
  EAGER_ZIP_CEILING_BYTES = 1 GiB memory guard is separate and stays.
- Bundle cost: fflate is also used elsewhere; a second zip library is dead weight if it doesn't replace.

Lower priority than the map's spine — at target scale the zip is not the archival route anyway. This
keeps SMALL archives working well and removes a cap that refuses honestly but still refuses.

## Implementation note (2026-07-27, branch `feat/zip64`, `56cf7c5`)

**Decided AGAINST the library swap.** `@zip.js/zip.js` was never added — confirmed absent from every
`package.json` in the repo, and no evidence found it was ever tried. Instead: fflate's own writer was
extended in place with a hand-written Zip64 EOCD Record + Locator, verified against fflate 0.8.2's
pinned source (npm-packed and read directly, not from training data): the only Zip64 code anywhere in
the bundle is `z64e`, a READ-side helper (`esm/index.mjs:1843`) — `wzh`/`wzf` (the write side) have
zero Zip64 emission. This confirms the ticket's premise exactly; "fflate 0.8.3" in the question above
should read 0.8.2, the version actually pinned (`packages/render-core/package.json`).

**What shipped — entries dimension only, streaming path only:**

`ZipStreamFilesystem` (`packages/render-core/src/fs/zip-stream.ts`) no longer refuses past
`ZIP_FORMAT_LIMITS.maxEntries` (65,535). Past that ceiling it now intercepts fflate's own trailing
`Zip.end()` chunk (`[central directory entries][classic 22-byte EOCD]`), discards fflate's own EOCD
bytes (proven corrupted past 65,535 — the entry-count `wbytes` write spills a byte into the adjacent
central-directory-size field), and rebuilds the tail itself from `cdOffset`/`cdSize` values the sink
already tracks independently (never parsed back out of fflate's own output) — a Zip64 EOCD Record +
Locator ahead of a classic EOCD sentinelled to 0xFFFF. See `buildEocdTail` and its doc comment.

Proven for a REAL 66,001-entry archive (no injected limit, production `ZIP_FORMAT_LIMITS`) against
THREE independent readers, none of which share code with the writer beyond fflate itself for the first:
fflate's own `unzipSync`, the repo's own open path (`ZipFilesystem.fromZip`, driven through the full
`Filesystem` seam — every entry enumerated via `root.entries()`, spot-checked by content), and —
entirely outside fflate — Info-ZIP `unzip -t` (clean) and Python's `zipfile` (`testzip()` → `None`).
Red-green: the new tests fail against the pre-fix code with the exact "more than N files" refusal
(confirmed by running them before the fix landed).

**Scope, deliberately narrower than the question above — flagged honestly:**

- **`ZipFilesystem.toZip` (eager) is UNCHANGED** — still refuses past 65,535 entries. The ticket itself
  names streaming as "the path that matters" (Chromium `showSaveFilePicker`, Tauri, and Firefox/Safari
  via OPFS staging all route through `ZipStreamFilesystem`); the eager path is the fallback for a
  browser with neither, already memory-bounded separately at 1 GiB (`EAGER_ZIP_CEILING_BYTES`). Fixing
  it the same way would mean re-deriving `zipSync`'s central-directory offset/size independently of its
  single-shot buffer output (the same corruption-avoidance the streaming fix routes around, but without
  the streaming path's incremental byte-tracking to lean on) — a second, differently-shaped surgery,
  deferred as out of scope for this low-priority pass.
- **The 4 GiB byte-size cap is UNCHANGED on BOTH paths.** Going past it needs a PER-ENTRY Zip64 extra
  field on every local/central-directory header whose offset would overflow — the fix here only touches
  the trailing EOCD block, not per-entry headers, because the entries-only case never needs one (the
  running total stays under 4 GiB by construction, since the byte cap is still enforced). Extending to
  the byte dimension is materially more surface (N per-entry header rewrites, not one trailing block)
  and isn't exercised here — a real >4 GiB archive isn't buildable cheaply in CI, and the ticket itself
  permits documenting-not-testing this boundary. `ZipStreamFilesystem.commit` still throws
  `zipFormatError("bytes", ...)` at the existing 4 GiB ceiling, unchanged.
- **The READ side did not move.** `SRC_MAX_BYTES` (1 GiB) and `ZIP_LIMITS` are untouched, per the
  ticket's own scoping — `untrusted-archive-open-seam.md`'s single composition point
  (`packages/render-core/src/publish/open.ts`) was not touched. Raising a hostile-input cap is a
  separate security decision this pass does not make.
- **No new dependency.** fflate remains the only zip library; nothing else in the repo needed to change
  (verified: no other production call site references `ZIP_FORMAT_LIMITS`/`zipFormatError`/
  `maxEntries` outside `packages/render-core/src/fs/`).

**Gates (render-core only — the only package touched):**
- `pnpm exec vitest run`: 98 files, **1261 passed**, 0 failed (includes the new 66,001-entry test at
  682ms and the rewritten injected-limit test).
- `pnpm typecheck` (TS7 native, per `two-typescript-compilers.md`): clean, exit 0.

**Follow-up, not filed as a separate ticket yet:** the byte-size Zip64 dimension (per-entry extra
fields) and the eager-path entries fix, if either is ever wanted. Both are additive to what's here, not
a redesign of it.


## Implementation note (2026-07-28, branch `feat/zip64-bytes`, `c27aa95`) — BYTE dimension closed

**The intercept from the entries-dimension fix does NOT extend to bytes — traced and proven, not
assumed.** fflate 0.8.3's writer (`wzh`, called from `Zip.prototype.e` — the SAME final chunk the
old intercept patched) writes the central-directory entry's local-header-OFFSET field via
`wbytes(d, b+10, ce)`. `wbytes` does `d[b]=v; v>>>=8` in a loop, and `>>>=` performs ToUint32 on
its left operand BEFORE shifting — so any offset >= 2**32 is silently truncated mod 2**32 in the
WRITTEN BYTES. That corruption sits INSIDE the central-directory bytes the old intercept passed
through as "unaffected, kept as-is" (true only for the entries-count dimension). A second, worse
corruption sits even earlier: fflate's streaming mode uses a per-entry DATA DESCRIPTOR (general-
purpose bit 3) for compressed/uncompressed size, written via the same unchecked `wbytes` and
flushed to the sink as an ORDINARY (non-final) chunk, DURING that entry's own commit — a finalize-
time intercept has no way to repair bytes already on the wire.

**Fix: stopped using fflate's Zip/ZipPassThrough writer entirely for the streaming sink.**
`ZipStreamFilesystem` now hand-writes every local header, central-directory entry, and the trailing
EOCD block itself, from offset/size/crc values it tracks independently — the same "never trust the
library's own unchecked write" discipline the entries fix established, just applied one layer
earlier. Since `commit()` already receives each entry's COMPLETE bytes before touching the sink, no
data descriptor is needed at all: real CRC/size go straight into the local header, which sidesteps
that corruption class rather than working around it. Per-entry Zip64 extras are added ONLY when a
field would overflow (APPNOTE 4.4.1.4): an entry's own size (rare — one file past 4 GiB), and/or its
local-header offset (the realistic case — cumulative archive bytes crossing 4 GiB at ordinary media
scale). `>=` against the threshold throughout (not `>`), so a real value that happens to equal the
sentinel itself is never mistaken for representable.

**Prior art, opened and cited by line (not assumed):** byte layout was checked against cpython 3.14's
`Lib/zipfile/__init__.py` (`structCentralDir`/`structFileHeader` field order; `_decodeExtra:578-621`
for the CONDITIONAL/sparse zip64-extra parsing this relies on — an extra can carry ONLY the fields
whose fixed-field sentinel is set, in a fixed order, e.g. offset alone with no size fields) and
against fflate's OWN zip64 READER (`z64hs`/`zh`), which parses the identical sparse shape. Also
found and documented a genuine limitation IN fflate's own reader: `unzipSync` locates the Zip64 EOCD
record via a 32-bit read of the Locator's record-offset field, though APPNOTE 4.3.15 defines it as
8 bytes — so fflate's own `unzipSync`/`ZipFilesystem.fromZip` cannot correctly reopen an archive
whose central directory starts past 4 GiB, independent of whether this writer produced it correctly.
Python's `zipfile` reads that same field as a genuine 8-byte value and has no such blind spot.

**Testing, scoped around that reader-side limitation:**
- Fixture-based unit tests on the exported builders (`buildLocalHeader`, `buildCentralDirectoryEntry`,
  `buildEocdTail`, plus `crc32`/`dosDateTime`) pin exact byte offsets against hand-decoded fields,
  including the classic/Zip64 boundary at exactly `0xFFFFFFFF` (a value EQUAL to the sentinel must
  still go via the extra field).
- A cheap in-repo round-trip test (injected tiny `maxBytes` threshold) exercises the real `commit()`/
  `finish()` path for both overflow axes (entry size AND offset) through fflate's own `unzipSync` AND
  `ZipFilesystem.fromZip` — safe because the injected threshold keeps the archive's real central-
  directory offset far below fflate's read-side 4 GiB blind spot.
- Manually verified ONCE (not committed as a CI test, per the ticket's own wall-clock allowance): a
  real 4.102 GiB archive (4 x ~1050 MiB STORED entries, central directory offset ~4.404 GB) streamed
  to disk, verified clean by TWO readers sharing no code with fflate: Info-ZIP `unzip -t` ("No errors
  detected") and Python's `zipfile` (`testzip()` -> `None`, all 4 entries + correct per-entry
  `header_offset`s, including offsets past 4 GiB).
- Red-green: 17 new/changed tests fail against the pre-fix code (missing exports for the fixture
  tests; the old refusal error for the round-trip test, where Zip64 handling is now expected).

**Gates (render-core only):**
- `pnpm exec vitest run`: 98 files, **1277 passed**, 0 failed (baseline 1261 + 16 net new — 17 new/
  changed tests, one of which replaced the old "refuses past 4 GiB" test).
- `pnpm typecheck` (TS7 native): clean, exit 0.

**Scope, matching the entries-dimension fix's own scoping:** streaming path (`ZipStreamFilesystem`)
only. `ZipFilesystem.toZip` (eager) still refuses on entries alone and has no bytes handling at all
— unchanged, and still out of scope for the reason already recorded above (re-deriving the central-
directory offset/size independently of `zipSync`'s single-shot output). `zipFormatError`'s "bytes"
kind was removed (dead code — nothing calls it anymore); "entries" (the eager path's own refusal)
is unchanged.

Both dimensions named in the ticket title are now closed for the path that matters at scale
(Chromium `showSaveFilePicker`, Tauri, and Firefox/Safari via OPFS staging all route through
`ZipStreamFilesystem`).

---

## CLOSED 2026-07-27 — both caps removed on the streaming writer

Entries: merged 2e1a509. Bytes: merged (hand-written local headers/CD/EOCD, per-entry Zip64 extras
on overflow; real 4.102 GiB archive verified by unzip -t and Python zipfile; render-core 1315/1315
on the combined tree). The eager non-Chromium fallback path still refuses past 65,535 entries by
design — its ceiling is memory; the streaming path is what every uncapped route uses. fflate's own
reader cannot reopen a CD past 4 GiB (32-bit read at :2684) — documented in the impl note; external
readers are the verification standard.

title: The export surface: the final option set
description:
## Question

What is the final set of export options, and how does the surface present them?

Left unanswered in the charting grilling. The findings that constrain it:

- All three destinations call the SAME publishLibrary. The only real differences are the sink, plus
  `withOriginals` (folder only) and `slugs` subset (zip only) — and those are BACKWARDS from what the
  names promise. "Share a working copy" ships a published, derivative-only tree with no masters.
- The duplication the user reported is a FALLBACK COLLISION: "To a local folder" silently downloads a
  zip when the browser can't pick a folder, so on Firefox/Safari two buttons produce the identical
  file. That is an unavailable capability masquerading as a choice.
- Availability is not uniform: folderSinkSupported() = isTauri() || supportsFolderPicker(), and
  showDirectoryPicker is Chromium-only. Firefox and Safari have NO uncapped path at all.
- Two things live outside this surface today and may belong in it: the CSV notes template download
  (App.svelte:1196) and the copy-paste embed snippet.

The three candidate shapes, from the grilling:
- ONE FLOW, pick a destination. Contents uniform by default; differences shown as FACTS, not choices;
  an unavailable destination greyed WITH ITS REASON, never silently swapped.
- TWO GROUPS by intent: Publish (the web / your own host) vs Save a copy (zip). Clean, but the folder
  straddles both — it is how you publish to a non-GitHub host AND how you escape the zip caps.
- THREE CARDS as today, with contents and limits stated and the silent fallback removed.

Decisions 1-3 already fix what each option CONTAINS, so this ticket is about the surface only.
Blocked on the probe ticket: if the probe already tells the user which route their archive can take,
this surface may shrink to confirming that recommendation rather than offering a menu.

/product-copy applies to every label and every refusal string here.

## UI/UX decided (grilling 2026-07-26)

ONE FLOW, WITH THE PROBE'S RECOMMENDATION PRE-SELECTED. The surface CONFIRMS a decision rather than
posing a fresh one:

    Publish your library

      Recommended for your archive:
      (o) GitHub Pages - free            web quality, ~900 MB
      ( ) Object storage  ~$1.10/mo      archival, ~74 GB
      ( ) A folder on this computer
      ( ) One .zip file                  [too big - 2,400 files]

      Quality:  (o) Web    ( ) Archival
      [Publish]

RULES THIS ENCODES:
- An unavailable destination is GREYED WITH ITS REASON, never silently swapped. This kills the fallback
  collision (folder -> silent zip download) that made two buttons produce identical files on
  Firefox/Safari.
- Contents are uniform by default; differences between destinations are stated as FACTS, not offered as
  choices. Decisions 1-3 on Archie-34a2 already fix what each one contains.
- The quality tier appears here as a pre-checked, changeable control (Archie-4b0a decided publish-time).
- Firefox/Safari see BOTH folder and object storage greyed, carrying the desktop-or-Chrome reason from
  Archie-c85f. State it; never hide it.

REJECTED: two-groups-by-intent (the folder straddles both — it is how you publish to a non-GitHub host
AND how you escape the zip caps); three-cards-fixed (three things producing the same artifact still read
as three separate features, which is what caused the original confusion).

BLOCKED ON Archie-7280 — without the probe there is no recommendation to pre-select and this collapses
back into a plain menu. /product-copy applies to every label and every greyed-out reason string.

---

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (batch grill — the two orphans)

**Embed snippet MOVES IN — CSV notes template STAYS PUT.** The embed snippet lands on the
post-publish success panel (it is only meaningful once a URL exists). The CSV template
(App.svelte:1196) is per-exhibit authoring INPUT, not a publish artifact — moving it in would force
exhibit selection into the publish flow.

Also binding on the mock's size estimates: audio now transcodes to Opus in the web tier
(Archie-4b0a), so AV library estimates must reflect Opus, not WAV.


---

## SHIPPED 2026-07-27 — branch `feat/export-surface` (`214dae1`, `6e8f4bc`, `640d099`)

The decided mock is the surface. `apps/studio/src/export-surface.ts` is the decision layer, kept out
of the component so it is drivable headlessly; `Publish.svelte` draws it.

**The final option set, as shipped:**

    Publish your library
    N items across M exhibits. Archie builds the same finished site whichever you pick.

      RECOMMENDED FOR YOUR ARCHIVE
      <the probe's `why`, in the author's own numbers>

      (o) GitHub Pages              Recommended
          free — 184 MB of the 1 GB GitHub Pages allows
          A free website at your own address. Archie puts it there for you.
          184 MB · 180 files
      ( ) Object storage
          free — under the 10 GB free tier   |   about $1.11/month on Cloudflare R2 for 74 GB, …
          Rented storage with no size limit. Archie writes the files and hands you the
          command to upload them — Cloudflare R2 charges nothing to serve them.
      ( ) A folder on this computer
          no size limit — … written to a folder you choose, ready to upload to any host
      ( ) One .zip file
          one file, 220 MB — and the only option that also carries your original files

      QUALITY
      (o) Archival   4.6 GB      Every image at the size you scanned it, every recording as
                                 you recorded it.
      ( ) Web        184 MB      Images resized to 2,400 px across and audio compressed. Notes
                                 stay on the right spot. Your original files stay on your disk
                                 either way.

      [Preview as reader]  [Cancel]  [Publish]

      ALSO, WHENEVER YOU NEED ONE:
      [Deposit a copy]      Every published file with a checksum beside it, in the BagIt layout
                            repositories ask for.
      [One .html file]      The library and a reader in a single file that opens by double-click.

On Firefox/Safari (`folderSinkSupported()` false) the folder and object-storage rows stay in place,
greyed, each carrying *"not available in this browser — writing to a folder needs the desktop app or
Chrome"*. The refusal keeps full contrast against the dimmed row.

**The fallback collision is gone at the source.** The `local` phase — the screen that turned "to a
local folder" into a silent .zip download — is deleted, along with its `done-zip` panel, the `onzip`
prop and `saveZip`. There is no code path in `export-surface.ts` or `Publish.svelte` that substitutes
one destination for another.

**Where each feeder landed.**
- Archie-c85f — object storage is the folder writer plus a success panel carrying the **two-pass**
  command (`rclone sync … --exclude archie.json`, then `rclone copyto` the marker), a remote:bucket
  field defaulting to `r2:my-archive`, the CORS note, and a "what is rclone" line. Pricing copy is
  R2's, matching the ticket's own estimates.
- Archie-039e — "Deposit a copy" is an additional export ACTION, not a destination row, per this
  ticket's charting. `saveBagZip` is new beside `saveZipToDisk`: the latter forces an `.archie.zip`
  suffix, and naming a bag that invites feeding it back to Archie's importer.
- Archie-4b0a — the tier is a pre-checked, changeable control set from the recommendation and pushed
  into the engine via `publish-flows.setTier`; the projection cache is already keyed on it.
  `unscaledSelectors` is surfaced on the chooser when non-empty.
- The **embed snippet** moved onto the post-publish success panel (collapsed, "Put an exhibit inside
  another page"), pointing at the live site's own URL. The CSV template stayed put.

**Probe cost, measured** (this ticket asked; `archive-inventory.test.ts`'s header carries the table).
`probeArchive` over a synthetic 10,000-entry inventory, 3 runs: **23.1 / 15.1 / 13.6 ms** worst case
(6000 px masters that tile at archival, 5.96 M published files); 10.1 / 4.9 / 5.1 ms untiled; 0.9 ms
at 1,000 entries. One frame at the top of the range, so it runs unchunked. The expensive half is the
INVENTORY — one OPFS stat per stored asset — which `archive-inventory.ts` runs at concurrency 6 in
200-object chunks with a macrotask yield between them, pinned by a test that queues a `setTimeout`
before the walk and asserts it lands first. Note the publish surface's probe is **fully sampled**
(`imagesSampledFraction` = 1): the library already knows its own pixels, so nothing is decoded.

**Gates.** studio vitest 1197 (baseline 1177, +20), typecheck clean, svelte-check 1212 files 0/0,
studio e2e **19 passed** (baseline 14, +5) on a private `STUDIO_E2E_PORT=5241`. Red-greened: the
