title: element.test.ts waits by draining a fixed number of event-loop turns — at least one is a CI flake
description:
## Question

`packages/archie-viewer/src/element.test.ts` uses **fixed-count event-loop drains** as waits, and at least one of them is a real flake. Replace them with condition waits.

## The measurement (2026-07-27)

CI's `test` job went **red** on `integrate/finder`:

```
FAIL src/element.test.ts:416
  AV medium branch (ADR-0019): a sound/video object mounts the native player, not OSD
  → opening a sound object mounts a native <audio>
  AssertionError: expected null not to be null
```

**It is not that branch's doing, and it is not noise.** Evidence, in the order it was gathered:

- the finder branch touches **six files**, none in `packages/archie-viewer`;
- the **tokens** branch shares the same base (`0c0b121`) and its `test` job **passed**, including this file;
- **24 local runs, 0 failures** — 12 on `main`+tokens, 12 with the finder merged;
- **`gh run rerun --failed` on the identical commit came back green.** Same code, red then green. That is the definition.

## The mechanism

`:360` waits by draining the event loop a fixed number of times:

```ts
for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0));
```

Twenty turns is enough under light local load and not enough on a loaded CI runner. It is a race with a magic number, and the number is invisible at the assertion — the failure surfaces as `expected null not to be null` on a perfectly correct mount.

**Four instances in this one file** (`8`, `20`, `20`, `60` iterations — the spread is itself the tell that these were tuned until they passed):

```
for (let i = 0; i < 8;  i++) await Promise.resolve();
for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0));
for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) await Promise.resolve();
for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) await Promise.resolve();
```

No other file in `packages/` or `apps/` uses the pattern.

## The work

Replace each with a wait on the **condition**, not on a tick count — `vi.waitFor(() => { expect(...).not.toBeNull(); })` or equivalent, with a real timeout. A condition wait fails with a message about the thing that never appeared; a drained-tick wait fails with `null`.

**Then prove it, because this is the exact class where a green run proves nothing** (`.claude/rules/a-green-run-is-one-sample.md`): run the file **≥20 independent times under load** (build something concurrently), not once, and report the denominator. The current code will not reproduce its failure on an idle machine — that is why it survived.

## Why this matters beyond one test

A false red trains everyone who meets it to re-run until green, which is the habit that makes the *next* real failure invisible. This one was caught only because the branch it fired on had no plausible connection to the file — had it fired on the embed slice's own branch, it would have read as a genuine regression and cost real time.
closeReason: Fixed in b84d50b. All four fixed-count drains (8/20/20/60) plus two bare setTimeout(0) ticks replaced with vi.waitFor condition waits. Proven red-green: 25 runs under 32-way CPU load, before = 21 pass / 4 fail (every failure the exact CI one, 'expected null not to be null' on the <audio> mount), after = 25 pass / 0 fail. A second instance of the same bug class was found and fixed in the process: waiting on .reader-surface returns BEFORE await import('./reader.js') resolves, so OSD's module body evaluated after teardown and failed the file while all 38 tests reported green (9/25 under load); waitForReaderMounted waits for the terminal post-import state instead.

title: desktop-boot.sh waits for library.json and asserts localStorage — a race, confirmed flaky
description:
## Question

`scripts/desktop-boot.sh` waits for one signal and asserts a different fact. Confirmed flaky 2026-07-27: **red then green on the identical commit** (`ebd7424`, `gh run rerun --failed`).

## The failure

```
booting …/src-tauri/target/debug/archie on :99
library written; stopping the app
FAIL   origin NOT packaged — localstorage holds: <none>
ok     no dev-server origin in the profile
ok     no 0-byte files (2 files on disk)
ok     no leftover .tmp-* files
ok     library.json is 21597 bytes
ok     library.json parses — 6 exhibit(s)
RESULT: FAIL
```

Every other assertion passed. The app booted, wrote a correct 6-exhibit library, left no torn or temp files. Only the localStorage assertion failed, and it failed with `<none>` — not a wrong origin, *nothing at all*.

## The mechanism

`desktop-boot.sh:71-89`:

```sh
for _ in $(seq 1 "$BOOT_TIMEOUT"); do
  [ -s "$LJ" ] && break          # ← waits for library.json
  …
done
echo "library written; stopping the app"
kill "$APP_PID"                  # ← kills IMMEDIATELY on that signal
sleep 2
```

The wait condition is **`library.json` becoming non-empty**. The asserted fact is **what WebKitGTK flushed to its localStorage database**, which is written asynchronously on its own schedule. Nothing in the script waits for it. On the failing run the app lived ~1s (`02:38:59.81` boot → `02:39:00.82` kill), which is ample for the fs write the loop polls and not necessarily ample for the localStorage flush.

**This is the same shape as `Archie-3e2d`** (`element.test.ts` draining a fixed count of event-loop turns) and as the finder's off-screen results (`Archie-8e73`, where text/count/`toBeVisible` all passed while nothing was reachable): **a gate measuring something adjacent to what it claims.**

## Why it matters more than one red run

It fired on `integrate/wave2`, a branch that touches **no** desktop file — asserted by set difference against `src-tauri/**` and `scripts/desktop*`, empty — while the same gate passed on `integrate/tokens`, which carries the only Studio change in that wave. So it read as "wave 2 broke the desktop app" and cost a real investigation.

Had it fired on a branch that *did* touch the fs seam, it would have read as a genuine regression and been believed. A false red on a gate built specifically because three desktop defects shipped invisibly is corrosive to the thing the gate exists for.

## The work

Wait for **the fact being asserted**, not a proxy for it:

- poll the localStorage database for the expected origin (with a timeout) before killing the app, the way the script already polls `library.json`; **or**
- shut the app down cleanly (SIGTERM and *wait for exit*) rather than `kill` + `sleep 2`, so WebKit flushes on teardown; **or**
- if neither is reliable, make the assertion tolerant and say so at the assertion — a documented soft check beats an intermittent hard one.

**Then prove it under load**, ≥20 runs with the denominator reported. `.claude/rules/a-green-run-is-one-sample.md`: the current code will not reproduce on an unloaded machine, which is exactly why it passed three times before anyone saw it.

## Do not
Do not fix this by increasing `sleep 2`. A longer sleep is the same race with a bigger constant, and it makes the gate slower for everyone while still failing under sufficient load — the `element.test.ts` sites at 8/20/20/60 iterations are what that path looks like after a few rounds.
closeReason: Fixed in c7b1631. The script now polls for the localStorage origin file before stopping the app (the fact desktop-smoke.sh actually asserts, not the adjacent library.json write), and shuts down with SIGTERM + wait-for-exit instead of kill + sleep 2 — WebKit flushes its databases during teardown, so the shutdown is part of producing the asserted fact. Not a hard exit: desktop-smoke.sh keeps ownership of the assertion. Evidence is a direct probe of the race window rather than a flake-catch: at the exact instant the OLD wait condition is satisfied, the origin file was ABSENT in 20 of 20 boots under 32-way CPU load (present 0) — so the old assertion depended entirely on sleep 2 covering a flush that had not begun, which is why growing the constant is the wrong fix. New script: origin wait resolved 20/20 with zero timeout warnings, desktop-boot passed 20/20 under the same load. HONEST LIMIT: the original end-to-end failure did not reproduce here — the old script also passed 20/20, because on a 32-core box sleep 2 still covers the flush. The race-window probe is the demonstration; the pass/fail runs alone are not.

title: selection.spec 'a REAL mouse click on a mark opens its note' fails ONLY in the full e2e suite — order-dependent, not random
description:
## Question

`apps/viewer/e2e/selection.spec.ts:96` fails **consistently in the full suite** and **passes consistently in isolation**. That is order/state dependence, not a flake in the coin-toss sense — and it means the viewer e2e suite is red on `main` right now.

## Measured 2026-07-27

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm run e2e -- selection.spec.ts` (isolated, this branch) | **9/9 pass**, the test in 552ms |
| `pnpm run e2e` (full, this branch) | **1 failed / 145 passed** — this test, 15.4s |
| `pnpm run e2e` (full, clean `main` @ 39f479a, separate worktree) | **1 failed / 141 passed** — the same test, 15.5s |

The third row is the attribution: it reproduces on unmodified `main`, so it is NOT caused by the fix/flaky-gates work. The 15s vs 0.5s duration is the tell — it is timing out on `expect(.note-pop).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15_000 })` after the real mouse click, i.e. the click lands somewhere that opens nothing.

## Why it matters more than one red test

This test is the ONLY gate on the real-pointer hit path. Its own header explains why keyboard Enter and a synthetic `click()` are deliberately not written here: both succeed against code where a real mouse click does nothing (`.claude/rules/osd-overlay-wrapper.md`). So while it is red-in-suite, that entire class is ungated in practice — and a red that everyone knows about stops being read.

## Where to look

The test derives its click pixel from `#archie-object-frame` AFTER an Escape dismissal, correcting for the ADR-0019 layout-row reflow (canvas grows, OSD re-centres). Both the halo box and the frame box are read from a live OSD viewport. Prime suspects, in order:

1. **A prior spec leaves viewport state behind** — the correction assumes a pure translation (measured at 1280x720: same width/height, y +71). Under a different starting zoom that assumption breaks and the derived pixel misses.
2. **Shared `.vite/deps` / server state across specs** — this suite runs against `astro preview` with `reuseExistingServer`, and a sibling boot rewriting the optimize cache is a known hazard here (`.claude/rules/viewer-optimizedeps-bare-includes.md`).
3. Something earlier in the suite navigating the same exhibit and leaving a selection/zoom that survives into this test's `goOffline` + `openPaintedNote`.

## Do not

Do not fix it by raising the 15s timeout or by moving the spec earlier in the file order — both hide the state leak rather than closing it, and the same reasoning that killed the tick-count waits in Archie-3e2d applies. Find what the suite leaves behind.

--- INVESTIGATED 2026-07-27, NOT FIXED — read this before starting ---

**Bisection says it is NOT one poisoning spec.** Measured, each a full clean run:
| set | result |
|---|---|
| `read.spec.ts selection.spec.ts` (the spec immediately before it) | 14/14 pass |
| the 6 specs before it + selection | 61/61 pass |
| the 8 specs *earlier* in the alphabet + selection | 59/59 pass |
| the whole suite | **selection.spec:96 FAILS** |
So neither half reproduces it. It needs the full set — cumulative, or a combination spanning both
halves. Do not go looking for a single culprit spec; I already did.

**It is Heisenberg-sensitive.** Adding two diagnostic lines before the click (a `console.log` and a
`page.evaluate` for `elementFromPoint`) made the full suite go **146/146 green**. Anything that
inserts a round trip between the measurement and the click changes the outcome, which is itself
strong evidence the defect is a TIMING/settle race and not a wrong-geometry bug.

**The one real clue from that instrumented run:**
```
halo   = {x:56.1, y:290.5, w:747.8, h:62.9}
anchorOpen   = {x:34.8, y:272.2, w:1841.1, h:1150.7}
anchorClosed = {x:34.8, y:272.2, w:1841.1, h:1150.7}   <-- IDENTICAL
d=(0,0)  click=(430.0,322.0)  viewport=1280x720
elementFromPoint at the click = CANVAS.a9s-gl-canvas
```
`d=(0,0)` — the frame did **not** move on dismissal. The test's header documents the opposite as its
premise ("measured 2026-07-26 … y +71"), and derives its click pixel from that shift. So the reflow
the correction exists to compensate for is **not always happening**, or has not happened yet when
`anchorClosed` is read. Note the test only waits for `.note-dock` to be ABSENT before measuring —
which is satisfied both when the dock was torn down AND when it was never there. A note that FLOATS
instead of docking produces no reflow at all; whether it docks depends on collapse state.

**So the likely shape (unproven):** `anchorClosed` is read before the post-dismissal layout has
settled, or in a state where no reflow will occur, and the derived pixel is right for one of those
worlds and wrong for the other. The fix is to make the settle observable — wait for the frame's box
to STOP changing (or for whatever signals the reflow completed) rather than for the dock's absence,
which is again the "gate measuring something adjacent to what it claims" shape this map keeps hitting.

**Still do not** raise the 15s timeout or reorder the file. And do not "fix" it by leaving the
diagnostic `page.evaluate` in — that is a sleep wearing a disguise.

title: Reading chips: replace the horizontal scroll with an overflow menu
description:
## The complaint
The readings row in the canvas dock looks bad and has an internal horizontal scroll.

## What is actually there (read before changing it)
The scroll is DELIBERATE and measured. `ReadingLegend.svelte:100-104`:

> ONE ROW, and the chips SCROLL rather than wrap. The bar's height is the entire cost of docking — it
> comes straight out of the image — so it is the number to be exact about. Measured on the narrative
> at 860px: wrapping chips made this bar 151px of a 698px stage (22%); one scrolling row is 34px (5%).

So any replacement must beat BOTH: no scroll, and no return to a 22% height tax. The comment already
anticipates this ticket — 'reversible if a future layout has the width to spare'.

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (human): overflow menu
Render as many chips as fit; collapse the remainder into a `+N` button that opens a small popover
with the rest. Keeps the 34px bar, removes the scroll, every reading stays one click away.

## What will bite
- **Measuring what fits** is the whole job. A ResizeObserver on the row plus per-chip width, or a
  CSS-only approach if one exists that does not thrash. Do not hard-code a chip count — reading names
  are author-authored and vary wildly in length.
- The gloss already hides below 1100px (`.gloss { display: none }`) — that existing responsive step
  interacts with this; check both together.
- `.opts.dimmed` (opacity 0.5 when notes are hidden) must still read correctly with a `+N` button.
- The popover is floating chrome. `Archie-40fe` spent a whole ticket getting floating chrome off the
  canvas — check its reservation rules before placing this one, and prefer docking it to the bar.

## Gate
Drive the narrative at 860px AND a wide viewport: assert the bar height stays ~34px, that no element
has `scrollWidth > clientWidth`, and that a reading only reachable via `+N` can still be activated.

---

## ATTEMPTED 2026-07-27 — not shipped. The blocker is a MEASUREMENT FEEDBACK LOOP.

A full overflow-menu implementation was written, driven in a browser, and **reverted** because it made
the row worse than the scroll it replaced. The WIP is preserved verbatim (never imported, never run):

- `ledgers/probes/2026-07-27-84af-overflow-menu-WIP.svelte.txt`
- `ledgers/probes/2026-07-27-84af-reading-overflow.spec.ts.txt`

### What went wrong, measured

The approach was the obvious one: ResizeObserver on `.opts`, measure each chip's `offsetWidth`, render
as many as fit, collapse the rest behind `+N`. It fails because **the row's width depends on the row's
content**, so sizing the content from that width is circular:

| viewport | `.opts` clientWidth | chips rendered | `+N` shown |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1600px | **210px** (of 1078px available) | **1** | yes — wrongly |

Collapse one chip → the row gets narrower → collapse another → it settles at ONE chip on a 1600px
viewport. Every chip but the first ends up in the menu, which is strictly worse than scrolling.

Loosening the flex did not break the loop, only moved it: `.opts { flex: 1 1 0 }` plus
`.legend { flex: 1 1 auto }` took `.opts` from 210px to **306px** and the legend from 537px to 633px —
still one chip, because `aside.legend` is itself shrink-to-fit inside a 1078px bar. **Any ancestor
that sizes to its content is an invalid thing to measure against.**

### What the next attempt should do

Derive the available width from something chip-count-INDEPENDENT — the chrome bar's own width minus
the legend's fixed parts (`.title`, `.gloss`, `.hide-toggle`) and gaps — rather than from `.opts`
or from `aside.legend`. Verify with the diagnostic that caught this: dump `optsClientW`, `legendW`,
`parentW` and the rendered chip count at 1600px, and require the chip count to be ALL of them before
believing any narrow-width result.

Alternatively, sidestep measurement: render every chip and let CSS decide, using a container-query or
a "hide what overflows" technique whose layout does not feed back. Not investigated.

### What IS still true and worth keeping

- The decided shape (overflow menu, not wrap, not scroll) is unchanged and still right.
- The preserved spec is a correct gate and encodes the two-sided trade properly: it asserts no
  `scrollWidth > clientWidth` AND that the bar stays under 64px, so a wrap cannot pass it either. Its
  third case — `+N` must NOT appear at 1600px — is precisely what caught the loop. Reuse it as-is.
- Keeping the popover inside the `role="radiogroup"` element is a real constraint discovered here: the
  radios must stay descendants of the group, so the menu cannot be hoisted to a sibling.


---

A full overflow-menu implementation was written, driven in a browser, and **reverted** because it made
the row worse than the scroll it replaced. The WIP is preserved verbatim (never imported, never run):

- `ledgers/probes/2026-07-27-84af-overflow-menu-WIP.svelte.txt`
- `ledgers/probes/2026-07-27-84af-reading-overflow.spec.ts.txt`

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1600px | **210px** (of 1078px available) | **1** | yes — wrongly |

## CORRECTION, same day — "feedback loop" was the wrong diagnosis. Here are the real numbers.

Measured against the SHIPPED (scrolling) component at a 1600px viewport, which is the baseline the
previous note failed to take:

```
bar        1078px  =  legend 671px  +  canvas-chrome-right 351px
.opts      clientWidth 402px   scrollWidth 790px      <- overflowing by 388px ALREADY
4 chips    175, 174, 164, 265  = 790px total
```

**The row is not being starved by a measurement loop. It is genuinely too small for its chips, on a
1600px screen, today.** The chips need 790px and have 402px. Every reading but one is already off the
right edge behind the existing scroll — that is the reported defect's actual cause.

What the earlier note got right is narrow and worth keeping: **the flex edit I tried made it worse.**
`.opts { flex: 1 1 0 }` + `.legend { flex: 1 1 auto }` took the row from 402px to 306px, because a
zero basis shrinks the shrink-to-fit legend around it. Do not repeat that edit. But 402 -> 306 was my
own regression, not the pre-existing condition, and reporting 210/306 as if they were the baseline was
simply wrong.

### What this means for the decided shape

An overflow menu still removes the scroll, but at these widths it would show **1–2 of 4 readings** and
put the rest behind `+N`. That is defensible for a long tail and poor for four items. So the menu is
necessary and NOT sufficient — the chips also have to get narrower, or the legend has to get more of
the bar. Concretely, in rough order of value:

1. **A 265px chip is the outlier** — that is one author-authored reading name at full length. Truncate
   the name with `text-overflow: ellipsis` and a `title`, capping a chip at ~150px. Four chips then
   need ~600px, which still exceeds 402px but changes the menu from "hides everything" to "hides the
   tail".
2. **Move the count badge into the menu only.** `.ct` is on every chip and buys little on a crowded
   bar.
3. **Look at the 351px `canvas-chrome-right` sibling.** The legend is not being denied space by CSS
   subtlety; another chrome group is simply taking a third of the bar.
4. Only then measure again and size the overflow menu.

### Method note, because this is the second time it bit

The first diagnosis measured the row **while my own half-finished change was in the tree**, and drew a
conclusion about the ORIGINAL design from it. Always capture the baseline from `HEAD` before
attributing a number to the code you are replacing. The preserved WIP and spec under `ledgers/probes/`
remain useful; the spec's third case ("no `+N` at 1600px") is now known to be an INCORRECT
expectation and must be dropped or rewritten against a real width budget.

## MEASURED: capping the name is NOT the lever (tried, reverted)

The correction above put "truncate the 265px chip" first. Measured, that was optimistic. With
`.nm { max-width: 13ch; text-overflow: ellipsis }` plus a `title`, at the same 1600px viewport:

```
before   chips 175, 174, 164, 265   total 790   (row 402)
after    chips 175, 174, 164, 192   total 717   (row 402)
```

The outlier drops 27%, the ROW drops 9% — 73px of the 388px that needs to go. And note the other
three chips did not move at all: "Cipher reading" is 14 characters and still measures 174px.

**So chip width is not dominated by the name.** It is padding + the 14px swatch + the `.ct` count
badge (which carries its own `padding-left: var(--space-3)`) + `font-size: 0.9rem` body text. A
13-character label costing 175px is roughly 58px of chrome around ~117px of text.

Reverted, because truncated names PLUS a still-scrolling row is not an improvement on the reported
complaint — it trades one visible flaw for two.

### Revised lever order, now measured rather than guessed

1. **Drop `.ct` from the bar chips**, keep counts in the overflow menu. It is per-chip and buys least
   on the crowded surface.
2. **Reduce the chip font-size** (0.9rem is body-size for what is a tab strip) and tighten padding.
3. **The 351px `canvas-chrome-right` sibling** — the legend gets 671px of 1078px. Whether that split
   is right is a layout decision, not a legend-local one.
4. The overflow menu, sized against whatever budget 1–3 leave.

Only after 1–3 is it worth knowing how many chips fit, because today the answer is one.

## 2026-07-27 round 3 — decided shape built, MEASURED, not converged. WIP refreshed.

User decided (grill): slim the chips + drop the gloss, keep the section nav, menu for the remainder.
All of that is built and measured. `ledgers/probes/2026-07-27-84af-overflow-menu-WIP.svelte.txt` is
refreshed with the current state. Reverted from the tree because two widths still overflow.

### What WORKED — keep all of it

**Chip slimming: 790px -> 572px total.** Three measures, all in the WIP:
- gloss deleted (92px — it only showed above 1100px, which is exactly where chips are most starved),
- count badge off the bar chip, folded into the `title` and kept in the menu (68px),
- name capped at 13ch with ellipsis, chip type 0.9rem -> 0.82rem.
Chips went 175/174/164/265 -> 139/143/135/155.

**The flex combination — this is the real finding, and it corrects my earlier "not a feedback loop"
note above, which was wrong.** Measured at 1600px, all three:

| `.legend` | `.opts` | row | chips visible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default | `1 1 auto` | 173px | 1 |
| `1 1 auto` | `1 1 0` | 306px | 1 |
| **`1 1 auto`** | **`1 1 auto`** | **468px** | **2** |

The loop is real: a default-flex legend hugs the collapsed row, so the row has nothing to grow back
into. Both declarations are load-bearing and only that pairing works. Height held at 24px throughout.

### WHERE IT STOPS — two things, one of them a genuine design conflict

1. **`flex: none` vs shrinkable chips is a fork, and I had both.** With `.opt { flex: none }` the menu
   works (2 chips at 1600, 1 at 1280, no overflow) but a chip overflows at 1024, where the row is
   82px. Making chips shrinkable (`0 1 auto; min-width: 0`) fixes 1024 — and then `chipW` measures the
   SHRUNKEN width, `fitCount` concludes everything fits, and the menu never appears at all: 4 squeezed
   ellipsised chips at every width. **Shrink-to-fit and collapse-to-menu are two strategies and they
   cannot both be on.** Pick one: either chips are rigid and the menu absorbs everything (needs a
   `min-width` on `.opts` so the legend cannot be crushed below one chip + `+N`), or chips shrink to a
   floor and the menu only takes what is left below that floor.
2. **Below ~1100px the legend is crushed by the bar, not by its chips.** Measured `.opts`: 82px at
   1024, **0px** at 860. No chip strategy survives a 0px row — that is the bar's allocation, and it is
   the "how much of the bar does the legend get" question the user chose NOT to reopen. It may have to
   be reopened for narrow widths specifically, or the legend collapses to a single `Readings ▾` button
   below some breakpoint.

**Recommended next step:** rigid chips + `min-width` on `.opts` sized to one chip plus `+N`, and a
below-1100px rule that renders the whole legend as one `Readings ▾` menu button. That is a small
amount of work on top of the WIP, and it needs the breakpoint decision in (2).

title: Viewer: a fullscreen reading mode that auto-hides the chrome
description:
## The ask
An option in the viewer to hide all the non-note chrome — like a fullscreen.

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (human): auto-hide, returns on pointer move
Everything except the image and its markers fades after ~2s idle. Any pointer move or keypress brings
the chrome back; it fades again. Escape exits the mode. The video-player pattern.

Chosen over a static hide because readings COLOUR THE MARKS — a mode that hid the readings bar
permanently would make the reader leave and re-enter to change what they are looking at. Auto-hide
gives the clean image without making anything unreachable.

## What is in scope to hide
Breadcrumb, object topbar, filmstrip, zoom cue, readings bar, notes aside. What STAYS at all times:
the image, its markers, and the note card when a mark is selected.

## What will bite
- **This is not the same as 'Hide all'.** That existing control (ReadingLegend) turns MARKERS off —
  the opposite concern. Do not merge them; a reader in fullscreen still wants the marks.
- The viewer already has piecemeal collapse state (`asideCollapsed`, `notesHidden` in
  ExhibitView.svelte). Decide whether fullscreen is a third independent flag or a mode that overrides
  them, and make re-entry restore what the reader had.
- **Idle-timer + `pointer: coarse`**: on touch there is no hover, so a pointer-move trigger never
  fires. Tap-to-reveal is the touch equivalent — and it must not also select a marker. Couples to
  Archie-cf4a's touch work.
- Native `requestFullscreen()` is a separate question from hiding chrome. Decide whether this mode
  also goes fullscreen at the browser level, or only reclaims the app's own chrome. Prefer the latter
  first — browser fullscreen has its own escape semantics that will fight Escape-to-exit.
- Do not let the auto-hide fire while a note card is open or a control has focus.

## Gate
Drive it: enter the mode, assert the chrome is gone after the idle window, assert a pointer move
restores it, assert Escape exits, and assert a marker is still selectable and its note still opens
while the chrome is hidden.

title: Narrative aside: scrolling makes the Sections/Notes toggle unreachable
description:
## The defect
Scrolling the narrative pushes the notes tab out of view — the further you scroll, the more
inaccessible it gets.

## Mechanism, confirmed in code
`NarrativeReader.svelte:904` — the whole aside is ONE scroll container (`aside { overflow: auto }`),
and `.pane-toggle` (:796) is an ordinary flow child of it with `margin: 0 0 var(--space-4)`. So the
Sections/Notes toggle scrolls away with the prose. There is no sticky, no fixed header.

## This is the SECOND symptom of a header that was already too tall
`NarrativeReader.svelte:315-329` documents a measured hole caused by the same header:

> the column's header — eyebrow, title, hint, credit, pane toggle, on top of the `--pane-top`
> reservation — pushes the first beat's box to 400-819px in a 720px column, so at `scrollTop: 0` the
> centre line at 360 sits ABOVE it

That required boundary predicates in the scroll-spy to work around. **And I made it worse today**:
Archie-36e6 added a `<MetadataRun>` at :793, directly above the toggle. So this ticket fixes a
regression I introduced as well as the reported defect.

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (human): pin the toggle AND shrink the header
1. `.pane-toggle` becomes sticky so it never leaves the viewport.
2. Credit + metadata move behind a small disclosure so the header stops growing.

Chosen over sticky-only (leaves the documented too-tall header exactly as it is) and over a fixed
header block (spends ~120px permanently in a 720px column, which is what the header comment says is
already too expensive).

## What will bite
- A sticky element inside `overflow: auto` needs the ancestor chain to not clip it — check the
  `.narrative`/`aside` chain for an `overflow: hidden` that kills `position: sticky` silently.
- The sticky toggle now overlaps prose as it scrolls under: it needs an opaque background, or the
  text will read through it.
- **Re-check the scroll-spy boundary predicates after shrinking the header.** They exist to paper
  over the header's height; if the header shrinks enough, the first-beat hole may close and the
  workaround may be reducible. Do not silently leave dead compensation in place.

## Gate
Drive `voynich-reading` at 1280x720: scroll the aside to the bottom and assert the Sections/Notes
toggle is still visible and clickable, and that clicking Notes still switches the pane.
closeReason: Fixed in 9db0dec. Two halves: (1) .pane-toggle is position:sticky;top:0, bleeding into the aside's horizontal padding so cards passing beneath cannot peek at its edges; (2) the exhibit's Dublin Core rows fold into a closed-by-default <details>. SCOPE NARROWED: the ticket said 'credit + metadata behind a disclosure', but Credit renders the IIIF requiredStatement, which is MUST-display (presentation.ts:31), and a closed <details> is not displayed — so only the metadata folds and the credit stays unconditionally visible. Gated by apps/viewer/e2e/narrative-header.spec.ts, red-green proven on both halves independently (sticky removed -> 'pane toggle scrolled off the top of the aside'; details forced open -> not.toHaveAttribute failed). 67 neighbouring specs green; svelte-check 1535 files 0/0.

title: Examples in the viewer: partition them like Studio, and let publish opt in
description:
## The ask
Separate the examples in the viewer the way Studio does — and Studio's examples do not appear in the
viewer at all. The showroom **sampler** exhibit in particular is missing.

## THREE separate mechanisms hide things, and they are easy to confuse
Measured 2026-07-27:

1. **Template exclusion (live path).** `App.svelte:1913` `buildFullLibrary({ includeTemplates })`
   excludes bundled examples BY DEFAULT, citing CONTEXT §"Local view loop": *'avoid the template ones,
   or opt-in'*. This is why studio's examples do not reach a live viewer.
2. **`unlisted: true` (published tree).** The **sampler** is marked unlisted in the viewer's own
   fixtures (`apps/viewer/fixtures/sample-data.ts`), so it IS built and IS URL-reachable at
   `/sampler/` — it is only filtered out of the hall by `listedExhibits` (gallery-view.ts:28). That
   is why the showroom sampler is missing specifically.
3. **Two seed sources.** Studio seeds from `apps/studio/src/seed-data.ts`; the viewer's published tree
   is generated from `apps/viewer/fixtures/sample-data.ts` via `gen-published`. The slug sets happen
   to be nearly identical today (viewer has `screenshots` extra), which makes the divergence easy to
   miss until they drift.

Studio already solves the presentation half: `partitionExhibits(exhibits, isTemplate)` and
`examplesDefaultOpen(ownCount)` in `apps/studio/src/library-home.js`, driving a collapsible Examples
section that auto-collapses once the author has their own exhibits.

## DECIDED 2026-07-27 (human): partition in the viewer AND add a publish opt-in
- The viewer hall grows the same own/Examples split, collapsed by default once own exhibits exist.
- Publish gains an **'Include bundled examples'** option beside 'Include source originals'.

**This qualifies a CONTEXT rule and the change must be recorded there, not just here.** CONTEXT
§"Local view loop" currently states a template is not the author's content; after this it is a
per-publish CHOICE rather than a blanket rule. The concern was raised before the decision and the
decision was made with it visible — so update CONTEXT rather than leaving the two in contradiction,
or a later reader will 'fix' this back.

## What will bite
- `partitionExhibits` / `examplesDefaultOpen` should move to render-core so both apps share ONE
  definition rather than the viewer growing a second copy that drifts.
- **The viewer has no `isTemplate` signal.** Studio knows its own template slugs; a published tree
  does not carry that fact. Decide how it travels — most likely a flag on the exhibit card, written
  by publish when the opt-in is used. That is a published-schema addition, so it wants the same
  care as any other (see Archie-fc75 on versioning `archie.json`).
- Do NOT conflate this with `unlisted`. Unlisted means the AUTHOR hid it; an example is a different
  KIND of exhibit. Two concepts, two flags. Decide separately whether the sampler should stay
  unlisted once an Examples section exists — it probably should not.

## Gate
With examples included: the hall shows own exhibits ungrouped and an 'Examples (N)' section,
collapsed when own exhibits exist and open when they do not. Without the opt-in: byte-identical
published output to today.

title: Wire tree-level schema migration: an older published tree must open, not refuse
description:
## The gap

`migrate()` (packages/render-core/src/migrate/migrate.ts) is a complete, tested runner with a
`MIGRATIONS` registry — and **no production caller**. Grep for its importers: only `stamp`,
`foldLayersIntoTags` and `SCHEMA_VERSION` are wired anywhere. The runner has never run.

So the property Archie-fc75 was really asking for — tldraw's 'old data loads cleanly after schema
changes because the loader runs migrations automatically' — is **not** true here, even though the
version stamp it proposed already exists (marker.ts:29 writes it, :67 gates on it).

## Why it is latent rather than broken

`SCHEMA_VERSION` is 1 and `MIGRATIONS` is empty, so no published tree can currently be older than
the reader. **The day someone appends `{ to: 2 }`, every tree already in the wild starts refusing**
with 'Re-publish it from a current Archie' — and re-publishing is exactly what the author of a
distributed archive cannot do.

That is the same regret curve fc75's decision cited, one level down: cheap now, expensive once files
are out there.

## Two things are missing, and only the first is hard

1. **A tree-level migration path.** `migrate()` is per-annotation-doc — it takes a
   `Record<string, unknown>` and brings one document forward. Nothing brings a v(n-1)
   `exhibits.json` / `collection.json` / per-exhibit manifest forward. That shape needs designing;
   it is not just a call site.
2. **The call site in the open path.** Once (1) exists, `validateArchieMarker` stops refusing
   `version < SCHEMA_VERSION` and the tree reader migrates on read.

## Do not simply loosen the gate

Accepting an older marker with no migration behind it converts a clean refusal into the downstream
undebuggable parse failure ADR-0020 was written to prevent (ADR-0020:44, 'validation, not
authentication ... catches accidents + version drift'). The refusal is correct until (1) lands.

## Where it stands now

marker.ts now distinguishes the two directions so they give different, actionable advice — newer tree
says 'Update Archie', older tree says 'Re-publish' — and the older branch carries a comment pointing
here. That is the honest half; this ticket is the real half.

## Acceptance

- A tree-level migration shape, with at least one real migration exercising it (a synthetic v1→v2 is
  acceptable as the proof).
- `validateArchieMarker` accepts `version < SCHEMA_VERSION` and the tree opens, gated by a test that
  publishes at v1, bumps, and re-opens.
- Red-green: without the migration registered, the old tree must still refuse.

---

## Absorbs Archie-7eae (closed 2026-07-27 as superseded)

7eae was the implementation ticket for fc75's decision. Its items 1, 2 and 5 (stamp the version,
read it in `validateArchieMarker`, test the marker) were already built — 1 and 2 since ADR-0020,
5 extended today. Its items **3 and 4** are this ticket:

3. `ZipFilesystem.fromZip` / the open path checks the version and runs migrations.
4. Wire the migration runner to that check.

7eae framed 4 as wiring. It is not: `migrate()` is per-annotation-doc and cannot bring a v(n-1)
`exhibits.json` / `collection.json` forward, so the tree-level shape has to be designed first. That
is why this ticket's acceptance asks for the shape plus one real migration exercising it, rather
than a call site.

title: Video transcode: desktop sidecar + Chromium WebCodecs (graduated out of Fog)
description:
## Origin

Graduated out of map Fog by the 2026-07-27 batch grill on Archie-4b0a. The earlier decline
(WebCodecs = Chromium-only) is superseded: the user chose to build BOTH paths rather than keep
measure-and-tell as the only answer for video.

## Decided shape

- **Desktop (Tauri/Flatpak): a native sidecar.** WebKitGTK has no WebCodecs, so the webview cannot
  transcode. Invoke ffmpeg or gstreamer (gstreamer is already in the GNOME 49 runtime — verify which
  before committing; cite tauri-fs-seam and tauri-csp rules for the bridge shape). This covers the
  primary desktop story.
- **Chromium web: WebCodecs.** In-browser transcode where the API exists.
- **Firefox/Safari web: the measure-and-tell hand-off stays** ("180 GB — run HandBrake, or budget
  ~$2.70/mo"), greyed with reason per Archie-c367's rules — never silently swapped.

## Constraints

- Tier semantics per Archie-4b0a: archival keeps bytes as-is; web tier transcodes. Publish-time,
  re-derivable from retained originals (assets-original/).
- Target codec/params are a decision FOR this ticket (likely H.264/AAC or VP9/Opus in MP4/WebM for
  static-host compatibility) — measure on real material, don't guess.
- Two implementations must produce compatible output; verify the published tree plays the same
  either way (wavesurfer/media-src CSP rules bind on desktop playback).
- perf-measure-the-flow binds: publish-pipeline impact measured via scripts/perf/publishrun.mjs.

## Prior art

Check the freecut study docs (docs/research/freecut-*.md) and Prior Art corpus for transcode
precedent before choosing the sidecar invocation shape.

---

## H1 DECIDED 2026-07-27 — target codec, and the runtime finding that constrains it

**WEB-TIER TARGET: H.264 High + AAC-LC in MP4, `+faststart`, 720p, CRF 23 / 128 kbit/s.**
Fallback when the machine has no H.264: VP9 + Opus in WebM, CRF 33 / 96 kbit/s — **offered, never
silently swapped** (Archie-c367). Both live in `apps/studio/src/video-transcode.ts` as
`WEB_TIER_H264` / `WEB_TIER_VP9`.

**Why H.264 despite being the encumbered one.** MDN's web video codec guide (fetched 2026-07-27):
MP4 + AVC + AAC is *"a broadly-supported combination—by every major browser, in fact"*, while the
WebM/open-codec recommendation is qualified *"generally well-supported, with the exception being
Safari on older Apple devices"*. A published tree is read by visitors we will never meet, on browsers
we cannot poll, and the bytes are un-fixable once pushed. So the ARTIFACT takes the compatible
format and the ENCODER side absorbs the awkwardness — that is the asymmetry that decides it.

### Runtime finding — MEASURED, not guessed (this is the load-bearing part)

The manifest (`src-tauri/flatpak/digital.compost.archie.yml`) pins `org.gnome.Platform//49` and
declares no extra modules. That runtime ships **both** `ffmpeg` 7.1.3 and `gst-launch-1.0`. But:

| capability | base `org.gnome.Platform//49` |
| --- | --- |
| VP9 encode (`libvpx-vp9` / `vp9enc`) | **yes** |
| Opus encode, AAC encode, VP8, AV1 (svt/aom) | **yes** |
| WebM + MP4 muxers (`webmmux`, `mp4mux`/`qtmux`) | **yes** |
| **H.264 ENCODE** (`libx264` / `x264enc`) | **NO** |
| **H.264 DECODE** | **NO** |

Evidence, four independent ways:
- base `libavcodec.so.61` DT_NEEDED = libvpx, libaom, libopus, libSvtAv1Enc — **no libx264/libx265**;
- its build config has `--enable-libvpx` and **zero** `enable-libx264`, plus an explicit
  `--disable-decoder='h264,hevc,vc1,vvc'`;
- `gst-inspect-1.0 x264enc` resolves to `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/codecs-extra/lib/libgstx264.so` —
  the **extension** — while vp9enc/opusenc/webmmux/mp4mux all resolve to the base tree;
- forcing `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to the base lib dir (simulating a machine without the extension):
  VP9+Opus/WebM encoded fine (23145 bytes, ffprobe `vp9`/`opus`) and AAC encoded fine, while
  `-c:v libx264` gave `Unknown encoder 'libx264'` and decoding an H.264 input gave
  `Decoding requested, but no decoder found for: h264`.

H.264 arrives only via `org.freedesktop.Platform.codecs-extra//25.08-extra` (runtime metadata :90,
`add-ld-path = lib`), which the Archie manifest does not declare.

**The DECODE half is the constraint that actually bites.** Most authored video IS H.264, so on a
stock runtime the sidecar cannot *read* typical input whatever it writes. That collapses the choice:
codecs-extra is required for the desktop sidecar to be useful at all, independent of output target —
and once it is required, H.264 output costs nothing extra.

### OPEN, and deliberately not done here (user's call)

**Declare `org.freedesktop.Platform.codecs-extra//25.08-extra` in
`src-tauri/flatpak/digital.compost.archie.yml`.** Not shipped in this ticket: it is a packaging +
licensing decision (AVC patent pool; x264 is GPL, which Archie's GPL-3.0-only accommodates), not an
implementation one. Until it lands, a packaged Archie transcodes only non-H.264 sources and only to
VP9/WebM. `video_probe_encoders` reports both directions so the UI can grey with a reason rather
than fail mid-publish.

## H2 — desktop sidecar: SHIPPED as code, packaged verification PENDING

`src-tauri/src/video.rs` + `apps/studio/src/video-transcode.ts` (commit `d2c50ab`).

- Two Tauri commands: `video_probe_encoders` (never throws — reports `ffmpeg:false` so the control
  greys with a reason) and `video_transcode`. Registered in `lib.rs`.
- **No shell, and the webview cannot express an argv** — it sends a typed `TranscodeRequest`; Rust
  builds the arg vector. `validate_path` rejects non-absolute paths, leading `-`, and NUL. Same trust
  posture as `assertSafeName` in the fs seam.
- Progress via `-progress pipe:1` → a `TranscodeProgress` event carrying `jobId`.
- The TS seam mirrors `tiff-transcode.ts`: lazy, `isTauri()`-gated, classifies rather than swallows.
  **It never falls back silently — it throws**, and `videoSkipCount()` gives a caller's skip the
  visibility `bakeFallbackCount()` gives a bake fallback (perf-measure-the-flow §2). Higher stakes
  here: a silently degraded video tier publishes the gigabytes the tier existed to avoid.

Three things measured rather than remembered, each of which would have been a bug:

1. **ffmpeg's `out_time_ms` reports MICROseconds.** A 3.000 s encode emits `out_time_us=3000000`
   *and* `out_time_ms=3000000` (7.1.1 host and 7.1.3 runtime). Trusting the field name would report
   progress 1000× high. The parser reads `out_time_us`; a test pins it.
2. **An absent INPUT and an unwritable OUTPUT both say `No such file or directory`.** They are told
   apart by `Error opening input` vs `Error opening output`, never by the errno text.
3. Both arg vectors were **executed and ffprobed** (`vp9,1280,720`+`opus`; `h264,1280,720`+`aac`);
   `scale=-2:'min(ih,720)'` is downscale-only (a 320×240 source measured out at 320×240).

**NOT VERIFIED, stated plainly:** there is no Rust toolchain in this environment, so `video.rs` is
**not compile-checked** and its `#[cfg(test)]` module has **not been run**. The desktop path is
**not claimed verified** — it needs `cargo test`, a `tauri build`, and a Flatpak run. Nothing about
the TS suite substitutes for that.

## H3 — Chromium WebCodecs: DESIGNED, NOT BUILT. A dependency decision is needed.

Probe: `scripts/probe/webcodecs-video.mjs` (commit `a94ec23`). Headless Chromium 148, localhost
secure context.

- Video encode is genuinely there — H.264 High, VP9, VP8, AV1 each produced a real chunk. The probe
  does a **real one-frame encode** as well as `isConfigSupported`, because freecut documents the
  declarative check as unreliable (`render-support.ts:261-289` — it omits frame rate and display
  size that a real encode supplies, so Chrome can approve a config then reject the first frame).
- **No demux and no mux surface exists.** `MediaContainerDecoder`, `MediaContainerEncoder`,
  `VideoMuxer`, `VideoDemuxer` all absent. `MediaRecorder` is not a shortcut — it muxes only a LIVE
  stream in real time.
- **AAC-LC encode is UNAVAILABLE; Opus was the only audio codec offered.** So even handed a muxer,
  Chromium could not produce the sidecar's H.264+AAC target — it could only emit VP9+Opus/WebM, a
  *different artifact*. This ticket requires both implementations to produce compatible output, so
  **H3 is more than a dependency question.** (Caveat: Chrome for Testing; re-run on a branded Chrome
  before acting.)

**DECISION NEEDED FROM THE USER — a runtime dependency.** The container gap needs a library. The
precedented choice is **`mediabunny`** (freecut carries 1.50.3 and does both halves with it: demux
`canvas-render-orchestrator.ts:300`, mux `client-renderer.ts:267-297`; it carries no other muxer,
no mp4box.js, no webm-muxer, none hand-rolled). Not added here — dependency approval is the user's.

Given the AAC finding, the honest recommendation is to **leave H3 unbuilt**: it would cost a
dependency and still produce an artifact incompatible with the desktop path's.

## H4 — the measure-and-tell hand-off: SHIPPED

`videoTierTell()` in `video-transcode.ts`. Computes from real inventory (count, bytes, duration) via
a **stated bitrate model** (`WEB_TIER_VIDEO_KBPS` = 2000 + 128), deliberately not a compression
ratio — a ratio measured on synthetic patterns would be fiction, and real material varies by an
order of magnitude. When durations are unknown it falls back to a blind ratio **and says so in the
copy** ("very roughly" vs "about"). `HOSTING_USD_PER_GB_MONTH` is duplicated with a comment;
Archie-c85f owns the real table and is in flight — swap when it lands.

Tests pin that it never claims Archie did the conversion, always names both ways out, and is empty
when there is no video.

## PRIOR ART

- **freecut is NOT a donor for the sidecar.** It spawns no encoder and links no native library —
  every ffmpeg mention in its tree is prose, and `headless/README.md:107` names ffmpeg pre-decode as
  explicitly not wired up. Stated absence; the sidecar design claims no precedent from it.
- freecut **is** the citation for the container gap and for mediabunny (above), and for the
  test-encode-over-declarative-check lesson now baked into the probe.
- The `freecut-lessons.md:13-23` erratum corrects **Archie-side storage claims**, not freecut ones,
  and says in terms "the freecut-side findings stand" — nothing in it touches transcode.
- `tiff-transcode.ts`'s header is the in-repo shape donor (lazy-load, caller classifies failures);
  `github.rs`'s `DeployError` is the donor for the typed serializable command error.

## FOLLOW-UP (out of scope here, by instruction)

1. **Publish-pipeline integration.** Wiring video into the web tier belongs after Archie-4b0a's tier
   engine lands. `site.ts` and `publish-flows.svelte.ts` were deliberately NOT touched (other agents
   own them). Note for whoever does it: video at ingest does **not** go through `saveOriginalFile` —
   `ingest-flows.ts:461-467` saves the asset directly, so for AV *the asset is itself the untouched
   original*. 4b0a's "re-derivable from retained originals" therefore holds, but only as long as the
   web tier writes to a derived path and never overwrites the asset.
2. **Flatpak manifest: declare codecs-extra** (see H1 OPEN).
3. **`cargo test` + packaged Flatpak run** for `video.rs` (see H2 NOT VERIFIED).
4. **perf**: `scripts/perf/publishrun.mjs` end-to-end once integrated — perf-measure-the-flow binds,
   and a per-object transcode is exactly the shape that looks huge in a primitive benchmark and
   modest end-to-end.

## GATES

Studio vitest **1085 pass / 81 files** (baseline **1042** at `d7ae26f` + 43 new — the brief's "1037"
was stale; 1042 + 43 = 1085 reconciles). `pnpm typecheck` clean. No `.svelte` touched, so no
svelte-check. Rust untested (no toolchain).

Red-green: **10 of 10 injections into the seam went red.** Two more stayed green on the first pass
and both were **probe bugs, not gate gaps** — one edited only an error-message string and left the
`throw` intact, the other had zero anchor occurrences (shell ate the backticks) and was reported as
SKIPPED rather than passed. Re-run correctly, both went red.


---

## MERGED 2026-07-27 (b7494ce) — code in; TWO DECISIONS NEED MICAH before this closes

1. **Declare the `codecs-extra` Flatpak extension in the manifest?** Measured: org.gnome.Platform//49
   ships ffmpeg 7.1.3 WITHOUT H.264 in either direction — the sidecar cannot even DECODE typical
   authored video on a stock runtime. codecs-extra fixes decode and makes H.264 output free. This is
   a packaging/licensing declaration, not a code change — user's call.
2. **Accept the H3 revision: leave the Chromium WebCodecs path unbuilt?** New evidence vs the earlier
   "both paths" decision: Chromium has no AAC encoder (Opus only) and no mux surface, so the browser
   path could only ever emit a DIFFERENT artifact (VP9+Opus/WebM) than the sidecar's H.264/AAC MP4,
   violating the compatible-output requirement. If revisited, the dependency would be mediabunny
   (freecut precedent) — a new dep, also user's call.

Also pending mechanically (not decisions): cargo compile + packaged desktop run, publish-pipeline
integration after Archie-4b0a's tier engine, publishrun.mjs pass. Note for the integrator: AV assets
skip saveOriginalFile (ingest-flows.ts:461-467) — the asset IS the original; a web-tier video must
write to a DERIVED path or re-derivability breaks.

title: Desktop gh push: fetch the remote branch into the staging repo so the pack carries only new blobs
description: Follow-up flagged while closing Archie-53e3. src-tauri/src/github.rs:339-341 stages into a throwaway Repository::init and :392 writes a ROOT commit (no parents), so pack negotiation has no base and every deploy ships every blob — O(tiles) in bytes, though in one request (so the API rate-limit motivation of 53e3 does not apply). Closing it means fetching the remote branch into the staging repo before committing, so negotiation excludes existing objects. Rust change; verify against a real remote or a local bare repo.

title: dist/ goes stale at every MERGE — one parent's bundle is kept while the other's source lands
description:
## The gap

`packages/archie-viewer/dist/` (mirrored to root `dist/`) is a committed, CDN-published artifact.
CI enforces it with `pnpm sync-dist:check`, which compares **root `dist/` against
`packages/archie-viewer/dist/`**. It never compares either mirror against the SOURCE it was built
from, so both being equally stale passes.

`checks.yml:239` records that this is deliberate — *"Deliberately NOT a freshness gate — the repo's
cadence is batch catch-up."* That policy is broadly working. The failure is narrower and different
from what it looks like at first glance.

## CORRECTION to the first draft of this ticket

The original text claimed drift of "~69 commits". **That was wrong.** The number came from how far
one working branch trailed `main` and was misattributed to `dist`. `dist/` is in fact rebuilt very
frequently — at origin/main, the tip commit *itself* touches it, as do most recent merges.

Recording the error because it points at the wrong fix: "nobody rebuilds dist" suggests a scheduled
regeneration job, and that would be pure waste against a tree that already rebuilds it constantly.

## What actually happens: the MERGE re-stales it

Measured at `origin/main` = `84bab01`, a merge of parents `2699f3f` and `c27aa95`:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| tip's committed `dist/archie-viewer.js` | `8a7a1fea1e` |
| parent `2699f3f`'s `dist/archie-viewer.js` | `8a7a1fea1e` — **byte-identical** |
| source files the merge took from the other parent (`c27aa95`) | **3** |

The merge kept one parent's `dist/` verbatim while incorporating source from the other side, and
nothing rebuilt afterwards. A no-op `node build.mjs` + `pnpm sync-dist` at that tip dirties **35
files**; the entry bundle differs by 6 lines and `dist-single/archie-viewer.single.js` by 146.

Ruled out two other explanations first:

- **Not build nondeterminism.** Two consecutive builds of identical source are byte-identical
  (`md5sum` of `dist/archie-viewer.js` plus the sorted file listing).
- **Not a merge blend of two chunk sets.** Every content-hashed chunk in the committed `dist/` is
  referenced by `archie-viewer.js` — no orphans. It is a real, internally consistent build, just of
  a source state that no longer exists.

So the shipped bundle will not 404 a chunk. It is simply missing whatever source arrived on the
losing side of the last merge.

## Why a per-PR gate is the WRONG fix

The staleness is *created by the merge*. Both PRs can be perfectly fresh and the merge still
produces a stale `dist/`. A PR-level `git diff --exit-code` is structurally incapable of catching
this, and it would impose a real cost for nothing: every PR touching viewer or render-core source
would carry a rebuilt minified bundle, and with many concurrent worktrees that means frequent
conflicts on a file nobody can resolve by hand. That cost is very likely why batch catch-up was
chosen in the first place.

## Proposed fix — post-merge, on main, auto-commit

```yaml
# on: push: branches: [main]
- run: pnpm --filter @render/archie-viewer build && pnpm sync-dist
- run: |
    git diff --quiet -- dist packages/archie-viewer/dist packages/archie-viewer/dist-single \
      || (git commit -am "chore: regenerate dist/ after merge" && git push)
```

Auto-commit rather than fail: there is no human decision in a regeneration, and a failing main is
worse than a bot commit. PRs stay clean; the published artifact is never more than one push behind.
The build is deterministic, so this cannot flake — that is what the determinism check above
establishes.

Related, and worth closing together: `.claude/rules/archie-viewer-eager-closure.md` records a
still-open follow-up that CI does not catch a HAND-edited `bundle-size.json`
(`git diff --exit-code packages/archie-viewer/bundle-size.json` after `bundle:check`). Same family —
*a gate whose reference point the gated thing can move.*

## Scope note

Tags are unaffected in practice but unguarded in principle: `v1`/`v1.0.0`/`v1.1` are from June, so
anyone pinning `@v1.1` on jsDelivr gets that tag's bundle by design. If a future release is cut from
a stale main, the released artifact inherits the staleness — a tag-time assertion would be the
belt-and-braces version of the above.

## Found by

Archie-1244's shadow recalibration, which had to rebuild `dist/` to ship a token change and noticed
the rebuild touching 35 unrelated files.

Maintainer chose the tag-time boundary after seeing the measurement: a post-merge fail-on-main gate
would have reddened main on 8 of the 11 source-touching merges in the last 40 first-parent commits
(~73%), for something mechanical. checks.yml:200 had already reached the same conclusion from the
earlier era's numbers and named the remedy - 'freshness belongs at the release boundary, not here'.
No contents: write, no bot commits, zero red mains.

Diagnosis on the ticket: the staleness is created by the MERGE, not by careless PRs. At origin/main
84bab01 the tip's dist/archie-viewer.js was byte-identical to parent 2699f3f's while the merge took
3 source files from the other parent. Both PRs can be fresh and the merge still ships stale bytes,
so a per-PR gate cannot catch this class at all.

Proven red-green-green: committed dist == source -> exit 0; token change injected into render-core
-> exit 1; restored -> exit 0. Injection restored from a /tmp copy, never 'git checkout --'.

Scope stated on the ticket: this does NOT keep main's HEAD fresh, by design. main may drift between
releases; a tagged release may not.
